Even TAs have told me how they see this class as unfair. Professor discourages outside help from tutors or videos online. You are expected to get ~40s on exams.

Assignments and exams can be difficult. Professors and TAs have plenty of Office hours to ask for help. Professors have their own grading scale, so don't pay too much attention to superficial scores, work harder and you will get high grades. Everyone's scores may not be high, but the grading scale is different from the normal, maybe 65 is an A.

HW is graded extremely harshly and you can easily get a 0 on the HW for simple formatting mistakes. Exams are online and typically half the class scores are below 50-60. Lectures aren't great since it's asynchronous. You're better off taking the class in person with a different professor. Feedback on HW is vague and honestly not helpful.

Professor Cai is incredible. Her humor and energy turned a difficult language into something I genuinely loved practicing. Teaching Chinese songs was a brilliant touch that made the culture feel alive. It's safe to make mistakes, you gain real confidence, take her course. Would definitely recommend Cai Lao Shi. She's genuinely wants you to learn and wants what's best for you. As long as you do the work and try, you will get a good grade. Very enthusiastic about your learning and creates a great class vibe.

An amazing teacher for Chinese Language, especially if you're learning for the first time! She's very understanding and is pretty lenient with grading. The classroom experience isn't intimidating at all, but there is a lot of speaking and daily vocab dictations, so be prepared to be prepared!

Her 3 exam is worth 75% of your grade, other grades comes from discussion post. attendance isn't mandatory but if you don't come you are not gonna do good on the exam. Lectures are extremely boring and dry. This is not a typical easy A elective.

This class is an easy addition to a schedule. She is very passionate about the topic and created all of her slideshows. The workload is light, and the midterms/finals are open note.

Professor Wilson writes and talks as fast as she can during the lectures, and she doesn't care if her students understand. Her handwriting is hard to read and understanding her lectures is also very difficult. Dr. Wilson is very knowledgeable. Lectures and class expectations are clear, but she is inaccessible outside of class and unreceptive to student feedback. reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Wilson is a caring person with a lack of teaching ability. She underprepared her students for every assessment. Left for two weeks for a "medical absence" and left a TA in charge. Came back for a week and spent roughly a day or so reteaching the material. To say the least, this was insufficient. Exams do not match the class work and the class work does not help complete the homework. If you would like to teach yourself a math course take it with prof. Wilson

Inaccessible outside of class, poor lecturer, and generally kind of rude to students. My grades drastically improved when I stopped going to class and started just working through the textbook. I think a research professor who has to teach to keep her funding. Definitely not something she seems to care about much. Avoid if you can!

Dr. Wilson is the best professor I have ever had. I feared calc II prior to taking Dr. Wilson, but her expressions of concepts and her examples for every unit are incredibly clear. Calc II has been my favorite course so far because of Dr. Wilson, would take the course 1 million times over again.

She tends to move quickly in lecture, but it is a very fast pace class in nature. It is sometimes hard to get individual help, as she tends to only explain things one way and has very busy office hours which can sometimes turn into another lecture. Very average.

She will give you plenty of resources to study and is readily available to help students that are confused. Keeping up in class can be difficult as she writes and talks very fast. Overall she's a good teacher but if you have trouble initially grasping concepts make sure to utilize the past recorded lectures and other resources or you'll fall behind

Honestly, while I wasn't fan of professor Wilson at the start of the semester she is actually a pretty decent teacher. The class is work heavy, homework each week and a quiz, but if you work hard and, most importantly, stay on top of the content, you'll do fine! She's also very patient and it was a nice classroom environment

Professor Wilson is someone who keeps up to schedule and updates her students throughout the semester. Examples are up in advanced to keep up with the lectures and the quizzes and exams are pretty straightforward. The only issue is if you're someone who needs to reach out to your professors, that may be the only drawback, otherwise she's great.

Her teaching style is writing the theories on the board then showing different examples. I found it helpful to come prepared with questions on the homework/reviews. She's not very accommodating with quiz remakes and your final grade is largely made up of quizzes/ exams. Attendance isn't mandatory and she has her past lessons posted on youtube.

Professor Wilson is good at math but not a great teacher. However she gives extra points on quizzes if you go up and do homework problems on the board which ended up being the reason I got an A in the class. If you struggle with math, don't take her. If you tend to teach yourself anyway, Professor Wilson is a good professor for that.

Professor Wilson knows what she is doing, but sometimes is difficult to understand. However, if you take notes during class and do the weekly homeworks which are not that long, then her tests and quizzes are easy. The questions are exactly the same concepts in the homeworks, just switched a bit.

If you need to contact her, she never answers emails on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I was kinda surprised by the negative reviews here. I think prof Wilson is such a good teacher. I wish I had her for Calc 1. I love her teaching style!

Attendance is not mandatory but if you answer questions on the board you can get extra credit on the quizzes that happen each week. Hard to reach outside of class besides office hours. Can be overwhelming and doesn't speak in a way that is easy to understand.

Prof. Wilson likes to give weekly quizzes and nightly homework. Pros: extra credit and hw grade is for completion. Cons: she regurgitates the textbook, can't explain topics well, tests are 80% of your grade, and if you want to meet with her to go over examples, better be lucky enough with your schedule to attend office hours. She is not flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Wilson gives quizzes every week, usually not that challenging, but the class is mostly graded on the midterms and final. Gives opportunity to get extra credit on quizzes and drops the two lowest quiz grades. Homework is assigned every class, but she gives the whole semester to turn it in full credit. DON'T BUY THE BOOKS. Overall good teacher.

Wilson is a really good teacher, which isn't something I can say about all my professors at Northeastern. She is excellent at explaining things and shows plenty of practice exams to study from. Know that the quizzes make up a chunk of your grade, and you have to stay up with the homework for those. 10/10

I'm not sure why there are so many negative reviews on Dr. Wilson. I had her for Math Fundamentals of Games and she was honestly the best. She responds very quickly to emails and always values her students' opinions on deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have taken her class multiple times and you will get a good grade if you pay attention. She reviews all the homework and is very accessible. Easy class, good professor who is clear and has reasonable but simple expectations. Good class, if not a bore.

reviews.comment: Professor Wilson is a good math teacher. She teaches clearly and effectively and answers all students' questions as they come. Overall, good teacher, good class -- nothing amazing and nothing horrible.

Either she's improved a lot or the other reviews aren't as accurate. I found Dr. Wilson's lectures to be well organized and she is very approachable and friendly during office hours. Homework packets were given out each week which was very convenient and very reflective of tests. Overall, one of the best math professors I've had at northeastern
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

she doesnt know how to teach. all she does is examples on the board and we copy it down. she doesnt explain what she is teaching. she doesnt understand that we dont know the material. the other day I asked her a question, she came to me to help and then got mad when i still couldnt understand after she tried to "help". you have to teach yourself.

her class isnt the worst thing i've ever had but your grade is almost entirely made up of tests. her class is unbelievably boring. she talks so slow and has no energy or enthusiasm whatsoever. her lecture are fine but im not learning much from it. if this is your only option it is not sadie piatt bad, but i would get someone else if possible.

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes but they weren't super difficult if you went to class and did the problems on the textbook. Also drops the lowest quiz, but don't trust the bad ratings very fair teacher IMO.

She was one of the first professors to make me retain math. She's super kind and understanding. Weekly quizzes were helpful in testing understanding. I don't know why she gets bad ratings because she's always super clear and knowledgeable.

The lectures were very unclear and did not help me learn the material. The course relied heavily on constant quizzes without providing the instruction needed to prepare for them. Expect to teach yourself most of the content, and it will be especially difficult if you do not already have a solid calculus background.

I don't understand the negative reviews! She is very patient and open to answer questions.  As someone who isn't naturally great in math, I found this class one of the best I've taken. She does not care about her students, when I went to office hours she was very rude and when I did not understand something she said "how can you not understand?? these are the most basic things" she isn't very kind i would avoid her.

She is not bad at all, super sweet and explains things well. Don't be afraid to ask questions in her class or go to office hours, she's very approachable and wants everyone to do well! If you struggle with math it can be hard, but she's not the issue. Only graded harshly on the group project

Just not a good teacher overall and her grading policy is awful. Would never take her class again if I had the opportunity as well as she is very difficult to understand because of her broken english.

Terrible at explaining concepts

Horrible professor, unless your a math whiz don't take her class unless you hate yourself.

Straightforward lectures, was sweet and willing to stop and further break down a problem in class. Gave a good amount of study material for quizzes and tests. Available during office hours. Would sometimes host a class on Zoom.

This class if very manageable and actual first teacher to teach me how to use my calculator! Professor Bai provides study guides that are very similar to the exam. tests you on stuff you never learned. good luck if you're in her class and aren't a math whiz. wish i had another prof. this sucked
One of the worst professors I have taken a class with at Northeastern. I have no idea why she is still teaching with all those negative reviews here.

Very, very, very poor teacher. Don't take this class unless you want to have a miserable semester and not learn absolutely anything. Hard to understand her because of her accent and she does not know how to teach.
she is the worst

I feel lost in this class. Vantage will cost you $139. Hard to reach outside of class, but there's no point anyways. I wish the “keys” she posted included steps instead of just the answer. I'm so lost lol

Honestly, if you're anxious about math or calc, this class is HARD. I am struggling so much. She doesn't answer questions directly, instead says "we covered it in class." Do not take if you've never taken pre-calc or calc before. She's hard to understand and moves onto different topics really fast. reviews.comment: honestly, what was that?? Idk why no one tells you about how bad she is, it really is impossible to learn anything in this class because of how she teaches. I wish I had read the comments here before taking a class with her.

Honestly made calc so easy to understand. I think the lectures were very well explained, and we did plenty of examples to solidify learning. Definitely need to pay attention and practice, but I never felt overwhelmed by the workload or difficulty of the course.

Dr. Bai is very caring, wants to see her students succeed in class, and she uploads the lecture notes on Canvas. Not a difficult class if you've taken Calc in high school. if you've taken calc before, it is very doable and honestly shouldn't be that hard. Her lectures were useless to me so I stopped going and relied heavily on the textbook to learn. Her quizzes are usually 15 minutes and 5 questions. Grade is heavily relied on the weekly quizzes and final.

Professor Bai is a really sweet and caring professor. Unfortunately, I just failed to understand her lectures, even as someone who took calculus in high school. she seemed really nice, but the way she explained things didn't make sense to me. I'm also not very math-minded, but for a very low-level course this seemed unnecessarily difficult

please. incoming economics freshmen. DONT TAKE THIS!! i beg you. I don't know who writes the good comments in here but none of the classmates/people I know who took a class with her liked her and her teaching style. Very hard to follow during the lecture and not accessible outside of classes.

Taking calc with her will be your worst nightmare if you have never taken calculus before/if you are an international student. Professor has a very hard to understand accent, so you have to do a lot of self-learning. Rekha is a very good professor, I would say I am willing to take her course again so many time. NEVER TAKE HER - literally the worst professor to take this class with

Class was very easy given I've taken Calc previously. She goes in depth with her lectures and very good at explaining. One group project and she drops the lowest test and quiz, great for keeping your grade up. textbook homework for every unit, good practice. FINAL IS WORTH A LOT (40%) !!!!

I Love Her teaching ways, which first tell you the formulas then bring you some exercises, this can help me understand how those principles works and remember them. Also, although she has several paper test, you have the chance to drop one of the tests which you receive the lowest grade.

She makes this class 100000% harder, and it's impossible to understand what she is talking about during her lectures most of the time. I have to study everything by myself because she cannot explain what she teaches clearly.
Classes are basically copying things from the board but not really engaging.  As a professor, she wasn't helpful at all, I had to study by myself.

reviews.comment: Professor Bai was very sweet, but I had no idea what she was talking about most of the time. Her lectures tended to be very confusing and she was not always clear when answering questions. A majority of your grade is based on a midterm and final exam, which I found to be pretty unfair. There was a quiz once a week that were a small % of your grade

Professor Bai is a clearly enjoys teaching calculus for business. She goes through some of the topics very quickly and without many explanations, but she always completes a worksheet with the students and is totally opened and patient when receiving a bunch of questions. The grade consists of a group project, five tests, homework and a final exam.

Only take this class if you've taken calculus before because her lectures will only make sense to you that way. Otherwise, she just teaches the basics and then goes 0 to 100 in her examples. For the group project, she doesn't give helpful feedback and will just tell you what's wrong. She's not sympathetic whatsoever toward extensions/ makeup exams.

This professor is so sweet and caring. Her lectures are very informative and she goes through a great amount of examples that helps you really understand the topics. Because she does a lot of examples you also hardly ever open the textbook. She also creates a pdf with review material for each exam which touches on all topics for the upcoming exam

If you have taken Calculus before and you can teach yourself, then you should not go to her class unless for exams. She has a thick accent that you cannot understand what she is saying most of the time and i know for sure if I did not take Calculus in my senior year of highschool, I would have definitely failed this class.

Very straight-shooting teacher. Works lots of examples in class, and gives very straightforward lectures. Not a super showy personality in the classroom, but she's interesting to talk to after class if you'd really like to. Classic good teacher, would take again. (Can be a bit harsh grading quizzes, but she drops the lowest 2)

I have taken calculus before, but her lectures were very clear and helpful. Great syllabus with clear expectations and tons of practice problems. She always asks if we have questions or need her to slow down. Easy homework and fair tests. Easy group project.

Explains every topic very well, but to a basic level. You will often find yourself understanding the very basics of how to do something, but need to figure out the depths of it on your own. Provides plenty of practice and is very nice in and out of class. If you try you will do well, even without attending class more than once a week.

Lectures are very boring but helpful if you're having trouble in the class. 5 tests (drops lowest test), 1 semester long group project, and 1 final. Very easy class if you've taken any kind of calc class before, but may be difficult if not. Not much feedback on tests. In my opinion, it was more valuable to self-study than attend her classes.
She is a good professor but teaches at a really fast pace. She gives a lot of tests which are not that hard if you study a lot. She covers a lot in one class so don't skip any classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Taking Rekha Bai's class was one of the worst things ever. Half of the time, you cannot understand her words because she doesn't use the mic and she writes poorly on the chalkboard. Professor Bai was a great lecturer who clearly explained all the material you needed to know. If you needed clarification, it was explained in the textbook or by going to her office hours. reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She does not explain things clearly. Uses a chalkboard and erases with her hand making it impossible to take notes. Her tests are often and extremely difficult if you havent been crunching for a week. Her classes are all but interactive and, when asked for an extension, she refused.

I took her Calculus - Business/Economics course as a part of NUAccelerate. Her lectures are mind numbing and the examples she explains are far from the difficulty of the homework. I basically taught myself the entire curriculum. Furthermore, she includes a semester long group project with vague instructions doesn't provide any clarification or help

Professor Bai is a nice person, but she is awful at explaining. If you are good at Calc or have previous knowledge, then this might not be too bad. However, if you are average at Calculus, do not take the class with her. Moves quickly, explains badly and very confusing. Do not recommend.

Professor Bai is the best math professor I've ever encountered. She is very helpful and willing to answer any questions. Her lectures are very clear and homework are relatively easy. She gives very clear instruction on quizzes and exams. Be sure to practice the questions in her "class pak" then you will definitely achieve high score.

Really nice but awful at explaining. The lectures are so easy but the homeworks and the quizzes are so much harder. Wouldn't recommend if you have not taken calc in highschool or struggle with math in general.

I took this class through NUStart. The material was okay considering it was Calculus and I had taken a precalc course in high school. Either way, she is very nice but can be hard to understand. Her teaching style is not my favorite. I only passed because I went to many office hours with her, TA's and an another tutor.

I'm not sure why her recent ratings are low, but Professor Bai is sweet and interpersonal throughout the lectures despite the online format due to COVID-19. Textbook reading isn't needed as she provides ppt slides and worksheets (which the tests/quizzes are based on) and there aren't any graded hw assignments. Doing textbook problems will save you
Long and boring lecture. Depend on yourself
She is the best professor to take for 1231. She very good explaining and as long as you pay attention you should get an A-/A.

Overall, she's nice, but her class can be very boring because she lectures at the board the whole time. Her explanations can be confusing at times, but if you work hard and make an effort it's an easy A. There are quizzes every single week and the homework is all online but isn't due until the end of the semester.

Took the course as a 2nd year and my class was mainly freshmen. they were sometimes really rude to her, but Professor Bai was a sass master and shut them down. She was very willing to give one-on-one help and allowed you to correct mistakes in your group project for points back. I enjoyed her teaching so much that I took her for MATH 1231 as well.

Rekha is one of the best math professors I've ever had! She is easy to understand, although she can be quiet at times. She has students do problems in class -- they aren't for credit, but they help. She is very available in office hours and is kind to students; she'll really put in extra effort to make sure you understand. Quizzes are reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: NICE PROFESSOR BUT MAKES THE COURSE SEEM HARDER THAT IT IS.

Precalc with her was honestly a huge waste of my tuition money. Yes the class is easy, but maybe a little too easy that it makes it hard to take it seriously and stay on track. She is very condescending if you are a weak math student, and won't reply emails or provide extra help to students outside of very limited office hours.
This class was a show up, sleep for 100 min, and get an A. I couldn't stay awake in the class, and the professor stretches out about 15 min of material for the full class time.

I saw some people mentioning her strong accent, but it's really not a big deal. She's very nice and really chill. On the rare occasion that people jokingly express being stressed in the class, she'll just calm everybody down. Also, she's really thorough when introducing mathematical concepts.

This is my second class with Professor Bai. I think she has a very specific teaching style which works for some people and not for others. Fortunately, she worked for me really well. She gives many quizzes but they are short and she will tell you exactly what to expect. I think she is a great teacher for some but not for others.
This class was comically easy. If you have a calc requirement, definitely take Rekha. There's no reason you shouldn't get an A in this class.

Rekha Bai talks in a pretty thick Indian accent, but if you pay attention relatively well and go to class most of the time it is an easy A. Quizzes are assigned regularly, and the lowest quiz grade is dropped, so it is easy to bring your grades up. Would recommend taking math with her if you are a business or econ major!

Very unhelpful for those who struggle with math, doesn't reply to emails. Yeah, there tends to be the students who are more math savvy who pretty much just fly through the class and grades in success. She is dull, difficult understand and approach, and has no personality to try and be more approachable. Her explanations are unclear.
A little hard to understand at first but you get used to her after a while. She is very very helpful and sweet. Loved her!!
Great teacher! She's a little hard to understand at first, but pay attention in class and do all the homework (not graded) and you'll do very well

She might not be the best orator, but her classes are well organized. Though it seems like she just got off the boat she has a lot of experience. She's approachable, open to questions and brings clarity to the subject.
GREATTTT Professor

Definitely a good teacher who cares for her student's success and who, despite her strong accent and monotonous voice, explains everything very well. Average grader and has lengthy office hours. Just do the work, revise the material several times and you'll do well.

Ok. I hate the class but with her its easy yet very boring. No need to do the hw or anything. Key to succeeding would be to master the guide and practice problems they make you buy. Do it the night before and you are set. Quizez are easy, Mid terms are okay but the FINAL is challenging to say the least.

She is a solid teacher. Not exactly interesting or the best but definitely teaches you the material. Pay attention, come to class, and if you need it schedule office hours because she doesnt exist on campus otherwise. I suggest read the book if you dont understand then ask in class. She likes questions. She has an accent-meh.

She teaches in a very organized, logical sequence, but does not mind stopping to address questions. She provides time for in class practice and circulates to make sure that everyone can do the work, even if they do not ask for help. She always graded quizzes in a timely fashion and very fairly. She is also flexible, moving the quizzes around.

Ms. Bai was a good teacher, she made everything very clear while she taught. You really only need the book for half of the class so if you can just share with someone in class you're golden. The final is cumulative so you need to make sure you study hard. Overall an easy class.
She is a tough teacher, she WILL make you work a lot and she has a difficult accent to understand. Nevertheless, her class was fun and interesting. Likes to assist students in case they struggle.
Overall a good teacher. could be a lot clearer and more caring. If you are not doing well in the course, don't expect her to help you at all, so work really hard.
Has an accent. Very nice lady and will help you. Like 7 quizes she drops the 3 lowest. Final and midterm are hard but an overall easy class. Great Prof!

She'll like you and make an effort to help you if you show up everyday. she was really mean to the kids that didn't show up. She likes students that work hard even if your not particularly skilled. Hard to understand.

I usually struggle in math, but Prof Bai was very clear and made sure I knew the subject matter. She gives you review the day prior to a quiz and it is almost identical to the quiz itself. drops the lowest two quizzes. One of the best math teachers I've ever had.
Great professor. Small accent but she is nice and understands where your coming from. Teaches well.
If you've taken high school calculus this class is a breeze.  She's a nice lady too, and you can probably get away without buying the book.

An extremely easy class if you do her review worksheets. They are practically copies of the actual quiz. She's a very nice lady, but the class is far from exhilarating....pretty boring in fact. But hey, can Calculus really be exciting?
easy class, amazing professor...

Her accent is not hard at all to understand. She is a really great professor and will gladly help you if you need it. Her quizzes are very fair - you get a review before each one that is exactly like what will be on the actual quiz.
Nice lady, if you go to class, it's easy to get an A. A little bit hard to understand her accent, but not too bad. Her quizzes are exactly like her quiz reviews.

If you have to take a calc class i would definitely recommend Bai! The project was easy and the quizzes were exactly like the quiz review she gives you for homework. I had a solid A in the class until the final, which i failed and brought me down to a B. The final is 40% of your grade and is MUCH harder than you will think.

Prof. Bai is a sweet, quiet Indian woman (slight accent, no problem).  If you want to learn real calculus, then this class is not for you.  Besides the few basic calculus concepts, I often felt like it was 10th grade algebra and not college calculus.  However, since the course is required, get Bai, it's an easy class made easier by an awesome prof.
professor Bai was a great teacher just do the class packet cuz thats basically all the quizzes are based on. Her final is hard and its worth 40 percent of your grade

Great math teacher. Nice woman, who wants you to do well. Takes attendance. Uses the textbook, but you really don't need to buy it. I stopped looking at it after the first few weeks.  Course only gets semi-difficult towards the end when the actual calculus begins.  Distribution was... 15% group project, 30% quiz, 15% midterm, 40% final.
Nice professor, very helpful, easy, clear, no homework.
she's a great teacher. EXCEPT for one thing. you better be damn certain that you do well on the final. my avg in the class was an 82.2 but my overall grade was a D+ because of my final.

Awesome professor. Wants her students to do well in the class. I never had a problem understanding her. I wasn't that interested in taking calc at first and it ended up being my best class this semester.
Great teacher, not totally easy, but no really really hard, i liked her overall!

Amazing woman.  She's a truly caring teacher who knows how to convey her material.  I paid attention, did my homework and got an A.  I don't see what everyone is talking about with her accent.  She's just as understandable as anyone I've ever talked to and I don't know one person in my class who had trouble comprehending her.

good teacher, has an accent but still understandable. sometimes move a little fast but just ask her to slow down. quizes alwasy exactly what she says they will be. so far as a frosh, best teacher ive had

She was a teacher that yes, did have an accent, but i didn't find it to be a problem, while she did move fast it was a fairly reasonable pace, her tests were always what she said they were going to be, no bull, overall good teacher
I've never liked math, but calculus is easily my favorite class this semester b/c prof. bai makes it simple and clear- plus she's really nice and can be funny! I love those quiz reviews
couldnt be any easier- gives practice quizzes that are the exact format of tests, even for midterm/final.  lets you drop 2 worst grades.  very nice woman.
All the quiz reviews are pretty much the same as the quizs you get.  She goes over anything you need help in during class and is very helpful.  Plus she's really nice.
Excellent teacher. Goes slow and makes sure all students understand material. Goes over quiz material, project is easy and lectures are clear.

i could not undestand a word she said, i had to change classes, and besides, she moves extremely quickly, i was doing bad becuase of her accent, and her rapid explanations and assumptions that everyone knows what they are doing.
Quizzes were easy, but I still learned stuff from her class. She is soft spoken, but covered all the material needed to do well on the final, great teacher.
The class is boring, shes a straight-forward teacher. You have to remember to practice doing the problems and pay close attention the 1st 2 weeks, or else the class is a struggle.
great teacher.... quizes, midterm, and final are exactly like the practice versions she gives you... hard to understand but very helpful
a little hard to get used to but an easy 100
Very Easy Class. Very Easy Teacher. Practice quizzes are exactly like actual quizzes. Honestly this is the easiest calculus class that you will ever take!!
Test and quizes are the same as practice quizes she gives out in class.Class is boring as hell and the group project sucks

She can't speak very good english, but she knows what she's talking about.  The practice quizzes are EXACTLY like the real quizzes, which rules.  She is fair and she doesn't take attendance.  I have never taken calc before, and I'm doing well!
This class would have been a whole lot easier if she spoke fluent english. Class is pretty easy. Gives you practice quizzes that are the same as the quiz you take.
No Comments
No Comments
IF you have trouble with your grades and try to email her do you get a response NOOOOOOOOOO definetly not cool
Nice teacher. Clear and understandable. Easy quizzes and always prepares you before tests.

Only professor that I've looked forward to going to lectures to. Super funny and makes the material interesting to learn. You have to talk occasionally in his class, but I found myself engaging beyond just to get a participation grade. Would take again.

About 3-4 assignments as week, each having over 10 pages of reading and analyzing. Discussion boards, Perusall, random books, but uses it to fuel a discussion every class so you have to read it. Grades tough despite the class being required for NuPath. No technology in class, and the first philosophy class that you struggle to maintain an A in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
I took Prof. Yelle for his Philosophy and Literature class but it wasn't available here.

Professor Yelle is very cool, funny and open. There is definitely a lot of reading and a good amount of writing, given it is a mix of philosophy and literature course, but it's super interesting and he gives great guidelines. Be ready to contribute in class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Yelle is a G. He has very particular ideas about how assignments should be completed, but if you're willing to talk to him, he tends to be more forgiving in his grading. The discussions felt unfortunately prefabricated- he has a predetermined outcome for each conversation, regardless of whether students agree with the readings being discussed.
Really funny and interesting lectures, but a tough grader at times. Forgiving of late work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures were always enjoyable, and Prof Yelle always made an effort to ensure discussions were inclusive. The topics we went over were interesting. He's not as tough a grader as other people here make him out to be, but be prepared to spend a good amount of time on the final paper.

If you are serious about philosophy, don't take his class. He has a strong tendency to avoid tough questions. He grades erratically and too harshly. Essays can only repeat his ideas rather than yours. And must be extremely straightforward, otherwise he will "not detailed enough" and give low marks for any rhetorical questions, irony, and intimation

Professor Yelle was one of the best professors I had. He was always welcoming and inclusive and completely unbiased. His classes were always engaging and funny and I made some amazing friends because of it. I don't know how anyone could leave a bad review, his classes are awesome. He's a harsh grader but college grades barely matter anyways.

Food Ethics with Ben was a MISTAKE. He was not an expert on the topic. Thankfully class discussions were typical, but he would still cut off meaningful thoughts to return to his poor slides. And assignment sheets were sloppy and not representative of how he graded.

If Ben graded his own materials like he graded student papers, he would fail BAD.
Nice teaching but tough grading

Prof Yelle is extremely likable and makes philosophy interesting with seminar-style lectures and no tests/quizzes. He's funny and cares about engaging his students. He is critical about the final project but not overly hard, I'd absolutely recommend taking him!

Has a genuine passion for making his class meaningful. No tests/quizzes. Almost all of your grade is comprised of writing assignments which he grades very harshly. You could follow all instructions and requirements for writing an essay and he will give you an 80 (coming from a decent writer). Generous with extensions
Really engaging class but tough grading for the final project

He is the most fair teacher I've ever had. You will walk away with exactly what you put into the class. He is a very tough grader, but if he sees you're trying he will cut you slack. Aside from that everything is 10/10. Great lectures. Very personable. Understanding with students. Just be ready to work and trust that you will be rewarded if you do.

I had for PHIL2143 (philosophy for children) not PHIL1185, Yelle was a great, energetic professor who fully engaged his students. You're not allowed to have your laptop out/open in class, which actually really helps focus, and I would love to take his class again.

Professor Yelle is one of the coolest professors out there! His classes are super interesting and engaging. He can be a tough grader on reading question assignments, but he gives good feedback. I loved his class and I encourage everyone to take PHIL 1101 with him.

His lectures are super engaging as he encourages everyone to play devil's advocate and analyze the reasoning behind their beliefs. He got me really interested in philosophy, a subject I was unsure of prior to taking the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ben made the classes enjoyable. However, he is an extremely tough and inconsistent grader and the feedback he gave was not helpful. If you want to succeed, GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS. Make him know you are interested in the class, regardless of if you are or are not. If you participate in class, you will succeed. If not, good luck mate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the toughest graders. You could go to office hours and spend a ton of hours on a single paper just to receive a B. The lectures themselves only require you to listen and sometimes contribute to the conversation. DO NOT take if you're expecting an A, unless you are an exceptional writer, because you won't get an A on your papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: you don't have to put much time outside of class. the class had weekly discussion board posts, reading assignments, 2 papers, and one final paper. VERY TOUGH GRADER on papers. i do not recommend if you are a weak writer. however, he does give thorough and specific feedback to help you improve on future papers.
Good.

This class was excellent, and I would ABSOLUTELY take another class with him. I'll be going to office hours next semester just to talk to him even though I don't have his class. Be prepared to write, but I would definitely consider it manageable if you're a decent or strong writer.

More than anything, Benny is entertaining and endlessly fun. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. Made lectures interesting. He is a tough grader but gives a lot of feedback so that you can improve on the next paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A good guy and a great lecturer, however he grades papers extremely unfairly, as if the people who are taking his class are doing so for a PHD in philosophy rather than NU Path credit. He also is insistent that you spend the money on the two books, despite his lectures come directly from them - turned out to be a waste of money in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are amazing. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DON'T LIKE WRITING ESSAYS. VERY VERY TOUGH GRADER. but an amazing professor. Would not take his class again because personally, i do not understand his grading.

Professor Yelle is overall a great professor, however his grading on essays was ridiculously hard and he gave almost no feedback. Any feedback that was given was very passive and borderline rude. The essay grading alone makes me not want to take another of his classes, but if you enjoy discussion based classes you will like this professor.

simply a king. very passionate about the subject matter and leads great discussions, I learned a lot about philosophy despite putting in not a lot of effort. you don't realllly have to do all the readings, maybe just skim to know important broad concepts but he leads the discussions. he is a pretty tough grader on papers, be very very thorough

Professor Yelle is very knowledgable about philosophy, and I enjoyed the lectures we had in class. He is quite a tough grader on papers, but if you go in to office hours for help with your arguments he is happy to help you out. I also recommend going to office hours after he grades your paper so you can get very specific advice on how to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Yelle is very knowledgable and class discussions are engaging. Readings are assigned, but not necessarily required because the material is gone over in class. A little bit of a tough grader on papers, but not a heavy workload. Professor Yelle changed my way of thinking, and inspired me to minor in Phil! Definitely take this class!!!

Professor Yelle is one of the best professors I've had. He's able to spark interesting conversation in a 30 person class of mostly first years. Lots of readings that make you learn and grow - this class turned me vegan. Grading isn't bad and I get by with skipping class a lot and not doing all readings. Take this class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof Yelle is clearly passionate about this topic and class was absolutely very interesting. My review of him would've been a lot different if he didn't think of himself and his class as the main focal point in his students lives. most ppl are just taking this class for an elective, and he is an extremely harsh grader to a ridiculous point.

Professor Yelle is really good at explaining philosophical topics effectively and has introduced me to a lot of interesting technological concepts. However, he rarely gave feedback which made his grading style confusing at times (we also did not get any feedback for our final paper aside from a grade).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: extremely tough grader and comments on papers feel like insults
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Yelle is a fantastic professor. His lectures and discussions are incredibly engaging, making the class fun to be in. Regarding homework, there are some small assignments and readings are very important to do, but the workload is manageable. Writing is a big part of the grade also, but he is available for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: tough grader, difficult for international students to get a high grade if you don't spend enough time in reading and taking reading notes, especially for whose major is not in liberal arts,

Unlike other subjects, it takes a solid understanding of philosophy and morals to be a good teacher and prof Yelle is extremely qualified. His lectures hosted some of the most thought-provoking conversations I've ever heard & I feel I'm better off for taking his course. As long as you read the passages and take notes, you'll be fine. Amazing class.

His Technology & Human Values class is very interesting and he really captivates the classroom with his lectures. There are a few quizzes, he tells you when they'll be but you'll need to take notes every day if you want to do well on them. There are only 3 essays throughout the semester, but he is a very tough grader, go to office hours to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Excellent in class conversation. He is truly an amazing devils advocate which forces you to think through your ideas far more deeply
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Usually would hate the idea of any class with pop quizzes, but besides the fact that they're usually easy to see coming, you'll want to be at every class anyway and as long as you briefly look over the readings they're pretty easy. Professor Yelle is really an amazing, young professor who cares about his students and also makes you think.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Stand up guy. *Slow clap*. His lectures are super engaging and he delivers the content in a way that really makes you think. The setup is pretty much based on lectures and discussions and most of your grade is made up of papers (which I like). I would recommend meeting with him for each paper assignment because he gives excellent feedback!

Entertaining professor and gets really into his lectures. Pop quizzes are super easy. Nice guy who always helps out at his office hours. He's really picky with his essays though, will take off points for minor things.
He's a good guy but he is pretty inconsistent with his grading.

Most amazing teacher I ever had! Had class at 8 am but it was a pleasure to come, he makes everything very interesting, and the classes are just discussions around ethical concepts. All exams are take home, and as he gives great feedback it pushes us to give our best. Plus he gives extra credit if you wanna give a presentation. Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! I took Intro to Philosophy with him and his lectures really made me think. The readings are always interesting and he always pushes you to be the best writer/thinker you can be! I would definitely take his class again.

I absolutely loved this class! He was amazing. He is very passionate about this subject and you can tell. He is NOT boring at all. No exams, just papers and a few pop quizzes. If you do the readings though they are really easy. Honestly best professor I have ever had. We talked after almost every class and I wish he could be my best friend lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Genuinely the easiest A ever, the only annoying thing is that attendance is mandatory. Some lectures are actually engaging, though, because he uses modern pop culture examples to teach certain units. 3 online quizzes, one written op-ed, and a few class activities make up your grade. No final.

He is really sweet and caring for his students. Class is pretty boring, mostly lecture and some awkward participation. But you only have 3 quizzes and most are online. Lots of boring readings but he goes over them in class so you don't need to read them in depth.

Very boring lectures, he just reads right off the slides. It felt like we learned the same exact thing every class and was repetitive. The class was really easy, simple in-class assignments and online quizzes, no midterm or final exams. Overall, pick a different class I don't feel like I learned anything.
He is so nice. Class is an easy A if you participate a bit and skim the readings. He's a bit boring as a lecturer but really nice to chat with and tries to engage the students.

Incredibly boring and irrelevant, I learned nothing new as the lessons were designed possibly for an entry level high school course at most. The readings were dry, and the discussions were dryer. However, there were virtually no assignments or work or responsibilities. Waste of money but an easy A.

This course was not good. The professor was not engaging in lectures, he wanted us to participate but did nothing to motivate us to do so. His material was not engaging and the in-class activities were made for middle-schoolers. He read off the screen and his notes and the material were boring when the class title seemed engaging.

Only way to pass this class is to get Bernal to like you....Had a fantastic TA who provided so much help if you needed it. Material and content are all over the place. One advice is to get your homework as correct as possible and easy to follow for open note exams and pray you can pass.

Bernal was a decent professor when he prepared for class, but often he prioritized other items leaving the TA to do much of the work. This resulted in a chaotic final exam where things we were told to expect on the final were left off, and problems were put on that the class was unprepared for. I was so disappointed by the quality of his teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bernal is a super caring professor, maybe my favorite at Northeastern. He really wants you to understand and will take as much time as you need to try to help. Taking statics with him before analysis was definitely helpful, as he has a unique teaching method. Asking questions is crucial! If you get confused, go to office hours

His lectures can seem a bit overwhelming to understand, especially in the beginning, but if you keep going to class and recitations, things connect well towards the end. A majority of the material was taught in the beginning, there was lots of time for review later. A very caring and funny guy, easy to reach, and listens to the class concerns.

Bernal is genuinely a nice guy. He was very available for office hours and email. Sometimes he could be all over the place and not very structured, but if you were confused, he would work with you until you understood it. He never left a student behind. His tests were very straight forward and simple. Def recommend taking statics with him.

He's clearly a genius and is very accessible - his office hours are basically whenever you need him (including weekends and late nights). He is extremely bad at giving partial credit, so don't depend on knowing only part of the process to answer questions. His tests are hard, this class is really hard. He's a great dude though.

Really funny guy. Lectures can be a bit hectic but if u get the basic gist you're golden. Tests can be pretty difficult but don't worry, the curve will be your saving grace. Do past exams for good practice for the exams. Homework can be difficult too but it's mostly for completion. Ask a lot of questions and he will answer them pretty well.

During lecture I felt like I, along with many others were very confused. It was difficult to follow his lecturers because the topics were challenging, and he often made many mistakes and was not direct to the point. For tests he made study guides with answer keys which were very helpful and that's how I learned most of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Would never take again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He could not teach, better off teaching myself the materal

Professor Bernal is the best Structural Dynamics teacher that I've ever had. Sometimes he thinks faster than he thought so you have to be very careful to listen what did he mean. But when everything going well, he can explain the most complicated things into an understandable simple words. Test was very hard, homework too.

Bernal is quite smart, but by taking this course with him is is clear he struggles to communicate the lecture material. Lectures were confusing due to algebra errors he made and round about examples he would give to explain concepts. He is very helpful in office hours, and available whenever.

The man is clearly a genius, but is horrible at teaching. Classwork is hard to follow & irrelevant to exams, no clear grading criteria, which is frustrating because it adds extra difficulty for no reason. Terrible at making sure the class can cover concepts & cant answer questions well. Your statics was graded higher than your structural analysis.

Very educated, but he's terribly disorganized and clearly not for teaching. Everything in his class is assigned randomly. There's no study plan and class material can be somewhat irrelevant to the textbook, which makes working with him rather frustrating.
Really disorganized
Took System Identification class. Great professor. Class assignments will consume a LOT of time!
brilliant mind. very easy to learn from even on the most complicated matters.  watch out for his tests...
he's too smart but not for teaching
Good teacher... Hard Test
probably one of the toughests professors! let's say he was the reason why i didnt graduate with straight A's!
tests are hard, lectures are good
No Comments
Most relatable prof., caring, funny, ask anyone who took him.
Ben is by far one of my favorite professors. He genuinely cares about every student's success in the class, but will be tough on you to whip up your skills to pass the NREMT.

Chillest guy on earth. Teaches you everything you need to know to be a good EMT while also being aware that we are students with a million other stressors. He is kind, but tough enough to whip you up into shape and clean up your EMT work. You will succeed if you try. Bro is highkey the absolute goat. Bless up Ben.

If you are thinking about taking this class or are interested in becoming an EMT, definitely do it. Ben was super easy to get along with and a caring instructor. I learned so much in this class and it is easily one of my favorite that I have ever taken at Northeastern. Highly recommend!

Class is fine, very, VERY easy. MAKE SURE your Final Project team is good. But be sure to read instead of skimming or expect to lose tons of points (sometimes a % of your grade!) on completely random, arbitrary things

Class is OK, videos can be long but the requirements aren't much each week, class def depends on your final project group. Project requirements are long word dumps (think 2-5 pgs) and you can expect to lose points on things you SWEAR aren't there but actually were: 5 words about something needing a trait n losing an entire half letter grade for it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Extremely heavy workload. Expect to have a major project due every 2 weeks, on top of tedious course modules due every week. And on top of that, a final project which has an extremely long rubric of items, while you are forced to work in a team of only 3.

Also, the professor comes off as really pretentious in his assignments i.e. smile emoji spam.

THIS MAN IS A LEGEND. The lecture videos are so well done, and he is passionate and ready to help outside of class. If you want to make games as a hobby, or are pursuing the major, start by taking a course with this guy. ++

So much homework. SUPER HEAVY WORKLOAD!!! Sometimes one homework was not due and he already released another one. Homework has extremely long instructions. Takes up to 24 hours to finish. Submission's a pain in the ass. Does learn a lot and make a lot of projects but none are useful unless you tryna be a game programmer.

Avoid unless super interested in Unity/Games. You can learn a decent amount if you apply yourself, but be warned that Calgar has some... let's just say issues when interfacing with his students, and that's if he manages to reply to your emails at all. If you do take this class, follow assignments exactly, and just avoid Calgar. Then you're fine.

DO NOT take HCI with him if you actually want to go into UI/UX+already have experience working with clients. This class is only helpful for students who are minimally interested in UX design because he doesn't teach industry-standard tools. He teaches the design process as if there's only one way to do it and uses Axure for the course and not Figma

Took him during the summer for the summer classes in Seattle, can be a bit condescending at times but can be funny. This class is based off of a group project so if you get a crappy team, be prepared to do all of the work yourself, get a good team, this class will be a breeze.

Sarcastic, condescending, and spends a disproportionate amount of class time expressing disappointment and frustration at students.  It would be better for everyone if the professor could maintain a level head and positive attitude, and put more effort into understanding why students are not enjoying the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Yildirim is the GOAT, and easily one of the most respected and beloved professors in Khoury. I've gone back to his lecture notes to prep for interviews, since he does an excellent job of explaining things effectively + concisely. If you're going to take DS3000, make sure you take it with Caglar!

Cared a lot about students and put a lot of effort to make sure even the people who could not make it to live lectures be able to understand the materials and participate with other students for group projects. Well organized lectures and materials, inclusive environment. I'd take all classes with him if he were teaching them! Highly recommend. <3

Without a doubt, one of the best classes I have taken! Prof is super friendly and loves Harry Potter! Course is extremely well structured and everything is laid on the table in the first class. Gives ample time to complete the big assignments and encourages class participation. He's very responsive to questions and makes sure the load is balanced.

The Professor did an AMAZING job curating online course content. He had prerecorded lectures with accompanying notebooks that could be watched at the students convenience. On alternating class days there were (very) short lab activities. He was also easily accessible, and sent out weekly correspondences reminding us of upcoming activities.

Brilliant, funny, and clear professor. You almost felt sad for him - he was enthusiastic beyond belief but the long class and intro level material meant noone was paying attention by the end. You can work on a cool ML project come the end of the class as well, and the class is usually taken just when you want projects for your resume. 100% take him

Quizzes are amazing, can help with grade. Homework assignments are straight forward, Can Be Done. No in-class tests and no final exam, but there is a final group project.
