reviews.comment: Out of the few Calc 1 professors, he is one of the better ones. Few days before a quiz, he will send out a recitation PDF that literally look like the exam and I would recommend just reviewing that for the night, and you will be all set for his quizzes. He assigns only two homeworks which count as a quiz and is very helpful to boost your grade.

Prof is okay: make sure you, like, really know all the material before bi-weekly quiz day or you'll inevitably lose 10% on ur exam b/c quizzes are ~6-8 Qs each. Grading demonstrates the 'butterfly effect': if you make a small error w/ your numbers you lose most of ur points on that question. Also does a 'meh' job of explaining course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I felt like I learned more from my online research to study than from his class. The only reason you make a good grade is from recitation and the online example quiz, not from his teaching. If you try you won't get a bad grade, but if you haven't taken calc in HS the prof is almost impossible to understand. Go to the recitation!

The lectures were straightforward and super easy to understand. As for exams/quizzes, he gives a practice quiz on Canvas that is literally the exact format as the quiz we get, so it was easy to pass. He also was just a nice/funny person.

Lectures are pretty boring, but the quizzes and tests are pretty easy and he gives a lot to practice from so there are never any surprises. Honestly, you probably won't get much out of lecture unless you already know what you're doing, but it doesn't take much time out of class to teach yourself what you need to get a relatively easy A.

Tziagatchev's lectures are soft-spoken and difficult to follow. However, his quizzes are very fair, and he always posts a lot of online material that help prep for the quizzes. There is also endless online (youtube, etc) material for Calc 1, so it's very possible to teach yourself the content necessary for quizzes.

Lots of people find his lectures boring but I got a kick out of them cause he's unintentionally a pretty funny guy. As long as you put in the work on homework you should expect no surprises on his tests and quizzes and get a good grade.

Hard to understand accent, very messy handwriting, and can talk in circles but you can tell he's trying. He's an easy grader and gives lots of partial credit just make sure you understand the material. His explanations aren't very helpful, and many times can confuse you more. Although he's nice I would take with Prof George instead
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hard class to take at 8 in the morning (or any time). Lectures are dull, and he moves very quickly over new topics and on to the next . Will answer questions, but gives long, meandering answers that may or may not give you the answer you needed. Be prepared to spend lots of time outside of class teaching yourself the parts you don't understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't know why he has such a bad rep. Lectures are boring, but it's an easy A with no surprises! Only thing is that you need to have a solid background in calc to understand. His quizzes are very straightforward, exactly like his practice quizzes. He is so sweet and always willing to help even though his feedback isn't great. Love him!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst math professors I've ever had. He puts a slide up and talks about it for 30 minutes without writing anything down. The notes he does right down don't make sense and he talks himself in circles. Wouldn't reccomend.
Quizzes are straightforward, and there are no surprises. He's very nice, but his lectures are a bore. He will help you if you have a question but his answers aren't always straight forward.

Lectures are boring, but easy to follow. He's a really nice person and will help you if you ask. Quizzes are straight forward, no surprises. Does practice problems in class that are like what you see on the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I went to the first week of zoom lectures him, and bailed on learning the material from him after that. His lectures were extremely difficult to follow and his notes were hard to read. I ended up teaching myself the material using youtube videos instead.

He teaches this class like its the most boring thing hes ever taught. Its very hard to stay engaged and he rarely ever checks zoom chat. He constantly goes back on his sentences and it makes it hard to follow what hes saying and he goes on very long tangents trying to answer questions and still doesnt answer them.

She's so caring. The class is very easy to excel in if you follow her instructions. Lectures are interesting and fun and she gets to know all her students. No exam. 3 projects, 2 individual and one group. You can choose your own group. Projects are spread out over weeks so you have more than enough time to complete. Most work is discussion posts.
She is really good
She is so kind, take care of our difficulties, like some time I must delay to submit the assignment
She is a very good professor, lets you off the hook if you make an honest mistake.

Impossible not to earn an A. Very understanding and nice. Class participation is fun and engaging for students. However, could be a little more focused on the specific writing skills of each individual.
Great professor. Easy to get good grade, light homework load, respectful lecturing.
Great professor! She creates a great atmosphere in the classroom and is very fair. She is very understanding and fun! It's an easy class. Three writing projects throughout the semester, no final.
Greatest professor in the University by far. I highly recommend taking a class with her.

She is the best professor I ever met in Northeastern. Her lessons are helpful to your understanding of writing. Also, she is a very kindly professor who aware anyone's weaknesses and help them to improve.
The classes are fun and the professors are very nice

Easy class if taken in the summer, only 3 large projects and graded discussion posts (but basically graded on completion.) Feedback felt unnecessarily harsh at times, but overall a much easier class than I thought it would be. She pays very close attention to detail, so make sure that you do as well, and read all of the rubrics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I used this class as a study hall. I didn't learn a single thing which is honestly fine because the project is self-driven and he wants his students to end with an A and makes it pretty easy to get there

He's definitely a sweet guy, and you can tell he's passionate, but he's not very good at teaching. He made us by his $30 book (only could pay cash to him) and I never used it all semester. I didn't learn anything all semester because he just rambles, but a good GPA booster. We basically spent the whole sem working on symposium project.

He taught the class out of his own textbook and I never really had a full grasp on the content so if that bothers you he probably isn't a great prof for you. That being said he is very sweet/ very easy to get a high grade, he wants you to succeed and learn a little about a topic he's passionate about which I really loved. It was great for my GPA.

His lectures make no sense, he makes up his own terms (can't find them on Google), he makes you buy his own textbook, etc. However, this class is an easy A. It is way easier than any of the other inquires classes. If you turn in the assignments and take the quizzes you will get a 100. You can write literally anything related on the quiz and get 100

very nice guy, but cant teach. his lectures are all over the place and impossible to follow. he makes up his own terms for things, so you can't even ask google if you're confused. no one learned anything in this class. however, he doesn't give anyone below 100 so its an easy A

O'Malley genuinely just wants you to do well in his class. His lectures can be convoluted and hard to follow, mostly because he just really loves what he teaches, but he gives you every possible opportunity to get an A. I really just used his class as a study hall. He is generally a funny and caring guy, so do your GPA a favor and take his section!

It is a great class. He is very nice as he brings candy to class to encourage participation among students. As long as you know something on the quizzes he will give you an A or allow you to make it up to get an A. The group project is really easy and he will help you with anything. 10/10 recommend taking his class! The final is a one-page paper.

Do your GPA a favor and take him! His class is very lecture-heavy there are open response quizzes which he will allow anyone who gets less than an A to redo. As long as you attend class and are somewhat knowledgeable about something he will give you an A in the class. No final exam just a paper. He's a great guy take his class!

Prof O'Malley's class was a joke. I attended class but you really done need to. Grade is based on 3 major tests and thats it. April 14th and no grades have been put in yet. The slides are wordy and he goes off on tangents a lot. Nice guy but I don't think his main interest is anatomy. Book is unnecessary, first test is hard others are prac tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don's class is the definition of lecture heavy. Longggg lectures that even I couldn't keep up with note taking just bc of how boring they were. He is sort of nice but kind of sassy and also thinks he is smarter than his own doctor (which he told us). DO THE PRACTICE TESTS!! Grade is not posted and our final is in three days...

His tests were just the practice tests. Literally same position and everything, I learned nothing in this course but just memorized the practice test the day of and got one of the best grades on the final.

Funny guy and good professor here at northeastern. Homeworks are long and hard, but I guess that's expected when you take Advanced Linear Algebra. Lectures are good and have bits of comedy in them. Responds quickly and thoroughly to all questions on piazza. Overall good stuff!
Incredible professor!

I had Dr. Dummit for MATH3543 and WOW! It was an amazing class! Dr. Dummit was funny when he taught the class and he was a great teacher too! I highly recommend you attend his classes and OHs are a good way to catch up. Overall, the class was amazing and I would take another class with Dr. Dummit again!

*MATH3543. Hands down the best math professor at NEU. The math department here is underfunded and understaffed, but there is a small batch of great professors, and he is definitely one of them. In terms of class, homework can be time-consuming, but it is well thought out and will help you understand the material. If you like math, take his course.

The actual content may be difficult, but the professor explains all concepts in a formulaic and engaging way. The lectures are accessible, but it's very easy to fall behind. The tests are much easier than the homework and the study guides, so as long as you do them well, you can get a good grade. TLDR: content is hard, tests easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a super good teacher, I will be taking his class again simply because of how good the lectures are. Tests count most of the grades, be ready to do a lot of homework, and actually learn the stuff.

Professor Dummit is talented at describing extremely complex mathematical concepts. However, if you miss even a minute, you are at risk of falling behind -- attend all classes, and unless you're ready for a LOT (and I mean a LOT) of homework, don't accelerate the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All around a great professor, and if you haven't found this before, look up ChipsChallenge fandom wiki, and search for Evan_Dummit. The man has his own damn wiki page in this random game I've never heard of. If that ain't qualifications, I don't know what is.

Couldn't have asked for a better math teacher. The kind of guy where attendance isn't mandatory but you still show up to class because he's so good at teaching. Tests are reasonable. Homework might take a few hours but is manageable especially with piazza.
Good prof

Does an excelent job explaining concepts. While his homework does take a really long time to complete, the modterms are pretty easy in comparison and he is a very generous grader -- giving lots of partial credit.
Great lectures and notes, a bit too much homework though. If you put in the work, you'll be able to get a good grade.

His lectures were amazing, as he clearly knows so much about the topic and is always willing to answer further questions. The homework is difficult and pretty much impossible to do if you start day-of, but if you start beforehand you'll be ok, and the tests are much easier than the homework. Overall difficult, but very rewarding class!

Dummit is the most talented math professor at NEU. His lectures and (detailed) notes are extremely easy to follow and interesting. He knows so much about a breadth of topics. His homeworks are extremely long but rewarding, and he is very fair when it comes to grading. I highly recommend taking any of his courses, you'll learn a lot.

This was a pilot version, so I was the lab rat. Professor Dummit knew how to explain his content thoroughly and was good at leaving notes online and was easy to review. That said, he did give intense homework and can assume you have learned a topic before. Good professor overall
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dummit's courses are a fabled right of passage at Northeastern. MATH 4527 was one of the most demanding classes I've taken. Incredibly heavy material is compacted into just 4 months. That being said, the course taught me a lot and was very enjoyable. Time seems to fly when you're having fun or when you're finding reduced quadratic forms.

Evan Dummit is a great professor. His lectures are always so engaging and his homework is usually straightforward. If you read his notes, it usually does not take a long time. Also, there are only 3 exams, which are generally very passable. Overall, you should take his class as it will boost your gpa without having a lot of work.

The homework can be very difficult, the midterms are usually easier. Attendance in lectures isn't mandatory but you won't get by if you try to read the posted notes because they are very dense and can be confusing.

The notes work great to review what you've learned already, but it's still useful to write your own.
Great professor for 3081. Explains in a calm and collected fashion - types out notes on canvas and supplies great review sheets for exams. Would totally take again.

It's only been two weeks but I've already found myself to be a lot more engaged and interested in Professor Dummit's class. His explanations are clear and concise, and the questions he works through are challenging but lead to a deeper understanding of the subject. One of the best teachers you could take 3081 with.
Great teacher, would def take again. Highly recommend.

Evan Dummit was an excellent professor in just about every way. It was clear that he had an enthusiasm for the material and would always provide excellent examples and feedback. He also created a ton of supplementary material that helped immensely with learning any confusing material. I would recommend any math course his name is attached to.

In one word: amazing. Evan is clear during his lectures and manages to make linear algebra intuitive and simple. I have taken another linear algebra course at NEU and the difference between the courses (the content was virtually identical) is insane. Homework is standard, once a week. For tests, he grades super fast so you always know your grade.

An excellent professor. His lectures are excellent and convey really advanced material in a digestible way, and his lecture notes are superbly written. If something comes up and impacts your ability to do well in the course, he'll accommodate. He genuinely cares his students.
I enjoyed his class immensely. Evan Dummit is a brilliant professor and his notes are amazing. I recommend taking any class he lectures at NEU.
Loved this class, expectations were very clear and he gave really good feedback.

Professor Dummit is the best! Knows everything there is to know about the material he is teaching, and gives great lectures. The material and practice problems are exactly like the exams. Has a great sense of humor, too.

Absolutely amazing professor. I guarantee you will not regret taking any course that he teaches. His brilliance and extensive knowledge on all areas of mathematics are obvious. He is a very pleasant guy. He makes every concept so simple and easy to understand and provides proofs for everything. Overall 10000000/10. Take his class fr.

Evan Dummit is a fantastic professor and a great person. He is really funny and I feel bad for him since I would be laughing during class, but my mic was on mute all the time. If you attend lectures and do the online project sets (which were immensely helpful) you will enjoy the class. Plus he writes his own notes that are better than any textbook.

Adjusted very well to COVID struggles and has very informational lectures.  The no questions asked homework extensions are amazing and the default extra time for exams has been very helpful.  Makes these calculus concepts seem effortless.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Dummit is one of the best professors I've had at NEU. He made the hardest topics of Probability + Stats straightforward and clear, and he truly cares about his students. He added in policies throughout the semester to help students (midterm drop, final exam percentage choice), and is overall such a cool and funny guy.

I forgot to do my Trace evaluations, so I'm gonna give my brother a bit of love here. In short, Evan is incredibly fair and transparent; he doesn't make you pay for a textbook, he doesn't have pop quizzes, and if you take the time to study, you will get an A. He is also funny. Take his class if you can. Seriously.
Great professor. He's funny and his lecture notes are thorough and easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dummit is one of the best instructors I've ever had. He's an absolute genius and makes extremely hard topics and math seem intuitive and straight forward. His lectures are incredible, and his free notes are better than most math textbooks out there. His grading is super fair, and he cares that you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I genuinely think he's a really nice guy who cares about his students and is very passionate. However, in class, you focus more on why something is the way it is rather than actually using or applying the formulas, etc for a test. So homework is basically you teaching yourself chemistry. The tests are pretty different from class problems
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Practice problems are so different from test
Never curves even when tests are hard
No empathy for students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really awesome professor. Never took chemistry before, but he helped me understand everything. Even when I bombed a test, I still felt proud of what I learned, and I eventually improved. Gives lots of extra credit on exams, has good policies, and tries to help you succeed. Just a really great professor to have, especially for such a hard course.

Very caring and fair professor. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and cares about their wellbeing. Easy to get help outside of class. Tests are a bit difficult and require critical thinking but he gives 3 extra points on every test. Lots of homework but ample time to complete it. Only critique: study guides often didn't match actual tests.
He was such an amazing chem professor. He made the concepts seem so simple and was so nice. The homework wasn't too bad, just a little tedious.
loved him! just do the homework and go to office hours if needed

Very kind and accessible and a great, great professor (like the best I've had thus far). Material was tough but if you come to lecture and go to office hours he's great at explaining things. Also gives extra credit and practice problems on Aktiv are super helpful on exams, and he'll replace your lowest midterm score so a good grade is very feasible

Super kind and caring, and great at teaching (like the best I've had yet). The material is hard but going to lectures and office hours made it seem very simple. Very feasible to succeed in the course if you put effort in, he also gives extra credit which is nice and will replace your lowest midterm exam grade.

If you're taking CHEM1161, take it with Dan Matthew. I would recommend the chem ramp up (it was extra credit but it was actually helpful). An A is totally achievable by completing all the homework (unlimited tries) and studying using the practice exams and aktiv problems. Of course, try your best to stay proactive the class can move fast at times.

The actual goat. I had zero chemistry knowledge coming in and finished with an A, and that's all thanks to Dr. Dan's teaching! Take notes on the homework, study the practice exams, and focus on what you're struggling with. Also the ramp up is helpful if you have no idea (like me) what to expect coming into a chem course. Thank you!!!

I would absolutely recommend Prof Matthew for gen chem!! If you attend class regularly and do the homework assignments you'll be set up for success in his class. He's a good lecturer and easy to follow, he takes notes during class that you follow along on. Attendance is mandatory, but he allows a couple of absences. He's also super nice :)

By far the best Chem professor I have ever had! He cares about how the students are learning more than grading, and his lectures really made me understand the concepts so much more clearly. Plus, he gives many opportunities for extra credit. Recitation can feel like more of a chore but you get a bump up in your grade if you go to all of them.

BEST PROFESSOR SO FAR! I was so worried about taking a good chem professor because the class can be difficult, but what you put in is what you get out. Biggest advice is follow along lectures, and you will be perfectly set. I went to almost all office hours and he bonded with all the students, taking hours out of his week and day to help. love him!

DAN MATTHEW AKA THE BEST PROF EVER!!!! He is an amazing professor. He really knows how to teach. He gives 4 midterm exams and a cumulative final exam. If you score higher on the final than one of your midterms he will replace your lowest midterm grade with the final exam grade. He gives tons of practice and is willing to meet with you anytime!

I LOVE DR.DAN! He is one of the best professors I've had here at Northeastern. His lectures are straightforward and the activ practice questions he gives really help for his exams. He really helped me enjoy chemistry and solidify concepts that I forgot in high school. If you understand the material well, the exams should be straightforward.

Dr. Dan is the best! If you're taking chemistry, definitely try to take it with him. He takes notes with the class, so the lecture stays at a good pace. He's willing to reexplain anything if a student is confused. He's so easy to reach outside of class and his office hours are very useful.

I love this man. So amazing at seeing what works and does not work for students and changing his teaching style around that. There were so many resources for the exams. He is so kind and very approachable at office hours. You will always get 100 on the hw because you get unlimited tries.
Good professor and makes the most out of lectures. Notes are really helpful, and going to his office hours are too.

Cool dude. Genuinely cares about his students understanding the course content. This slows down his lectures heavily, but he helped me actually learn some things I had memorized and forgotten in high school. Though while the material was often familiar and low-level, his tests reached into dimensions class time couldn't dream of.

Take him for Gen Chem! He can be reached outside of class and really cares about his students. Also, instead of having slides for his lecture, he writes out his notes along with his class, so it goes at a natural pace. He structures his class with the textbook (not essential), but you do have to purchase Aktiv (practice problems). Overall, great!

Challenging for those uncomfortable with chemistry. He did not curve any exams but he gave extra points at the end of them. If you make a good-faith attempt, but come up with a D by the end of the semester, he will boost your grade so you will pass. He is a safe bet, but the other professor did curve exams which would've been extremely useful.

Dan is one of few professors I've had who genuinely cares about students. If anything were to happen, whether its falling behind, simply sleeping in, or an emergency, he's gracious and understanding. Chemistry is not easy but he taught it well. Homework and class work is easy to get 100s on despite the tests being difficult, so avg grade is boosted

Dr. Dan cares a lot about his students and wants you to succeed. He provides a lot of study/review resources for exams. I liked his teaching style too-- he walks you through the notes/example problems on his iPad. Highly recommend!
Dr. Dan was an amazing teacher. He did a great job at explaining the material in a simple way. He also gave us tests from the previous semesters to help us prepare for exams, which was super helpful.

Overall the class was pretty good. I like his lecture style (he writes his notes in notability) and he cares a lot about his students. The one thing I did not like was how he stated he purposely wanted the tests to be harder. Better than other professors for gen chem.

Dr. Dan is a fantastic professor. You can tell he really cares about his students by how he always stops to answer questions. His tests are very reasonable and have questions that appear in the homework.

If you want to have a (fairly) easy time in gen chem take it with Dr. Dan. I withdrew from chem class my 1st semester and thought just I wasn't cut out to understand the material. That all changed with Dr. Dan. He's a great lecturer and cares a lot about his students. He's very personable and hosted in-person review sessions before every exam.

I liked his teaching style (actively writes out notes during lecture) and his tests were fair. He is generous with partial credit. An etextbook and 2 online accounts are required to be purchased for this class.

dr dan is a tougher prof than people say - he even prefaced this semester by saying he knew on rate my prof he was known to be easy, but he's not anymore. this class isn't impossible, lectures are good (though a bit rushed), he's amazing with extra credit on tough exams. my biggest piece of advice? stay on top of lectures and USE THE TEXTBOOK.
I was not a fan of the way he lectures. His notes were not conducive to review after class. he also mentioned that his goal is to make his exams harder than past semesters.

Great professor, despite his tests being a bit challenging. Writes his notes with the class, making it easy to understand and visualize. His practice tests were not like the actual exams in terms of difficulty, but if you understand the material you should be fine if you study outside of class. Great guy, super nice and approachable.

Dr. Dan was fantastic! Such a caring individual who puts in the effort for you if you are willing to do the same. Exams were slightly difficult, but as long as you prepare with the resources he provides, you should succeed.

great, intelligent professor with riveting lectures on fascinating content. very engaging and allows abstract concepts to make sense. 
class moves very fast DO NOT fall behind, exams do not match up to practice tests or problems in terms of difficulty. exams are tricky and challenging. hard to earn a good grade. deep concept knowledge guaranteed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Dan during spring 2023 and he was one of the best professors I've had here! His lectures were so helpful. He usually takes notes while teaching in front of the class and makes them accessible for everyone at any time. Notes are clear and everything on the tests will be stuff that has been in the lectures. He's genuinely a great guy too!

He started off the year strong and was a great prof. He made chemistry understandable. However, his exams are way harder than they need to be. He said he purposely made them harder than past exams. He often would recognize that they were harder then they needed to be b
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dan's pretty easy. 3 exams before the final and attendance is mandatory but he takes attendance by giving out a code at the beginning of class so if you have friends in the class it is helpful. The exams are pretty easy but get harder as the semester goes on just because of the material. He posts all his notes online so it should be fine.

Awesome guy, made me love Chemistry after I hated it in hs. Honestly a very nice dude that goes over all the content clearly in his lectures and his tests are all very fair. If you show up to class and do HW then you will be fine, he also gives out a lot of extra practice problems that prepare you well for the tests.

I dreaded chemistry coming into college but Dan has made my chem experience amazing. His lectures are clear, not overwhelming or over complicated. Would 100% take him if you think chem is not your best subject because he makes the material understandable. VERY generous when grading exams. Exams are difficult and long but manageable.

Wonderful professor. Reminder, always go to his lectures, unless you want to miss a TON of materials. Class pace was incredibly fast but his lecture and explanation were super detailed. Exams are VERY DIFFICULT but very fair. Get ready to study a lot for this course, and if you do you will learn a lot and in good shape.

Prof. Matthew is an amazing lecturer. Instead of slideshows, he opens up pages in notability & writes notes with you which is a much more effective way of learning/teaching chemistry. His tests are also fair, simply practice & make sure you fully understand important concepts (conceptual questions are asked). There is also always a bonus question!

Dan is super approachable, and knowledgeable about chemistry. His office hours and extra help sessions were helpful, and he posted lots of practice problems. It wasn't all good though, he would say his class was too easy in past semesters and purposely made exam questions more difficult or trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although I really enjoyed his lectures, his exams tended to be extremely difficult. He does give practice exams before every exam, and when I would take those, I would get high 90s. Then when it came to the actual exam, the questions would be different formats and would ask you to do things that were never taught in class.

Dan is great at explaining. Only thing I would say is that they can word some test problems weirdly, and it just throws me off. I don't understand why they can't just clearly state open response questions. Other than that, great professor, there were 3-4 exams + 1 final. Go to class, do your homework, and study a lot, and I think you'll do well.

Professor Matthew is a great professor. He explains concepts very clearly and cares a lot about his students and the subject. Tests were not too difficult as long as you studied, and the weekly homework assignments had unlimited attempts, so they were good practice.

DAN SLAYS but it was a difficult course due to the material. As long as you stay on top of the homework and do the practice exams you will do good.Dan is really caring and his office hours help a lot.
As long as you put the work in you can get a decent grade.

Expectations are very clear. Most of the class finished with an A- or an A. Lectures are easy to follow and he makes the concepts easy to understand. Go to the class the week of Thanksgiving for extra credit!!

Dr. Dan is amazing! He is very clear about grading. There were 3 midterms and the final exam. Participation is mandatory and he gives weekly homework assignments. He explains everything so clearly and always answers questions.

Dan is such a great teacher. He makes concept very simple to understand. His office hours are very helpful.   Exams are fair and he post a lot of practice exams/questions (+ easyy bonus points on every exam). Attendance is mandatory every day which is meh. Other than that, no other complaint, loved the class and the teacher.
I love Dan!!! Everyone loves him. He makes the information so understandable and you can tell he really cares. He is very accessible outside of class.

Professor Matthew made general chemistry a breeze! I hadn't even thought about chemistry since sophomore year of high school and he made everything engaging and easy to understand. He posted practice exams that were almost identical to his tests. Class averages were consistently above 80%. Every test has a bonus question for extra credit.

Overall, the class is not too hard, he teaches well, the only complaint is sometimes it is frustrating that class is mandatory especially if you have taken a course like physics already and know some of the material.

explains everything in a way that's easy to understand and will take the time to make sure you understand topics. assigns weekly homework but it can normally be completed in about an hour. tests are very fair and he gives you points whenever he's able to on non-multiple choice problems
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Probably the best instructor I've ever had - take Dan if you can! He is very clear and lectures while he projects his own notes which is super clear. Fair grading, accessible, and great explanations. I took chem in high school but this class has left me with a totally higher level of understanding.
You can just tell he really care about his students and how they do. He is very reasonable with grading and genuinely teaches well. I would take more of his classes for sure
Took Chem1161 from him in Spring 2022, very easygoing and is a very fair grader. Super accessible outside of class and does his best to make sure all of his students learn the course material

I loved professor Matthews' class. I had such a hard time with chemistry in high school, but he made me enjoy it. There's weekly homework assignments (they're fairly long), 3 midterms, and a final (score will replace your lowest midterm grade), as well as attendance in lecture and recitation that goes into your grades. Work hard and you'll succeed!

Professor Matthews is the best professor I have had so far at Northeastern. He gives amazing lectures and makes sure students thoroughly understand content, and is always available outside of class for help. He also only tests on what he lectures, so there are no surprises on his exams. For new chemistry students I couldn't recommend him more!

Amazing professor! I hated chem back in high school but he made the class enjoyable and he taught concepts extremely well. He is always willing to help and there are many different tasks that make up your grade, so it's not just based on exams. Take the class, you won't regret him as a professor.

Take this class! Dr. matthew makes all the material very interesting and does a great job explaining it, he also uses his ipad to write lecture notes during class which makes it easy to keep up. Clear grading and gives a good amount of partial credit. Weekly homework assignments and exams make up most of the grade.

Really good teacher! He explains concepts very well and is always willing to help and answer questions. Also a really nice guy. He gives fun bonus questions on tests like, "What's your favorite place to go in Boston?" and they're usually worth a lot of points. Chem is hard and you do need to study, but he makes it a lot easier and more fun.

Wonderful professor, his lectures are very clear and easy to follow. If you struggled with chemistry take him, as he takes the time to explain theoretical concepts. I would definitely take a course with him again.

Dr. Dan was a really good professor for gen chem. He took the time to explain the concepts in class through his interesting teaching style which is writing on his iPad and we copy down notes. His tests were very true to what we learned in class so you wouldn't expect any surprises on the test if you study all the material from class.
Great for chemistry - teaches well and is understanding

Wonderful professor, goes every extra mile to help with student understanding and is great at explaining theoretical concepts in understandable ways. Also just a super cool dude, really patient and makes a hard class (chem 1 and 2 accelerated) understandable for students. Would definitely take a course with him again.

Dan is a really knowledgable professor. He's clear, direct, and caring for his students. I really enjoyed learning with him, and I think that other student's did as well.  Homework was genuinely helpful.  Unlimited attempts and no point penalty for wrong answers. He encourages guesses in lectures because that's how you learn.  Highly recommend!

Best professor I've had at neu so far. Love the way he teaches lectures; he basically writes the lectures on his iPad as he is teaching you, making them very easy to follow and visualize what he is talking about. He explains concepts simply and clearly, and is very accessible for office hours. 10/10 would take again

Dr. Dan is the best professor I've had at Northeastern. I took gen chem 1 and 2 with another professor before and withdrew from the class because I was struggling and unsupported but I have done well in this class. Dr. Dan is an amazing teacher, his lectures are easy to follow, and he cares deeply about his students' success. A rare find, amazing.

this class is agonizing. class is boring if it isn't confusing. He introduces topics by giving layered problems and expects you to already know the material. I have already taken the class before and I still get confused when he introduces a new topic. He might be the most condescending teacher he creates a culture where questions are bad.

if you've never taken calc before, RUN. he basically just takes notes on the book and then just writes them on the board with little to no explanation/teaching. if you go to office hours and display an ounce too much of misunderstanding he quickly gets condescending. just a bad teacher overall, your better off switching

How tf does he still have a job. In class he just copies worksheets onto the whiteboard and expects you to make sense of it- gives NO explanations . Absolutely no partial credit on quizzes and he refuses to put anything into canvas so you dont actually know what your grade is.  Over half my class withdrew.

reviews.comment: At first, I thought that these reviews were being dramatic because calc is expected to be difficult.  He seemed to be approachable and accessible during office hours.  However, he can often get snappy, rude, and treat you as if you are dumb.  He starts off with difficult examples that he won't test on and lectured fast. He also has weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Terrible Teacher and even worse grader. I have not gotten a question wrong on some quizzes, yet  I was given an 80. If u know calc 1 already, just don't come to class and read the textbook. AND IF U TAKE THIS CLASS, SHOW ALL WORK DO NOT MISS A SINGLE SIGN OR NOTATION U ARE WARNED.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Read these reviews and assumed that it couldn't be that bad.  It was.  I often went to him for help when I didn't understand material, and at first, he was welcoming.  But, when it took me longer to understand the material, he was very condescending, despite seeing that I was trying and seeing that I often scored 90's on the (very short) quizzes.

reviews.comment: was going to give him a higher rating until the final which covered a topic he straight up did not cover in class. no mandatory homework is a problem waiting to happen and literally nothing graded besides weekly quizzes, a midterm, and a final means your grade is unbelievably volatile. classes were not awful but not amazing.

Its better to show up for the weekly quizzes than for class. This guy faces the board the whole time, copying things from the textbook. He doesn't make sure we're following and skip steps. When you do have a question he is completely condescending. its bareable but make sure do all the prac. problems. He grades like he's rationing the points

reviews.comment: He does not teach. He literally reads straight from the textbook and gives exact examples from it. You can simply skip class, read the textbook, take notes yourself, and it would be the same. He grades only 3 things: quizzes, midterms, and final. If you do poorly on the quizzes, then goodluck, because his midterm is way harder. DO NOT RECCOMEND

reviews.comment: Dr Hudon is super funny! also very passionate about physics/astronomy. the quizzes and tests come straight from the homework in the sylllabus

reviews.comment: really funny! the quizzes/tests and pop quizzes come straight from the homework

reviews.comment: The class is much harder than I expected, but it was quite rewarding. I love space and everything astronomy so doing the work didn't feel like a chore. The homework takes hours but you have between 1-2 weeks to do each one and you have a partner. Prof Hudon loves the material which makes the class more enjoyable. Lectures are long and important!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: skibidi toilet

If you attend the lectures and do the homework, you'll be fine. There are weekly (not pop) quizzes and 2/4 quiz problems will be from the homework. He goes through content quickly, but similar lectures are available online for free (linked in syllabus) and help if he didn't explain something well enough. There are only 2 tests.

reviews.comment: Doesnt teach information, and then blames students for not paying attention

reviews.comment: If you want to take this class as a fun elective, save yourself and take something else instead. Lectures are very dense and fast, and there's way too much material for a one semester class. Literally harder than a physics class, too. Homeworks take hours, he grades them super hard, and provides little feedback.

reviews.comment: He seems like a nice guy, but rarely ever spends time to actually make sure we understand what's going on in class. I have spent countless hours studying for a course that should be 1/3rd of the difficulty. Only graded on tests so if you're not a great test taker, find a different professor.
doesnt speak to students, only gives quizzes with few questions, extremely boring, does not care.

reviews.comment: Makes the homework have nothing to do with the lectures
Great professor who likes physics. Very funny and has good conversations. Lectures heavily and don't skip class because he gives pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof Hudon is clearly very enthusiastic about his subject. However, that does not translate in teaching or how he treats students. He was not very understanding or caring when it came to any of the students in class and had the tendency to be sort of mean.

Professor Hudon is very inaccessible, does not answer emails, and overall is not a good teacher. He does not explain the topics and with a midterm average of 68%, refused to curve or scale it even though a majority of the class had not been able to complete the exam. Also does not explain topics or WEAR HIS MASK IN CLASS!!

This professor is pretty bad at actually teaching concepts. He usually briefly explains the material and then does a few examples that he does not explain well. It's hard to follow along what he teaches in class, but he always offers extra help outside of class. Some homework is graded and there are weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very very poor instructor. All he does is write problems on the board, solve them, and say does everyone agree? He also takes off full credit on exams even if you show work, and a small mistake will cost 8/10 points. Learned nothing from his mandatory lectures. Got through the class via textbook and online videos. Never take him if you can.

Lectures can be a bit boring at times but he is a really nice man who does plenty of example problems to make sure you know how to apply a certain concept. Homework isn't graded and as long as you understand the material presented in lecture you don't really need to do it.
best of the best
love her !!!! miss her now that I'm not in her class this semester :'(
very generous grading, and easily explains the readings from the seminar during our recitation time

gokcen is the best design recitation professor there is. she cares deeply about her students, reminding them frequently to drink water so they can achieve their greatest hydrated potential. she has a good artistic vision, however she is not always the most competent when it comes to technology. overall i can't wait to take more classes from her.

Very enthusiastic, but not the most effective professor when he teaches. Clear favorites, but if you are able to study alone, quizzes and exams aren't bad at all. Often goes on tangents about personal stories and opinions. Try not to sit in the back if you don't want to be picked on lol.

reviews.comment: cant even lie i felt like i was listening to google translate with an accent. he was telling stories more than lecturing. quite easy to finesse a grade in tho so ill give him that

I passed this class because I took AP Calc in High School. His tests and quizzes are super easy and he tells you what is on them. He prepares you well for the final, but if you don't know calculus going into this, don't take this class.

Before each quiz/exam, goes through each question & tells u exactly whats on it. Responds to emails quickly. *Go to his office hours he will help you* Grades very fairly, will reconsider points off if you talk with him.
Sometimes a bit scary. He's from the Soviet union, so thats just his personality. He wont hate you unless you never come to class.

Prof. Karapetian was a great teacher and I felt he prepared us well for each test. If you attend class and pay attention, you will be fine. Weekly quizzes that are pretty easy and have extra credit questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Karapetian is alright. He gives quizzes weekly, but he tells you exactly what is on it so if you write down what's on it and study the quizzes are super light. Midterms are the same. He is absolutely hilarious and often goes on rants about random topics during class. One time he told us to go to China and work as engineers there.

Ok, this dude is hilarious. Hands down one of the funniest guys ive ever met, and it's not because he tries to be. Lectures are a bit all over the place but you'll know what's on your test. I thought he was a great teacher and his stories were awesome. SIT IN THE FRONT ROW (I promise it matters).

First two weeks of lecture were confusing and unrelated, don't feel overwhelmed. Lectures are disorganized but tests are EXACTLY like what is covered. tells you ahead of time what the test Qs are. likes to call/call out students, makes lectures fun. lectures go really fast; if you're confident in calc 1 class is easy. No HW and tests have bonus pts

Prof Karapetian was such a funny guy. In class he walks you through exactly what you need to know and teaches to understand. He tells you exactly what will be on tests/quizes and offers extra credit questions on most tests. He can sometimes go off on tangents about the American education system which can seem targeted but he really cares.

He teaches the class like we already know the material. During his lectures, he moves too quickly to grasp the lesson, and then he pauses and says "everybody understands?" and wait a second and then move on. If you ask a question about what he just tried to explain, he flames you for not understanding and your old teachers for being unable to teach
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: textbook was HORRIBLE and he's not great at explaining things either. it helps to review the topic before class because he works so quickly on the board that you WILL get lost if you dont know whats happening. however it's hard to get lower than a C on quizzes because the partial credit is crazy generous

He can be very nice and friendly in class AS LONG AS YOU PAY ATTENTION. He clearly outlines the exact types of questions in the exams and quizzes and provides practice questions. He can sometimes drone off on unrelated tangents and he can be condescending to individuals depending on your major. (If you're a business major, don't tell him.)

Very passionate guy. He clearly cares about his lecture and about the subject he's teaching, and he's pretty funny when teaching. But, be prepared to learn everything during his office hours or by yourself (Organic Chem Tutor was a life saver). Edgar moves really fast through his lectures and for the love of God I could not read his handwriting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a hard course, even if you took Calc 2 last year. He can be difficult to understand at times and moves very quickly. However, he will answer your questions and is VERY helpful during office hours. He doesn't sugarcoat anything, which can come off as rude, but he doesn't mean it in that way. Also, the exams are a HUGE part of the grade.

Amazing teacher and cares about making sure that students understand but can be tough in class. if you ask a stupid question, he will say you should know the answer and your past teachers failed but then he will answer the question as clearly as he can. you will either love him or hate him.

Edgar Karapetian is by far the worst professor I've ever had the displeasure of taking. I'm telling you, you should never, and I mean seriously never take his class. Even if you need the class and he's the only open section just wait until next semester even if it delays your graduation. He's horribly rude and discouraging to students. Bad teacher.

He moves extremely fast and does not make sure students understand the material. He is hard to follow with his handwriting and the lack of explanation he gives. He doesn't fully walk through problems and instead just does them and yell at the class. Very mean and condescending to students. Most unprofessional and rude professor i've ever met.

If you already know calculus, this class is very easy. If you're new to calc, the professor may be challenging because his teaching isn't very clear. Attendance isn't necessary, but keep track of test and quiz dates. He can be a picky grader. He always tells you exactly what q's will be on test+quiz. Also kinda funny, but it gets old.
He basically tells students exactly what is gonna be on the tests/quizzes ahead of time. Super funny, his lectures are very entertaining. Best math teacher I've had.

Probably the worst teacher I've had in my life. Not only can he not teach, he is also a very unpleasant person. He spends half the class time ranting about how we shouldn't be allowed to become scientists and engineers and then tries to catch up to where we should have been so he always holds us over time. Horrible professor. Do not take his class.

Don't take Calc 2 with him. He's disrespectful, condescending, and has an inflated ego. His lectures are confusing, and he mumbles. He always publicly shames students for mistakes, creating a hostile environment. Additionally, he makes inappropriate, racist comments. His notes are messy and hard to follow, making the course even more challenging.

Great prof who really wants you to learn. Not for very sensitive students, but if you can handle a bit of pressure he's awesome. Tells you what's on the tests, gives similar practice, super generous cheat sheets, funny, fast-paced but manageable, and truly passionate about math.

This professor is very rude, disrespectful, moves very quickly, hard to follow his handwriting, and patronizes students when they ask questions. The ONE single benefit is that he tells you the questions on his tests beforehand. He WILL publicly embarrass you in front of the class for a variety of reasons (it's awful when you don't know an answer).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Karapetian can make learning Calculus stressful. During lecture, he often shouts at his students, going on fervent tangents about the school system. In my class, he said that we are all on a fifth grade level and we should not be taking Calculus. It is hard to ask questions during lecture because of the fear of being called out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not seem to care for his students. He moves extremely fast, even knowing the material it is hard to understand. He does not wait for students or make sure they understand and he bullies students for asking questions. He is very condescending and I i never felt comfortable asking questions. He also has no tolerance for missing quizzes, ever.

She's a great professor. The class itself isn't too hard; you just have to actually understand everything and know a lot of definitions. Her final was easy too, just questions pulled from exams 1-3. Lectures are funny/engaging, and the material is interesting.

Prof. Greiner structures the course around three in-person exams with multiple-choice and open-response questions. Exam content is taken directly from the slides and study guides. The cumulative final is based on material from the previous exams, which helps with preparation. Lectures are engaging, and extra credit opportunities are available.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i really liked this class! there is a LOT of material but she makes study guides that are pretty accurate and help a lot. the final only had one question that wasn't on a previous exam which was really nice. very interesting class!!

Dr. Greiner is an excellent professor! She's down to earth, kind, and the most knowledgeable prof I've had. You can tell she's very passionate about the field and wants her students to learn and succeed. There is a lot of material, so her classes are lecture-heavy but super interesting. Definitely use the study guides and go to her review sessions!

very passionate and knows material well. tests on paper in class (i had 500-600 flashcards for each test (3). If you work hard, you will do well. Only annoying thing was that the final was repeat qs (i get it was to pull up grades) but as someone who already had a high grade in the class, it felt like a waste of time to re-memorize old test answers
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she's very personable and flexible, i loved taking this class lowkey. grade is calculated off 3 tests, final, and attendance. lecture is engaging but there is SO MUCH material, and can be overwhelming sometimes. however the final is only made up of past test questions, so it kinda balances out. also all exams are half MCQ and half short response.

Professor Velazco overall was a great professor! His classes are discussion based so be prepared to be called on but he makes it a fun environment to participate in. I will say although he is great, his grading is a bit all over the place. He isn't very clear with his expectations and his grading reflects that.

This class is genuinely confusing, difficult tests, no study guide, many students are failing, just gives us a handbook and practice tests, which closes down the night before the actual test. Many students don't know where to start studying or where to go, as he only refers to the textbook. Tests are also really inconsistent, DO NOT TAKE AT ALL.

He doesn't teach at all in lectures. If you take this class, you're kind of on your own. His lectures are pointless. The only examples that you do in class are math calculations, which make up a small part of the exams you take. There are 3 exams in total. He does post practice exams, but he makes you use a lockdown browser to take them?? Avoid!!

Honestly the professor is not that bad the only reason he's getting a 1 star is because he is not consistent with his tests. The first exam was 90% the same as the study guide. So you would assume that's the best way to study. Nope the next two exams are completely different and doesn't match his teaching style. If u can avoid it's better

Lectures wise were not that great for me. He's ok with grading and he rounded my final grade up after I asked. I would say definitely a good professor to talk to, especially if you are into SC as a career. Be active and ask him for clarifications on assignments and you will be fine (above B). Final was online. Tests are tough, but fair game.

Prof Enio is a nice guy but structures his class like it's the only class you'll be taking that semester. Group projects are intensely difficult with untold strict guidelines and bad group mates, & he does nothing to remedy how lost everyone in the class is. Take only if supply chain is your life passion or if you hate yourself!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely evil professor, not in the way he interacts with students (he's a nice dude), but straight up just how he grades. Long assignments, terrible group projects esp if you have bad groupmates, and he's really unclear with every guideline. DO NOT TAKE unless this is the only class you're taking that sem or your rlly passionate about schm.

Professor Velazco is a great professor and a really nice guy. He moves through lectures quickly but uses good examples that the class reviews together. He keeps everyone engaged by asking for their thoughts and opinions at random. I'd definitely recommend him, but be ready to work!
He's a great professor who's always available during office hours and genuinely helpful when students need support. He does tend to call on students during class, but overall he's excellent.

He's a tough grader, doesn't give enough guidance on what he wants. For the group project (50% of our grade), not all expectations were spelled out in the syllabus. In a 1 month DOC, there was not enough time to adjust to his expectations. A lot of us were unpleasantly surprised by our final grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he's honestly the best prf I've had. he's funny, caring, and witty. material was engaging, and even though he's a tough grader, if you stay on top of the work and put effort into it, he's way more understanding. Just show up, join the discussions, and you'll walk away having learned a ton.

Lectures were helpful, but his tests and projects just seemed wasteful. He doesn't go into depth with concepts past what the presentations say, which had useless information that never got brought up again. He wasn't helpful outside of class, and his feedback is awful. He also doesn't care about the test averages (our midterm average was a 67).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Projects are 40% of the grade, so just pray your team pulls their weight. He loves teaching but he won't curve so just be ready for a low test average which is 30% of the grade.
Prof Velazco is super passionate and knowledgeable about supply chain. Lectures are not super helpful, but the group projects are super fun.

Prof Velazco is a super nice guy and is very passionate and knowledgeable about supply chain. His lectures aren't super helpful, and he just repeats the textbook material, so if you need good lectures, this class might not be for you. no final in the class, just three exams throughout the semester. Overall would recommend.

He is a very interesting professor with lots of cool stories and engaging lectures. He is passionate about supply chain and makes his students intrigued as well. There is a lot of work and tests are not easy. There is lots of textbook HW, multiple written assignments, 3 tests, and a project. It is a lot of work but you will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really like him regardless of how others may feel. He is strict but wake up people, it's an upper level college class in a tough major, it's not supposed to be a breeze. His class is a great refresher from my other classes that are just Exam 1 + Exam 2 + Final. There is a massive variety of projects, case studies, and other interesting content

He's awesome! I love that he does many things not just tests. There are many different projects and such. He also always has good stories about working as executive in the real world so it is not just lectures and textbook

Many of the reviews tell you to avoid him because of his harsh participation. However, I believe this is not the case. Professor Velazco provides ample opportunities for you to participate and is really just looking to see if you are engaging the classroom. As long as you put in an honest effort, you will do great things in this class!

Professor Velazco is a wonderful professor who spices things up with a wide variety of class activities. There are several different group projects, case studies, papers, and readings that make his class much more exciting than an average lecture heavy, textbook-only course. He is a tough grader on participation though, so speak up more!

Beware of the participation grade at the end of the year. It dropped my grade very low. For the case presentations, his rubric is unclear and he's a harsh grader. His tests were very difficult and didn't match his material. His exams were online with lockdown browser but it was still difficult and the class average was low but he didn't curve it.
I would recommend taking Enio's class. Slightly disorganized and vague in his requirements for papers and projects, but for the most part if you put in decent effort you will do well.

I was doing well in his class, which took a lot of work and effort to be consistent in, but he ruined my grade with participation. Beware you must participate throughout the semester or it will kill your grade by the end of the semester.

This class is based on 3 tests, that are not related to the LONG lectures given by the professor. All the projects are impossible to get a 100. He is passionate about the class, but his way of teaching is of the 20th century. If you want to learn with a mediocre grade take this class, if you want a good grade avoid it!

This class is hard. Everyone I know, regardless of professor would say SCHM is hard. The exams are also very difficult to get the grade you want on. Despite this, the professor is still amazing. He is very passionate and makes lectures fun. Of all the SCHM professors, I would recommend Velazco the most.

Nice guy but very difficult class. Could've gotten a B+ but the prof refused to bump my participation grade 5% despite actually participating in class. Most of your grade comes from the three huge tests that are throughout the semester which are confusing and cover content that was not gone over during class. Do not take SCHM with him.

He is a nice guy, it was his first semester at school. I learned a lot because I read all the chapters, not necessarily from the class. The major problem was that the exams were extremely confusing and hard.
The material taught in class didn't match what was on exams. It was difficult to prepare for exams given the differences between the information in the textbook/slides versus what was on the exams.

A lot of pаpers to writе, but they're not tоo hаrd/lоng, and you have lots of time for them. The exams were hаrd at first, but I eventually understood the formаt and what to study for. Overall, a good professor, mеdium diffiсulty class, but hоnestly, еasy if you are gоod at memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: really nice guy, everything you need is on the slides and the final study guide- personally im not good at math so i struggled- but the way the course is structured with a big part of your grade based on HW you should be fine unless you literally don't try at all.

I loved Dr. Eidson's class! He was super sweet and got to know all of us individually which I think is rare!! His lectures are thorough and there are plenty of easy assignments to raise your grade (you drop the 2 lowest assignments too). There was 2 extra credit assignments at the end. :)

Classes get boring because he sometimes rambles a little bit. Information is not very organized in the lecture slides, so there are a lot of gaps in information that you won't have for the tests. However, if the class doesn't perform to his expectations he gives extra credit. He was a nice teacher, just not many resources given to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredible lecturer, very smart and knows what he's talking about. Your grade is composed diversely -- online quizzes, three exams (plus final), and writing assignments. Offered extra credit for every exam bc averages were lower than he wanted. Tests are easy if you follow the study guide. Super nice, and accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
4 quizzes, 4 HW assignments, 4 electronic HWs. Can be boring, but it's just the nature of the course and he does his best. He's a very good lecturer and cares ab ur success. 

I already took stats in high school, so I definitely was not the most checked in. If you haven't taken it, as long as you put in some dedication and effort you will be fine.

He is super nice and an engaging lecturer. His class is paper based to a ridiculous degree. He does not allow calculator shortcuts and we barely use excel or spss. We run ANOVAs by hand. I didn't even think that was possible. There are easier stats profs. This is old school stats you will never use again. If that's your thing, then he's great.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS the exams are like 50 ON PAPER mcqs and are impossible to study for, he rambles on in his lectures and his study guides are so broad compared to the specific questions he puts on the exams. theres writing assignments but they barely count so its all based on these awful exams. wanted to drop and withdraw the whole time
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Eidson was a pretty caring guy, and he did try his best to make cognition interesting for us. Tests were pretty much entirely based on lectures, and he released all topics the exam would cover before said exam. he also gave tons of extra credit to curve his test averages up to 85.

Prof Eidson is genuinely such a nice and relatable person. If you get the chance to take a class by him I def recommend. He gives so many extra credit options and the homework is just poll everywhere. I went to class just because how much I enjoyed him as a Professor. I will be taking him for my lab in cognition too!
AMAZING professor. So caring and makes assignments extremely clear to understand. Cognition Lab is a heavy class but he makes it super manageable. He's incredible!!

He is nice, makes the lectures pretty interesting in the way he explains things, the tests carry a lot of weight. Just the slides aren't enough to do very well on the tests, but if you attend lecture and pay attention you'll be fine.

Cognition is an objectively boring class. Eidson does his best to make it interesting, but I feel his lectures do not do a good enough job at preparing you for his tests. That being said, If you're a natural at memorization, you would have to put in 0 effort for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I forgot there was a test one day and I got a 55 bc I winged it and I could not recover my grade (fully my fault lol)... professor is super sweet, fun, and extremely engaging. The only bad thing is how fast he goes through his notes.. get ready to self study but this class is way easier than the other sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Eidson is a great professor for foundations but, his tests were rated pretty heavily (21% each). There are three tests which make up the majority of the grade. There are VERY EASY writing assignments, poll everywhere questions, and extra credit for 5 points on each test. Super nice professor and very caring of students.

FYI, Eidson has switched from his previous online take-home test model to lockdown browser (in person with extra credit) so do with that what you will. Overall great guy and his lectures were engaging. He was available outside of class and is always happy to help if you reach out.
I'll give him some leeway because this was his first time teaching this course (I think), but I can't recommend. Everything felt rushed and underprepared.

great guy. conveyed the material in a way that's easy to understand and made stats fun. the only annoying part is the Excel/SPSS assignments, which were a pain and a bit useless in my opinion. however, the class is pretty easy and he drops your lowest quiz and homework grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Edison changed his testing from take-home, open notes to in-class w a lockdown browser (w/o adjusting the test). That being said, he gave extra credit to help offset the difference in grading. Honestly, he is a great teacher and truly cares about his students learning the material. You have to study for the tests, but that is why we are at NEU.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Edison is such an awesome professor! He really knows what he's talking about, and he cares so much too. He explains things so well, and his exams were exact copies of what he discusses in class. He tends to go for the full lecture time, but personally I almost never got bored. I would 100% recommend this class!
Very fair. What he said he would test is exactly what he tested. Never tried to trick you.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy to pass class, but impossible to reach professor, assignments aren't graded for like years, if you like getting extra help from your professors, don't expect it here. You'll probably pass but won't understand everything you're doing. If you want an easy A, this class is for you, but if you actually want to understand the content, it's not.

Teacher was very nice and taught the class well. Exams weren't hard if you understood the homework, nothing tricky. Would sometimes have a hard time reaching him outside of class, but other than that the class was easy
Professor Eidson is very caring and an amazing professor. His lectures are good, tests are online and open-book. Homeworks are easy to do. This was a very chill class. 100% recommend!

Professor Eidson is super funny and easy to follow in class (he made stats fun!). Grade is based on 4 tests, 4 electronic data sets, 4 graded homeworks, and a final. The grading was super fair, and the lectures prepared me  for everything. Textbook is optional, but I was disappointed at how difficult he is to reach outside of class.

grades with exams and papers but are extremely easy, writings can be practically stories and informal just connecting the topic to your personal life. exams are also online and his study guide goes over everything covered honestly copy and paste the study guide into a doc and fill it out as the units go easy A.

Really nice guy and super easy class. 4 tests which are open-note and an open-note final as well. Extra credit was also offered on the final. However, he's very hard to reach and never responded to my emails, and took forever to grade exams and papers. All that aside, interesting class for an easy A.

The best prof at NEU! This is my 2nd class with him and I'd just like to say - if you can take any of his classes, do it! His teaching style really helped me navigate the process of writing research papers. Feedback is super specific, improving my 2nd drafts. No exams. Grp project was an experiment you come up with and was such a fun experience.

Professor Eidson is one of the best professors I've had so far. Cognition class was overall easy, textbook is not required, only assignments are 8 writing assignments (short) total and exams were open note. Agree with the other comment about class being like a podcast and sometimes I find it hard to pay attention. Could be just me though

TBH Prof. Eidson is one of the nicest guys. The issue with him is that he is impossible to contact. Never responded to multiple emails I sent through the semester. Quizzes exactly like the HW. Lecture isn't necessary because he reads right off the slides. Many examples in slides and an easy A if you submit everything. Easy class would recommend.

Love Dr. E! He's such a great guy. No readings!! Almost no outside work other than a few one-page writing assignments and studying for the exams. Exams were all open note. I thought cognition would be hard, but it was super chill and interesting. (His name is Robert on the official registration for anyone confused.)

Cognition with Dr. E was a very interesting course! Lectures were very informative, and required little outside learning. Textbook is not required, but I found it helpful. Also tests are open note! There aren't many assignments, just two writing assignments per unit and only 5/8 are required. Overall, I'd recommend that anyone takes Cognition!

Dr. Eidson is a really good professor. His lectures are clear and easy to digest while also being informative. The work is super manageable. Cognition is a good class if you want to learn a lot but not do a ton of outside work.

Really entertaining classes; he always tries to keep his students engaged. Homework assignments were manageable and actually contribute to your overall grade. Exams were a little difficult, but if you take good notes in class, you will be fine. No need to teach yourself via textbook. He's a great professor and I wish more were like him!

I genuinely can not recommend Professor Eidson enough: he is easily the best professor I've had. He's caring, kind and more than willing to help students at all times. His lectures are interesting and convey a lot of information in a thoughtful way. He also offers many ways to boost your grade, but does not overload you with work. 100% recommend!

Dr Eidson is amazing. He is kind, calm, and very approachable, gives great feedback and makes class discussions really interesting and funny. In 4612 you watch a bunch of movies and analyse them (amazing for a film buff, good fun for others) can't rage about Dr E enough, a really great prof (plus fair grader) HIGHLY RECCOMEND

Prof Eidson was a fantastic professor; one of the best I've had at NEU. He's caring and approachable and really wants all of his students to succeed in his class while also giving us skills we can use in research beyond his class.

If you like podcasts, you'll like this professor. Prof. Eidson seems to have adopted the speaking mannerisms of someone delivering a podcast. The downside is that he often overexplains simple concepts, which draws out the class.

prof Eidson is an alright professor, he makes the material easy and honestly does care about his students, he's just the slowest grader I've ever had. he even has TA that grades quizzes for him, but we get those grades back like a month after we've actually taken the quiz. That's the only frustrating thing about him , otherwise he'd get 5*.

One homework packet due before each test. Tests are exactly like the homework. You have to do Data Sets on SPSS and Excel which are a pain, but he grades them easily. Nice teacher. Lectures have plenty of examples.
He's an interesting professor but class never starts on time and he takes forever to grades exams.

Talks in circles. A lecture that could take 20 minutes takes 2 hrs bc he drags everything out. Promises that assignments/grades/study guides would be posted by a certain day and then didn't post until 3+ days later. His exams are mostly multiple choice with one open response at the end. Very nit picky and takes of points off for irrelevant stuff.

Dr. Eidson was a great professor for Developmental Psych this semester. Only 4 exams, 6 writing assignments, and no final which was super nice. He is always willing to help you and is very accommodating, just be sure to let him know if you have to miss class for any reason and he'll be understanding.

He's a really nice guy who just wants his students to succeed. He was the most accommodating professor I've had in terms of open office hours or scheduling things around my schedule. He made sure we really understood statistics rather than just memorizing the computations, which I appreciated.

This Professor really knows his stuff. I thought this class would be difficult but his teachings are interesting. Class style is mostly lecture but you can learn a lot. He is fair and respects his students on an individual basis. I would highly recommend him to anyone needing to take Cognition for their PSYC major or minor.

Dr. Eidson is a young professor who cares about his students. He is intelligent, but not uptight. He tries hard to make class interesting and gives detailed feedback on lab report drafts. I didn't like how he always returned them a few days to a week later than he said he would though- he should either make realistic claims or not make them at all.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Study guide solutions are wrong. When a majority of the class failed a quiz, he gave an extra credit assignment as a grade booster, BUT THEN NEVER UPDATED THE GRADEBOOK.
