reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Professor Grabiner during my first semester at Northeastern and would highly recommend him to anyone who is taking Gen Bio! At first, I was a bit nervous to talk to him, but he's a really nice guy and wants you to succeed! He posts lots of practice material for every chapter leading up to an exam, so go to office hours and do those!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor G was great. The only thing to be worried about if you take him for bio1111 is that you are graded on very few things; 4 exams, 1 final, and some online quizzes. I'm very glad I took this class with him!
Best professor I had first semester without a doubt. His styling of teaching and his practice tests genuinely made me LEARN the material. He cares about his students a lot!!

Tests are super easy, all of the questions come from the lecture slides. To get less than an A in the class you have to try and do bad on the tests/not study at all. Lectures are recorded but are generally very dense and wordy. Overall this is basically high school bio, and an A is achievable by just reading through the lecture slides.

Grabiner posts all of the recordings online. I didn't go to lectures much because of timing, but I listened to the recordings, took notes on the slides, and retook the weekly quizzes to prepare for exams. There were really no surprises. All MCQ exams are very reasonable. Grabiner is a cool dude!

10/10 would recommend! There's four unit exams and one cumulative final exam. He gives study guides out in advanced so you know what to expect on the exam. My advice: Go to class and preemptively study for exams using the study guides - to get an A you really do need to understand what is being taught.

Grabiner was a wonderful lecturer. taking notes and studying a reasonable amount will get you a very decent grade. He is also a very nice person and is very easy to talk to, I highly recommend going to talk to him if you don't get a concpet

He's a pretty good teacher. Grades are based mostly on exams so be prepared for that. Your lowest exam grade can be replaced by the cumulative exam at the end of the year. Quizzes have 3 attempts, so you're guaranteed a 100%. He does a review before each exam which is super helpful. Finals was a back-to-back Unit 4 exam and a cumulative portion.

His exams are poorly worded and there are very few questions on each exam, so you need to do perfect to get an A. The lowest exam gets dropped. During finals week he assigned an essay, a unit 4 exam, and a final back-to-back so it Was hard to study for everything. I think the other teacher is better bc he has online exams.

Dr. Grabiner is a brilliant lecturer who provides many practice problems, but his exams are extremely challenging and heavily weighted. Even dedicated students often struggle, and one bad exam can ruin your grade. Don't be fooled by reviews claiming it's easy; those are likely from exceptional test takers. Be prepared for a tough course.

He's a very good professor but make sure to take notes on what he says and not just the slides, because a lot of the exam is based off what he says. Also, the exams are multiple choice, and they are not very difficult as long as u study the material well and go over practice questions and quizzes!

Lecures were extremely helpful and slides provided most of the information needed for the exams. Exam 1 and 2 were quite manageable, but it progressively gets harder with exam 3 & 4 being quite difficult. He is just strict about his policies which is sometimes disappointing and annoying especially if you have an unforeseen circumstance.

Professor Grabiner is very nice and approachable. The class does not require attendance and the lectures are all posted online after class. Grading consists of online quizzes and exams so it is test heavy, but the tests are all multiple choice and not too difficult. If you take time for studying for exams and taking good notes you'll be all good!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was nervous to take biology but Professor Grabiner made it super comprehensible!! His lectures are dense, but he records them so you can go back and listen/watch them. Attendance is not mandatory. If you take notes on the lectures and put in the time to understand the content, you will do great on the exams (which are not particularly difficult).

He has engaging and detailed lectures with just enough dad jokes and good opportunities for participation. He includes practice questions for every section, and the answers can be found easily in his slide decks. The only outside assignments aside from self-studying are quizzes which you have the option to take multiple times.
One of the best professors I've had at Northeastern.

The lecture is very helpful. He is very caring. He inspires students to do research or at least keep in touch with new things happen in biological world. Very great professor and person. Definitely recommended.

For Dr.G's class, you definitely gotta know the content inside out. He can be very sassy but aside from that, he is awesome. Lectures are clear, informative and recorded. His tests are all MCQ and 85% of your grade. Just rewatch lectures and study everything under the sun, and you'll be good.

Dr. G is definitely very passionate about biology and it shows. He is very eager to answer questions during lectures, and his slideshows are very well-made. He gives some practice questions that you can use to review the material, and his lectures are also recorded which is nice to go back for studying. His tests and quizzes are also very fair!
Prof Grabiner was great he always was very transparent about test content and provided a lot of practice
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are very well organized and delivered. He always makes time to thoughtfully answer students' questions. All homework and exams are multiple choice. If you study the practice problems and quizzes you'll be golden. Easy A.

Dr. G is great!! He is pretty chill, but sometimes the lectures become a bit of a drag because it is a ton of information. Nonetheless, he is very good at explaining things and giving lots of practice and tips for success. Plus, he records all of his lectures! His quizzes are open-note and are really great practice for the tests. Would recommend!
You will learn a lot in his class. Everything you need to know is in his lecture slides. Organized well and relatively easy if you stay on top of the material.

He is a very smart, and knowledgeable person, and he teaches pretty good. His classes are just lectures with good slides. Overall, he is good. His quizzes are helpful for studying, but he doesn't post enough practice problems. I found I had to find extra practice online.

Dr. G was easily one of the best science teachers I've ever had. His lectures are easy to follow and accessible online. Your grade is based almost solely on tests (the quizzes don't count for much comparatively), but if you actually pay attention, participate, and study, the tests themselves really aren't difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Grabiner is very knowledgable and passionate about the topic. His slides were very helpful and the lectures were clear and helped a lot. exams are difficult but fair. lowest exam grade gets replaced by the final if your final grade exam grade is higher and lowest quiz gets dropped. I would definitely recommend taking him for bio.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Wow. One of the best professors I've ever had at Northeastern. I am not great at science, and this class was hard for me. However, he is easily accessible and makes his content as easy to digest as possible. Don't underestimate the difficulty of the exams + put in the work to truly succeed. He is so passionate about biology + a really kind person.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Grabiner. You can tell that he is passionate about what he teaches, and the c

Dr. Grabiner is hands down the best professor I have ever had. Not only is he super passionate about biology, but he is also so good at delivering hard information in a clear and understandable way. If you put in the time to study and take his practice quizzes, you will see the effort pay off in your grades. Office hours help a lot!

Class is well organized. He has the slides and lecture recording posted for you to look back over. He also posts practice versions of all the quizzes which are extremely helpful when studying for the exams. The tests are all multiple choice which is nice but they are also not very long so there is little room for error.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was an excellent teacher. His lectures were always very thorough, so make sure to show up to those. The majority of your grade comes from 5 exams (including the final) that are spaced out through the year. As long as you are going to his lectures and doing the practice problems he assigns for (optional) homework, you should be completely fine.

Really great class taught by a very passionate and well-spoken professor. Each quiz gets 3 attempts (keeps highest score), and then your lowest test score is replaced by the finals grade (if you do better). I recommend doing practice problems and using Quizlet (use study guides as template for Quizlet) to prepare for exams.

Dr. G was an ok professor. Despite the exams being multiple choice they were a little difficult in terms of the wording. I was left second guessing a lot. With that being said the exams make up 85% of your grade and quizzes are 15%. I felt like it was hard to get an A in the class because of how exams are weighted. Was helpful to rewatch lectures.

This was honestly one of the easiest class I have ever taken. There isn't a lot of work besides from attending lecture (which isn't mandatory), taking quizzes (he drops the lowest), and taking unit exams (he replaces your lowest with your final exam grade if your final exam grade is higher). Just attend the lectures, take notes, and you're all set.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you take him he is not the worst option. If you don't go to class or office hours you won't understand what's going on unless you have a strong background in Biology. Other professors do exam corrections, he doesn't so it kind of screws you if you are a bad exam taker. He has a lot of office hours so its really what you put into the class.

His lectures are concise and well put together - provides structure for notes. Exams can be deceivingly easy, but not too difficult to get a good grade. No homework or outside content for this portion of Gen Bio.

Great professor! Gives us clear and concise information, is great at answering questions, has a good sense of humor, and gives us opportunities for discussion in class. Posts his lectures online so you can go back and rewrite your notes just because it is a pretty dense class information-wise. Recommend him over and over for genetics!

Dr.G is a great lecturer and does a good job of breaking down complex concepts. This class is not lecture-heavy and is more of a Socratic seminar. Be prepared to work on your public speaking skills because you will have to do (casual) presentations. class conversations and well as peer presentations are great preparation for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: real good. grade is mainly determined by exams, but they are all multiple choice with fair questions. attendance is not mandatory so you could honestly pass by just reviewing all the lecture recordings on your own time (not recommended but still possible). all around, a solid professor and a manageable course.

This class is a great class. Anyone interested in Biology, I highly recommend take really any class with this professor. Not only is he good at answering questions, the class is of a reasonable difficulty and all tests are multiple choices. Participation is helpful, and I highly recommend asking questions. I'm not sure why he has bad reviews, 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grabiner is a great professor who gets the class involved in discussion about the papers. The inquiries section I took with him is on the ubiquitin proteasome pathway. Coming out of it I have a significantly greater understanding of the pathway, along with increased ability to read scientific literature and knowledge about the process of science.

Dr. Grabiner is a great professor. He is really nice and accessible outside of class. His lectures can be a little boring but he clearly covers all the information necessary for exams. All the exams were straightforward and reflected the material taught in the lectures. Definitely recommend taking him for genetics!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Honestly I was shocked that his rating was so low. He's a pretty great lecturer. I don't do much studying, but I did attend and take notes every lecture.

Exams are all mc, there are online quizzes each week (3 attempts allowed so almost guaranteed 100)

If you show up and pay attention I think you'll do fine. I'm glad I had this prof.

Good professor! Gives all the materials and support you need to succeed and do well in class. Cares about students grades and will help you out if you need it. Shows a genuine care that students are actually learning and is clearly passionate about teaching.

He's a chill professor and is willing to re-explain concepts to you if you don't understand. The material was easy, but his lectures were kind of boring so I ended up falling asleep a lot and had to rewatch the recordings. The only work outside of class are the quizzes which are easy. Overall, you'll get a good grade if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was a solid professor and definitely has a love for the subject. Overall grade was primarily determined by 3 midterms and a final, but one midterm grade gets dropped. Only criticisms are that his presentations are pretty vague and the practice material for the midterms are not really thorough. But lectures are recorded for you to rewatch.

I didn't attend a single lecture and still got an A. The tests were so easy, the content was basically taken straight from the class lectures, which were all posted online. Just watch the lectures the day before a test, take notes, and you'll be fine. Everything was super straightforward, and Prof. Grabiner explains the course material really well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought Dr. G was a great lecturer, they were very engaging. But his exams were extremely difficult, and we were not given the exams back ever. The only study material he gave were broad overall gist questions, but they did not help prepare for the questions on the exam. If exams were fair, the class would be great.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems like a good prof, very knowledgable and everything on the tests is in the lectures. There are weekly online quizzes, but the grade was mostly made up of 3 midterms and a final. Requires a lot of studying outside of class.

His exams were about 30 questions each and filled with unfair, confusing and difficult questions. Questions were correct because he said so. He would just tell us to study more. He does
not even hand back exams and gives very broad feedback via gradescope. Plus exams make up most of our grade. Although he is very dedicated and explains things well.

Prof G's lectures are very good and you do not need to read any textbook to study or learn material for his exams (all MC). Weekly online quizzes to boost your grade + one midterm grade is dropped if you do bad. All lectures are recorded so attendance isn't required but being there definitely helps understanding. You can tell he cares about biology

I'd say he's pretty much okay. He does grade by a few things (3 midterms, final, and quizzes). Quizzes were easy but counted for a small percentage of your grade. As for the midterms, I suggest using his study guides he provides and rewatching his recorded lectures. One bad grade on the midterm can take a toll on your grade so beware and do well.
This class was really easy as long as you reviewed the slides before the tests. The tests were pretty much entirely based off the slides and if you knew those, the tests were easy. All mc tests.

Professor Grabiner was amazing at lecturing! The class was straightforward and based on assessments. The quizzes were online with multiple attempts, but the exams were in person and not very difficult at all. If you come to class, or watch the lectures on zoom, take notes, and do the study guides he provides you should be able to succeed.

He is a good professor, he is very lecture heavy, but you do not have to attend class because they are posted, yet it is recommended. I took him for BIO 1, but this course was the only option to write a review under. Overall, good class only thing that's frustrating is your grade is completely 10% take-home quizzes, 60% midterms, 30% final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved his class! He's a really good teacher and knows the material inside out. I took Genetics with him and thank God I had him and not one of the other professors. Attendance isn't mandatory since he records his lectures, but I recommend attending his lectures cause you can ask questions and he dressed up as a lamb for Halloween lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Worst Professor I've ever taken. Case studies are graded harshly, with unclear directions. Test questions have little to do with relevant content and are impossible to study for even if read the textbook. Thick Accent & Participation Matter. EC only helps participation. Lectures are super dry.
Prof Shan is really a good prof! Lecture is very easy to understand.

You can tell he really wants to be a good professor, always asking for feedback, listening to criticism and will adjust accordingly. He's really passionate about the subject, but since he's new to teaching lectures can be not the clearest sometimes. Get to know him, and you can tell how much he cares for his students. (Knowing Mandarin helps.)

Cons: harsh grader, (especially on case studies), difficult online exams (sometimes unclear, confusing, and with little time), accent heavy so it might hard to understand, mostly reading/explaining off from powerpoint with little class engagement.

Pros: caring profesor, open to feedback, willing to help students outside of class, knowledgable.

Professor has to be my favorite I have ever taken in Northeastern. He cares about all of his students and makes a effort to get to know all of us. His accent may be a little hard to understand but he is extremely accommodating and willing to help anyone. All the exams and quizzes are take home and there are two group projects.
Your parents pay $10,000 for an attendance code.
Would take again only if I need more material for my experimental noise album. Holy pretentious yapperoni and cheese.
This professor will use great opportunities to push his christian values on you. Held us captive via the attendance code until we got a prayer service bestowed on us by the Fellowship club.

Gutierrez is the most pretentious professors I've ever had. Majority of students take 1001 as a requirement, but Gutierrez expects everyone to be passionate about music. He uses a condescending tone and acts as though he is smarter than everyone else. The workload is heavy considering the course level. It's not super hard but very time consuming.

This class required me to do more homework than all of my other classes combined. The TAs take weeks to get back and a few more weeks to grade assignments. But an A- or above is very attainable, even if you put in the bare minimum effort. Find a better NU-path class. Take this only if you have to.
There is very little work for this class, and the professor is very engaging. I wish the class were smaller, but the content is interesting.

85% of the class takes this course to fulfill a NU-path, and I genuinely had more homework and projects for this class than my STEM requirements. Attendance is MANDATORY even though it is a massive lecture hall, and don't even get me started about the TAs.

I genuinely cannot stand this professor with all of my being. You know those people who become professors just to hear themselves talk? That's him. He thinks he's the next coming of christ and that he's the smartest person to ever exist. PAINFUL
The class is very interesting, easy and taught well, pretty much an easy A but the way its set up sucks. no contact with the teacher.

Professor doesn't grade assignments himself so your entire grade rests upon his TA's which are horrible and don't give constructive feedback and are unreachable. Insane given the amount of projects we have and don't receive feedback at all.
Free A for the MUSC1001 class. Midterm was open note, 17 MCQ. Doesnt mind you being on your laptop in class, and only takes attendance 1/3 of the time. Pretty much just show up and you will get an A

It is our third week, and we're already getting grades that we don't have feedback on. I got a 72% from a module assignment, and the TA is unresponsive. Most of us are not interested in or in love with music; we are mainly STEM majors trying to have ONE easy course and this professor is just being unnecessarily complicated, giving a heavy workload.
I have him right now and I already hate it. He is just one of those bad professors

Professor Gutierrez acknowledges that this is just a required course to fulfill NEU Path. However, the workload is the equivalent of high-level music major classes. The class itself isn't hard; it's just immensely time-consuming, which doesn't help if you're in a hard major like STEM. The grade breakdown is insane, with multiple projects.

I took this class asynchronously, but it was very work-intensive. There were many group discussions, and the projects were pretty time-consuming.  There is also no communication with prof, you can only contact the TA's which I thought was weird.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The material is easy and it would be more straightforward if all the articles weren't so pretentious and pseudo-sophisticated. The course flow is so confusing. Module 2 is due before module 1, module 4 (big project) is due before module 3. I don't know if it's purposeful or a mistake but it's so confusing to follow.

I took him summer 2, I didn't interact with him much but most of the assignments are easily although they get progressively more annoying as the semester goes on, but they are never terrible. He isn't too tough with grading either.

the class was okay i took it summer 2, definitely not just an easy a class but not difficult or anything, but this guy wrongly accused me of using ai and wouldn't believe any evidence i showed, not even edit history in the doc i wrote it in. him and the ta basically called me a liar and told me to learn to write better

Professor Gutierrez is hit or miss. He is a very nice guy but as a professor is extremely arrogant and speaks in a condescending tone with fancy language to make himself sound smarter. He is an easy grader though

I don't recommend Dr. Gutierrez. Everything is done by a TA, so there's zero personal connection. The rubrics aren't clear for grading. He'll ignore any emails for extensions. The TA also ignores any requests for help. MUSC 1001 is ok except for tedious projects. The grading is slow and feedback isn't given or its just bad. The TA polices diction.

Overall, easy A course. Weekly quizzes were not timed w/ 3 attempts. Assignments and discussion posts were fairly simple. There are 3 major assignments submitted through VoiceThread which is kinda of hard to navigate if you've never used it before. Everything graded by TA (so very opinion-based) with no feedback. Email responses from Prof are quick

There were many participation-based grades and weekly quizzes, all of which were simple but a lot of modules. There were a few major assignments- also not too bad, but he ended up putting some of these grades in the week final grades were due and doesn't add comments for why you got the grade you did. Working with VoiceThread is also a nightmare.

Says things like "superfluous" and "capricious" and "trepidation" just because he knows how to use those words, not because they actually add any sort of depth or specificity to his lectures... rolled my eyes a few times. How about making academia more accessible and inclusive by ensuring your lectures are something everybody can understand?

Do not take this class if you want to get an easy A or fulfill NUPath. The TA's grade the assignments and do not give any feedback, even if they take off a significant amount of points. Dr. Gutierrez is passionate but his lectures are long-winded and he will take attendance only when he feels like it. Choose a different class to fulfill electives.

This class would probably be a little more work than you'd expect, but definitely doable, and the online midterm and final are both very easy. I don't really get the hate this professor gets for "being pretentious" (?) He just seems like a good guy trying to give a good lecture. Nothing seemed pretentious to me.

Engaging lecturer who is clearly passionate about what he teaches. He teaches with a great depth of knowledge while still being entertaining. You can get a lot out of this class as long as you come in with an open mind

The pretentious professor made the class unbearable. The assignments, although they were very simple, were graded very harshly and with no feedback. He never submitted grades for multiple assignments and when this was brought to his attention, he reacted very defensively and put the blame back onto the student. Don't waste your time and money.

Prof. G is great! There are weekly async quizzes on the readings and class notes, but they're all very short and super easy. The class material is really interesting and it's clear that he's really invested in what he teaches. The course is good for anyone, regardless of prior music experience. He's really enthusiastic and it makes class very fun.

He is clearly passionate about music and knows the topics very well. However, he is very pretentious in his lectures and has an inflated ego. Content is easy, but if you aren't a music minor/major, can be a little harder. Also, not super clear in grading criteria. Easy content but annoying teacher.

Such an incredible professor and the content was always so engaging and interesting. Prof G is very smart + this class is so much fun! Projects are fun to complete and the exams are very doable. I highly recommend taking this class, you will not be disappointed and if you show up and pay attention, you will get an A.
Had a quiz, discussion, and assignment due every week. Quizzes, midterm, and final were all online and open book. Grading rubrics were provided, but not always clear.

Professor Gutierrez's class is organized by unchecked readings (he assigns an interesting and diverse curation of articles), weekly discussion posts, weekly open-note, untimed mini-quizzes, a few large projects, a midterm, and a non-cumulative final. He's thoughtful, passionate about class materials, and an engaging, qualified professor.
Really engaging class. The lectures are pretty interesting. You can tell he is passionate about what he teaches.
Professor Gutierrez is the best!!!!! His lectures are so interesting, and he is so knowledgeable and involved. Great man. great class.

The type of professor that uses big words to sound smart, but in reality is saying a bunch of nothing. Useless class that overanalyzes the minutia of things most people don't care about or will ever study again after this.

Overindulgent explanations on topics that are less than riveting. Tries WAY too hard to sound smarter than he is. Won't stop mentioning he lectures at Harvard. Just a lot for a 1000 level course imo...

I absolutely loved this class. Definitely take it with him if you are able to. Lectures were extremely interesting and he was clearly knowledgeable about every subject he taught. I would want to talk to him about music after class just to hear more about it. I am in love with this man.

Steve is a very entertaining professor. His class isn't too hard as long as you pay attention in lectures or do the readings. There are 3 tests usually, and they are multiple choice, then you have a poster project at the end of the semester. Would recommend his class, also you can find the textbook online for free so don't buy it.

First, please note that the score is inaccurate, as critical/negative reviews are immediately flagged and removed. The class itself was mostly fine; don't expect to get responses to emails or know your grade until the last week or so. Grades are arbitrary, so you'll want to rely on the multiple-choice exams (60% of your grade, 3 total).

super funny guy with lots of interesting personal stories (stories that actually connected to the lectures themselves). his exams are a little more difficult than expected, but at least they're all MCQ. great personality too, i just wish his presentations were a bit more bearable to look at. no cumulative final, and final project was graded fairly

Professor Steve explains concepts clearly and offers office hours to support students who struggle with exams. However, his stories can feel distracting, exams are harder than necessary, and he sometimes responds differently to students. I'm also uncomfortable that critical reviews appear to be removed. Don't let the score fool you.

Steve made the material really fun and engaging in his lectures. His grading criteria and grades felt fair, and I had a good idea of what grade I was going to get based off of the rubrics. He offered study guides to help us prepare for the tests which were really helpful.

Assignments from September graded on literally the last day of classes. Doesn't respond to emails half the time, also rude when he does respond. Grades are arbitrary and no feedback is provided. Unnecessary and strict conduct from this professor when it's a required class. Each class he goes over only like 5 slides. Waste of time, just talks a lot.

grades at the very end, test grades (3 tests, 60% of grade) graded faster, textbook easily found online but you don't rly need it for the 3 tests (use quizlet), tests are all 80 Qs, 4 mult choice: 50 easy, 20 "should study for", 10 specific ex. from class, attendance "optional" (he took it thrice lol), double dip gen ed but unnecessarily tedious

Steve is one of the only teachers I've had where I'm actually engaged in lectures. His lectures were the best! he made jokes and analogies so that everything was super easy to understand. He is super passive-aggressive, though, and was definitely on a power trip sometimes. He will call out students in front of 100 + people.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You NEED to prepare well for the exams. Easy class if you put in the work. His teaching was engaging & not too boring, I respect. He sometimes includes the story he tells in the exams. He is a 4/5 because he's quite passive-aggressive, which is very off-putting, but he's chill I guess. He also doesn't grade anything until the very end.

He didn't respond to a SINGLE one of my emails. For the final group project, one of my group members stopped responding. You'd think professor would respond to emails when the class is asynch. No. He ignored me and gave me a unsatisfactory grade. I've emailed professor 3 times and he responded to none of them.
He was a good professor and had interesting lectures. Fair grader.

The class was pretty easy. As long as you attend class the tests aren't hard. Professor has kind of a rude sense of humor that could be off-putting, but he clearly tries to make class engaging. He will definitely call you out in front of everyone for talking or being off task.

I took this class thinking it was easy A but I was wrong. I am not good at memorization and this whole class is memorization based. I will warn as well that the tests have questions that are very specific to examples given in class, so if you are not in that class you are screwed for that question. the teacher is entertaining but u get bored.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Steve's lectures are amazing and so engaging and I learned so much! It's a huge class so there's no professor-student engagement at all, but it's fine if you sit with friends in class. Very little actual work with a few easy assignments (make sure not to do them late!) but then the exams are very important!

Class itself is pretty easy as long as you memorize definitions. You need to get at least a 94 for an A (he doesn't round) and tests are long and worth a lot of your grade. Steve is very charismatic and his class covers two NUpaths so overall I recommend.

I had Steve last term and loved his teaching style. I thought his personal anecdotes helped me retain the course content easily. He outlines what is going to be on the test so making a quizlet and studying it well is what I suggest to get a good grade. Yes, he grades down to the wire, but I wasn't too pressed!

Had him for COMM1101 and was miserable because of how annoying he was, but took him this semester and I truly think he's more tolerable in smaller lectures. I surprisingly really enjoyed his lectures and he made it fun to listen to (which I would have never said last sem). Lets class out early, take home exams, but he still grades off no rubric.

He was a funny guy, and his class was very interesting, but he can seem stand off is at times. I did not like the way that he spoke to some of the students during his lectures, he seemed like he was annyoed at times. He also takes forever to grade work. I still don't know my grade for his class. His TAs are also rude, but that's a longer story.

Steve is one of the best professors I have had. He makes all of the lectures interesting and even though it's not required to go, I would still show up just because he made them interesting. The tests are multiple-choice and require some studying but they are not hard. He is a great guy and easy to access outside of class. All his notes are online.
great prof, makes the content really relatable and understandable and is very entertaining

Always a good time in Steve's class, looked forward to going to his class. He made all his concepts into a story which made his tests much easier. One large group project, 3 test, and an couple hw assessment. Very manageable.

I had Professor Granelli for asynchronous COMM1101. It was the WORST class I have ever taken. He did not lay out specific guidelines for what needed to be completed and graded harshly on rubrics that were not posted. Unrealistic expectations. 
Exams made up 60% of our grade and the questions asked were so specific it was impossible to memorize.

If you're just looking to fulfill an NUpath requirement like I was, look elsewhere. As require a 94%, and tests are a game of endurance at 100 questions each. Content itself and assignments are interesting enough. Engagement with the lectures/textbook is forced because exam questions will be taken word for word from specific lectures or readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very funny, uses personal experience to help teach the material, expectations were very clear and he was very approachable

Steve was SO fun! Definitely one of my most engaging professors as he always had funny stories to tell in class that directly went with the material we were learning. I chose to go to every class but if you just looked at his powerpoints and read the textbook you didn't really need to show up.

I love Steve! His examples and the way he can reillustrate the same concept in different ways makes it so the content really sticks -- you onlyy really need to review for exams if you pay attention in class. He makes that easy by being entertaining too. Can be "adult" I guess but nothing like you wouldn't experience in real life. Fun chats too

He is funny and his lectures were entertaining, but the examples he used from his personal life made him look very bad. Definitely had an attitude, but was usually nice one-on-one. Not a difficult class, if you do the work and study a few hours for each test it is an easy A.

Steve is not my favorite professor but he's not that bad. He can be funny but definitely a little rude sometimes if you don't enjoy bluntness. The class is all about the slides and a poster project at the end and his other  assignments are pretty easy. If you just study for a few hours for each test and try on the poster project it's an easy A.

Amazing professor. Entertaining lectures. Class is about leadership and teamwork. Content is very basic (you will not learn a single insightful thing all semester, it's all obvious observations about how groups function). Your grade is mostly made up of group projects and two exams (super easy if you study for a few hours the night before).

I barely went to lectures, but they were entertaining when I did go. You can look over the vocab in the textbook and the slideshows on Canvas before a test and you'll be fine. The grade comes from three exams and a group project. There are also a couple of assignments that aren't worth as much.

Really easy class if you just look at his lecture slides the day before the exams. Talks about himself and his stories he thinks are funny (they're not). Had like 6 TAs who managed to do nothing because nothing was graded til the day before grades were due. Even tho he had a rubric, he did not follow it/it wasn't specific.

I LOVED this class. It's a big lecture class, so it's easy to just not pay attention/ skip, but his lectures are worth going to because he makes them interesting and mostly story based. If all you want is to get the material and leave, you will hate this class, but if you want to enjoy material this is the one for you. great intro to comm.

Live laugh love Steve. Best professor ever. Lectures are material heavy but he is so entertaining and tells us so many stories. Very little homework. Tests are straightforward and pretty reasonable. Project was super fun and a great time passer. Would take his classes over and over if possible.
This class isn't hard but the professor is, he don't even be grading, like do your job.

Felt like a comedy show because hes so funny!! His stories made it easy to remember certain things on the tests. Please take. Best professor Ive had yet. AND I also learned things. The tests are very easy.
Good professor. Has long online lectures tho. Lots of opportunity through homework, exams, and projects to get a good grade. Pretty easy course, would recommend.

This class is entirely based on popular culture. If you wish to learn ANYTHING about communication competence in any form that is not related to pop-culture, stay FAR AWAY from this class. Also, the professor is ridiculously nitpicky and will not follow the grading rubric at all, so good luck guessing what he wants out of you.

Interesting Class! The class has 3 tests out of 200 points and a big group project in terms of big assignments. Tests are manageable he gives you a study guide w/ everything on it. You have to read a good amount of the textbook to understand the concepts and do well on tests. He also includes video lectures. Funny and fair professor overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class is fairly easy if you stay on top of your notes and watch the lectures. Your final grade is mostly dependent on the 3 tests he gives, so make sure you study. Tests are easy if you memorize what he puts on the study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor ever! He has great character and a sense of humor beyond compare. Prepare for intense belly laughing in every lecture. Absolute gem!

I really had no connection to him and felt like he basically turned everything into something about himself - the stories were sometimes funny, but mostly just things no one really cared about. He makes small things difficult just because he can.

The content is nothing special, I feel like I did learn something, but was annoyed in the process.

found the textbook online, and its not bad found myself accidentally reading it when assigned but even then its not necessary, read the slideshows see what concepts he left out (he has a slideshow dedicated to it) and then read that portion, fill out the study guide and its an easy A. I found that it feels like common sense + attend class

Prof Granelli is probably one of the most entertaining lecturers you'll encounter at Northeastern. People saying his grading is too tough are a bit ridiculous. Go to class, read the textbook, treat this class like any other class and you'll be fine. People think that because he's funny he's easy-going. He's not, but he's fair.
Best professor ever. You will have fun and love the subject after taking this class with him. Must take for any COMM class.

Take him if you want an EASY A!! 3 non cumulative tests that are just MCQ's and if you go through his slides you will definitely get an A. He is funny too and gives tons of extra credit. However the class is really huge but it can be an advantage as he rarely ever takes attendance.

Essentially, if you show up every once in a while and then memorize the slideshows you will get an easy A in the class. I loved going to class every day because of how engaging Steve is but, at the same time, I don't feel like I've left the class with bounds of new knowledge. Truly just an intro class but fun nonetheless.

It's a big class, expect to not get emails read, so go up to him in person. I would rather have him as a prof for a small class than a big one, because he's a prof I would genuinely want. The tests are ok as long as you study enough. BE PREPARED TO STUDY. He's funny too and as a person he's genuinely a fun and nice guy.

Steve is such a funny, inspirational professor who is able to effectively introduce students to the various concepts within communication. He does a great job of incorporating his real-life situations into the concepts in class. I was always engaged in class and never felt like it was a chore to show up. The class is overall fairly easy and great.

Since it is a large class it is only lectures. It gets tedious but Steve does his best to keep lectures interesting with personal stories as examples. Grading is fair and the 3 exams are 80 multiple choice questions that require memorization and concept application. Steve is a great person and really helpful if you meet with him IN PERSON.
Awesome professor.

Granelli gave no feedback on any assignments and did not give access to view what questions we got wrong on exams. Therefore, I felt that this class was not worth money and self study of communications would have been just as useful. 

Pro tip: download lecture slides instead of watching the videos & use the quizlets someone made to study.
Amazing!! Super engaging and informative. Very clear and fair grading, and lectures are very interesting. Amazing guy and teacher, could not recommend more highly

Professor is great at presenting and teach material but getting an A in this course is a bit unattainable due to the grading scale. Grading was quite harsh for an intro class and very specific on detail. There were quite a lot of things to do per week but the grade is heavily skewed to just the exams and group project. :/
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class content was very easy as long as you take good notes on the lectures. Personally, I found some of the questions on the test annoying as they were asking for minor details. Workload is not too heavy, but grading was harsher than expected. Overall, it will take more time than you expect but very easy content.
you won't regret taking his class, Steve makes learning actually fun. I would recommend his intro to comm class super easy, super fun. Easy A too.

Professor Granelli is one of the most entertaining professors I've had. He is very funny and his tests are clear if you have the textbook and kind of pay attention during class you will do well. Although I did not continue studying comm, I do still think about his class.

Took steve's class this past fall, one of the few classes i had I really looked forward to. while lectures weren't mandatory, they definitely helped improve your understanding of important concepts. He's also just fricking hilarious to listen to. Really appreciated the extra credit opportunities. seriously there were 6 in total.

COMM 1101 with Steve is great! There were 3 exams and a final project with a few assignments in between. Definitely worth taking if you are interested in Communications, it was an awesome starting point. Steve makes his lectures really interesting with real-life examples, cannot recommend this class enough!

Steve is an overall nice professor, but he doesn't respond to his emails, at least in a timely fashion. This has given me a lot of anxiety when it comes to certain things and I really wish he was more accessible outside of class. He is nice and funny though, just not my favorite.
He is funny and easy going. Seems like a very chill guy and doesnt give too much work at all

I didn't really have any sort of connection with Steve, and I was tuned out for most of the lectures. No feedback given on assignments, but the class is huge so I'm not mad. Overall, the course was super easy.

Steve is a great professor who uses fun examples and really cares about what he does. He's structured the class in a really clear and helpful way. There's one group project at the end of the semester and three exams but you'll be well-prepared if you pay attention. He's a chill guy who will answer any questions in-depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Did not grade anything until the last moment. So I had no idea I was doing the assignments inadequately until all of them were submitted and grades were due for him. To this day I still don't know what I did wrong on them because he did not submit anything to show what I did wrong. He just gave me failing grades on them all.

If you have the chance, absolutely take Steve's class. Lectures are entertaining and hilarious and have a lot of knowledge packed inside his insane stories. If you're having a bad day, sit in the back of his COMM1101 lecture and you'll leave in a much better mood then you entered in.
Took the Summer 2 class. Steve is funny, makes the content more interesting than it is and the tests are really not hard. 5/5
Great prof but he is too boring . talks non stop and becomes irritating after a while . this class is an easy A with this chap

Steve is an amazing professor and integrates communication curriculum with storytelling, which always made me excited to attend class. However, this class is big in size, so when group projects come along, make sure you have friends to work with. Otherwise, definitely take Steve for this class, ESPECIALLY if you're a NON-MAJOR

Your'e doing yourself a disservice if you don't take Steve. Great guy who makes lectures super, super interesting and funny. So far, he's been my favorite teacher here even though it was an entry level class. Class is graded from in class assignments and 3 tests that are based off of lectures. Sign in sheet to check attendance.

Steve is by far the best professor I have had so far at Northeastern. I took his Comm1101 class and he is captivating in class, is extremely funny and does a great job at teaching his subject. He has a high emphasis on attendance so don't skip class unless you absolutely have to (we only got 6 absences before a failure this semester).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Public Speaking with him, he's great. He makes you feel comfortable even if you have bad stage fright like I did. He'll make you laugh every class and takes the time to talk to each student and actually cares about how you're progressing. It's a great class and the way he teaches it makes it all the better!

Awesome! Funny, entertaining and straightforward. One of the best I've ever had. Take this class, you're guaranteed to love it. You get 4 unexcused absences and after that he drops a letter grade, he gives you review questions for exams that are actual questions in the exam.

Actually the best professor I have had at northeastern, he is engaging and really just wants you to do well. You have to come to class but he will make sure you want to. I did not do well on the final which is why my grade isn't higher but I am awful at even the simplest multiple choice.

He is a really funny professor and makes the content easy to remember because he tells personal stories to link to concepts. If you miss the lecture, you wont fall behind that much with the content, but your grades might take a hit- so try not to miss his class more than you have to. Also so many extra credit events so its really no stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: An amazing professor who makes the dry material interesting. His lectures are hilarious and engaging. The best professor I've had so far.

Professor Steve is an excellent professor. He knows his stuff and tells the best and funniest stories ever! He will offer 25 extra credit added to the overall grade. Also, the extra credit can be used to erase one absence (you're only allowed to have 4 unexcused absences on his class) if you have more than that, you're grade will be affected....

Steve is one the best professors I had. If I will ever have a chance to take a class with him, I definitely will! He makes the concept easy to understand and adds his jokes and experience of life. Honestly, if you have a chance to take this class, take it without questions!

He makes class extremely interesting and the class is lecture-based, so it's easy. You have a group project and many extra credit opportunities, so this class should be easy to pass if you try just a little bit. Steve makes the content seem vibrant, even though it's actually super dry.

Steve is such an awesome teacher! His stories are hilarious but always relate to the concepts we're learning and help keep us engaged. You don't really need the textbook so save your money. There are a ton of extra credit opportunities and you can miss class 5 times before it starts affecting your grade. Take his classes!

steve granelli is the best thing to happen to this world. He is a passionate, hilarious, and wildly intelligent professor. He taught my intro to comm class and it will remain my most favorite class i've ever taken. He tells stories that relate to the material and genuinely cares for his students and the subject. 100% take anything he teaches.

Steve is an amazing professor! The material is very easy and straightforward and he's absolutely hilarious! Attendance is taken every class so as long as you show up, pay a reasonable amount of attention, and study for the tests, you'll be completely fine. I loved his class and definitely recommend him as a professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a fantastic professor, if you have the chance to take one of his classes 11/10 recommend it. I swear he could make any class enjoyable, he doesn't disappoint. He also really respects his students which is very refreshing.

Steve is a fantastic professor, probably my favorite I've had in college so far. Attendance is mandatory, but his lectures are so good you'll want to go to class. He uses a lot of humor and personal examples in his lectures, and manages to make you learn a lot of information without even realizing you're learning. I highly recommend him to anyone.
Super respectful and incredibly considerate. Patient and provides a significant amount of preparation and review for exams. Most enjoyable math class I have ever taken!

Evil human being, any other professor would be better. Can't teach the subject at all and is rude to her students. She treats the course like a review even tho most in the class have never taken the class. Very hard grader as well.
Bad professor. Can not explain concepts to undergraduate students. Take anyone else, help your self in the long run.

Just a bad teacher. She is terrible at getting students to understand material and overall is rude. Also her office hours are online only and seems to get mad that you show up to ask questions. I retook the course with a different professor and got a B-. take it with ANY OTHER professor if possible.

Your Grade comes down to two tests and a final. Lectures are rushed and don't always align with the quizzes. Will grade harshly and sometimes incorrectly. Try to avoid her, but if you must take her, start studying early. Go over your graded test to. She knows her stuff but lacks the ability to teach that knowledge to others.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough grader but its a fair process. She wants you to do well and even though there are a lot of quizzes she drops so many of them that you get many chances to do well. Practice tests and quizzes are helpful. She wants you to do well and is very nice. Yes you do have to study, its a math class.

(I actually took math1213 with her but that's not an option on the drop-down) Reading reviews of other students, it sounds nothing like my experience in her class. She was very kind and patient when you struggled with concepts, and is a great explainer. Her tests are copy-and pastes of the study guides just with different numbers, so very easy.

first half of sem was so easy, then all of a sudden went completely downhill. practice quizzes became nothing like the actual quizzes, went from 100% to 50%. i am relatively good at math, and i actually like calc, and i show up to all lectures. she makes soooooo many mistakes especially on test reviews so its difficult to actually learn

Her lectures are kinda easy to follow during the 1st QUARTER of the semester but she oversimplifies things that dont need to be simplified. She only takes the highest 5 quizzes, but she grades harshly. her lecture and hw questions arent overwhelmingly hard, but it doesnt prepare you for quizzes. Its not worth taking her class.

Literally the worst teacher I have ever had. She is extremely condescending and isn't helpful outside of class. She treats this course like a review course for engineers alone, so if you haven't taken the class before do not take her. I did so much tutoring but still couldn't keep up because of quizzes included topics barely touched in class. Awful
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Where do I even begin, If you do not have a very strong foundation of calculus before this course DO NOT take it with Professor Gibbins. The quizzes and exams within this course do not match the difficulty of her lectures at all, they are extremely hard! She grades very hard as well with barely any partial credit. 0/10! Trust me!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I failed calc w another professor and idk why Gibbins has such bad reviews!! It's like night and day, she is so much nicer and her style is great for visual and auditory learners. Ppl may find her rude but she just has a dry sense of humor and can be sarcastic. That aside, you can tell she really cares and goes out of her way to provide extra help
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gibbins is good, though there are daily quizzes, low grades dropped. They aren't hard but need to pay attention in class. I LOVED that she gave practice exams that were EXACTLY what to expect for the actual test (not the same questions, but the same format/types of questions). Good at calc? take her you will do great. She is a fair grader!
She is really really bad. She should not be a teacher, she is very rude and gets mad when you dont understand. Shes very condesending.

She is a great professor in my mind, does homework session every night so you could ask her questions constantly. She does make mistakes in class sometimes and I see the test averages are horrible. So if you know what you are doing with your math, you can choose her since she gives out help. But if you are bad at math, not her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The worst teacher I've ever had. Constantly makes mistakes in class and in exam reviews. I gave up on using her solutions to study due to the sheer amount of basic arithmetic errors. The average grade for her second midterm was a 61, and the first was barely a 70. She offers no curve and always responds with slight attitude. Do NOT take her class.

no homework,  pop quizzes (drops your lowest quiz every 4 quizzes) 2 exams + final. hard to access outside of class, few office hours. does problems as examples and the practice exams are like the real exams. definitely dont take her if you have no calculus experience, but if u pay attention and do the practice problems u should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I went in with no calc experience terrified, but landed a B. Her lectures are DENSE but she outlined each step clearly, plus lots of examples to practice.

4/5 bc you only get points from tests, plus she made a few mistakes in class that if not pointed out by students, would leave us with incorrect answers to study from. Overall, great!

Not sure why so many low ratings, maybe she improved as a professor. She does do a lot of example problems so if that's how you learn take her class, if not I suggest a different professor. She is very understanding and cares about her students.

Very fast paced lectures and made mistakes everyday. Expected things said once to be memorized by the next day. Quizzes were always either very fair or insanely hard with no in between. She also always has a slight attitude and it feels like she thinks her students are dumb. The one good thing I will say is that a lot of partial credit was given.

Just sort of did examples every class. The quizzes and tests are a lot harder than what she did in class, and little was explained. The rare times a review sheet was made helped, but it didn't really make up for not learning it in the first place. Little partial credit for us even though she always messed up the examples in class too.

Thank goodness I took some calculus in high school. While some of her lectures are pretty understanding, some aren't and whats worse is the test are more difficult and advanced that I never seen in any calculus course. While I did enjoyed some of her puns, the course would be very difficult if you come in with very little experience in calculus.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly, cannot even believe she is a professor. Sometimes you learn stuff that she says we wont get tested on. Why are we learning it then? Her exams take forever to do and are 10x harder than what we learn, and she wonders why people dont do well. My tutor explained things much better than her. Pick any other Prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Gibbins has been the worst professor I have ever had. The class consisted of poor lesson planning, useless homework and unnecessarily hard problems. Exams were very hard and often contained lessons we weren't quizzed on. Her lectures proved to be inadequate for the final. Dumpster fire of a class brought on by pure laziness. AVOID AT ALL COST

Prof Gibbins obviously cares about math and students, but her teaching style did not work with me at all. Ive struggled with calc in the past, but Gibbins teaching just made me more confused. Additionally, so much unnecessary hw, only two exams + final (exams that were much harder than anything we did in class), and hardly any partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably the worst teacher I have ever had. When Prof Gibbins teaches, she makes so many mistakes and often asks the students if what shes doing is correct. Her quizzes and exams are more difficult than what you do in class, she gives minimal and confusing feedback and grades so harshly. Shes a sweet person, but she really should not be teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not the best professor I had, to sum it up, you will have to do tons of unnecessary work. The homework for me averaged from 50 to 70 problems a week. Combined with poorly explained material, this makes the subject very difficult, as half of the problems are not explained in class. The tests are also very hard, so my advice: pick another professor

Aliska genuinely wants you to learn. She takes your best quiz scores, and drops the rest, with ample room for extra credit. She also has an excellent sense of humor and writes on her iPad, which makes reading her notes super helpful. Everything is very digital, which makes things painless, and the practices closely resemble the real deal for exams.
Best summed up in one word: Yikes.

The single worst professor I have ever had. She doesn't know how to explain anything, and fails to engage with her students at all. She gives out an unnecessary amount of classwork and homework, half of which the material she doesn't go over in class. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS IF YOU HAVE THE CHOICE!

Worst professor I've ever had. She puts questions on the quizzes and tests that are WAY harder and longer than the homework problems, and she doesn't even respond to emails. She has no energy and always sounds like she doesn't wanna be there when she's giving lectures. Doesn't give a lot of partial credit or feedback either.

Worst teacher you can have. If these reviews aren't enough she is the same Aliska Gibbins that comes up for Florida Institute of Technology and got away by making a second account. Take ANY OTHER professor. She does not care about her students and made my life a living hell while in her class. She does not respond to emails either. I can counite...

The professor is decent. She teaches clearly and follows the syllabus. She is really good at preparing students for exams (she makes practice tests & questions). Sometimes she doesn't explain fully. I would recommend her if you have taken calculus before/are good at calculus. She teaches mostly by showing lots of examples.

Gibbins was the worst teacher that I've ever had. Her lectures consisted of doing problems on the board using new material without explanations. She expected you to learn on your own but the textbook provided was not helpful. She is a very tough grader and partial credit is almost non existant. Absolutely would not take again.

Great professor. Clear about the syllabus and what is necessary to know for the tests. Posts all her notes online. Really good about leaving time for students to ask questions and explaining when students don't understand. Available outside of class. She is great at preparing us for tests and making sure we all get good grades. Highly recommend.

Zero clarity in what we were doing and on how to solve problems. She just sat in her wheelchair on her iPad, at least her dog was cute. She did give credit for hw but the tests were roughhh. Avoid at all costs especially if you didn't take BC calc in high school.

Its never clear what you're supposed to be learning. Just teach yourself everything from the textbook and the internet and use class for examples and practice. She never explains what shes doing in class. Its an easy grade if you know what you're doing but if you're learning the info for the first time its very hard to actually learn anything.

This guy is extremely difficult, if you have the option to avoid his class, I would. He spends most of his time discussing his history with general electric and osramslovania along with his kids accomplishments. He rarely responds to emails, gaslights any confrontation of an error, and doesn't teach or care about how his students are doing. Avoid!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I wish I could take an exam on his life because he talks about it for 80% of the class time. Very picky about how he wants things done, specifically with the Excel assignments. The subject itself is not difficult at all compared to financial accounting. The exams are relatively easy and straightforward.

Easy A, the hardest part is sitting through class. He's a chill guy but just talks SO much. I somehow made it to every single class and we usually got out early, he's a caring and good guy, but doesn't know his audience. Must but Mcgraw hill. Almost all serious due dates were flexible. Final exam study guide didn't really help.

super easy class but such a boring professor. if you can drag yourself out of bed and sit through his life stories to get the attendance points, it's the easiest accounting class you'll ever take. beware that all assignments are on mcgraw hill, so you'll need to pay for that. but otherwise such an easy class

The practice tests and study guides helped a lot. Got sick once, emailed him about it, he ignored it, and dropped my attendance grade even though I literally couldn't get out of bed. Honestly talks more about his life than accounting. I basically know his whole life story that I didn't ask for, because he tends to ramble a lot during classes.

Professor Glencross truly loves accounting and cares about his students. He tells you what to study to help prepare for exams, is pretty understanding, and is available outside of class. The cons are that his class sometimes lacks engagement, and he doesn't provide many extra resources/practice questions other than the textbook and slides.

He was a super chill professor and was pretty flexible when things came up for students. He moved a midterm and was super accommodating for students that had already made plans. His lectures felt a little long sometimes, but he's a nice guy and I learned a lot in his class.

He is a very nice guy but his lectures don't really help with exams. For quizzes he does let you know what's going to be on it which is helpful. The average for the last quiz was so bad that he had to drop it the average was around 40%. Overall, he is a nice guy but not a good professor.

Professor Glencross is passionate about accounting and loves to talk about his work experience/life advice. Weekly assignments and group project are easy good grades. He tells you questions on every exam (including final), but lots of the material is self taught and many test questions are not straight forward. Lots of work put in outside class.
absolutely terrible. he does not know how to teach and thinks his students care about his family's accomplishment. i dont care! can u pls teach

I don't see why glencross doesn't have a higher rating on here. For all quizzes/exams he tells you exactly what to study for each question, minimizing study time. Weekly homeworks aren't hard. Gives out bonus points throughout the semester for the final. Lectures get repetitive but he's j a sweet old man. J show up to class & study what he says

This professor is mean forget about sick days or even wellness days if your not there even one time your grade will go down. The homework is honestly not bad but the test and quizzes were difficult. Overall not the hardest class ever if you are willing to put the work in but he was just not a good professor.

Glencross is boring and talks so much without any of the information he says being important.He doesn't even review the slides he's presenting before class, and spends more time talking about his son's accomplishments than accounting.I survived his class by self studying everything before the test.Don't take this class if your goal is to stay awake

Not a hard professor, but does repeat the same personal anecdotes over and over again throughout the year. He's passionate about what he teaches, but doesn't know how to structure his lectures very well. Relies heavily on the slides and usually ends up repeating them back to you, so just take notes on what is posted online and you'll be fine.

He is a very nice guy, but does not know how to teach. He spends the entire class telling personal anecdotes and attempts to connect them to the lecture but it does not work. He repeats the same stories over and over all semester and barely teaches you how to do the actual material.

Glencross may be a bit eccentric in his lectures, but he gets the point across. For each of the exams, he provides a study guide as well as goes through the content that will be covered. This was extremely helpful in preparing for exams. He hosts office hours 3-4 times per week, and you can always get your questions answered. Definitely take him!

Yes, his lectures are not super engaging, but he gives out GREAT study guides (basically the exam). He does not deserve a 2.8 rating. He is pretty boring, but you will learn a decent amount and get a good grade. Take this class for an A. It's accounting, no professor's lectures are interesting.
