No comment.

This was my second time taking Financial Accounting. he is WHY I PASSED! Thank you so much Dr. Glencross... He taught so well and easy to understand. He didn't move on until everyone got it and he kept lectures interesting. Great guy.

His lectures are boring at times, and he does talk about his personal life stories a lot. His class isn't difficult if you put in some slight work though, and he's an extremely fair grader who really does want to help his students out.

Dr. Glencross is my fav prof. The last few reviews had to be written by the same dude... He relays life stories and talks about his personal life, without fail. But it did not take up a majority of classes. We spent most time clarifying back and forth with the Prof. He wouldn't move on unless we got it. Will tell you what's on the exams!

Avoid Professor Glencross's financial accounting class at all costs. His teaching is appalling, with nearly all discussions focused on his USELESS "life stories" &  achievements rather than the actual course. The class's performance throughout the semester was abysmal.

AVOID Professor Glencross's financial accounting class. He's a poor teacher, focusing mainly on his son's achievements, not the actual course material. The class final average was a dismal 67, with some test exam scores as low as a paltry 37. I got a C+ in the class, my lowest Northeastern grade. Professor Glencross should be fired immediately.

DO NOT RECOMMEND!!! worst accounting class ever. going to class felt pointless, never taught during lectures, only shared life stories (the same ones throughout the whole semester). felt extremely unprepared for the final had to teach myself. northeastern needs to get rid of this guy.. HE CAN'T TEACH!!!  and i never wanna look at accounting again.

Lectures consist of 60% monotonic speaking, 20% completely irrelevant, gibberish personal stories (such as how his son got a job [nobody cares dude]), and 10% pithy life lessons that can be deduced by a middle schooler. The best thing Northeastern can do is fire this guy as he is doing a disservice to his students.

I took his ACCT1201 class. The guy is a former shoe salesman (so he has said), which should tell you all you need to know. He's a nice guy (sometimes) but teaching is not about being nice, it's about educating your students. At that he is a complete failure.

Professor Glencross was a terrible professor and I'm so glad I will never have to take his class again. Super boring and the material is very tedious. This class is made worse due to the fact that everything we learned how to do is now done on a computer so the material is outdated. I hated this class and prof Glencross is not a good teacher at all

Lots of stories but always cover what we have to! Most application learning can only be done through homework anyways. Spoon-feeds exam content as much as possible and provides so much information on grades and expectations. Lectures are fine, it's a boring subject but he makes it enjoyable! Won't move on until you get it. Very sensible and sweet!

Prof. Glencross does care about his student's success, but he simply reads his slides instead of explaining what the slide is trying to convey. He brings up examples from his own days as an accountant that lead to other tangents about his own experiences instead of the concepts we need to learn. Learn by doing the homework and textbook problems.

Prof Glencross is one of my favorite prods. a sweet man with the best of intentions for his students. you can tell he wants us to learn, not just from the textbook/lectures, but also from his experiences. he strays from the class material, but the only way to really grasp accounting is by practicing anyway. plus keeps us awake from boring material!

Glencross is nice but his lectures are about 60% him talking about his career in accounting, 30% him telling a story he told last class but forgot, and 10% teaching the material. His tests are quite easy throughout but the final is made by the department head and you will know nothing because of his non teaching style. Prepare to teach yourself.

He is a very nice and organized professor who cares about his field and the material he teaches. Sometimes he can go off on tangents, but his stories are entertaining and we always remain well on schedule. He hopes that we all become future accountants.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Glencross is very caring and easy to talk to. I always felt comfortable in his class and he always wanted the best for his students. Lectures can be boring and the class requires a lot of studying but having him as a professor made the class more enjoyable. He is super nice and respects his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor does not teach very effectively. Class time wasn't very efficient as he tended to read off his presentation slides and repeat the same stories of his life as an accountant. He seems very knowledgeable about accounting but is not great at teaching the material. I learned more from self-studying on Youtube than from his lectures.

He doesn't really teach you how to do the actual maths in accounting but is more focused on theory so you'll have to teach yourself. He also tends to go off-topic by repeatedly talking about his experiences. However, he is very kind and wants his students to pass. There is a lot of homework but it is very helpful when it comes to exams.

ACCT 6200 - He's just great. I want to retake his class just for the stories about Sylvania, GE, and his current AP consulting project - hilarious. Do the HW.. He's extremely reasonable and he wants his students to succeed in understanding the way financial statements flow - he's not interested in making you memorize useless accounting jargon.

Prof Glencross is definitely a little old school but he's very kind. He makes his own study guides so the exams were very doable and the homework's easy. Tells a lot of personal stories but still covers everything he needs to in lecture. He made accounting bearable.

The guy is super outdated in every aspect in his life. Incredibly boring and inapplicable, goes on about the same stories from his life over and over again. Homework is alright, but will not curve any grades. We had a 60% mean for an exam and he just does not care if it is hard or not.
Nice guy but assigns A TON of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Really nice guy but he spends entire class telling stories of his experiences. Long winded stories that are somewhat relevant only because he was an accountant. Heavy use of power point, each slide he would tell a story. I had to do a lot of learning on my own because we couldn't get to relevant material. Not necessarily a tough teacher though
Because, He explains the topic with the examples which is easily understandable and also he is very much friendly
Super easy grader, but he has no idea what he's talking about. Drones on and on about his work experience, which is almost entirely unrelated to the subject matter.

took cost accounting with Mr. Glencross.  he relies on power point a lot, but did an overall fair job compared to others at NEU who use power-point as a brain substitute.   you can tell he enjoys teaching and is not just coming to class to earn his tenure.  if he lectured he'd have been that much better because i think he really knows his stuff.

The professor has a strong materials background. However, this course is quite intensive, covering a broad range of topics including atomic structure, electron configuration, crystalline lattice, miller index, defects, phase diagram, phase transformations, diffusion, polymers, mechanical properties, and strengthening mechanisms. Not an easy course

Her class is pretty intense. I'd recommend it if you really want to learn, but if you're not very interested in research or science, it may not be the best fit. She is a responsible and hardworking professor and sets high standards, especially in research.

I learned so much from Prof Zhu in MATL6280. The course content was vast. There were topics that were more difficult; she gave great attention to those topics for students to cement concepts. The lectures were long but definitely all necessary for a deep understanding of the content. Performing well on the final presentation is a must for an A!

I learned a lot about battery materials, how battery works, and how they're manufactured. This course truly changed my future career plans. I'm very confident I can pursue battery companies after this course.
She is very knowledgeable, and I learned a lot in the class.
I got 94 in the final. She always responds to emails promptly. I learnt a lot in this class. It inspires me to pursue a career in Materials in the future.

I took her class and scored 97 out of 100 on Midterm 1 and 91 out of 100 on Midterm 2. Her class is well organized. However, this course includes many concepts, terminologies, and calculations, so it does require additional efforts to read textbook outside of class. I personally have no difficulty understanding her lectures. Just my experiences.
It is hard to understand the professor. She will help when asked questions but the explanations are difficult to understand as well

I'm in Professor Zhu's Materials class this semester. This Thursday, when I asked her about my Midterm 1, surprisingly, she know every single number-even the exponents-at every step of the solution! Then when I saw her notes, I realized-she had worked through every single step of the exam questions herself step by step in every single number.

When I asked her questions, she always provided detailed, step by step explanations. A responsible professor. However, she seems not in industrial engineering. I'm quite surprised a professor in another field was assigned to teach this senior IE core course.

I took her class in spring 2020, during the hit of COVID 19 pandemic. While many classes faced challenges during that time, her classes always ran smoothly. She was consistently punctual and never missed a class due to COVID. Well, she had an accent. But I'm from Texas myself. I'm proud of my Texas accent. This is where I'm from. How can we blame?

I had the opportunity to work with Prof. Zhu for two semesters in IE4530-first as a student in her class and later as TA. During my time as her student in the Fall 2025, I was truly impressed by her dedication. Despite being 9 months pregnant, she stood and lectured for 100 minutes without any complain or excuses. This left lasting memory.

I'm in her ME2340 this semester. Based on my experience, Professor Zhu is approachable, smart, and passionate about the class. Her slides are well organized. She come to class with sufficient preparation. When I ask her question, she always response with patience and clarity. Meanwhile, she encourage us  to her office hour. She is responsible.
Worst college Professor EVER. Never take her class or work with her. Beware Bad Experience.
His voice makes you sleepy in class. He's always immersed in his own world, you cannot not learn anything from him in class.

Very cool prof! If you want a deep understanding of the mathematical side of Machine Learning, take his class. He focuses heavily on the theoretical aspects, which is rare and valuable. Despite the rigor, he is extremely understanding and patient and is always willing to go the extra mile to explain things during office hours.
Sometimes he UNSURE of what hes trying to say. Poor communication skills.

had him for cs4100 but that wasnt an option. Freest A of my life. Midterm was takehome, attendance wasn't mandatory, and homework assignments had so much starter code I was basically just uncommenting lines and submitting. Learned absolutely nothing though.
He is a highly approachable professor with a wealth of knowledge. As long as you complete the homework and put effort into a strong final project, achieving a high grade is very manageable!

This course covers conventional machine learning materials. I have taken cs6140 under another professor, which actually covered similar topics compared to this course. But that one is more profound and interesting, I guess it's due to the teaching style. This course could be more solid and easy-to-understand for whom just got into this area
Course itself is great, I have learnt quite a lot. However, I wouldn't recommend the professor to take his session on. He is great, but not good at teaching.

I learned a lot from Professor Zhang's lectures. Each presentation/class had a well-structured flow and the content was relevant and useful. He is also very well-versed in the topic which meant that additional comments were typically insightful. He also cares about students and wants to help them in any way he can.
It's ok class. Prof knows a lot in his area, but he's not a good teacher.

Professor Zhang is clearly very knowledgeable in the field of machine learning, and did an amazing job explaining difficult theoretical concepts during lectures. His class includes a reasonable mix of machine learning theory (underlying mechanisms of machine learning algorithms/techniques) and opportunities to apply them to practical datasets.

Professor Zhang is approachable and encourages students to ask questions. Office hours are well-utilized, we often go to his office after class to ask questions, and he was always patient and happy to answer.

Professor Zhang displayed exceptional knowledge and passion for machine learning, making complex topics understandable and engaging. Also, feedback was always constructive and insightful, significantly aiding in our learning process. Besides that, I love how the final project was laid out and presented which gave students many free discussions.

A must-take class if you want to claim that you understand why deep learning works. He comprehends and complements the difficult-to-self-learn textbooks very well so that the large topics fit within a semester. Through the project, he trains you how to read, critique, and build on the latest literature. He is very considerate and accessible.

reviews.comment: Take other courses if you have chance. The grade is fair, but if you really wanted to learn something from the course, probably NO. You won't feel any passion from the instructor at all.

Professor Zhang taught this course very well and I have learned a lot from this course.

If you are going to do research, please this course. This course will prepare you very well for research.

Professor Zhang is a nice person and answers students' questions patiently.

The course is tough with often unclear lectures. Grading is fair, but a foundation knowledge is recommended. Prof focuses on theory, lacking practical examples. Would recommend other courses at Khoury unless you don't have any other choices.

Prof Zhang's class was a good mix of applied and theoretical ML techniques and was a fair grader. CS7140 is a challenging course, but you will learn a lot if you dive into it. Please take CS6140 machine learning before you pick this one, or you will feel lost for the entire semester. He is the best lecturer if you want to learn machine learning. He teaches tough topics effectively using his own words that makes us much easier to learn the topics by reading texts. If you have no experience with ML,take cs6140 or NLP,before taking this course. Prof. Zhang didn't provide any solid examples for each theory. I personally just learnt the topic from textbooks/online sources,and used the lectures for review.Northeastern should hire some professors who know how to teach and convey their knowledge to the students

Prof Zhang's 7140 class was focused mostly on mathematical deep learning theory. The materials were in-depth, and I learned a lot from the lectures and the assignments. Extremely condescending. I went to his office hours once to get an explanation on a concept I was struggling with, and the entire thirty minutes was instead telling me I needed to become better at studying. I took notes in class and did all of the homework. I still struggled because of his insanely high grading standard on quizzes.

Does not make things easy on students. Lectures straight from the textbook and grades quizzes unnecessarily harshly. He does not try to make things easier when the class is struggling and is not understanding at all. Super condescending but at least he tries to explain things.
Would not reccomend MATH 1341 by Dr. Hudon to anybody. Lectures directly from the textbook and talks down to students. Office hours were more critical than helpful.
Super helpful and kind. Class is super easy if you do all of the homework and pay attention. If you took calc in hs this class will be easy.

If you pay attention and do all the homeworks you'll probably be in great shape. Homework is rarely collected. Quizzes and tests are pretty fast paced, but sometimes are the same thing as what we did in class. Not fantastic, but not bad by any means.

Disclosure: I took an entry level course with this prof. Homework was not collected, tests and quizzes were your entire grade. If you do the homework and go to class you can do well on the tests. His lectures are good but he can move a bit fast and doesn't leave much time for questions. Overall a nice guy, he cares about his students too!

Professor takes this class as a an opportunity to make kids rue the day they chose this elective. Incredibly hard homework assignments and tests. Lectures are interesting; however, there is so much work. By far my hardest class and my classmates can say the same.

He grades the quizzes ridiculously hard. Even if you do the work out if the answer isn't correct he will take full credit off and is an unfair grader. He does not give extra credit or scale anything. I, along with almost half the class ended up withdrawing.
Class review and homework solving in class really helpful! No need to do self review at home

Professor Hudon went out of his way to teach the material in a way that was understandable and made a real effort to make sure students were understanding the course. So nice and easy to learn from! Amazing professor and credibly knowledgeable. I would recommend to anyone!
Great prof clear grading and very accessible

One of the best finance professors at NEU. Lectures are clear and well-organized. He cares his students. Weekly quizzes make up 80% of the grade, and the final is just three quizzes' worth of material. You can drop three lowest quizzes and homework score.

Best finance professor at Northeastern. Prof. Herron really cares about his students and goes the extra mile. Quick grade turnarounds, stays after class, held extra office hours. Also very knowledgeable about finance in general.

Prof. Herron is the GOAT. Very unique but effective teaching style. Assignments can be a bit tough but are some of the most interesting assignments I've done in college. Grading can be sometimes a bit unclear, but if you put in a decent amount of work you will be more than fine. Great person and teacher overall - would take again for any class.
Professor Herron is honestly one of the best professors ive had in Northeasters. He knows what hes talking about and makes complex concepts super easy to understand.

Professor Herron is truly amazing at teaching and as a person. He cared and tried to understand the mental health problems I was having(anxiety, depression and adhd led to skipping classes, etc.) He ccommodated me by allowing me to attend thru zoom and supporting me instead of replying dismissively or not believing me like my other professors.

He is a nice and carrying guy, but his grading of cases and test is rather harsh. Furthermore, his tests are really difficult at least for FINA4320. Most annoying thing is he assumes you know all the concepts in previous classes and the homework doesn't really help you learn.

Richard is truly passionate about Corporate Finance. All assignments are worth 15% except Final, which is 30%. He really cares about the subject and goes above and beyond to share real life examples which is really helpful. He is an easy grader (all my tests and projects are 95+). His tests are easy and as long as you study, you'll do well.
He grades too tough and his office hours was not helpful at all. He has a big ego. Dont take guys class if you actually wanna do good in calc 2.
Great professor who wants and loves to see his students succeed. Couldn't recommend anymore.

If you see this man listed as your teacher do whatever you can to switch. He has an insane ego and talks down to his students constantly in lectures. He is also the most unfair grader I've ever seen. he teaches like he is trying to make himself feel better about his sad little life.

guy is just rude to classmates

heather is the best ever

Though the lecture videos are quite lengthy, Heather explains each topic very clearly- making the homework straightforward- and has extra credit for each module. She is easy to reach, incredibly kind, and understanding. Would absolutely recommend!

Heather is excellent! The class is a lot of work since there is so much to cover! Expect about 2-3 hours of videos per module, and a problem set for each module. Further, there is a summative problem set which is much longer. She was also accessible outside of class, and was happy to meet over Zoom! I definitely want to take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is awesome, kind, and her lecture videos were so interesting! However, the class was a lot more time-consuming than I was expecting. MANY hours worth of lecture videos to watch a week, and you can't get away without watching them because then you can't complete the assignments. But if you do all the work, it is pretty straightforward and easy.

Professor Littlefield is an amazing professor. I took her class Summer 1 and it was really enjoyable. Her lectures are a little long and the homework does take some time. If you are looking for an A, you just have to do the work and it's easy to. There is extra credit for every module that can add over 10% to your overall grade if you do it all.

littlefield is approachable and takes the time to care about you individually. lectures were instructional and easy to follow. no exams; grade mostly homework-based (~1-2hrs of hw/week; no readings). only downside is lecture slides are kinda bare--most explanation is done verbally; recordings aren't accessible--so prepare to pay attention in class
Heather is incredible and everyone should take a class with her if they have the chance. Super friendly and genuinely cares about the students' thoughts.

Littlefield's honors inquiries was very fun. Discussions were a huge part of what we worked on. She welcomed every question and idea, and they were my favorite part of class. It's a lot of reading but the reading is interesting, and she wants everyone to do really well. The projects are tedious, but she gives clear feedback and you'll learn a lot!

The assignments were very time-consuming and not always straightforward. However, she is very accessible for outside help as she will schedule 1:1s with you outside office hours to help on projects. Checking projects by her before I submitted really boosted my grade for the second half of the course.

Ling Analysis is a hard class but Heather did her best to make sure we all were prepared for writing our papers and doing our research. She does the best with what she has considering each intro to ling class is different meaning everyone starts with a different knowledge base. She's super understanding and is always willing to work with you.

A lot of reading, but we had really good group discussions! This was my first class in linguistics, and I really enjoyed it overall! Heather is very compassionate and genuinely wants everyone to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Nice lady. Very knowledgable. Expects way too much from her students. Avoid courses with her, if you can. The linguistics department has great professors, all of whom are much more reasonable than her.

Professor Littlefield is really funny and has interesting stories. However, I do feel that she is an overly tough grader. The assignments are interesting, but it's hard to know what she expects, and you get points off seemingly at random sometimes. I also agree with one of the other commenters that she can be somewhat condescending at times.

Incredibly difficult course that requires a lot of outside work. However, it's most definitely worth it. You will leave that class a much better student. Heather is incredibly kind and offers all sorts of help and takes all of your comments and concerns seriously.

Heather is very kind and helpful most of the time. She can also be condescending. Her assignments are very difficult and she's a pretty hard grader. She's always open to answering questions though. The key is to explain yourself in the papers that you write for her class; anything is admissible with an explanation.

Extremely nice lady, always glad to discuss the material after class and very intelligent and knowledgeable - you can tell she loves linguistics! However, Linguistic Analysis was one of the most work-intensive and harshly-graded classes I've ever taken. She's a great teacher, but almost too tough to recommend.

One of the best profs I've ever had. She's very smart and really knows her stuff. She's also incredibly helpful and HILARIOUS! I looked forward to her class every time. She is the goofiest, nicest person. Answers emails within the hour. She challenges you, but it's always within reason. love her love her LOVE her! I was so sad when class ended.

Good: super nice, passionate, incredibly knowledgable, willing to help, and energetic. Bad: apparently doesn't realize students have other classes and assigned a gratuitious amount of work (and I didn't procrastinate). Reasonable final. Tips: pick the simplest language you can and take phonology, syntax, and semantics courses first. It will help.
The class was really interesting but the work was really demanding.  She's slow on grading, so don't expect to see that paper you worked all night on ever again.

Work intensive class. Thoroughly goes over concepts and brings people of all levels to the same speed. Huge language research project of your choice - best not to procrastinate. She's tough but very fair and funny as heck. Quite dedicated and passionated about linguistics and helping her students.

nice, sweet woman. horrible class. attendance is mandatory (only allowed 2 absences..excused or not) structure of class very boring, most notes i've ever taken in a class. if intro to linguistics isnt required for you, i reccommend taking a different class.

Littlefield is an awesome teacher and person. She's sooo funny and down-to-earth, which is VERY refreshing in academia. Class has a very communal feel. My time commitment for the class is low since the only assignments are a few homeworks and a final. No book is necessary-- just take good notes and you'll be fine.
Great sense of humor and quirky lectures kept me interested and regularly attending class, but the homework kicked my ass. Probably the first class I'm failing but would recommend anyway.

She is a great teacher, and I would tell anyone to take this class. You need to spend some time on the homeworks but if you do them you will do fine on the final! its an easy class if you put in some time....she has a great sense of humor and wants to be there teaching you!

Teaches well. Good sense of humor. Homework was tough. Exams were reasonable. No need for a textbook. Has a passion for what she teaches. I recommend her for any linguistics course. She could be more clearer and give the bigger picture instead of focusing on details all the time. Great teacher. Always cheerful.
Very helpful. Really bright.  Loves the fulani culture.  I loved to learn in her class.  I  still remember the samoan culture from that book.
Challenging homework--NOT busy work. Grades attendance and participation. Good sense of humor. Expects a lot from students, but grades fairly.  You will EARN your grade. Good office hours.

Heather is an amazing teacher.  She's interested in what she has to say and makes the classes fun.  She's a tough grader, but she's usually fair.  She puts in a lot of effort and expects her students to do the same.

Prof. was a very effective teacher in this basic linguistics course.  Any problems with clarity came from the course material not from her lectures.  It was a challenging class.  However, she used a great sense of humor and good teaching strategies to explain the concepts.  Enjoyed it thoroughly.

Hard but interesting class. Very smart prof, work every class, mainly lecture. homework, midterm, and final, all difficult and time consuming. EC offered on homework. tests aren't curved. highly recommend going to class otherwise material very hard to understand.
I like Dr. Thurston, and she's really nice and everything but oh god is this a boring class. It's fine, take it for an incredibly easy A. The textbook is available through the library which is nice.

Such an angel shes my favee. Quizzes and exams are 70% of the grade but she uses quiz questions for the exam and gives a ton of guidance on whats on the tests. Most people will end this class with an A. Just show up and she will love you. If anything happens during the semester she is so understanding but she does follow the syllabus too closely.

Relatively easy but heavy workload. Quiziz, in person, almost every single class. Weekly discussion posts, along with regular work, too. Very kind and passionate teacher; however, an overwhelming amount of work at times.

one can not maintain good Gpa under him, if u want to increase gpa I would not suggest his class. Exams are too heavy, you need to memorize 20+ pseudo codes, and in assignments also, you will not get full marks always. He is a strict professor and would not listen to what you have to say, if he sets his mind to something.

0 for n > 10." I signed up expecting to learn algorithms, not to play a guessing game where every

Amazing lectures. If you do the work, you'll learn a lot.
One of the best professors I've ever had. Very clear and helpful.
No matter how much other students berate him, one can't deny that he is a great instructor for algo. He knows what he's teaching and his lecture delivery style is also clear.

Little concern for students. Take this course only if you can memorize and reproduce CLRS exactly as expected.

I got baited into memorizing 30+ pseudocode for the final.
which i guess is alright to know 
but it didnt feel good when i didnt get to apply my 30+ pseudocode of knowledge on the 5 questions which are on the final
it feels like he said gullible is written on the ceiling and i looked up

The grading practices are excessively punitive, communication is effectively nonexistent, and the lack of transparency has caused extreme and unnecessary stress. This experience has significantly impacted my mental well-being and delayed my academic progress, and it should be formally reviewed.

If you want to sharpen algorithms, this course delivers. Lectures are structured and well paced—until the end, when it suddenly accelerates. But if you're aiming for a smooth learning curve or you're protecting your GPA, think twice: grading feels bureaucratic, partial credit is hard to defend, and the pressure can make learning feel punishing.
Run, worst professor of all time, would ask you to follow EXACTLY how the slides or the book implement the algorithm, or you lose a lot of points even if you are correct.

reviews.comment: Algorithms is a very hard class to take in general. Materials are heavy - it's just not a fun topic. But Prof. Herc really tries his hardest to make it work in the short time frame and the knowledge people already have (1st Sem. Grads all the way to PhD).

Poor learning structure. Exams are questions directly from the textbook but the textbook is dense. His lectures help a little with the exams and homework but they are more so supplements. Also, not enough questions on exams, if you miss just one, you fail.

I am pretty sure the good reviews are fake reviews. He is a bad lecturer and barely explains anything. He insists on following the book and visiting office hours and TA's but the book is dense af and the office hours are just a repetition of the class. Given how abysmal he is at teaching it feels almost criminal how harshly he grades. AVOID!!
Worst professor ever seen in my life. I failed by 0.21% and gives direct 0 even if your approach is in correct direction. RUN!!!!

Won't Recommend. 
The grading criteria for assignments and exams is non-sensical. Each exam has 4 questions, so if you commit a mistake in one, you risk falling by a letter grade. Highly theoretical, will not help in passing interviews. Nothing to learn here, stay away. Take some other worthwhile course, and LeetCode if you wanna pass interviews.

Do not even think of taking this class, professor is very rude and does not care about students. Run away from this course and professor. I failed by 0.1%, the professor didn't consider my case, didn't reply to any emails or messages. Grades ruthlessly.  If you mess up even one of the exam, be prepared to retake the course. RUN!!!!!!!!!!

I really enjoyed being in class with this professor. His course work was very flexible and fair, his lectures were very engaging and informative. His class was the perfect length. Overall I feel this was one of the most effective educators I've had in my program this far. I would absolutely take his class again if I could.
run, don't take with him
not a good lecturer

Worst grader I have ever seen. agree with other comments. he is a nice guy but an awful lecturer. his slides are just copying textbooks and it is hard to understand what he talks at class. i attended all the classes and felt it was such a waste of time. he is also very tough grader and he makes everything more confusing. this is the worst course I ever took.

However, not an easy A, you will need to study and may need to attend OH often. 5-8 hours a week outside of class is expected. 

Grading appears harsh sometimes, but all assignments(and exams) have some bonus points.

The professor grades based on concept clarity. If you understand and justify the concepts well, it greatly benefits you. He is clear on fundamentals and pays attention to details that matter. His challenging assignments prepare you for exams and promote growth. The subject is easy if you're strong on the basics. TAs are responsible and helpful.

This was the worst I've had. Useless lectures with empty slides. Condescending on Piazza and impossible to understand due to his accent.  Grading was insanely harsh. Lost 10 points on a 15-point problem for a small mistake! Even with the right answer, a missing step meant you were wrong.  He also refused to give us homework solutions.
Grading criteria are unclear, and TAs require excessive explanation of basic concepts with no partial credit. very frustrating and inconsistent.

This course was pretty difficult. I took it as an undergrad as part of the PlusOne program. Prof Herc is super nice and willing to help you out. The lectures are informative, but reading the textbook is essential for doing well on the exams.

he is the best professor I know and its the best to get good gpa

complete disregard for his students success and just wants to see you fail.

just a rude professor most of the time. He is really hard to connect with any issue. Honestly most of the time it feels like he just wants you to leave right when you step in office hours. he's the best professor i've had since i study here. he explain everything very well. really concern about the level of understanding in the material and eager to help us to be more understand. 4 exams, 20% each. study from his study guide. REALLY HELPFUL! if you master the study guide, guaranteed 90+ grades because the questions are 90% the same.

Not a good teacher. Expect to teach yourself as you'll have a hard time paying attention in class. He has a very low inaudible voice and slurs his speech which makes it even more difficult to understand him. Will include material on the test he did not teach. Attendance is mandatory. Overall avoid unless you plan to teach yourself.

Professor is a harsh grader and was not helpful during office hours. Attended class, participated, read the chapters before class, took thorough notes, but still was not able to get a good grade.  I would not recommend this class.

Class was okay at first, but this guy was not helpful at all, he basically failed our whole class and half the class dropped it. The tests were hard, even though I studied and my notes were thorough and informative. His lectures were helpful...he doesn't believe in extra credit, he thinks extra credit is for slackers.
Good teacher. Very clear when he talks. Make sure you go to class and read the book and you will do fine in the class

Sort of entertaining to watch teach. He has an interesting sense of humor. Expects you to read the chapter before class, but it doesn't really matter because he teaches everything you need to know in lecture. 4 exams 20% each and 20% for participation (attendance, questions, etc). Forget your notes and study the study guide he gives out!!!!
His lectures can be difficult to understand, but he gives ample time for questions. Covers a lot of material, but you can be successful in this class if you study.

Micro theory. 4 exams - 25% each. He grades hard and you have to know the exact definition, all questions are short answer. Good professor, takes attendance for extra credit and expects you to participate. USE THE STUDY GUIDE! Some of the questions from the guide will be in the exam! free points for that! you can get an easy A for this course.

Really nice guy and very helpful too.  Class lectures can be boring, but he always lets you out like an hour early.  His tests are in 4 chapter increments with no cumulative final or midterm.  Tests are easy if you do the study sheet he gives you and go to the review session he holds.  Really wants his students to do well, i highly recommend him

Quirky guy, I enjoyed his class.He really knows his stuff and is passionate about economics. The lectures can be a little overwhelming but if you take good notes and review them, like he suggests you really start to understand the material.The reading does help, but you can get by without it. Definitely study before tests, and do the study sheet!
Very Reasonable
Good teacher, you do need to put the work outside of class.  Study hard before tests and you will get good grades.  First exam is hardest but use study questions and you will know whats on the exam.
Helps you if you need it. Sometimes doesn't understand your question right away but so what, he will answer your question til youre satisfied. Interesting lectures too. Recommended.
He is nice, but the exam is really hard and weast time.
SOOOOOOOOOO BAD!!! Switch out now, total ****, bizarre grader, only 4 tests.  get out now!

Pretty good prof. I've always been horrible at economics and only took this class to fulfill a major requirement but I found him to be really helpful and easy to understand. He goes over the same things repeatedly which really helps to drive home what he's trying to teach. Seems to genuinely want his students to understand everything and succeed.

The tests are based on about 15% of the study sheet that he gives you, and he expects that you know much more than just a definition of the given terms. There are four tests and each one is made up of about eight questions, each of which either having to do with graphing or intuitively explaining something. Hardest class I've taken thus far at NEU.

Take notes and write down everything he says. Tests are short but difficult. Make sure you explain yourself entirely. and hes right, you have to study at least a week prior to the test. Hard/weird grader. Say exactly what he wants or you'll getpoints off. Pretty okay teacher.

Ok professor. Study the study sheets he gives out before each exam. Make sure you know every word and an exact definition. He  wants an exact response, anything close he won't give credit for. You can read the book and do well, compare his notes to the study guide

I tried BSing the answers on the first test and it didn't work. I started giving long, detailed responses and got a 100 on every test. He's very smart and knows what he's talking about. He takes attendance only every few classes. His review sheets are  very helpful and similar to the tests. Come to class having read the chapter!

I have had Ilter for 2 courses, and in both he has not done a very good job of explaining the material.  The book is much more reliable. He often confuses himself and draws incrrect graphs. Also he does not answer questions very well. His grading is a bit too hard and he does not change grades when the answer has many options- he only looks for one

a good guy.  his classes are interesting, hes funny, and the tests arent that hard.  as long as you pay attention in class and take some notes you'll be fine.  He has review sessions before every test (but i never went to one).  he sometimes goes off on tangents in class, but are usually interesting, but sometimes brings politics into the class. :(
study his notes

He sucks at teaching, and he is such a hard grader on exams, and I put a lot of time into studying for the exams.  He wasn't helpful at all during office hours, and was actually kind of a jerk.  I'm probably going to get a D in the class, and I have a 3.2 GPA, along with making Dean's list, so avoid his class if you know what's good for you.

I <3 Bakkal! He is so good! His tests are hard but as long as you write a lot in response to the question and really work out and know the problem you're good (BS IT!) He has helpful reviews and his review sheets aren't the test but they help make sure you studied the stuff... use them AFTER you look over your notes.
Ilter is great. Presents boring material well and gives applicable examples. Polite, respectful and all-around a professional teacher.

Macro class - nice guy, presents 100% of the material upfront in class. If you get the answer wrong on a test it's because you didn't pay attention or critically think about what he was teaching. Those who complained probably have never evr had a HARD cours. He was nice and not too dull despite his slightly goofy Turkish accent. Ex "Sply and dmnd".
Got an A, tests were pretty straightforward with never any surprises, always willing to explain until you understand it, Good teacher overall

if u want a class where you dont have to show up take this..it's not that he is cool so you don't have to show up..it's that it wont help you on the tests because he sucks at teaching..so just take the class and read the book thoroughly and you should do ok on the tests
not bad. go to class. do the study guides. and you'll do fine. class is pretty dull, but not terribly difficult.

He's very helpful and fair. In order to do well, you need to show up take notes, know the study questions and thats it. If you do that, you can get an A. You can even get by w/o reading the book since all the info you need to know is on the study sheet. It can be a little boring and repetitive at times, but it helps you learn the info.
No Comments
No Comments
tests are so easy!!! he goes over everything pretty well, doesnt take attendance, gives extra credit, nice guy
hes a good teacher and good man

bakkal is a great professor. hes engaging and really cares about both the subject and the student. why do other students rate him poorly? sure, his tests require alot of thought. he wont accept multiple choice because macro isnt that kind of subject. he wants you to know the material, and you will.

Good MACRO professor.  The way to do very well is to show up to all the classes (he will pass around an attendance sheet some days when attendance is low) and to study and MEMORIZE the study sheets he gives you to work on your own for the tests.  One of the better macro teachers.

As everyone has said, his review sheets don't go over what's on the test, very hard to study for and very unclear what exactly will be on the test. Even going to class and going to class and taking notes doesn't help either. Confusing lessons and not clear at all. Terrible teacher.
horrible, unclear, tests are not like the study sheet or what he goes over in class...and im an A student in every other class this semester except his
He is the worst economics teacher ever! I am an economics major and after his class I took Macro theory and my professor told me everything I learned was useless and wrong! What a waste of my time!
Great teacher.. one of the best...

Ok, so the class is really boring, but you learn SO much in it.  If you go to class, get the notes, and do the review sheet you know exactly what is going to be on the test.  Explains everything, and is happy to help if you don't understand.  Nice guy.  If you can stay awake, I recommend this class.
VERY UNCLEAR TEACHER. POOR EXAMPLES. SOMETIMES HARD TO UNDERSTAND ACCENT. EXPECTATIONS ARE SOMETIEMS VAGUE

I've only had this guy for a couple of weeks but I already dread going to class every day.  Dry as sand, confusing as hell, and he mumbles on top of it all.  I haven't learned a thing in 8 lectures.  But I don't dislike him as a person-seems pretty decent

I am a senior now, and I really believe that he is the worst professor at Northeastern. There is no way to know how to study. He contradicts himself in his lectures. The only way to get a good grade is go to the study sessions.
VERY Easy class if you just go to every class and take all the notes he writes on the board and do the study guides. Tests are exactly what he talks about in class.
He is not a bad teacher! Boring, yes, but Ilter is the cutest--he tells you exactly what you need to know on the test, making them very easy to do well on. Always offers to help. A++
just a bad teacher

I went to every class, wrote down everything he said and didn't get what the hell he was talking about...I'm an A/B student and ended up with a C and had to spend time in the Economics lab...find another professor
Dr. Bakkal is the man.  He is perfectly clear, no suprises on the tests.  If you don't understand him, get out of economics, you suck.
Oh Ilter...ditto to what people said about going to class, taking notes, cramming before tests just to know review Qs (review sessions help) kind of boring, but not terrible,kind of feel bad for him

The class is pretty easy...The key to success in this class is to skip lectures, read the book day before the review, go to review and answer all questions on review sheet, and you get guranteed A or A- on the test, cake.
Sooo difficult to understand- can't follow his lectures. just go to review sessions and find out the EXACT answers to his review sheets- it's the only way you'll pass
This guy is so confusing. Nothing he says connects to the next topic and nothing comes out of the book so dont bother reading it. He doesnt go out of his way to help you to make it better.

Nice man, but made things way too complicated.  Hard to understand.  I went to tutoring to pass this course and even they didn't understand him!
i have never had a teacher as confusing as this guy. I never have any idea what topic he is on and what ever he is talking about makes no sense.
1 word: LOSER i hate this teacher never take him ever
Unclear. Makes concepts hard to understand. Take notes on everything, even the non-economics examples. He expects EVERYTHING he says during lectures to appear on tests or he takes points off.
foreign and doesn't use book.  Reel foreign.
Do not use the book. Take notes from his lectures and study them to the dot! If you do this, along with completing his study guides, you will be able to get a solid B or above.

stupid, makes the course material seem more difficult than it really is
shes the best
Pretty easy class make sure to do the homework on time, everything is through canvas and cengage, caring professor, attendance not necessarily mandatory, one duo project that isn't too difficult
A very nice lady, teaches effectively & makes learning fun. Material is relatively easy. Take her class!

Professor Dupree is very nice and caring. Her lectures are easy to understand and she makes sure students are really thinking about the material. However, her voice can be a little too good at putting you to sleep. Her lectures are all recorded, so most people skip often, and her test are all take-home and open note. TAKE HER CLASS.
Prof Dupree is super straight-forward with all of her assignments and exams which makes it easy to do well in this class. Very understanding professor and overall a chill class!

Guys at first I was like I'm so scared of economics so I went to every class, but one day the class was freezing and I kept hearing noises so I was like maybe I will stop going a little and I did some work on my own w/ A+. She is very generous with what she gives; open note at home exams, drops lowest grades, etc. Take her she is kind
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Exceptionally easy but extremely boring. Lectures are just her reading slides and telling tangential stories with no point, which sucks because she's clearly passionate/knowledgeable. Still recommend though. 1 test is dropped (including final if you don't wanna take it). 3 HWs are also dropped. Textbook is expensive and mandatory for assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I never went to class, attendance wasn't mandatory. She is a very nice person. HW is long but online and so are tests. very easy class take her for sure

Professor Dupree is knowledgeable and excited to teach. Class was overall easy ... tests were all online and considered "open note, open resource, can do it with friends, etc" (her words). Very few people attended lectures, and they were not very engaging, so I felt I didn't learn as much as I wished. Wish she got to know the few who came to class!

Professor Dupree was great. She clearly cares about economics and comes to class prepared and interested. Class was okay, it was hard to learn deeply in such a large lecture hall, and many times I felt myself zoning out. Overall, it was great, and Professor Dupree did a great job teaching a large lecture.

Lectures were extremely dry, she just regurgitated the slide decks provided by the textbook. I got a good grade, but all tests were assigned through Canvas so basically everyone cheated and no one went to lecture. Nice professor and easy class but you don't really learn anything

Very kind professor and great course. Yes, there are quite a few homework assignments and 5 exams, but nothing too hard. Content is very understandable and class is quite easy. Would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was great. So easy, you literally just have to complete the weekly HW assignments which are all online and ALL of the tests are take home (including midterms and the final). Her lectures are good too you just have to show up and want to learn. I highly recommend taking!
easy class, just do homework and ur chilling, all tests are take home open book but if you need help you can get it very easily, occasional assignments, but hella easy.

Jill is great. The class is easy, don't worry at all. She responds to emails quickly and is very caring, willing to work with you. Doesn't take off points for late assignments. Tests are open-note, asynchronous. I would take this class again. It was a relief to have an easier class like this one.

Lectures were a bit all over the place. Textbook reading is unavoidable as there are quizzes on the reading every class (they're easy though as long as you did the reading). When writing the essays, it's best to attend office hours to make sure you're going in the right direction. Class was really interesting at times but overall a little boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Grading seemed random at times - on multiple occasions, it was unclear why I was getting points taken off. She would get somewhat defensive when asked about this. Lectures can be hard to pay attention to as they directly reflect reading we are told to do before class; hearing everything twice was boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: i loved prof dupree's class! the whole semester for american econ history was based on 1 book, and we covered 2 chapters a week. discussions are student-led and very engaging! short reading quizzes every class made by students, and total of 4 papers throughout the sem (1 paper per book section). very understanding and lenient grader!
She is nice professor, but her classes don't really help with tests. She usually grades assignments at long intervals, which makes me confused about grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not the greatest lecturer, she reads of the slides which are not very thorough. There are many unit tests, they are not difficult if you read the textbook and do the homework. You do need to self-teach yourself but the class isn't very difficult.

Second time taking her, have taken Conflict Ec 1916 and now American Econ History 3470. In 3470, we had 3 papers about one long book (800pgs), Ages of American Capitalism by Levy. Late grader. Class is very participation based; you teach a few chapters of the book for a week as a group. Fair grade. She loves what she teaches.

Easy class overall if you aren't interested in economics. Take it asynchronously if you want less work. There is a big group project which takes a lot of time each week, so make sure you have a good group and you get to choose your group in the beginning of the semester.

I don't know why this professor got such bad reviews, she's entertaining, kind, caring, responsive, and easy grader. There are reading, graded outlines and 3-4 test units but the concepts is so easy to understand it's really not stressful at all. I don't think the in person lectures add anything to the textbook but she gives detailed explanations.

So far, definitely the most useless class and professor I've had at Northeastern. Professor sets her things up for 10-15 mins each day while we sit in complete silence and do nothing. Her teaching is poor, takes very long to explain concepts, and doesn't really do any in-class examples to prepare for the test. Would not recommend
Took Conflict Econ 1916. Hard material, not recommended as first econ course. Gave make up exams. IMO lectures too slow for content. Great TA Roy.

As long as you do the homework and readings, you'll be fine. Late homework is accepted with a 10% penalty 3 days after it was due, you'll have 5 tests and the lowest is dropped, and your lowest two lowest homework grades. All in all I think she's pretty fair, not that much interaction bc it's online, but she emails back pretty quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The entire class is asynchronous and relies only on the textbook. You're graded on tests, homework and a group project. It's heavy reading and homework but the project isn't that difficult. She explains how to do the proper steps and as long as you're coordinated with your group you should be fine. Only take this if you're okay with reading online.

Took Professor Dupree asynchronously during Summer II and did not enjoy it in the slightest. She doesn't lecture, just assigns textbook chapters and homework. Overall pretty easy to do well if you put in the work, but not a fun course.
Easy class fully virtual easy A as long as you do the work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is extremely easy to pass and all exams are easy. She drops your two lowest homeworks and your lowest test score. There is a multi-part group project but she gives clear instructions and walks you through it step by step. I did however take this class online and not sure how in person class is.

Took this class online and asynchronously, so barely interacted with the professor at all. Everything is taught through textbook readings and homeworks, no lectures. Basically a self-taught course but easy to get an A if you put in the work. One big group project, easy grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: This is a terrible class to take online. I've never met the professor or directly interacted with her, and I'm pretty sure it's the same for everyone else in the class. There is a ridiculous amount of reading every week, too many exams, and the group project is such a pain.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her class is pretty okay if you read the textbook, but I barely learned anything. Literally no interaction with the student.. way too much homework sometimes...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Here are something I wish I knew before taking Dupree's ECON1115 class -it's completely asynchronous (besides going to office hours ONCE, I've never met her) -it's all taught through online textbooks (if you don't read you're done) -be ready to schedule yourself. 1 hr of recitation is all you get. I made a time table so that I'd get stuff done
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very nice. I'm not sure what people are on about with her NUstart/online class being difficult. The readings and homeworks each week can be done properly in 3-4 hours just by reading through and comprehending the material before doing the homework problems. Tests are shortish and are no problem if you study a bit - or Google the answers.

ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE. How are these teachers so disconnected from there students? Ridiculous amounts of work for an intro econ class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS ONLINE. The group project is an ABSOLUTE NIGHTMARE and this lazy piece of crap literally doesn't do any work. She makes US grade each other's work. Such a waste of time and money

For an intro online class during a pandemic, it's WAY too much work and a confusing format. 2 homeworks per chapter (20 chapters), discussions, 5 tests, 5 parts to a group project, and peer reviews. Barely any teaching done by prof. I'm so confused where to go for what assignment. This prof was not meant for online teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: The format is absolutely terrible. Apart from one group project the whole class is conducted through Cengage Mindtap, a textbook software. All homework assignments and tests are conducted through this and most of the actual teaching as well. The prof is available outside of class but not super helpful. Overall a waste of time and money.

Like all other reviews, Professor Dupree is highly relaxed in terms of attendance. You cannot show up all semester and still receive an A regardless. There is a presentation at the end of the semester which you will have to go. I gave her a 4/5 because you will not learn in class, all exams and HW are online and in Chegg. The textbook is $100!

Definitely the easiest macro theory class as it is not quantitative heavy at all. Make friends with the smartest kids in the class because she lets you do homeworks and exams together (Exams are take home). Also get a tutor for the exams. Not sure how much I ended up learning through this method but she is a very nice professor and is very caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dupree is a very kind person and professor. She is very accommodating and understanding. The tests and quizzes are online, which makes doing well in the class much easier. One nice thing is that she does actually teach, for those who want to learn. She goes over the presentations and clearly understands and conveys the material. Great professor!

First level of difficulty is called "show up and you'll pass". In this class you don't even have to show up to pass. Test and quizzes are taken online, you can find all the answers and solutions in the internet. Final project she will just take a look at the poster and discuss it with you. If you have a heavy semester - take it, easy A.

Professor Dupree is a great choice if you're looking for a laid back class. Attendance wasn't mandatory, and all the tests and homeworks were online; this makes it very easy to get a good grade. However, with this system, you'll only learn anything if you put the effort in, which is pretty much optional. Overall, she is very nice and accommodating.

Prof. Dupree is great! She's super funny and amusing tbh. She really knows what she's talking about, but might overlook the fact that the students do not so be sure to ask questions. All assignmentsincluding midterm and finalsare online so it's fairly easy to get a good grade. Just read the power points, show up to class, and do your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's very intelligent but the class is based on 4 assignments and she grades incredibly hard for an introduction class. Goes on tangents that take up class time and doesn't post on Canvas, leaving many assignments unclear. I took this class for an NUPath requirement and I would only recommend taking it if it's required.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall really chill course. Consists of 2 midterm papers, a final presentation and a final paper. She doesn't take attendance but it's important you go to class because there are no in class slides on canvas. Because of that classes can be a little dreadful and long cause you have to make sure to pay attention, but I would take again!

Professor Kelting was a very nice person. However, her class is only graded on 3 assignments. 2 exams and an essay which is only done outside of class time. The only lecture notes are the ones she says during class and there are no slides to follow along to, and her lectures are not recorded. Dont take this class unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: prof. kelting is very nice, seems like she cares about her students and the class load is generally pretty light. the final paper was graded in less than a week so the grading comments read like she only took a cursory skim of the essay. i'd reccomend taking another class if you're actually knowledgeable or passionate about the topic

Never done a review here, but Kelting definitely deserves it. Essentially, you come into class and sit down and take notes on her lecture for the hour. But she is incredibly knowledgeable, engaging, and clear, and I look forward to class every time. If you go to the classes and take notes, the tests are intuitive, and she is a very fair grader.

Professor Kelting is a very good professor overall. Lectures were very interesting and she knows her material well. There were two exams, which were free response questions. You should attend lectures to answer them well, and don't need to do any of the readings. There is also a ten-page research paper, but there is ample time to do it.

Please do yourself a favor and do NOT take her class. As an elective, this class is very hard and requires so much writing. There’s also a 10 page research paper with exams every few week. She’s a nice lady but doesn't explain stuff relevant to the exam. DO NOT TAKE IT!!!! I did the mistake of taking because it’s “online”
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Kelting is an amazing person and very easy to approach. Get ready to attend all classes and take notes because her exams are based on that. There are many readings but I didn't do them and still got an A. She isn't the most responsive person by email so it's better to ask your doubts in class. Also her grading is vague with no feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The topics in this class are super interesting and she clearly knows a lot about the subject, but she is incredibly aloof, does not reply to emails and gives very vague instructions to the assignments, which leads to low grades for things you didn't even know she wanted in the first place! Just avoid if you can, unless you love the subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: while she is a very kind and positive person, kelting is not a good professor. she is all over the place when it comes to her lectures, she is inconsistent with providing information about class work and exams/homework, and she is very bad at responding to emails. i would not recommend this class as it is just so much to deal with.
Very Good Professor, smart in Eastern & Western Religions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: OMG! I would never a take class with her again. She is all over the place and dosen't know how to deliver her thoughts. I probably didn't have one complete sentence written in my notes. She also has many facts about Hinduism and Buddhism wrong, since my family is Hindu I could vouch for certain traditions. She also never gives back papers on time.

You don't have to do any readings to get an A. Show up to class and prepare to take notes. 3 grades are a take home midterm, take home final, and research paper. She's a ridiculously easy grader. Tries to be open minded nice but was surprisingly rude. I will never forget hearing her say people with skin conditions are broken and need to be cured ew
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Kelting is an amazing professor! In her class on Islam, I have learned all about that religion and beyond. You absolutely have to attend lectures as she is the main source of information and without the notes you won't be able to get a good grade in the class.

Kelting is super cool, really smart, and one of the nicest profs you'll ever have. She's super down to earth and understands what it's like to be a a student. However, she is all over the place. She has a lot going on and puts grading on the back burner. I did not get a single grade (for either of the two classes I took with her) until mid-April.

I took her class last year and she was an amazing woman. She's so fascinating. Knows a TON about religion. She assigns a couple cool projects - like she'll have you go to a religious service (of a different religion than your own) and write about it . Very cool. She uses blue books for exams.

I really enjoyed her class; I think she's a great teacher. You do a lot of reading, take a mid-term and final and write a research paper. It isn't an extraordinary amount of work. We're in college, right? She knows her stuff--speaks Farsi and has lived extensively in India. Very friendly. I took detailed notes, used those for exam and got an A.

Kelting is great. One of my favorites and I would love to take another of her classes. Seems to really know what she's talking about and makes for some truly interesting lectures. Assigns a great deal of reading but doesn't use it on the exams, which are essay format.

Loved the class and Kelting and am definately planning on taking her other course offerings. She is interesting and passionate about the class and accepts and encourages student input both in and outside of class. A great professor, my favorite so far at northeastern.  Good amount of work and fair.

Prof. Kelting offers challenging courses (I've taken two) and heaps on the work. I have no problem with that. I'm here to learn. She's taught me a lot. Her enthusiasm, availability, and helpfulness are above and-beyond. It's sick that the negative reviews of Prof. Kelting here stress how much work she requires. Stop whining and try studying!

Kelting is one of the best professors at NU.  She is funny, open, warm, engaging, and INCREDIBLY knowledgeable.  She is constantly striving to improve the classroom experience in any way possible.  She does a great job of writing notes on the board as well as giving examples most people can relate to.  Highly recommended!!!!
Awful class. Huge amounts of reading, but tests/papers are on her terrible notes. Took class as requirement, bad idea. Way too much work, and way too difficult. Take an easier class.

Very smart, personable.  Lectures are very interesting, Kelting makes room for some discussion and interaction.  Reading is decent except for when we start a new unit.  Midterm was difficult, but papers are easy if you pace yourself responsibly.  2 papers, 1 is small, 1 is a larger research paper.  In class essay midterm and final.

Obviously, there's a difference between the Islam and East. Rel. ratings. Here's my opinion: This prof is AWESOME. So funny, so enthusiastic, so clear in how she explains things. One of the best NU profs I've had. Easy tests if you read and take good notes.  HE IS SO SMART and has knowledge about practically everything in the world. Great person.

Clearly a very inteligent professor and deserves respect for it.  I took this course to satisfy a diversity credit (as most did) and there was more work involved than I anticipated. A lot of reading to do. Her tests are passable if you do the readings. If you are just trying to meet a diversity requirement however I suggest taking an easier course.

This ... is the world class I've ever taken in my whole life. I wish I would've come here to see what people had to say first. Do yourself a favor if you're thinking about taking this class ... and just run away. Anywhere. Anywhere but wherever Kelting is.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS  It's awful. There is so much work, including a 10-page research paper.  It is so hard and everything about it sucks.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

Worst professor I've ever had.  Erratic, unclear teaching style.  She pays attention to 1 or 2 kids in the class and then forgets anyone else is even there.  Thank god we had some books to read because what she taught us in class was utterly useless.  Do youself a favor and avoid her at all costs, that is if she still has a job!!!!

Fabulous professor - best ever! Lots of reading, lots of papers and wonderful, engaging and respectful class discussions. Not an easy class but you get back what you put in - she is very open to students and one of the most intelligent people I've ever had the pleasure of meeting.  Would highly reco

Terrible teacher, unclear, crazy in a bad way, immature.  Bad teacher = uninformed and confused students = bad grades = bad vibes.  Acts friendly to your face and stabs you in the back.  Stay away from this one, if not for your time than for your GPA.

Don't take her for this class! She's a very nice and fun person but won't teach you anything worthwhile and her grading sucks. She expects you to write quite a few papers the second half of the semester and there's lots of reading. Tends to repeat what's in the reading. Made a cool topic very boring
This class sounded great in theory but is SO much more trouble than its worth.  Her essay assignements are unclear which makes her hard to please and the expected reading every week is unreasonable
She's very funny, but that doesn't really make up for the boring class...I don't feel I've learned anything in it, pretty much a waste of time.

Very nice lady, but this class is extremely boring.  It has no modern world context whatsoever, and often focuses too heavily on the theoretical/historical aspects of Islam.  Random, boring tangents are not uncommon for her.  After the class, you feel like you've learned nothing that day.

She is extremely personable and excited about her classes.  She is very intelligent but she teaches on a level for beginners.  I agree with the statement that her tests don't always let you showcase what you know but overall I don't think she's a hard grader.

This professor is AWESOME. Very funny, has great stories. The class is easy esp her essays. she can unclear about topic. her tests are little tougher because they don't quite pertain to lectures; her readings don't at all. overall, the class is great- highly recommended

I agree with the previous comments: very friendly, excellent sense of humor and TONS of knowledge. Still, the tests are based on "pick two out of three" essays that are somewhat narrow and don't allow you to show what you really know. Definitely an interesting and rewarding class, though!

One of the best professors at NU.  She knows everything about everything, presents it with great sense of humor, and is very personable and friendly, and very flexible with grades and deadlines.  Short essay assignments, essay exams, opportunities for extra credit- easy to get a decent grade.
Sooo funny.  Lots of reading, but not too hard of a class

Probably the worst professor at Northeastern. You cannot understand what he is saying most of the time. The TAs are not helpful and take days to respond to even the most basic questions. Exam averages were around a 50, and weekly assignments take hours to complete.  Avoid this class.

Pros:
- Lots of time spent in Excel, great for experience
- LAMBDA knowledge definitely sets you apart from most users

Cons:
- Weekly assignments always a number 1 priority (shortest one took me 6 hours.)
- Instructions for these assignments are super unclear
- TA help isn't great
- Huge over-reliance on AI teaching
- First few weeks are brutal

Seriously avoid this class if possible. I took it because I needed a class with a lab for 5 credits and this was offered online. Serious mistake. The assignments are very hard and the professor essentially makes you use AI to learn everything and do the assignments. However, on exams, you cant use AI which makes them very difficult.

By far the worst professor I've had at Northeastern. As someone with ZERO excel experience/knowledge, I took this course thinking it would be an introductory course (1000 course). But, this professor has decided to overcomplicate topics as if we're all experts at CS, designed hellish weekly assignments, and the TAs are unhelpful.
I'm an economics and business administration major, and this class was rough. Tests were hard, tons of homework, and honestly just not worth it if you're not a CS major. Wouldn't take it again.
Assignments took hours and hours and made absolutely zero sense. If you are an Econ major and need this for reqs take either of the other courses offered and save yourself.
If you're a CSSH major (or basically just not cs and don't have much experience w/ excel) avoid taking this class. All i can say is thank god there were makeup exams otherwise I would have failed
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I spent one week in this class before dropping it. I cried myself to sleep every single night. Most of the TA's are useless except the girl one. This class is impossible if you have no cs background. Holy hell. Zero guidance, no one teaches you anything, actual hell on earth. Run, run, run, run, run, run.

This class was hybrid. The online portion was very easy, I had an A. However, the lab portion of this class was stupidly difficult. It did not match the online portion and Dr. Lieberherr did not seem to understand that this was an intro level class for non-CS majors. Assignments took HOURS to complete, and he made us use ChatGPT to teach ourselves.

I took this class as a requirement for Criminal Justice, but dropped it without a W a few weeks in. Online lecture material is taught by a different professor and is barely (if at all) related to weekly assignments. Weekly assignments take multiple hours a day to complete, they are confusing and frustrating. I do not recommend this class at all.
Run. Whole class tested 33% average score on exam 1, we all almost failed. I am an elite academic and had never withdrawn from anything ever. I withdrew from this. Run, you will not pass. Run.

Genuinely the worst course I have ever taken. This professor does not teach, and he relies on ChatGPT, yet you can not use it on exams. The TAs grade everything! It is way too difficult for an intro class, and just horrible. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Run.
honestly save yourself while you can.

This class is unnecessarily difficult for an intro class. Assignments take 12+ hours to complete, so it just feels like the work is never-ending. Weekly lab sessions are essential because it's the only time you can get in-person help. Go to TA office hours even if you feel like your question is insignificant because the grading can be harsh.

This class was basically Excel 101 which is super helpful for future jobs. Almost all of the learning is done outside of class on your own time. We met once a week and the professor would work through problems. The assignments can be tedious and long but are doable. The use of ChatGPT plus was required for the class.

Prof Lieberherr isn't uncaring towards his students, he is just so out of touch with them he doesn't realize how unrealistic his curriculum is. The hw & online modules were extremely outdated and clearly hadn't been revised in a while. Helpful when I would come to him for office hours, thats abt it. Unreasonably difficult class. Avoid if possible.

If you have to take this course I'm sorry, it is impossibly hard due to Prof Lieberherr. The online course material is confusing and hard to follow. The in-class labs are useless, when you ask a question he will pull up ChatGPT and tell you how it will answer it. Assignments and exams are hard to read and deceptive in what part is being graded

This professor does not teach anything, only advice I have for you is to make sure to show up to class because the one-hour labs per week is useful to completing SOME parts of the 4-5 hour long time-consuming assignments. Way too much content for an introductory course, and way less teaching. Now he has implemented chat-GPT teaching, good luck.

Weekly 1 hour class barely scratched the surface of what we actually needed to know for the assignments. Highly advise against taking this class unless it's a requirement, you will be countless hours working on the weekly project. There are 2 exams each worth 25% of the grade, so you have no choice but to learn it

Online lectures are useless. They tell you the basics of functions but you must figure out how to use them. Lab sessions are essential, as he goes through assignment for the week and teaches you how to do it. Quizzes easy grade boosters, but assignments are confusing, unclear, time consuming and hard.
