3. BAD Communication (essay-style instruction for each homework, has to be read very carefully, otherwise F is waiting for YOU)
4. The left brain attacks the right brain

Unfortunately, she does not know what she is teaching. Although she is a great person and cares for her students, I had to learn all the course material myself because she cannot teach. 

Great person, horrible teacher.
The professor is very sweet and approachable, but she's not very skilled at teaching and the class can be confusing. You will have to spend time outside of class to learn the materials yourself.

Don't believe the haters. Prof. Yeaman is awesome. She is super caring and works hard to teach us everyday. When she doesn't know something she admits it and then figures it out and updates us quickly. It's rare to find a teacher this caring and humble.

Yeaman is a sweet and kind soul, but barely knows what's going on herself. You can tell she cares for her students, but is just often time confused on the concepts as she is teaching them. Grading is pretty clear, and she does allow you to see what your grade is throughout the semester.

Professor Yeaman is very kind and sweet, but she knows nothing. Assignment take weeks to be graded, lectures are completely useless, and she's lost the entire time. If you genuinely want to learn, DON'T TAKE HER CLASS. If you just want an easy grade and have a basic understanding of the concepts, take it.
Does not have any knowledge of the material. Always lost.

You can tell Mrs. Yeaman is genuinely a kind soul, but she doesn't know what she is doing. Answering questions only leads to more confusion and she has stated that she is "learning with us". Grading is light so nobody is failing, but nobody has learned from class. Classes at Northeastern are expensive, and I didn't get anything out of this one.

Professor Yeaman is extremely kind but unfortunately she seems to not know any of the course material. Hopefully this is just a result of it being her first time teaching the course, but as it stands she is unable to make it through a lesson without confusing herself and the class.

doesn't really know what she is doing; class can get confusing if you don't know the material already. however, but she's super nice and the class is chill. grading is not too hard and assignments are easy; workload is not bad at all. tests are take home but can be confusing.

The pace is extremely slow, and yet she fails to understand the concepts of what she is teaching. Its as if she's learning with us and is seeing the slides for the first time while presenting. If you don't understand the basics of coding and CAD going in, she won't help you. You can watch a 10 min video to learn the same thing as an hour class

(Physics) His passion, adaptability, and genuine care for students creates an engaging learning environment. He adjusts his teaching to meet us where we are. His willingness to listen and reflect makes him stand out. He's transformed me into an active participant when I typically don't speak in class. I wish professors adopted his teaching style!

If you are a continuing education student who is decades past your last math class and not in a mathematical field you will have difficulty passing this class. Feed back on final paper was belittling to say the least but I did get an apology. Many in class dropped by third week. Professor makes the assumption math is all anyone should do. I MO

Took his class during the summer. He let you know from day one what was expected. LOT'S of homework (mostly bc it was a summer course and we had to crunch so much in). However, always there to help. Also, if something came up he was reasonable for extensions, etc. Great guy.
Very good at teaching the material. Highly recommend taking the class with him as you will learns lot

Possibly one of the best professors I've had so far. He knows his stuff and is genuinely interested in the performance of his students. He's also pretty funny. Best guy to have for Mechanics, hands down.
Best professor so far

The most engaging professor I had this term, and overall one of the 3 best professors I've ever had at Northeastern. He challenges students. Also, as a STEM education expert, he does research in how students best learn these topics, which means he is super good at teaching them.

Learning SolidWorks isn't really something you need a teacher to lecture for. He makes it harder by assigning lots of homework and having a harsh test grading distribution. At least once a class, he finds a way to berate his students/Gen Z population in general. He seems pretty stuck in his ways, and honestly looks and gives off Disney villain

He lacks empathy. It is truly fascinating how he is still teaching in this school, especially because every single upperclassman that I've talked to was just as traumatized. And I can tell you right now, he truly doesn't care what you think of him. There were times I believed he was here for the fun of seeing his students struggle.

Assignment instructions can be contradictory + vague. He often skims through slides without explaining. When he does explain, it's very helpful. You must attend class and show respect in order to do well.
nice guy, doesn't teach well and lecture is very long. Super work heavy class. 10-20 hours weekly.

He sold us his own textbook and every  class session was him reading the tutorials out of the book word for word. Every tutorial is click-by-click instructions. He managed to detract from the value of the textbook by making it distracting to follow along with his bumbling, half complete sentences. He would also insult us in class.

Professor Zeid is much better than many people say he is. Yes, his lectures may be long and boring, however, he does a good job at explaining the info and making sure that students understand the topic. Homework is long but good feedback is given on all of the assignments and help is very accessible. He will call you out for not paying attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the rudest professors at this university
So so class need do some work. Fairly easy. Homework a bit hard and heavy.

Professor Zeid doesn't care how his students study. He was my capstone instructor and he merely responded to your request to meet. Even though he agreed to meet he would tell you he cannot meet before the scheduled time without telling you the reason. DO NOT expect to communicate with him.
Awesome Professor. Tries his best to help our students. TA was accessible too. Helped in getting a good grade.
tests are bad

The course is useless. The entire semester was just aimed to study SOLIDWORKS, which is easy. It's a waste of time and money. If you already choose this. Remember don't spend too much time on it. And It's hard to communicate with professor after class.

Zeid really knows his stuff, and he teaches it right at the proper level for Industrial Engineers learning to write code. Some of it may seem to obvious at first, like the HTML, but trust me by the time you get into the more complex PHP, the level of intellectual challenge will make you learn a lot

Be ready to take notes! Zeid's method is to write on the chalkboard for the whole period and he expects you to take everything down. Willing to help. Somewhat lenient. If you have a decent reason that you couldn't complete an assignment just tell him, he will almost always help you out. Will probably learn the most in the lab though.

Great professor who very much cares about his students, their learning, and their success. I couldn't recommend any more! There isn't much work outside of class, and in class activities are genuinely fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Liao is a very caring and smart professor. His lectures are very insightful, but can run on.  He has many in-class activities and encourages everyone to participate. Attendance is mandatory, and not participating will hurt your grade. Overall, he is a great professor.
Amazing professor, amazing person who actually cares about his students. I wish more educators were like him.

Prof. Liao is the best choices for ORGB! Although he has an accent, he is very caring, very inspiring, and always wants his students to do their best in his class. He understands that high GPA is important for his students and as long as you put a decent amount of effort in, he will fairly award your hard work!

Very friendly and caring professor. He expected a lot from students, but he was always very good with feedback and communication. Lots of discussion based classes and the professor was always enthusiastic about the topic.

Professor Liao is one of the most caring and kind professors at NEU. It can be difficult to understand him at times due to his accent but his classes are extremely engaging and fun. You can see that he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Pay attention, ask questions, and remain engaged and you should be fine!

Very caring and respectful professor. Many interesting class discussion, but he'll not force anyone to speak. Many group work, and test is hard, but he will curve the grade so no worry. He give good feedback and always be a good listener to student's request. He is passionate about the lecture. Love him very much.

Great professor! Shows enthusiasm during classes and gives very thoughtful feedbacks on projects/emails. Lots of class discussion, but in a relaxed way (he won't force you to talk). He respects & values all students' ideas. He wants student to do well, and can extend ddl you have reasonable excuse. He actually makes the course very interesting.
No homework, quiz every week. Very important to study for this class

I had professor Zhang my first semester and she is such a caring and thoughtful professor. She is a very easy grader, but there are quizzes every week, two hour cumulative test, and a final. She is very rinse and repeat with problems and is overall a very nice person. Textbook is online and free given by her. Tests are like practice quizzes given

Very nice prof with quizzes basically every week, two hour tests, and a final. The previous quizzes she gives for practice are very helpful and I thought she was a decent lecturer, but hard to understand sometimes. Overall I would recommend her for calc 2!

Prof Zhang tries her best and is very caring and kind. I found that the lectures were hard to follow along but this improved over the semester. She's very knowledgeable but sometimes speeds over important concepts and through practice problems. There are weekly quizzes which are quite manageable but keeps the pressure high.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 0 material for exams review. Heavy and confusing poll questions popping up in class.

He somehow manages to move too quickly in class to follow and also be at least 1-2 lectures behind all other sections. Constantly having to use my friend's professor's slides just to finish the labs. He's quite passive aggressive and it just feels like a chore to have to be in this class.

I regret waking up every morning because I will have to suffer this class. He rushes through lectures and is passive-aggressive when students ask questions, yet we are still behind the other classes, which makes labs impossible. We just covered Lab 1 material...we're in the middle of Lab 3. For the exam, max 10 letters PER INCH on the cheatsheet.

Tests are beyond fair. Our first exam was so incredibly easy I couldn't believe it. I saw the work in my friends who are taking a different professor for this class and it seemed MUCH harder. He can be condescending and will call you out if you don't pay attention in class, but it's just because he wants you to learn. Would definitely take again.

Professor Aboelela is one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. He is caring and understanding and can explain topics really well. He might throw comments at students who aren't paying attention and be a little sarcastic, but if you are someone who can take jokes, you will absolutely love this side of him. Highly recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very great professor, Dr. Emad is passionate about his lectures and insures his students receive the help they need if asked. Would take again.

Like most COE coding classes, it was easy if you already know some coding, and probably horrible if you didn't. Very passionate about his lectures but they can still get a bit dry at times. Exams were quite easy and the labs are pretty easy as well (and the reports are a joke). Plus all lab stuff can be split with a partner.

Prof. Emad is really caring. He puts learning first instead of giving too much homework, which is one of the best things about him. If all teachers used his approach, the COE would be a lot better, and students would learn more without just struggling to finish homework. He's simply the best.

Professor Emad is highly regarded for his teaching abilities. His lectures are so well-structured and engaging that it's difficult not to grasp the subject matter. He is, without a doubt, among the best in his field.

Amazing professor. His in class slides are detailed and easy to learn from. He goes over many examples to ensure students understand the concepts. Midterms and homework are both VERY fair. He is also just a great guy and cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice professor with detailed slides. Even though the attendance is mandatory, he is still a good professor. Homework is resonable and useful.
Easy exams, easy homework. Class participation is quizzes in Poll everywhere that no matter if it is right or wrong.

I thought he taught the course well. It's clear he's passionate about the subject, and knows a lot about it. The grading is generous in my experience and I wouldn't hesitate to take one of his classes again in the future.

I don't understand all the hate for Emad. Had him for embedded, and I thought his lectures were interesting, and that he really broke everything down logically to make it easy to understand for the students. Visited office hours with him a few times, it is evident that he cares a lot about his students and gets excited when we are learning!
Good as far as EECE professors go

Spends 2 hours lecturing and often does multiple chapters in one day, there is practically no practice material and what little there is will not help you for tests. Lectures are boring and it is incredibly hard to know what is important and what is filler. Does not prepare students for exams and is then confused when the class average is a 50.
Super nice guy an so knowledgeable on terrorism and national security. Lots of reading but only af ew graded pieces of work that he doesn't put too much pressure on you grading wise.

Canvas is empty, he has a strong pro-I$rahell stance (because obviously)  which is way too evident and   and way too pro-Endian which at times got super vexing. All he does is talk and talk without any slides and does not let the session become interactive.

0 slides, he talks the entire class after watching 30 minutes worth of YouTube videos. Does NOT really tell you your grade until a week before final paper is due. Syllabus is 5 million years old and Canvas is barren. 0 rubrics, goes into depth abt prospectus and paper in 1 class. if you miss, you're cooked. best about him thing is his x account.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely knowledgeable however one of the most unenjoyable classes I've ever taken. At times it seems as if the prof himself doesn't even want to be teaching the course. Final grade is only dependent on a few assignments however he does not use canvas at all and barley provides feedback.

Your grade in this class is based on participation, one 10-minute presentation, and a final paper that's 10 pages long. Class is pretty chill; the professor talks the entire time from his desk with no slideshow or anything. It can be quite boring and make you want to fall asleep. Just make sure to share a thought once or twice every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting overview of the topic, though it was clear that the Professor's area of specialty is in terrorism as was clear through his lectures and recounting of personal experience. Overall interesting course and not too difficult

Terrorism and counterterrorism could only be taught by Max. He teaches seminar style, with him summarizing the readings and some videos, and then a class discussion, with him adding in his knowledge. Only 3 assignments, one presentation, one paper prospectus, and a 10 page paper, + participation (if you show up and talk a little pretty easy A)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Max gave great lectures and provided clear guidelines for his assignments. He made the course really interesting and I would recommend taking a course with him.

Unless you're incredibly interested in the subject, he can be a very boring professor. His lectures have very little structure because he's very knowledgable on the subjects, so this means it's super easy to get distracted and stop paying attention. I didn't enjoy the class but it wasn't awful. You'll be fine if you spend time on the final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor gives grade based on one presentation, participation, and final essay only and gives no feedback for any. Class is him basically just speaking with no presentation or anything and can get boring. He's very knowledgeable and very respected, just not the best professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice guy, knows more about terrorism than pretty much anybody. Only issue was entire grade was based on presentation and final paper and did not receive feedback on either. Would like if he used canvas rather than email for assignments.

Max is the best professor I have had in Northeastern's political science department. He is an expert in his field, yet still invites criticism and agile thought with regard to his own work. I strongly, strongly recommend taking a class with him if you can. I am writing this review because he's that good. Also an easy class if you engage with him.

Max is a great professor. He doesnt waste time talking about grading policies and other boring aspects of the course. Instead, hes all about imparting substantive knowledge. He wants to get you excited about international security. And he really does!
Great class discussion. Expert about ISIS and Al Qaeda and so many theories about terrorism. Fun paper assignment if you can think of a good topic.
Max is funny. He calls us counterterrorists. He knows a lot about terrorism and counterterrorism, a real expert. The reading list is huge but helpful for writing the final paper.

Prof Abrahms will challenge you to think differently about the world. You have to do lots of reading but there are no tests and the final paper gives you a lot of flexibility to come up with an original thesis. It was a very fun class.

Governments need to listen to this guy, really smart about fighting terrorists. ISIS expert. Too much reading but no exams and a final paper. Can get an A if you work really hard and participate in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Max is a very down to earth prof who doesnt take himself too seriously and teaches students to think more clearly and smarter about international affairs. I would def take him again.
Best prof. Knows his stuff. Will challenge you to think differently about international affairs. Ridiculously smart. Also a chill and funny guy.
Smart, very very smart
Really sharp guy
Knows everything about terrorism studies

Max is probably the most intelligent counter-terrorism professor. He constantly wants students to see the different views in this field. Classes may become very tedious and boring sometimes. He also requires students to do lots of readings between articles and his papers. He is always available in office hours and can help if you dont understand
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Extremely intelligent and one of the brightest minds on the subject of terrorism. Encourages students to question existing theories constantly.

I'm sorry to say that a lot of professors don't really care about their graduate students because they are so busy doing research.  Max isn't one of them.  He's a world class terrorism researcher and also on the news but he really helped me as a masters student to create my research design.  No other professor is this helpful.  Interesting lectures

If you are curious about the world around you, this class is for you. Max (he prefers that to being called "Professor") is super chill but you will come away from this class having a better understanding of the news, international politics, real world events, and human psychology.  This is hands down the best class I ever took at NU!

Chill guy, not much work to do in the class.  Took the graduate seminar along with an independent study with him.  Very discussion based, and lots of connections to terrorism.  As in, if you have no interest in terrorism, stay far away.  Fairly enjoyable and pretty lax grader (received full letter grade higher for similar paper)

Worst professor I have ever had at NU. Not understanding at all. Too sarcastic and its borderline offensive, and he simply does not care. Definitely a terrorism expert, but honestly I wish I hadn't taken this course with him.

Mostly a discussion based class, so participation is important. She's one of the sweetest profs I've met that genuinely cares for her students. Lectures can be info dense, but discussions are easier to follow along with. The community you find in that small classroom is very enlightening.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Summer 1 only graded by 2 papers and a midterm (short essays). Interesting material and insight from the professor but its all provided reading. (rating keep in mind im a bad essay writer)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Margot is a very sweet professor but her lecture style wasn't for me. The prompts for papers were vague and unclear, making this intro-level class more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Really good prof who cares about the students. Grades harshly so you have to work for a good grade and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Margot is super caring and always created a very comfortable class environment. Assigns lots of readings and most of the class is discussion-based. Margot is super flexible if you are uncomfortable talking in discussions. Lets students meet with her to discuss assignments and think of other ways to increase a participation grade.

Professor Abels is a very caring and interesting professor. Her class leaned a little too far into discussion for my taste, and sometimes it felt like an echo chamber of opinion (as someone who agreed with the opinions discussed it was a bit redundant). Overall, super informative and fun

The majority of the time we just had discussions in class, and if you just talk and add to the discussion you will definitely be fine. She assigns a TON of readings but you don't need to thoroughly read the majority of them, just skim and you will be fine. The class is echo chambery too - if you want discourse this isn't the class for you.
Grading too harsh for an intro-level course, instructions of papers are long and confusing.
Absolutely loved her!

Margot is very passionate about Women's Studies, but I don't think the intro class is the best for her to teach. Most of our work was graded and reviewed by the TA, not her. It was also a little scattered with topics and most lectures turned into random class discussions that somewhat related to what we were learning. Very interesting, and easy A.

Margot was a lot of fun as a professor. She's very sweet and understands you have a life outside of class. There is a lot of reading but a lot of it can be skimmed. The classes are very discussion based and you participation is a percentage of your grade. Essay and discussion heavy. The TA usually grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Margot is an amazing professor! Her lectures are very discussion based and she genuinely respects all her students. I wish I could take more classes with her.

Very unclear and difficult grading criteria with all assignments graded by the TA. Lectures were sometimes meandering and focused too much on discussion. It's expected that you agree with what she says.
he was lowkey ragebaiting us the whole semester but the class is an easy A. you won't learn a thing tho lol

He was not organized or professional. He showed up to class late, and all exams had errors; he makes MCQs that are unclear (e.g., all four answer choices are wrong, or two choices are equally right). Also all homework is in groups, so everyone receives the same grade even though some people barely do their part.

He really cares about his students succeeding. Sometimes his class could get tedious and wasn't very clear in terms of assignments in the grade book but he's very passionate about the topic and very intelligent. Also just wants his class to do well

Best prof ever. His lectures can be a little confusing and disorganised but he is very smart and passionate about what hes teaching. THE TESTS ARE SOOO EASY. I dont understand how he has such a bad rating he is just so nice :( He also makes all the exams open note and doesnt even show up for them. I highly recommend you take his class!!
he is super hard to understand and he does often ramble about politics and nonsense but either way its an easy grade if you know what you're doing

No idea what's going on! You'll probably be saying this if you take him too. Easygoing, understanding and very smart, but he cannot teach. Never knew what he was ever rambling on about, tedious homework assignments and an inconsistent syllabus. Professor's smart and not uptight; but everyday I left class with more questions than answers. What a guy

Professor really likes to yap, while often being off topic. Midterms were dumb, he sent emails 20 minutes before that he wouldn't even be in the room for the midterm so i wasted like a week studying for them. Also homework assignments are TERRIBLE, all online on achieve where each little module is SUPER time consuming if done earnestly.

This class was low key psychological warfare. He tells us the midterm is closed note, but doesn't even show up for the exam? Studied 20 hrs for NOTHING!! He's so smart but cant teach for shit and talks about random history that isn't even relevant to the course. Half the class was spent laughing to myself like a crazy person asking if we was real.

This professor is TERRIBLE. He assigns everything through Achieve, and does nothing on his own. He assigns 40 tedious assignments a week, and he doesn't even grade them (autograded). He assigned a midterm on Memorial Day, and it was only available to take on that day. Do not take his class if you actually want to learn/want an enjoyable class.

If you're considering this online class, DONT. Canvas is inaccurate, and the due dates didn't match what was on Achieve, making it confusing to know what assignments were due. It added unnecessary stress, and I spent more time trying to figure things out than focusing on the material.

Prof. Mughal is a true academic, simple as that. You are there to learn; he provides that experience. While the actual course content can be hard to digest at times, Prof. Mughal does a fabulous job breaking down complexities. You should ask questions if you're confused. This is the best ECON2315 prof, not even close. Online content hard to follow
amazing professor, so kind, good at teaching, passionate.

Love this woman. Very clear lectures, frequently pauses for questions, and quizzes are literally pulled directly from the HW. She also gives you multiple practice midterms and finals that are almost identical to the real thing. Best math instructor I've ever had, and a super easy A if you do the bare minimum amount of work. Definitely recommend!

Took her for geometry but that wasn't an option so posting here. She's an incredibly nice woman, but the class took up an irrational amount of time for a math elective, and the grading was unnecessarily harsh.

Professor Williams clearly cares about her students and is passionate about what she teaches. I enjoyed this class a lot, and it was very straightforward. Quizzes are just HW problems and all the notes are posted on Canvas so it's not hard to do well in this class even if you miss lectures. Would highly recommend!
Really nice person and thoroughly explained topics during lectures. Would take again. Good lecturer.
She is super passionate and absolutely loves what she does, which makes the class better. I have always struggled in math, but her lectures made sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very great teacher go to class take notes and you'll be fine she moves fast but very good at explaining everything and quizzes once a week but if you do the homework they are easy and the exact problems from the homework
Amazing. Best professor I've ever had at Northeastern. If you put in some work, you are almost guaranteed an A.

I'm not a natural in math, but I loved Professor Williams' course! She was always quick to respond to emails, gave extra credit if you did the homework, and quizzes/midterm had reasonable questions on lessons she covered thoroughly beforehand. This class takes effort, but she definitely teaches the course fairly, which helps a thousand times over.

Best calc teacher in all of Northeastern. She genuinly tries to make an effort to teach the class and is engaging with all students. 36% quizzes which are verbatim hw problems but it takes time to understand them so beware, 24% midterm and 40% final. If u stay on top of homework and use all practice materials, u should get an A (99 on final).

Dr. Williams is one of the most caring and supportive professors I've ever had, even though I math isn't my strongest subject and I was struggling a bit in her class. She provides so many resources (past exams/lectures) that are so helpful when studying and helped me do well on the final exam. Genuinely makes calculus fun and easier to understand.

Honestly an amazing professor. She did a great job explaining calc. Had taken calc in high school so was a repeat pretty much but things i was confused on she was always willing to help. quizzes were basically homework, exams were exactly the same as practice tests especially the final. she sets you up to succeed - couldn't recommend more!

one of the best math teachers I've ever had. Quizzes are verbatim hw questions, and you can get extra credit for them. Midterm and Final are super similar to past exams and she's super accessible if you need any additional help

She is honestly the best math professor/teacher I have ever had. The content on the quizzes all comes from homework and the midterm and final were very clear and pretty much the same as the past papers. She really cares about her student and explain content very well. Take her class!

This class (Geometry, no option to select) was extremely difficult. All the exams were take home, and they took HOURS to complete. She was very specific with her proofs, and she was not very lenient with grading. While she is very enthusiastic, I do not recommend taking this class. I do not feel like I have grown as a student with this class.
Great professor. She doesn't go too fast and tries to make class enjoyable.
Caring professor but not the best lecturer in my opinion. Good amount of homework and quizzes every week. Could've explained topics better
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Williams is the nicest and most caring professor I have had. Calc 2 is a difficult concept but she made it a lot easier with her lectures and examples. She was also accessible for office hours and very patient and helpful in them. If you have the option to take a class taught by her, do it without a second thought, there's nobody better.
Dr. Williams is an AMAZING Calculus professor. The course itself is test heavy no matter what, but she is good at explaining the concepts and she is a fair grader. I couldn't recommend her more.

We love Abby. I had a horrendous calc 1 prof and I was scared going into calc 2, but she was immediately willing to help whenever needed. She makes math so easy and approachable. I used to dread math, but now I dread it less because of Abby. She is so sweet and caring. Take her for any class if you can!

One of my favorite professors at NEU. Williams is so sweet and genuinely wants students to do well. The quizzes are verbatim homework questions and the tests are always on topics we covered and not a surprise. Highly recommend

Content-wise - it's such an easy class. There is a lot of busy work with the in-class activities and homework. She is a very harsh grader when it comes to the problem of the week and portfolios. There aren't clear guidelines and expectations, so she takes off a lot of points for things she never specified, which can be very frustrating.

Prof. Williams is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. She's a great lecturer who clearly has a passion for teaching and is always willing to help. I would highly recommend taking her for any math class at Northeastern.

She is awesome and so nice. As a Political Science/Journalism major, I wasn't ecstatic about taking a math class. She made it simple, fun, and I learned a lot. If you're like me it'll probably be the first math class you've ever fully enjoyed. If you do the homework, get her feedback on the portfolios, and do the practice tests, you will get an A.

If I had another math requirement, I would choose Abby again in a heartbeat. As a journalism/poli sci major, I had no interest in taking math again and was dreading what ended up being my best course of the semester. She genuinely cares about you and your understanding of the material. She's flexible on attendance but definitely recommend going.

Dr. Williams is the kindest and most understanding professor I've ever had. She's brilliant when it comes to math and has two PHDs. She understands we have other classes and other things on our plates and never over loads students with work. Make sure to go over study guide before exam. Exams are easy of you know the study guide.
Great professor, her lectures are super easy to follow and make the tests pretty easy (as long as you practice). Definitely recommend.
I would die for Dr. Williams. She is so compassionate and patient and she got me to look forward to math, which is insane. If you have the opportunity, take her!

I absolutely loved Professor Williams' class. She kept me engaged in calculus, something that is very difficult for me. She is a very fair grader and gives tons of partial credit on tests. Her lectures truly are great and she is passionate about what she teaches. A true gem at Northeastern!

Lots of info and course content is all what he says in lecture. Online tests were reasonably difficult and final bird ID test was very fun. Loved this class and bird trips!

Professor Roth is very passionate about birds! I took bird class to fulfill my population and organismal biology requirement, but I really enjoyed it and learned a lot. Exams were all online take-home, and we got to go bird watching in the Fens for some of our classes. I would definitely recommend to anyone looking for a fun and easy elective!

Quizzes are based entirely on his lectures even if that's not what is factually correct, a lot is misspelled, very little time allotted, and his slides are written horribly. In the class I took, his quizzes were weighed the same as the midterm and final exam. Easy enough professor, but prepare to be frustrated.
All I have to say is, he is an icon, he's a legend, and he is the moment. Truly hilarious, but professional,  professor. Will make you laugh until you cry. He ate.

took this course summer 2 for nupath requirement and it consisted of 2 group projects and weekly discussion boards + mastering hws. honestly i loved this class bc it was really interesting, yet not hard at all. really recommend

He's super nice and funny, but the material can be difficult towards the end. There is a massive amount of material on exams, but if you study and take really good notes, you'll be fine. Exams are usually 60% multiple choice and 40% essay, and he lets you know what the essay questions will be about beforehand. The final was not cumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Aaron is one of the best professors I've had at NU. He makes every lecture into a story, clearly knows his stuff, and he wants all of his students to succeed. We even had a day bird watching trip. For vertebrate anatomy there can be some small details on the exams, but if you take good notes during the class and study before, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's one of my favorite professors I've ever had. I took comp. avian structure (AKA bird class) with him and it was very straightforward. Your grade is based off 2 midterms and the final, which are all multiple choice and very easy if you take note of what he says during class. His slides are very bare though, so it is important to attend class.

Took comparative avian structure and function with Aaron. The man knows his birds and is absolutely hilarious. Fairly easy class, he really just likes talking about things he wants to talk about (birds, his disdain for his dogs, spatchcocking, Victorious) and isn't trying to fail anyone. Not a bad choice for an upper bio elective with no lab

Aaron is amazing! I took his Bio and Society course during a summer semester and he made the course easy but meaningful. I wasn't a good bio student in high school but the contents that he taught and included in his powerpoints got me really interested and finished the course with an A. I took his class for nupath requirement, highly recommended:)

Lectures are fun and interesting, exams are very easy (all multiple choice), and he's pretty laid back. If you haven't taken a basic bio class before, it will be difficult because he doesn't explain things in detail.

Aaron is hands down the best professor I have ever had. He brings profound storytelling experience to the classroom in a laid-back way, as a result, his teaching effectiveness is substantial and needs proper recognition. If you are interested in the sciences or are considering a STEM career, I cannot recommend a better place to start.

I graduated 4 years ago and I still say Aaron Roth was my favorite professor. Super dry sense of humor and passionate about zoology when he gets going. He introduced us to a hilarious YouTube series about weird animals and we spent a Mammalogy class in the Fens listening to him nerd out about birds. 10/10 would get a beer with Roth.

Took this class online during Summer 1. I did not read a single chapter of the textbook or watch a single lecture yet got an A. If you have already taken a bio class you will do well in this course. Graded by weekly discussion posts and textbook assignments (which you will get good scores on if you already took a bio class), and 2 group projects.

Professor Roth is super chill and hilarious! Don't get me wrong, he knows his stuff! Took his BIO1100 on Saturdays and the lectures were about 3 hours long. He knows how to keep the class entertained while teaching us about things that can get a bit boring. Be sure to take notes though because his slides are minimal and only made for reference

I took comparative avian structure and function with Aaron Roth and it was one of my favorite classes I've taken at Northeastern. He's a great teacher, super funny and engaging and his tests are totally fair. The slides had barely any info on them so you had to go to class to get the notes, but other than that class was a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Literally the best professor I have ever had. His lectures are great. He is hilarious. His exams are straight forward. You will enjoy learning in this class.
BEST PROF EVER. You come out of his class having learned SO much. He makes 11/10 Dad jokes, and doesn't expect you to memorize everything for his exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor and very understanding, super easy online class, prob best bio prof at NEU
Super chill guy, pretty easy summer online class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dope teacher. Higher than a 4.4
Great Professor ever had. This guy is good and he knows his stuff.
VERY HELPFUL. HAS GREAT ABILITY  TO MAKES HARD STUDY TOPICS MAKES FUN AND EASY. HE IS ONE OF THE VEST PROFESSORS IN MY ALL STUDY LENGTH.

Roth is the funniest professor I've had so far.  I took his Inquiries into Bio on Zoonotics & really enjoyed it.  His lectures were informative & he always managed to squeeze in some really cringey yet twisted yet hilarious jokes in there.  You can't just skip and rely on the online slides though.  All his tests are given on Blackboard :)

Roth is 100% the best professor you will ever have! His lectures are SO interesting.  He's also really funny and an all around cool guy!  His tangents are always hilarious and keep you entertained.  If you're confused on something don't hesitate to go to his office hours, he's really helpful one on one.  Not an easy A, but worth the work!
Professor Roth is a really great guy. I liked his class a lot, and he is pretty funny.   Help is there if you need it, but most people get by with mild studying.
Well respected, Very understanding, Provides plenty of time to complete assignments.

GO TO CLASS. His powerpoints for VertZoo are a bunch of photos, so if you miss class, you'll have to get notes or you just won't have anything. He's a zoologist so he cares about the class a lot and loves questions from the class. Hands down most interesting class I've taken at NU.

Respectful, understanding and very hardworking professor. Roth is by far my favorite biology professor. He's so clear, passionate about what is teaches, easy going and respects his students. He's funny and the way he present the course is so interesting and funny that not only you understand it but he makes you interested in the subject.

very nice, funny guy. midterm was somewhat tough but he gave an extra credit assignment. all quizzes and final were online, taken at your own leisure. course was dumbed down a little compared to elsewhere but I also retained a ton more because of how laid back the setup was. Roth's tangents also improved my overall Bio intuition a ton. highly rec!

Had this guy for a course called Animal, a course about Animal, the psychotic drumming muppet from Dr. Teeth and The Electric Mayhem.  Roth is basically a cool cat all around. Very casual, and more importantly he knows his stuff. Ask him any question. If you can't get an A, you didn't spend enough time stdying or you aren't a cool enough cat.
He's very funny, interactive and makes the course even more interesting than it already is. The course itself if pretty intense but he makes it fun.

Great Teacher, he makes class worth going to, hes really nice and really tries to help everyone understand, he can speak a little fast but its not bad. His tests are hard but you'll do fine if you study and go to class. Plus it helps that he's a funny guy, friendly and easy to talk to if you need help.

hes a really nice personable guy who cares about his students. really knowledgeable and gets excited about what he teaches, so sometimes goes on about things that wont be tested on. makes class fun to go to. definitely recommend

I took General Bio2 with him, and it was a very intense course. It wasn't difficult but there's too much information to know! His lectures are very boring, but unfortunately, his exams heavily depend on what he says in lecture. His exams aren't impossible, but his questions are specific.

He's nice and apparently very engaging because people would not stop raising their hands in my class to the point where I became very annoyed. He's cares about all his students regardless of class size and he even gave me an A- when I had an 89.1 at the end of the semester. He does, however, mention too much information that is not tested on.
He is extremely funny, which makes me want to go to class.

Hes a great teacher. Makes class fun and entertaining. He obviously knows everything about bio and wants to share it with the students. His tests are difficult and you have to study a lot for them but theres no secret, just take good notes and read the book. Its gen. bio 1 so its not that  hard but if you put the work in and listen  your golden

He's legit. You'll like him. Many nervous laughes. Always willing to help. Loves loves loves bio. He'll teach you everything he knows and put 50 questions on the midterm- Tip: think "what would Roth test me on".

Awesome, hilarious guy. Great teacher. Definitely take gen bio with him. Really straightforward, fair. Super easy class if you put some work in. Don't ever need textbook. Will tell you what will be on exam in class sometimes, so go to class.

He's young, he's funny, and he loves teaching. You will love taking Bio with him, and if you don't get an A it's your own fault.  Misspellings plague his PPT's but at least he has a PPt and animation for every topic you'll cover. I looked forward to this class everyday.

This guy is hands down the best science teacher I've ever had. He has really funny digressions and jokes and keeps us entertained throughout the class. I wouldn't want to be in any other Bio class if he wasn't my professor. Thankfully Im taking Bio 2 next semester with him. If you have this professor for bio, be very grateful.

Aaron Roth is the perfect professor to teach Gen. Biology 1. He makes the class interesting and fun even while talking about the Kreb's cycle.  The tests are easy, especially if you have a background in biology. Nevertheless, you should still study. Don't buy the textbook unless you have never taken bio before, then you should.
He's a great teacher, teaches from slides but makes it interesting.  Tests aren't bad as long as you go to lecture and study moderately before the exams.
Simply he's the greatest teacher ever. He's helpful,nice,and funny.It's not enough to say he's the best.I highly recommend taking any of his courses.

So good.  vert zoo with him was fun, but be prepared to do a lot of studying/memorizing.  He really knows his stuff and doesnt expect miracles from the class.  the exams are easy as long as you study, and the same goes for lab.  highly recommend getting in one of his classes

I loved his class. I was considering changing my major because my professor before him was awful. But he made me love bio again. It's a hard class because it's all memorization, but he makes it easy and clear. I wish he taught more so I could take me classes with him.

He is very good teacher to have.  His tests are easy as long as you show up for the lectures.  He can take very boring subject and make it seem exciting.  I was dosing off and DYING of boredom in general bio 1, but for Arron's class which was general bio 2,I was very interested in lectures.

Engages class in very interesting discussions. Be aware if you take any stance other than the traditional evolutionary view (like if you point out contradictions to evolution theory) that he'll mark you off on tests and won't bother to acknowledge valid points, etc.

He is an awesome teacher. Def my favorite so far. His lectures are all online. He really understands college kids and he tries to make everything interesting. He's funny and relaxed and his tests are hard but nothing on them is unexpected. He often gives test questions in classes so you should go.

He has experience as a field biologist and likes to use his stories to help teach the class.  As long as you attend class, take notes/pay attention you should do fine.  He's actually really fairly interesting/lively/funny if you participate if you make him feel like he isn't talking to a class that's just staring at him.

very good teacher. he is good at and comfortable with public speaking=interesting to listen to. done lots of cool research and knows a lot, young & funny! gets class involved, cares about what he does & wants you to learn. lots of materialPPT lectures & reviews posted online. lab practicals are pretty tough but dont count for much. very fair guy, A

I think he's pretty new, so he's still developing a teaching style. A power point teacher...speaks for itself.  Class can be monotonous, but he will get excited if the class shows interest.  Tests are multiple choice, very detail oritented, but his pre-test reviews are pretty comprehensive.
HORRIBLE

Ron Thomas is one smart cookie! He gave great lectures and he has a voice like a grandfather-- so soothing. His sylabus made it seem like we were gonna be loaded down with work, but there really werent many assignments. Just dont be lazy and do zero of the readings cause he's gonna call on you, he ain't dumb he knows when you didnt read. Love u Ron

Great guy, cares a lot about his students and has a vast array of knowledge. However, his grading policy and habits are confusing and sporadic and the group TJX project is a nightmare. Doesn't convey directions or deadlines very effectively. In class debates and discussions are useful and informative.
Great professor, he always makes clear what he expects from you. Has a lot of knowledge and cares very much for his students. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The group project was kinda annoying but he gave great feedback and was very helpful throughout the process. Other than that the class was super easy with only a few essay type tests which most people got Bs on which is fine.
Professor Thomas made the overwhelming topic of international business very interesting and manageable. He really, really cares about the subject matter and all of his students. I would

Overall , professor Thomas is a great teacher who is passionate about what he does. But, he is a hard grader! He will criticize every small detail of your work! Be prepared to work a lot and participate in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He is nice and kind. His lectures are clear and interesting. However, he is definitely a tough grader and he gives a lot, a lot, a lot of Homework (reading, essay, mini essay,...). The hw given in his syllabus is understated. Be prepare to do much more than what you saw in the syllabus.
Ron is a great professor, and is very helpful both inside and outside the classroom. There is not much homework, but he is a tough grader on tests and the final projects.

Avoid! Super hard grader. Unless he likes you it doesnt matter how hard you try you wont get an A. I studied for the quiz got a B-I didnt study for the 2nd quiz, still got a B-shows me he is biased based on his opinion of you. My group slayed the presentaion, still got a B Unless he likes you A-is impossible let alone an A. Harder than it should be

He's probably the hardest grader I've ever had.  Not even that he holds you to a ridiculously high standard (which he does), but that standard is unclear, and often swayed by his personal opinion.   Make a claim in a presentation and support it with evidence?  Incorrect.  He read something different. Class dragged on, most fall asleep.

Probably the BEST professor I have ever had. If you put in your best effort, participate you will get a good grade. After taking a class with him last semester I loved it so much I took public speaking this semester because he teaches it. The discussions in class, his enthusiasm, intellect, humor makes class so much fun! Take his class you can!!!

A very smart man. His lectures are based off the textbook. Be sure to read and participate in class. His exams are essay based so you really need to know you stuff. And you do a market entry project. Be creative and know your project well; don't read off of your powerpoints. He is really bad about returning grades.
He is charming teacher. Very respect to students, if you have any problem, he will help you friendly. Even though his class is not that interesting, but you will love him.

True that he's intelligent, and coursework is stimulating but his style is dry and boring, doesn't have much personality. Expects a lot but doesn't give much back in return- he's awful about giving grades back. Extremely critical of presentations, focuses more on presentation skills than content.

Awesome professor. He is really really smart, he definitely knows a lot and has the experience to teach us highly valuable things. He was highly respectful of students and really cares about what you have to say (as long as it's not dull). The class is really challenging though, it is a capstone class. He's my favorite professor ever.
Overall good class. Project was challenging.

Excellent professor. Interesting class and learned a lot. Project is challenging and during the summer it is a time crunch. Exams are straight forward and a lot of writing. Prof. Thomas knows what he is doing and has a lot to offer in this course. I highly recommend him for IB social and would take another IB course with him later.

Great Professor! He knows almost everything about Buz. world. If you are someone who really want to learn, def. take him! otherwise not, because he's exams(blue books) are hard, you need to write for 2hours full non stop. Whereas some other professors giving out multiple choices in the exams.

He's awesome. a great and interesting teacher. project is a lot of work but ultimately pretty rewarding, and if you mess something up he's always willing to hear you out if it's reasonable. definitely take his class!!

Awesome, brilliant guy. Unbelievable smart and shares his extensive knowledge during lectures. pretty liberal graders and just a great guy overall. only complain is the project - very similar to intro to business project, but assigned it halfway through the year and very in depth. i would definitely recommend him.

Prof. Thomas brings to life the materials of his class and explains the relevance in history and present day. He strives to provide a full understanding of the material and delivers interesting lectures even on dry topics.

Prof. Thomas has a great intellect and a strong lecture style that keeps the attention of the class focused and interested. He assigns a lot of work but it's relevant to the class material and exams. Great professor; he is insightful, up to date with the world, and has a great point of view and internaional voice.

Very intelligent and interesting guy.  He really knows whats going on in the world and gets you that information in an easy way.  The tests involve a lot of details, but it isn't hard to do well.  Big market entry project at the end of the year weighs a lot on your grade but it isn't hard, just time consuming...take this class!
Profesor thomas is one of the BEST teachers i have ever had. he makes the course veryvery interesting, although you will have to work. I will surely take him next semester
Great teacher. Hard class. Hard project. Learned alot. If you read the cases and listen him/take notes you will learn alot and really appreciate the class.
The best professor at NU, although there may be a heavy workload
Very well prepared and clear in class. Not a whole lot of surprises in this course, but you'll still learn a lot.

Very respectful, wise and correct. Very preparated about any topics and issues. One defect; He gives to many hands out, after two classes you re not even able anymore to fit all those papers in your bagpack.
The best Professor at Northeastern

Professor Thomas is perhaps the smartest man in the entire Northeastern University. Absolute genius.  No matter what your major or concentration is, you should try and take one of his classes. You will have to read a good amount of text for each class.  His exams are not too hard either.
Very smart guy - he really cares about what students have to say. Extremly respectful

This guy is a pro at what he does. Extreamly educated in internationl business. has a phd in physcology. Very interesting class, its actually enjoyable believe it or not... I only have 1 warning.. be prepared to do alot of work and reading. but its worth it, b/c u will walk out of that class with a brighter sense of international business
This class is very interesting. The professor's teaching method is great because he tries to always provide more points of view to a topic.

Prof. makes class extremely interesting through a mix of videos, readings, presentations, facts, articles etc.  Promotes an intellectual curiosity never so far matched by any professor or mentor; this guy is brilliant!!
Has a great way of teaching which promotes curiosity and understanding.

the Prof. is extremely knowledgeable and I loved the class.  You do have to do a lot of work, but its not hard.  Overall the class was really helpful in learning whats going on in the world and very interesting at that.  He's a cool guy
Boring class.  Easy A, if you can do tedious work, does not require too much thinking, just memorization of facts.  However, Thomas is very knowledgable about international business.

Probably one of the most knowledgeable prof. i have ever met. The class is really interesting at first but gets kind of boring towards the end. I would still recomend takin a class with him, you will learn alot
really knowledgable guy. the class can sometimes make you sleepy, but i still learned a lot.
Great professor!

Graded heavily on groupwork and very few assignments. Doesn't teach much in class, mostly info is from readings (A LOT). Makes some racially questionable comments and "cold calls" students for participation (graded heavily). Cheat sheet allowed on exams too. The class wasn't super difficult, but there are just so few opportunities to earn points.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm not sure why Prof Aguilera has these negative reviews, she always provided good feedback to all groups, and yes participation matters for your grade but if you do the reading you'll be fine. She's caring for her students, and maybe she's changed since others had her. I enjoyed her emerging markets class and learned a lot.
Would highly recommend taking this course! Professor was super knowledgeable and kind.

Awesome professor at Northeastern. Brought in very high profile guest speakers to class. She cold calls and is literally RUTHless, I loved it. Anyone who has her is lucky. Just put in a decent amount of effort in assignments and participate (Easy A).
A lot of home work. Pop quizzes. One 30 minute long group presentation during the semester. She was okay.

Her pop quizzes suck and the grading can be harsh, but she's really nice and an interesting and reputable person to learn from. In general, I don't think a lot of her low ratings are warranted and its not too hard to succeed in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class would've been fine without the pop quizzes and the professor's sometimes unfair standards. Barely enough time was given to do the pop quizzes, and she randomly chose 2 people from each group to present, but some groups were allowed to have everyone present. She's clearly knowledgable in the subject but sometimes it comes off as bragging.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: You can do all your work in this class and still perform badly. The pop quizzes are killer, with less than thirty seconds to answer a question (no going back). Plus she grills you mid-presentation and made racist comments. The cases we read were fine and she is knowledgeable but her grading is harsh (especially on participation). Do not take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable but is somewhat disorganized and harshly grades only a few assignments. This course isnt super hard but its hard to get a good grade if you dont consistently do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ruth is one of the best professors at Northeastern. She is funny and straightforward, which is rare these days, with professors reading slides and calling it a day. The cases we used in class were insightful and applied to the real world. Don't be mad someone with a personality is teaching you...

This woman is a cartoon villain akin to the likes of the Joker. Timed pop quizzes 30 seconds per question or less (you can't go back). Interrupts group presentations all the time, makes racist micro-aggressive comments, grades participation out of 3 (never gives 3s), and made the first assignment due before the class even started. Trust me, AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I am currently taking the course. She is very forward(not in a good way) and definitely makes some questionable comments towards students. She lacks general respect towards her students: interrupting during presentations to tell groups they need to hurry up and  telling other students that a student presenting is "bs-ing".

The worst Professor I have ever had. She made comments to students that were inappropriate/racist. The work she assigned was inconsistent between students. Her pop quizzes often had typos. She made extremely disrespectful comments to my group project team and me when we approached her with a question. I would avoid her at all costs.
He was a super understanding and fair professor. If you are to take an online course for political science take his. I've never had such an organized professor, nevermind being online. Great guy.

Professor Agatstein cares so much about his students, explains things clearly, gives relevant examples, is very understanding about giving extensions + grades kindly. He would have a class every couple of weeks dedicated to letting us access his knowledge + ask him about things going on in the world from an IR perspective. Best professor I've had.

Professor Agatstein is an intelligent, organized, and kind professor. Overall, if you are looking for a good, chill class with a Professor who knows his stuff, take his class!! He is excellent at considering each student's needs while being fair to the entire class. His specialty in humanitarian crises is fascinating.

He's super chill. The class was weekly essays, and the same went for the final project. He's a really fair grader and was super understanding. Definitely a great online course, and managed everything well.

Great professor! The classes are discussion-based, and he always makes sure to explain the material thoroughly. Provides study guides for exams and posts all lecture presentations, which is super helpful!

I have never rated a professor before, but I have to, for Dr. Agatstein was amazing. I loved his discussions, as they were always interesting and relevant. He doesn't force you to reply. All assignments are argumentative essays, which I love. He responds quickly and gives great constructive feedback. Great class to take for NU Path or for credit.

Do not take this class with her if you are a STEM major or have ANY other demanding classes! I was taking Orgo at the same time and I genuinely feel like she lowered me a letter grade by requiring 2+ hours of my time every night doing homework, projects, or essays. However, the class will definitely improve your Spanish speaking and writing!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The class material wasn't necessarily difficult, but she assigns lots of homework and will assign homework on topics before teaching them, which can make homework difficult and confusing and can lead to poor homework grades. She also comes off as rude very often and if she is in a bad mood she will take it out on students.

Hands down least favorite class and professor in my 5 years. She is an advisor and uses it to plug her own class even if its not right for the student. Came to her for extra help every week and still almost failed me/made me drop the minor(got >B+ In my other Spanish classes). Also a pronunciation class is so useless u dont learn a single word

Made an account solely to her. I am a bioengineering student.... this woman is more organized, more professional, and altogether a better teacher than anyone I've ever had in the STEM departments of northeastern. She made an online class (fall 2020) engaging and personal and fun. love her tons and could not rec her more! lotta work but worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved both of the 3000 level courses I took with her. Her classes aren't easy, no matter what level, but she always knows how to break it down for all types of learners.

She is nice, accessible outside of class, & willing to reexplain concepts during office hours. Authentic Spanish Grammar was a difficult class b/c the material was high-level & could be complicated, plus there were a lot of assignments, essay, videos, & readings, but tbh I didn't read everything & still did fine. It's a summer course so fastpaced.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Her special topics spanish classes are hybrid classes, so half online half in person. Her RISE lectures are super detailed & contain a lot of links & videos. You definitely learn a lot of material but it's a project-based class so no tests or memorization. She can be a picky grader but if u go to her office hours & do what she says you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not listen to comments that say that she gives too much homework!! This was the BEST SPANISH CLASS AT NORTHEASTERN. I cant even tell you how much I learned, the flip classroom is great and there are so many assignments that nothing will kill your grade. This is not an easy A,(but not hard!) it's a class if you truly want to improve your Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher. Most I have ever learned. Fantastic structure of the class, uses various topics to teach grammar and practice. Goes over all grammar again and helped me feel more prepared to use spanish than any other course. Definitely take if you want to get better at grammar. Always nice and helpful at office hours.

Here's the thing: she's nice, in class is easy, and discussions aren't hard. What's hard is the fact that there is a ton of homework and reading due every class, which sucks the fun out of Spanish. This is the third advanced spanish class I've taken at NEU, and definitely the worst. I'd rather risk it with Brucato in conversation again. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Agostinelli-Fucile is a good professor. The class (advanced Spanish II) is pretty much all in Spanish. There is a good amount of writing for homework but as long as you do it, you get full credit for it. There is a lot of conversation and she calls on you if you don't talk much. Make sure you come to class prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: SO SO passionate about finance and really knows his shit. Exams are hard though they've got a sweet curve. Probably the only 8am I consistently attended. Take him if you actually want to learn. What an incredible guy.

Aggarwal made me want to go to an 8am class. His lecture style is engaging and he is clearly a master at what he teaches. His class is not easy but if you attend his lectures (which are not mandatory) you will be fine. His exams are difficult but they are open note, you can use excel (which is extremely helpful), and there is a heavy curve.

He's a great guy, lectures feel long but you will always learn a lot. If you miss a few you fall behind very quickly. Tests are few, but very difficult. Heavy curves on tests, you'll do fine as long as you do the homework

He is so passionate about the subject and I learned a lot about finance from this course. You won't know your final grade in the course until the end, the curves are approximated so you may have a rough idea but will not have a true estimate until the end. Takes the time to genuinely answer any and all student questions, this was my favorite class!

A+ professor! I have never found a professor who cares as much about the subject as he does and is as passionate as he is. wifi issues during the final which many people will rate him poorly for, but it was not his fault, and these people are just upset they did poorly on the final and trying to find an excuse. Take him if you want to learn!
like wow
the best it gets. No 1 finance professor. I learnt so much. He loves finance and will make u love It. He went to Harvard and yale
Loved him. If u really want to learn about finance. he is the best. Teaches so much of the class on excel which is so helpful. Best lectures. You need to attend class.

He has good lectures and does not post class notes. The exams on all online and open note on the hw platform, however there is zero partial credit. Exams are weighted heavy.  Final exam is cumulative so there is a lot of material. Everything is on a curve to a B- so that helps.
Challenging course but so worth it, he really taught me how to think financially and assess risk. 5 Stars.
If you want to learn, he is the guy. Amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy who has a ton of industry knowledge, the lectures can get insanely boring and the class is heavily graded on a curve. Open book open note but the tests are aids. Take him if you're serious about finance but don't expect an easy A, and actually participate even if it's a big lecture class

Excellent professor. One of the most engaging classes I have taken at Northeastern. It was helpful that the students in my class were also excellent and asked questions frequently. Class material is straightforward and requires critical thinking. Teaches you more than just the fundamentals of finance. Would take any class he teaches in the future

Good professor and knows his stuff. One strange thing about his class was that the exams are much harder than the homework and practice material. It is not a big deal because he heavily curves grades, but it was stressful and frustrating in the moment.

There are very few grades and the class is entirely lectures however he is very knowledgeable and overall a good teacher. Always willing to answer questions and he is upfront about what he expects. The midterm was extremely difficult, very few did well however it was graded on a scale. Not an easy A but he is a good professor

Worst Professor I have ever had at Northeastern for the 3 years I have been here. His lectures are impressively boring and very difficult to follow. His tests are impossible with the midterm having an average of 30% and students cheating the whole time to find answers online. I would never recommend to anyone who wants to actually enjoy Finance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take him if youre serious. Exams were hard, but we were asked on what we covered in class and in homework assignments. Has actual knowledge in the field and taught us actual skills, not concepts. Great Professor

Our class all really disliked Professor Aggarwal. The whole class is graded on a curve, which means you don't know your grade until the semester is over. You absolutely need to take textbook notes if you want to succeed. He is pretty chill in that he doesn't really care about participation, but you still need to attend and work for the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: All you have to do is show up to class. He does talk a lot, and it's very easy to get lost in what he's saying, but he did have interesting things to say, and he's clearly very passionate/experienced with the subject. Lots of field trips around the city, which were cool.
Basic intro to arch class, lots of fun field trips, some boring guest speakers, only graded on attendance
Attendance is mandatory but all he does it talk, super easy
fun and relaxed professor, very passionate about architecture!

Dan Adams is one of the most inspirational teachers Ive ever had. His lectures are interesting and his perspectives are really helpful in critiques. Hes also funny and laid back. I absolutely recommend taking his classes even if you dont plan on majoring in architecture.
Very inspirational and knowledgeable teacher in design tactics, highly recommend him for that course.  Get him to show you his projects in his firm, it is very interesting!
Wish he still taught the fundamentals studio.  Dan was amazing!
I had a great freshmen year studio experience with him. Wrote me a stunning recommendation letter for co-op. Very thankful for him.
Very good.

Talks like a machine gun but he's an interesting person. Make sure you don't put mulches in your design because he hates mulches. Very knowledgable and goes beyond the syllabus. The down side is that the class often finishes late, which is quite frustrating sometimes. Overall he's a great professor who has a good sense of humor.

He's very knowledgable, probably one of the best architecture professors in Northeastern University. But you will need to put in a lot of good and hard work to impress him. He also talks a lot so you'll always need to stay behind after class for at least an hour.

He's a good teacher who knows what he's talking about but he talks so much that you are sometimes forced to stay over an hour after class before he critiques you.  You'll learn the most from him but you're also assigned the most work.
Great professor, lots of fun, and very interesting. Assigns a lot of work and is quite tough with the grading but is very informative.

This studio teacher is such a jerk. The amount of work he assigns is nearly impossible to complete in the allotted time. He'll look at your work for 2 seconds, laugh in your face, and tell you that your work is hard to look at.

The class itself is very heavily project based, and one midterm. Bhutta is a good prof, but his lectures are a bit monotonous at times. A lot of things in the class require more practice on your own time, and the projects do take a while, so don't make the same mistake I did about procrastination. Overall, good prof but the course itself is hard.

It's like a speed run of OOD but in a more complicated language. Each homework assignment given feels like a whole project, and they're usually assigned with 6 hours of lectures to watch, 5+ readings, and two practice activities. It is difficult to balance with other responsibilities.

It's an insane amount of work if you have responsibilities outside of this class. It's nonsensical as to why so much work is assigned each week. I find myself constantly trying to finish the assignments rather than learning and absorbing the material. I'd try to avoid this class if you aren't good at time management.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is a ton of work and not a lot of leniency. I understand that the Professor expects 20+ hours of time commitment per week for quality learning, but the EXTREMELY harsh grading criteria and little to no exceptions given make it very difficult for students with obligations outside of the class. If you have another class or worse, a job, then GL
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had the pleasure of taking your CS3520 during Summer 2024. Throughout the course, I consistently attended TA office hours to deepen my understanding and improve my programming skills, and I greatly appreciated the support and guidance from the course staff. Course was both challenging and rewarding, significantly enhancing my proficiency in C++.

I took CS 4530 in spring 2024. Taking this class helped me develop strong programming, design, and development skills. Because of the final project I completed in this class I felt ready for graduate-level work and improved my proficiency in coding.

I truly enjoyed the C++ course, where I earned an A, and I'm currently in Software engineering class, where I expect to achieve the same. These courses have strengthened my programming and problem-solving skills, and I deeply appreciate the insights I've gained from his teaching.

It was a great semester. I genuinely learnt so much from this class, and it was one of my favorite CS classes. I have grown so much as a person having learnt the skills that I did in this class. I appreciated all of the lectures very much, so thank you Professor Bhutta for giving us such a wholistic view of software engineering.

Thank you so much for an amazing semester. It's been a blast learning with Professor Adeel and I can't believe how much I've learned in such a small period of time. This class has been so rewarding and I enjoyed a lot.

This professor and his entire team of TAs are so unhelpful. It's a summer class, so things move pretty quickly, so the support of TAs and the professor is critical. However, these TAs would answer every one of my questions with "I can't tell you that" or "You're going to have to figure that out yourself" which I found bizarre.
This professor gives a LOT of work.

At first I could not tell if I liked the guy or not, but eventually realized he was a good lecturer, very professional, and treated the students like adults. The class was very fair. Not really anything to complain about.
