With this professor you can have your cake and eat it too, literally. She's a strong-willed Canadian with a flagrant fashion sense. She's one tough cookie with a soft gooey inside. I had a dream my life would be so much different from this hell I'm living. She also loves morphing.
Very good professor, kind and fair
I loved this class! Exams were difficult but very fair, nothing we hadn't seen before.

took 2331 lin alg, great professor, interesting lectures, funny and entertaining. very well organized, no surprises anywhere with tests, content, grading, etc. tests and content was difficult, questions are similar in difficulty to practice problems so review well
Super easy-going prof who taught an interesting course. Wish I had him for a more interactive course, seems like a good teacher. Really easy on grading.
Highly recommend. super easy class and all the topics were explained really well. all the tests and quizzes are like the practice that's provided and the group project is super easy.
Super nice guy. I didn't do too well because im an idiot but this class is very doable.

Amazing time in Calc 2. Came in super rusty on all fronts, but really enjoyed the class and felt like I learned quite a bit. He curved everything massively, weekly quizzes were easy, he dropped probably a quarter of them, and gave ample opportunities for extra credit. No excuses if you did badly in this dude's class haha.

Blankers is the goat. Best professor I've had at this school so far. Clearly and concisely described all the annoying Calc 2 topics. Funny guy that made class enjoyable, although would go off topic for a little too long during class time but idc. Had lots of office hours and study groups. For sure take him for Calc 2

This is genuinely one of the best professors I have had. From explaining concepts thoroughly through interesting lectures, heavy partial credit, and holding extra office hours before exams, he truly cares about his students succeeding. Attendance and homework is not mandatory, but there are new concepts everyday, so I recommend it.
He is not caring at all. He doesn't care about the well-being of students. He is not good at all. Find another professor.

Great guy, loves to interact with his class. Easily accessible both via email and during office hours (go, don't be afraid to ask questions), grades more than fairly, and gives adequate opportunities for extra points through test corrections and dropped quizzes.

I had him for calc 2 and honestly enjoyed most lectures. He would typically go off on funny tangents and made class more enjoyable. Allows you to earn half credit back on the tests and drops three lowest quiz grades. also gives practice exam before each test, so you know exact structure and questions you'll see. I'd suggest for calc 2.

Professor Blankers rocks. He does a great job of presenting abstract concepts in math iteratively; through examples and results that are approachable and build a deep illustration of the topics at hand. He takes the painstaking effort to give rigorous feedback on every problem, on every assignment. This is indispensable for learning math.

From my understanding, almost half (at least one third) of the students dropped the class, and that should be a fair indication of the quality and the difficulty of the class. He seems like a nice and understanding guy, but honestly the way he teaches are not so organized and often leaves students confused.

Vance is terrible in terms of teaching. Whether it's his first time or not, his whimsical attitude towards students will be the downfall of your grades. I've take a lot of classes in college and no matter the grade, I learned. For this class you will NOT learn. He assigns long assignments that no one finishes. Go to another section.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the writing class you want to take. Not too taxing but you still feel like you learned something.

I recommend this professor for your writing class. This teacher challenges in way where you have to think outside of the box. He truly cares about his students and gives amazing feedback on what to improve on. Take this class for first year writing. I would love to take his class again for advanced writing.

Professor Huggins is a super nice guy who really helped me learn more about English without additional stress as an Engineering major. His class was pretty easy as long as you tried. I'd 100% recommend taking him!

Extremely considerate of your circumstances. His grading is clear and manageable. Just get your projects/papers done and you'll receive the maximum grade. He often compliments students work and uses student examples which makes writing enjoyable.
very good professor and he really cares about his students!

Best professor ive had yet . Very chill guy and gives really good feedback . Went into the class not expecting much but left with so much more . Gives a lot of freedom with your writing and is open to discuss everything . The class does has work but the work is very fulfilling .Overall great guy and a great professor

Prof Blazek is very caring and understanding for all students. He understands students start the class with different levels of experience with physics and gives resources to those less experienced. Slides and lectures are very clear and well structured. I slept through the midterm and he let me take it the next day.

He is a very caring professor who wants students to succeed in his course. He makes an effort to be available for extra help and is very patient. Has good demonstrations during lectures that help enhance learning. Clearly very knowledgeable and always encourages further learning. I absolutely recommend him for anyone taking Physics 2.

Overall enjoys what he is teaching which makes the lectures fun. Lots of cool demonstrations which were fun/helped me visualize what we were talking about. The grade is broken up between a mixture of things which is nice in case you don't do well on the midterm or final. Homework is a little tough and takes some time but you have a week to do it.

Prof Blazek is really nice and cares about his students! I learned a lot in this course and would take him again. Homework, practice exams, and group office hours were really helpful! Online quizzes were a bit annoying but not really an issue. I really liked his in class demonstrations, and lecture slides were filled with helpful visuals!

He's the best professor I had at northeastern. Clearly knowledgable and cares about his students. Super friendly and is always willing to help with homework. Lectures are easy to follow and always posted on canvas. Gives lots of practice material. Likes to do demonstrations.

I feel bad leaving this review bc Prof Blake is such a nice guy, but this class was odd. While the material was cool, I felt like class time was not used effectively. He spoke really fast and class felt like I was watching it through somebody else's eyes. The amount of homework was also wild, even as someone who enjoys writing. Fair grader tho.

Just a pleasant and caring person who clearly has a passion for what he teaches. Most of the class time was spent watching movies, which is fun. If you like writing, this class is thoughtful, interesting, and a great elective overall. But be warned, there is a hell of a lot of writing. A great professor that I'd recommend to film and writing lovers
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is incredibly demanding. I took his Film 101 class this semester, and it was packed with work. We had daily discussion board posts of at least 350 words, weekly screen notes for films, and six quizzes, each accompanied by an essay. On top of that, both the midterm and final included not only exams but also large papers to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you come to class and try and participate you will succeed in his class. He makes the class environment very welcoming and if you get sick or anything he is the most understanding of your situation. He wants the best for his students and obviously loves what he is teaching. One of the best professors I have had at Northeastern.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Overall ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really like professor Blake. He is a really good person!

He's gives excellent feedback on papers and open responses. His Film 101 lectures are pact full of all the information you'll need for quizzes/midterms. All necessary knowledge is within his lecture notes. His grading rubric allows you to achieve an A relatively easy as long as you complete all the assignments with reasonably good effort.

This was one of my favorite classes by far, Professor Blake is enthusiastic and knowledgable about film, he teaches because he wants to share his passion. Speeding up the movies can make the workload lighter. He is an easy grader, if you put in visible effort you get an A. Engage with the content and the work is easy, only takes 1-2 hours a week.

Professor Blake is a great teacher and knowledgeable about almost every film. There is a significant issue with the criteria of this class. This class requires you to watch over 30 movies in which you will write specific screening notes. I absolutely love movies but honestly, this class has temporarily ruined movies for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
*MSCR 2895 REVIEW*
Professor Blake is extremely passionate and knowledgeable.  As someone who took this credit purely out of interest, he made the class far more than what it was on the surface.  There's a lot of reading and writing assignments are pretty detailed, but he is a fair grader and is transparent about what he's looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Blake is a nice guy. Even though this class is honestly a lot of work because you have to keep up with the readings and watch all the films, he makes it interesting. He goes a fast in lecture but he posts everything online so you don't really need to go to class. The quizzes and exams are online which is nice and there are only 2 papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I got turned off of the class quickly due to how much work was required outside of class time. I spent more time working on this class more than my actual required classes for my major. It just felt a bit unnecessary. To his credit, the tests and quizzes were online, so it was fairly easy to get good grades on them, though they are timed.

Nathan is caring, passionate, knowledgable and attentive! This class is asynchronous this semester which can be hard at times but he is devoted to making it as easy to manage as possible. The course is still well thought out and grading is clear and easy to understand. He really cares about students thoughts on films and gives insightful feedback.

Really thoughtful and kind professor. Genuinely super passionate about what he teaches and it is sad that not many people participate in class over zoom as much as they should. Great guy, it's a difficult class in terms of concepts but he makes it accessible.

Nathan outlines exactly what he wants, with very clear percentages. He tells you exactly what you need to do to get an A, and if you are engaged in class he will bump you up to the next letter grade if you're on the cusp.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Courseload is heavy but tolerable. He is very nice, saved my grade. Replies fast and very helpful and caring. He'll help you learn a lot about film.
Such a nice guy. Honestly my grade saver.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading for the midterm and quizzes, but the class is well balanced with a great selection of films. Professor Blake is very nice and caring who cares about his students and is always accessible outside of class. The class is mostly lectures which can get boring.

Professor Blake is incredibly intelligent and kind to students. I love our conversations in class and he makes some abstract film theories very accessible, which everyone appreciates. I'd love to take another one of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Nathan is a great professor. He's very patient and he treats everyone's work seriously. He gives a lot of feedback in details. He replies email very fast. Overall, if you really want to learn about film, he is a great choice. Workload is kind of heavy so it depends on your choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: You will learn a lot from this course, but I don't recommend co-op student to take this course because there are just so many readings, lecture recordings and movie clips each week. And you won't get a good grade if you skip any of these. Not an easy A- class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lots of reading. Gave good feedback. Great in-class discussions. No 2 classes were the same. Students helped each other w/possible sources for their individual research projects. Classroom felt like a community. Didn't always understand students' perspectives. Banned computers by saying that he would look things up on his computer,  but never did.

Blessington was the worst professor I have had in my time at Northeastern. I took his class because I was interested in poetry and he basically destroyed any chance of me ever pursuing that interest again. He was extremely rude and never responded to emails. He made fun of students and faculty repeatedly and was incapable of using online resources.

Created a classroom environment that made students fearful of reading their work because of his abnormally harsh criticism. Was incredibly unsympathetic and did not care about his students in the slightest. Ruined poetry for me and he clearly has no idea what a subjective writing course is supposed to be about as he was very objective when grading.

Course was called "Origins of Genres," and was part of a PhD program. I have no idea if attendance was mandatory because I wanted to go. I didn't mind putting work into it because I was there to learn and develop.  He was thoroughly prepared, hugely literate and immensely interesting. One of the top profs I've had, and I've had some good ones.

In a class about self-expression he promoted a critical, toxic environment. He made bigot comments on pieces outside of his own perspective and students felt uncomfortable/anxious about contributing to the discussion because of his scrutiny. If you want your self-confidence shredded then I recommend this class.
Professor Blessington ruined poetry for me. Never take a class with him.

I took Greek Tragedy so we were assigned mini reports for each play we read. It was fun, no pressure because of how short they were, and helped you dive into the material. Vague about what he wants from your assignments. He is more lecture based and he really knows what he's talking about, though sometimes class questions go right over his head.

Best teacher I have ever had.  I was at NU from 99-01, so it's been a while.  I am now an Eng. teacher, and I can honestly say that interest started in his class.  He is probably the smartest person I've ever met, but doesn't live in an ivory tower.  He's spent summers farming and Spain and just seems to know everything about everything.

Blessington is the best.  Wish he was my grandfather.  He is brilliant, hilarious and nice.  I was doing horribly in the class, probably because I never went during the first half, and he helped me get back on track and completely turn my grade around.  Makes the material interesting and fun, and I would recommend him to anyone.

Best professor I've yet come across. This man is a genius, and it's almost impossible to believe the extent of his knowledge of literature. He has translated Greek plays to English, is avid about Milton, can point you probably to any precise line in Homer or Virgil. Just the best, I want another class with this guy. Smart, funny, memorable for sure

He is brilliant and hilarious. I enjoy listening to what he has to say in lectures. He makes material fun and helps you to understand. I would recommend him to anyone. He's a bit of a hard grader, but it pushes you to work harder. I learned so much from this class.

AMAZING! He has seen and done it all. His knowledge of literature is astounding. His lectures are clear and while he does veer away from the topic at times, his stories/antecdotes are witty and interesting.

The readings were at times overwhelming, and much of the assignments I never finished.  His lectures were amazing, however, and made the class worthwhile.  The man really knows his stuff, and is HILARIOUS.  There are too many Blessington quotes to count.. and too many aren't acceptable for younger readers to see! ;)
Definitely intense reading, I would recommend keeping up with it. Other than that he is extremely knowledgable and impassioned about the subject.

The reading is INTENSE.  I'm an English major and I had difficulty keeping up.  Pay attention to the readings in class - they WILL be on the midterm/final!!!  But beside that, he is an incredibly intelligent guy and keeps a fairly uninteresting topic somewhat interesting.
Blessington is extremely intelligent. He makes a few jokes, and has some interesting things to talk about. He is a fairly tough grader but if you do the work you will do well.
One of the best professors I've had in NU.
No Comments

Blessington is the man. He knows his**** inside out and if you ask him a question on what you don't understand, he *will* clarify it and be direct. He's funny too, at random moments. Quite quirky and definitely the biggest character out of all my teachers
professor blessington is very brilliant although can be a bit boring

Blessington is the best professor I have come across at this school. Some how he made paradise lost and a**** load of poetry about god interesting. Extremly intelligent, a fair grader and, he's actully kind of funny. This guy could teach "the evolution and science of tax reform policies" and somehow make it captivating

One of the most intelligent people you will ever have the good fortune to meet in your life.  Honestly, such a great professor. His comments  anecdotes are also quite funny at times.  Although he might as well be the most knowledgeable professor at NU, he doesnt seem conceited.  Good Guy.

This guy has so much knowledge over such a variety of literature, it's unbelievable. One of the few professors I really feel I learned something from. A bit tough sometimes, but stick with it and you'll do fine.

He is obviously very intelligent, but the class was BORING.  Lectures very dry, I wanted to sleep through all of them...  Don't worry about going to class, most of the material on tests is from the reading assignments

Probably the best prof. I have ever had.  Made me want to become a teacher of literature myself.  The reading requirement isn't that bad if you stay on top of it.  Besides, by the time you get to college you should have read most of those texts anyway.
very very smart man.

The best teacher I've had at Northeastern. There is usually a good amount of reading and lengthy lectures, but I've never known a teacher who gives as interesting and informative of lectures. Recommended more for English majors or those who really love Literature.

although the course content is somewhat dry and a lot of reading is required in a fairly short amount of semester time he does make it as interesting as possible. And though he is a relatively tough grader he is always willing to help when you need him. He also really knows what he's talking about.

A smart man...but doesn't know how to teach. His lectures are full of tangents, and he doesn't really explain text very well. He's nice enough, though, and every now and then makes a good point, but overall...I'd say you had to be really into the subject matter to put up with this class.

Loads of reading--a novel each week, sometimes more.  And Blessington is something of an elitist--he belittles popular fiction, or anything that isn't considered "literary"--but he's a thorough marker, and smart as hell.  Recommended course.

Be prepared for a****load of reading.  Illiad, Odyssey, Aeneid, Bible, Bacchae and some other plays in a VERY short period.  Seems like a nice guy, very knowledgeable, but the material can just get boring I guess..

Very interesting course but look forward to a lot of reading. Blessington is a really smart person so that makes the class interesting as well. Only two papers and a midterm and a final besides the reading. I learned a lot though.

I just graduated and am looking back at the worst professors I ever had, and no doubt this guy was it. I'll never forget when he wouldn't let us use the restroom and someone in the class had a disability. Straight up bad person and an even more impossible teacher who would give out bad grades just to give them out. Cant stand him, don't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely the worst professor Ive had so far at Northeastern. Ill never forget the time they just graded my question wrong when it was correct and he wouldnt give me the point back because he wouldnt work the problem out himself to see the answer. Save yourself the trouble

Definitely an unorthodox teacher, but you can tell he knows a lot about the subject he is teaching. Beware that he customizes his own syllabus and the topics covered are very difficult to find examples of online. Also, the only grades we have are quizzes and the final and there are fewer quizzes in the honors sections.

FYI. In the canvas, in the quizzes, there were all of last year's bi-weekly quizzes and the final exam there. I found that out a bit late. It's not enough though; many of his quizzes are unpredictable. Just make sure you understand what he covers in class. Don't worry about unfamiliar things in recitation, since those won't be on quizzes.

As a person he is probably a good guy but he is a horrible professor. Very condescending and his course does not make sense. Impossible to find practice tests and exams, unpredictable and makes up his own way of teaching the material. You have to show up to classes to understand the way he does things. Office hours are weird sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: "Old SAT" grading only occurs for matching questions or MCQ, and quizzes rarely had those. While explanations of concepts can be kind of convoluted, he explains HW problems very well. If you are cannot switch out don't fret. An A is very possible. Do your due diligence of doing ALL the HW and going to office hours, and AP AB Calc was easier too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible professor. He is so rude to students and fails to explain concepts. Absolutely avoid taking his class at all costs.

I'll never forget when he wouldn't let us go to the bathroom, and a girl got her time of the month and yelled at him that she had to go. Mean person, mean grader, dropped this class and preferred to take it with anyone else. AVOID. Absolutely terrible person. Miss class? Good luck. Have to go to bathroom? Hold it. 0 empathy here
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is made up entirely of quizzes and final. If you miss class, you won't be able to understand what's going on in class at all. Most of his methods that he expects you to use on quizzes and tests are not commonly used and googling to understand these concepts is not really an option. He does go over questions before the quiz which can help
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have a choice, do not take his class at an honors level. He makes the quizzes much more difficult by putting questions that related to topics we never learned in class. Also, his grading criteria for the honors section is much more harsh than his regular section, for example, an A in honors is anything above a 94.5. I would not recommend him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Doesn't seem to know how to teach. He's clearly very knowledgeable, yet he holds us to a higher standard on quizzes than even he is able to perform during class. Your grade is exclusively based on quizzes and tests, and if you make even a minor mistake on a quiz that can bump your quiz grade down to the 70s. Overall extremely difficult.

Professor Blank is extremely condescending to his students and laughs at "dumb" questions. He frequently makes mistakes on the board while teaching and students often correct him. Regardless, he is extremely smart and knows a lot about what he teaches. If you cannot keep up with him, you will not be able to excel in the class. D- required to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: sandy blank is by far the worst professor at northeastern university. he does not care for his students' success at all and in fact, enjoys when students do not perform well. He puts in minimal effort to explain topics to us and even purposely gives us incorrect problem solutions to work on at home. I promise that you will regret taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sandy is not a great teacher. He doesn't respect the learning process. If you don't get it, he fails to explain the concept in simpler terms (or at all). His tests were graded in such a way that partial credit is nonexistent, and you could only miss about 3 problems (over quizzes and the final) to still secure an A. His grading style is "old-SAT".

Hes willing to answer hw questions but spends too much time on hw and not enough on new lessons. Final is harder than quizzes and half the grade. Quizzes are the other half. Theres lots of pressure on the end of the semester because quizzes are weighted progressively more. Also grades no. right minus half times wrong , so a pretty hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 40% of the class is based on the final and 60% is based on quizzes. He talks in a very quiet voice that can hardly be heard in the classroom so lectures are difficult to follow. This class is meant to be Calc 1 and Differential Equations, but he skims all of Calc 1 in the first week and skips through to linear algebra by the last month.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the strangest men I have ever met. Spends a large portion of the class giving background information on topics instead of teaching them. Quiz difficulties fluctuate. Would not take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: As much as I love Sandy as an individual, he expects his students to be able to understand complicated math theorems after doing one problem together in class. Be prepared to have to teach yourself the concepts through doing your homework. Attendance isn't necessary, but if you miss a class you'll fall behind and it can be hard to catch up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If you already took AP calc AB, then itll be an easy A

I personally love Sandy and would recommend his class. He is exceptionally smart and likes to teach. His content is difficult but if you attend class and do the assigned homework problems/ask questions, you should have no problem getting an A. I have always loved math and Sandy is one of my favorite professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sandy is a very smart man but he taught so students were supposed to learn how and why certain formulas/strategies work without him explicitly explaining it. This would work if the subject matter weren't already confusing enough. He does his best to answer all Qs but he's often hard to follow and makes a TON of mistakes. Harsh grader as well. Avoid

He won't be a good teacher for everyone. I personally did very well in the class but many people struggled especially if they hadn't taken calculus before. He can come off as condescending at times but if you just ignore it and ask your questions regardless you'll get a clear and helpful explanation. Show up and study hard and you'll be just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Must have a general understanding of Calc 1 BEFORE taking this class. Very heavy on differential equations. Don't recommend if you're not a good self-study. Grade is 50% quizzes, 50% final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awful teacher. If you did not have calculus in high school do not take his class. He uses his own methods to teach and your grade is solely based on tests designed by him. Awful.

Not very helpful outside of class &doesn't offer extra credit. Came in with 3 yrs of Calc experience &knew all the material but performed poorly because of my test anxiety and he wasn't helpful at all. Makes everything more complicated than it needs to be, and tells you to learn things his way when there's and easier way. Quizzes  50%, final  50%
Awesome professor. Very clear, helpful, straightforward. Very clear homework and quizzes. I learned a lot and it was no easy, but he gives homework every night to help you keep up.

Took him in my first college semester and thought I was going to pass with a B but got a C+ after the final. Try to take a different professor. I practiced and participated, and even went to his office hours a few times. He's a cool guy but I would not have taken his class if I had the choice. But don't fret if you have to; just practice.
Sandy Blank makes up math terms, teaches you things in round about ways, and then lets you know you were learning derivatives etc. all along.

I personally didn't struggle in his class. I had a great calc teacher in high school so my foundations in the subject were very strong. However, if math isn't your strong point I wouldn't recommend Blank. He barely teaches in class, you basically teach yourself the material by struggling through the hw. But if you can do that the class is fine.

Blank does not know how to effectively teach calculus. He often gets example problems wrong, and his students are forced to correct his math multiple times per class. You're better off just reading the textbook and teaching yourself. As lon as you can do the practice problems, though, the quizzes are a breeze.

Sandy is not a helpful person. He is very disrespectful and generally not approachable. Usually spends the first 20 min of class on attendance the next 30 doing hw problems and then crams a whole lecture into the last 10 min. His quizzes aren't bad as long as you can do the assigned problems. If you cant teach yourself math it wont be an easy class

To get an A in this course you MUST do the homework and do it well. Take your time on the homework, and then the quizzes should be fine. The quizzes are pretty easy and its fairly easy to get an A for the class. The final is much harder than the quizzes, but doable if you know your stuff. If you are in honors and can take non-honors I recommend it
Awful. Doesn't care. Doesn't know how to explain. Takes joy in tricking and deceiving.

Prof. Blank is a really funny and nice guy, and extremely helpful when asked.  This does not mean his class is easy.. his quizzes are difficult and are 50% of the grade, with each quiz worth more than the last.  The final is the other 50%.  He makes the material clear and is always willing to explain things as many times as you want.
Though the material was difficult, Professor Blank was a good teacher. For someone who has trouble understanding math, he made the topics clear and easy to understand. Overall, a very good teacher.
Prof Blank is funny and really nice. His quizzes are pretty difficult, but bearable. Stay on top of the things and it's not that bad of a class.

I loved Sandy! The comments on here scared me at first and the first day of class he even acknowledged that people thought he was mean. His jokes are funny, and he's a really nice guy. He doesn't mind joking around during class. While his quizzes are hard, he's always available in his office. Sandy's one of my favorite teachers at NU :)

I had Prof. Blank for Calc&Diff Eq for Bio 1 and 2 my freshman year. He is definitely the hardest of the teachers for this class, but you will actually learn the material. Go to class and do the homework because the quizzes come directly from these two things. He is actually pretty funny and his hats were always entertaining.

Hated him in calc 1 but loved him in calc 2 since finally understood how to excel in the class: DO ALL HW in time for every class and ASK QUESTIONS for EVERY problem you don't understand. Uses hw for his VERY HARD quizzes and bases midterm/final off these quizzes. He's glad to go over problems and is helpful if you take initiative to ask questions.

ok teacher, not so great of a personality.. although there are only a few quizzes, they are hard -- STUDY for them!  don't be intimidated by the material covered the first day, it's not so bad.. the whole semester builds on basically the same stuff

Prof. Blank was a pretty good teacher. He knew what he was talking about. The online notes are really helpful, but overall he's kind of strict and condescending. He can be a jerk sometimes but when it comes down to it, he's a decent guy. Kinda funny, also will count good quizzes twice as much as quizzes you do poorly on. He's a pretty good guy.

Not to bad.  He is boring in class and moves pretty fast.  He quizes are on exactly what you do in class so if you study you will be fine.  The overall subject is very easy anyway and he is very fair with his grading.  Never uses the book though all the hw is on blackboard.  dont waste your money like i did on a book.
this is the best teacher ever. he look s great funnnyy, just the perfect genes. SOOOO U GUY BETTER STAYYY COOOLLLLLLLLL OORRRRR..... yeah just stay cooll

He was extremely rude to use if we didn't get something. One time he even said to us "It's not rocket science." If you pay attention in class then the tests aren't that hard and he'll replace you're average with what you get on the final if you get a better grade on the final. He had annoying mannerisms that bothered me the entire semester.

i once missed a quiz because my flight got delayed. i showed him my ticket as proof and he wouldnt excuse me saying it was my fault for not scheduling an earlier flight to be safe. but he excused my friend and she had the exact same situation and proof. his quizzes and tests are very fair if you listen and do the hw, but he's just a mean person.
Doesn't explain well.  He's also a little bit rude.  Enjoyed my other calc profs much more

I usually like math a lot but I did not enjoy this class. He trys to trick you on the quizzes. Will replace your quiz average with you final grade though which helps. Do good on the final and that is your grade for the class!
i had him for calc 1. do your hw and ask q's on which ones u dont get, and ull do fine. quizes usually have no surprises, and final is very fair. hes a fair guy, i thought he was easy
would take off lots of points when you only got one question wrong on the test. does not explain very well.
Pretty good class.  Quizzes are easy if you do all the homework and ask questions in class.  The final had no surprises.
This guy is great!!  Tries to be funny and makes classes interesting...not bad lookin' either

This is the worst teacher I've ever had. Class average was below 60%, and he refused to do anything about it. His explanation: "Well two of you are doing well and I'm teaching to them. You should all withdraw." Waste of my time and money.

He acts like you're an idiot if you don't understand something on the first explanation, or tells you to drop down to lower level math courses.  Who the hell wants to do that, and then have to take your class all over again dick.

I don't know why everyone gives this guy such a bad rating. Lectures are VERY helpful, problems are clearly explained, as long as you keep up with the material the tests are fairly easy. You want a bad math prof? Take one of Braverman's classes. <s
worst math teacher i've ever had. .  makes fun of your mistakes, talks to you directly in class - embarassing.  mean.  incompassionate. BAD TEACHER
pretty easy class, very helpful. knows when you dont understand and will try to re-explain

worst professor i've ever had!  very intimidating! loved to ridicule students and display their mistakes!  this is college!  he is the reason so many kids grow up fearing math!  teachers like him are why our country is behind the rest of the world in math
No Comments
Prof Borkin is a very chill teacher. Great woman, love her
Prof. Borkin is a strong lecturer and clearly passionate about the topic. The course pushes you to think deeply about how visualizations influence interpretation.
easy class, not a lot of work tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fantastic course. Prof. Borkin provides real examples from research and industry. The class helped me build a strong portfolio piece for visualization work.
The class content is interesting, but it can feel disorganized at times. Prof. Borkin clearly knows the material, but some assignments require a lot of interpretation.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the most useful classes in the data science curriculum. Prof. Borkin emphasizes both technical skills and communication, which is incredibly important for data scientists.
Excellent instructor. Prof. Borkin gives great feedback on projects and encourages creativity in visual design. The class requires effort but is extremely rewarding.

This class changed how I think about presenting data. Prof. Borkin constantly shows real-world examples and explains why certain visualizations succeed or fail. Highly recommend taking this course with her.
One of the best professors I've had in the data science program

Great class overall. Prof. Borkin is passionate about visualization and pushes students to think critically about how data should be presented. The workload can be heavy because of the programming and writing components, but the assignments are meaningful

Prof. Borkin is an excellent professor for DS 4200. She clearly understands visualization at a deep level and explains concepts like perception, color theory, and encoding in a way that actually sticks. The projects are challenging but very relevant to real data science work. If you put in the effort, you will learn a lot.
you have to go to clas or else the teacher punishes you. so hard to learn if you dont go to class!!!
Class was pretty challenging.
I learned a lot about Excel and Tableau in this class. Really helped prepare me for my coop.
great teacher not that much work. def take her if you can get into her class
Her lectures are interesting.

In my 2 years of going here I have never left a rating, but Prof Borkin is the most inspirational teacher I have ever had. Lectures arent mandatory but I go to them because they are so amazing. I hope every student at northeastern has a chance to have a class with her.
Prof Borkin is such an easy A

The lectures are repetitive and mostly intuitive, but then homework is unnecessarily long and time consuming with convoluted instructions. The altair and matplotlib tutorials were the only useful aspect of this class but were not even a significant part of the course. The course is 98% writing short essays and busy work and 2% coding.

In my 4 years at Northeastern I have never rated a professor before but this class is so awful that I felt I needed to protect future students. This course has an unbelievable amount of work and the strictest grading policy I have seen in all my DS courses. The professor is extremely passionate and knowledgable but has no sympathy for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Unfortunately if you are a DS major you are required to take this class - just be prepared to be bombarded with time consuming, virtually useless assignments. The class is lengthy and no information you learn is useful. This is the first DS class I have not learned anything in. If you can take this class with another professor I'd recommend it.
though enthusiastic in her presentations, she has a poor class structure and the content is repetitive and useless.

Her class is prolonged and the content is virtually useless. The service learning aspect prevents you from making any sort of visualizations that could help you in the real world. The coding tutorials are barely touched upon while it's more focused on writing 400-word essays weekly. If you want to take this class take it with someone else.

She is a very enthusiastic speaker and her lectures are good if you're interested in visualizations, but grading takes a ridiculously long time and I have emailed her 3 different times and she has failed to respond each time. The group project at the end of the semester is whatever and homework is fine, I just wouldn't take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The entire lectures are made up of her explaining visualizations, and she's great at it. But from homework 5 and after you are required to code in D3 which the TA teaches for about 40 mins once a week. I'm sure he was great but just not a good teacher, and the starter codes are not enough to complete the homework that make up most of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Best professor!!
Great Professor! Extr
bob's great. he has great speakers and interesting personal anecdotes. he still skis all the time which is insane... overall, i really enjoyed his class and my friends did too. i recommend :)
The prof is awful, I was at a high A and but my final grade was something else. He did not disclose as to what my grades are for participation and negotiation. All my efforts went to waste.
In SCHM6318, you get more than a crash course in all things supply chain, you also get the opportunity to guess how your professor wants you to write your answers!

He definitely makes an effort to make a somewhat dry subject (if you're not interested in it, that is) engaging. A decent amount of work every week, but it's necessary to stay on top of everything. Gives plenty of opportunities to ask him questions and really cares about learning.
I learned a great deal and although it is a lot of work, he is an incredibly helpful and caring professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Bob was an awesome and inspirational supply chain professor. He made a seemingly boring subject so interesting that I'm pursuing it as a concentration! We did write a lot of small case analyses which he graded fairly and quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was nervous going into SC because I heard that it was very tough, but I found Bob and I really enjoyed going to this class. He has lots of real life experience, and friends in the field that come and give guest lectures. Prepares class for the tests very well, fair grader, makes sure everyone understands the material and overall class avg was B+.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Bob is a great person who cares for all his students. He takes attendance and participation greatly. Learn from all the materials in class and you should end up with a pretty good grade. He brings in speakers and offered students who are interested in internships with connections.
Great class. If you are serious about learning more, I'd highly recommend. Workload is very manageable.

Bob Murray is a very down to earth, nice guy. Very much enjoyed having him as a professor- he is super intelligent, has worked in the field, is well connected and is passionate about what he teaches. I would highly recommend him and if you put in honest effort into the class, you will do well.

Methodical approach to how class operates. 1 page executive brief every week, 2 tests, and a case study presentation. He comes straight from industry holding multiple VP roles and organizes his class towards the real world. Incredibly smart and teaches you a lot. Put in a decent effort and you can get an A.

Bob is absolutely an awesome guy, both as a person and as a professor. He really is one of the good ones. He is incredibly knowledgeable about supply chain and has decades of experience in the industry, and it proves so worthwhile in class. I hope to have him as a professor once again, I've really never learned more  from a professor than from Bob.
dont take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is long, repetitive, and truly made to be boring. Do NOT take if you've had any previous art training.
Meh. I took this class because I needed an art elective and it was time consuming but not the worst. Doesn't really teach unless you seek out her direct feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Gives far too much work for a 2 credit hour class. 5 weekly sketches in addition to textbook reading and reflection, as well as occasionally videos. Class is a bore, and she doesn't speak to you unless you seek her out. Grades weekly sketches very harshly. Don't take this as an elective unless you're great at drawing and willing to put the time in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Skylar Borgstrom is an awful instructor. She forces everyone to draw only her way, ignores prior experience, and grades you unfairly. Class is just two hours of mindless still lifes with zero teaching. She falsely accused me of copying photos and handed out C- and D- grades despite accurate work. This class ruined drawing for me. avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The HW for this class is 5 30-min drawings every week without exceptions for holidays. She claims that a 30 minute drawing every day isn't time consuming, but this simply isn't true. I took this class as one of my general electives because I thought it would fit well with my very busy schedule, but that was not the case.

She takes this class far too seriously and does not accept absences even if excused or wellness days. It is an introductory drawing class but she grades harshly. There was no final/final project which was nice, but the outside of class homework and writing just got so tedious and it is difficult to know whether she is happy with your work or not.

Class was less drawing-focused than expected. There were readings, weekly sketchbook assignments, weekly self-evaluations, etc. She gives good advice but only if you seek it out, otherwise she won't speak to you. It felt like I had to do the learning myself and she was just giving work. Workload exceeded what you'd want from a 2 credit class.

this class made me not like drawing anymore. assignments are repetitive & the sketchbook homework was time-consuming & did not teach me much. she prides herself on giving feedback, but most of the time her suggestions are so vague and not helpful, and when grading homework she will often give a low grade with few words instructing on how to improve

Professor Bordbar was great, fair work load, clear grading criteria, fast feedback, no issue getting an A, don't fall behind though in this class or any classes here. Smart Professor, clearly a leader in his field, and wish all my other professors tied lectures into real world and discussed AI trends instead of dry theory, highly recommend him!

I perform as a professional ballerina and occasionally need to travel on short notice. The professor was very accommodating of my schedule. I earned an A in the course and highly recommend this professor. He's intelligent and the class was well organized, the workload was fair, and the topics were interesting and current.

I am a professional baseball player. It was  great class given the hectic traveling and schedule with games.
Professor was always available and I Ieaened a lot, got an A..

I'm grateful for a class that really went beyond the text book that I can apply to my job and a class that was fair to achieve my A.
Professor Bordbar is a rare find who wants the best for us, makes himself available even after the course closes.
Highly recommend and I will take all classes with him.

Loved the class and based on my emails to Professor Bordbar and his feedback, he's clearly top notch in his field. Talk about a bonus, he helped me with a job reference and even spoke to the head of HR on my behalf and they were so impressed, I got hired on the spot! Yay!

Smart Professor, but his skill is in teaching you what is trending, not dry theory, to benefit you and open your eyes. I'd rank this the best class ever, learned more this semester than all my business classes combined. Professor's feedback and grading are very fair. He is also very polite and respectful. Wish he'd teach more classes!

Wonderful class, Very fair pace and do the work and an A grade is easily attainable. The professor did a great job bringing to life textbook concepts.  I never knew anything about crypto and thank him for educating me on this and the new trends we can expect to see. Highly recommend him !

I got an A grade and Prof Bordbar is the best. Very fair pace of class and thorough feedback. Also, the only class with an actual discussion forum that had real world beneficial info. Professor Bordbar after reaching out to him also graciously shared one of his top tier CEO contact friends with me, cant believe it landed me a great job. He cares.

The syllabus was clear. We had quizzes each week with answers straight from the textbook, though I found the wording a bit strange on a couple of questions. Discussion posts each week & required replying to at least 2 more times after the initial post. Lots of reading. I felt unprepared for the final project based on how we learned though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: We read a ton, but Prof. Bordbar did a great job of getting us to take what we had learned from our reading and understand it better through discussions around real-world examples in the discussion board. Quizzes are very clearly straight from the textbook. Prof gives great feedback to keep you thinking critically about the business world.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bordbar is a great teacher. He stuck exactly to the syllabus and I knew what was expected of me. You will read the entire textbook, 1-2 quizzes per week, a final exam and a final paper. It was a lot of work. I felt he was a fair grader. I would take another class with this Professor.
professor gives lots of homework, however you do learn a lot. grading can be sometimes unclear

He is very passive aggressive in class and in grading. Definitely do not take if you have no prior knowledge of Portuguese or Spanish. I would avoid at all costs if possible. Multiple homework assignments before each class and quizzes/projects almost every week.

I would avoid taking this professor at all costs. I found him to be extremely passive-aggressive and not flexible. Grading felt nitpicky. Points were taken off for everything, including things that had nothing to do with language, such as margins or tiny technicalities. The class was unnecessarily stressful and not a supportive learning experience.

Profe is a good teacher and I learned a lot this semester. There is A LOT of homework, but it doesn't take super long and allows for more speaking time in class. Take this course if you want to learn Portuguese, not if you want a fun, chill elective. It is definitely helpful to have a basic understanding of Spanish before entering this class.

Prof. Yelin is very passionate about the Port language. The class had different methods of conveying information, and you will learn a lot about Brazil (and Portugal) and parts of its culture. The assignments were interesting, I enjoyed the films and short videos. I would focus on grammar review in class- it gets confusing with all the tenses.

He was fine. He is not even close to a native speaker. He gives A LOT of homework and grades pretty strict especially on unit tests. Everything new we learned was online and for homework so class didn't add much. He mixes different dialects of Portuguese, which is confusing because they have partially different words and conjugations/grammar.

Profe Yelin was the best! I had him for PORT 1101 and he was super easygoing and did his best to answer everyones questions and accomodate everyone. A lot of times language teachers can be really intimidating but he was great.

Profe Boris is such a great professor. He really cares about students learning a new language and therefore requires a decent amount of work. Work is very manageable if you are organized and do not let assignments stack up. Also, be ready to participate in class and do not miss classes because it will affect your grade badly.

As long as you participate and do all your work on time, you will be totally fine (I did not, which is why I got a B+). He encourages coming to office hours and talking in class, and if you do so, there is a high chance that he will be more forgiving with the rest of your grades. Homework can take a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Profe made class fun with his jokes here and there. Learning Portuguese was made simple with all the help we had by working with groups and having a small class size. You will get called on randomly, and make sure you are prepared with homework and the textbook.
He made basic Spanish impossible.

Profe is great. I've taken two classes with him and he obviously is very passionate about the material he teaches. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and so he will hold any conversation in Spanish so his students can practice. It is extremely helpful.
Literally loved Professor Yelin. Very good teacher and he makes class entertaining. Participation is VERY important. If you want a class that will teach you spanish skills take this one.

Profe Yelin is awesome! He structures the class as mostly group work and discussion- which really forces you to be engaged and learn. He's very accessible outside of class and responds to emails super quick. You just need to come in being ready to put in work. Overall he really cares about his students.

Great teacher, sets you up for success with clear lectures. Quizzes and discussion posts every week with other assorted papers, all easy As if you complete them as instructed. Very encouraging and easy-going.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Botchkovar is absolutely amazing. I adore her because not only is she intelligent, witty, and caring, but she is also a brilliant criminologist! That probably sounds forced but I just really enjoyed her teaching and I immediately liked her when the class began. I am not a general pushover so the fact that I adored her was meaningful!
She is an angel on this earth.  So accommodating to any conflicts with the class.  Tests are pretty easy and class is interesting.  Love her to death. Wish she was my grandmother.

Super sweet teacher. Cares about how you're doing in the class. Make sure to use the extra credit opportunities because the mid-term and final are worth over half of your grade. Also, make sure you try to participate in class, it goes a long way.
Took two classes with her and liked both a lot.

I am still puzzled by this teacher. She gives the impression that you're doing great and then hits you with a low grade. She is not at all specific about expectations. Her feedback on tests usually doesn't make any sense and it's like she takes points off for not dumbing down your work. As a grad student, I think we're beyond that.

She is one of the best professors I have had in my 4 years! She is excited about the subject (gender and crime). She used video clips and, while long, very interesting readings! She encourages participation and loves class discussion! Highly recommend!
Loved the class!

Tough to follow anything she's saying between thick Russian accent and condescending manner of questioning the classroom every few minutes. Mandatory attendance because of random pop quizzes. Zero discussion and class involvement. Was a very painful class and I would not recommend.

Amazing professor, interesting topics, interesting readings assigned, fair grader and tests, attendance is encouraged as there may be a pop a quiz at any time...this professor came to class with such enthusiasm every time, even brought candy a few times to encourage students to participate and get excited about the material.
Great professor! Very enthusiastic, interesting class material, straightforward tests, lots of reading, 1 project a mid-term and a final plus class participation and multiple reading respons papers

One of the best teachers at NU. Always there to help her students and truly wants everyone to do well. You can email her any question you have and she always gets back to you as fast as she can. A really nice person - definitely take one of her classes

She is very, very nice and really enjoys what she teaches.  The content is pretty interesting.  The journals are kind of a pain and heavy on the reading but you can get by without doing all of it.  She is very willing to help outside of class and really wants you to learn. Class participation is very important and there are some pop quizzes.
Botchkovar really knows her stuff and is extremely helpful. The class is long but its not too bad half od it is discussion. Take her class its not very hard as long as you go to class and to the work

Seems knowledgeable about subject but is poor at emphasizing this.  Lengthy class discussions lead nowhere and she does a very poor job at getting the class to the point.  Easy class but poor teaching.  Attending class is excruciatingly boring.  If we are going to have so many discussions let us discuss more and try not to lead us so much.
No Comments

Mid-term, final, paper. That is the entire class. You are allowed to use a cheat sheet for the tests-essay form. Ten page paper. Overall a really repetitive subject; boring teacher, but potential to do well in class.

Interesting ML course and material. Exams are very hard and will need to be massively curved. Homeworks are easy. Kind of an odd guy, he is very worried about people recording the class or distributing his lecture slides online among other things.

The class consistently runs 20+ minutes overtime despite already being 3.5 hours. Homework is straightforward, but exams are closed-book, closed-note, no cheat-sheet allowed. No practice exam or study guidance for exams beyond “just review the slides.” Lectures aren't recorded, and slides are uploaded days after class.

I enjoyed Professor Braun classes, the material is up to date and provides great NLP basis. The books he refers to are great and he takes time to explain concepts in the class. His exams are difficult but he applies curving to the grades. His classes are theoretical and his homeworks and project require to apply the concepts using python.

great professor, gives insightful lectures to help prepare data scientists for industry. the material was useful and informative. easy class as there were no exams and only homeworks/"take home exams" that were basically homeworks. TAs were excellent as well and always graded on time

The lectures were quite scattered and had to learn the materials myself. The piazza questions were almost never answered. The project was brought up extremely last minute so everything had to be rushed. We werent even informed what score we got on the project. Would have dropped out but the course was mandatory for me and no other prof taught it.

No clear grading criteria, never responds to emails (including his TAs), is not at all accessible outside class hours, does not grade assignments on time (assignments from January were graded right before the semester ended), cannot receive timely feedback on your work.

This guy's "office hours" were just him answering questions after class for like 15 min. Before the midterm there were about 20 people lined up and he just goes "dont have time for this today" and leaves. The midterm had almost nothing to do with the class material and was just advanced probability screwed if you didn't have enough prior knowledge.

Honestly this class was like the twilight zone in the worst ways. I would go in to office hours and he would not be there. He would show up late and cancel class randomly. You only get feedback on things you do well and never seem to see quizzes you do badly on. In addition we were graded on 3 quizzes worth more than 3/4 of the entire class grade.

David Brady runs a very lecture heavy class for EECE2540. He goes over the text book material from slides provided by the textbook's publisher. The homeworks are spaced out, so there's not too much, but the problems are from the text book, so expect to pay for it (or find it via alternative methods). You could easily not show up and still pass.
No Comments
One of the best brains I have ever met
Only professor in ECE with biceps and brains.

Easy homework (unlimited attempts), easy quizzes (2 attempts), and lectures are very clear. He's accessible outside of class and helps anyone who needs help. You have 6 makeup attempts for assignments you did poorly on/forgot to do. Exams are also easy; he helps if you ask him. Don't cheat, doesn't make sense. Also, the final exam is take-home.

This is the most peak professor ever. He let us introduce ourselves during the first day of class and I mentioned that my favorite show was Hunter Hunter, and he actually looked it up in front of the whole class. TALK ABOUT PEAK. Deserves a raise after that one for sure.

Bradley was great for psych stats; grade is made up of TYK, homework, quizzes, tests, and a presentation. Quizzes were taken in groups, and the tests were open-note for a section every time. Tests also mirror some of the quizzes. Lectures are clear and concise (we got out early almost every day), and the course was overall not too difficult!
Good guy. Funny. Easy A if you do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teaching methods! More then fair exams and great professor. 10/10 would recommend.

Love this professor so much. Gave so many opportunities to learn and internalize the information. Spent a lot of time on extra videos, spreadsheets, and practice tests that helped so much. Quizzes are open-note and mirror exams. Homework is simple with 2 attempts. Not much classwork. Easy to do well if you pay attention. God bless Kristopher!!!!!!!

I LOVE Kristopher Bradley. I cannot recommend him enough. He is so passionate and clearly cares about each and every one of his students being successful in his course. He puts in so much effort outside of class that he is so proud of, and we are proud of him too. Not too assignment heavy, pretty easy A especially if you do the quizzes. TAKE HIM!!!

No reason you should not be getting an A in this class. Group quizzes, 2 attempts on homework and TYK quizzes, and he drills the content into your brain. Also, super nice and funny guy, and very flexible about retaking quizzes and how you do the final presentation.
Good professor, class is an A if you put in the work.  Kristopher is also very caring of his students and smart.

Ok yes I got an A, but I don't think I learned a whole lot. Love Bradley as a guy but his class is basically guaranteed to pass so it kinda takes away the actual learning and more about just getting random stuff done for your grade.

If you want a zero-effort course, Bradley is your guy, which is not a recommendation in my opinion. It's frustrating that there is nothing that differentiates a hard-working student from a lazy student. He is just okay in my opinion.

Quizzes: In class taken as a group, open note open everything, he sometimes even lets you check your answers before submitting it (For formatting purposes). Tests: Take home open note untimed. Classwork: None Homework: some (very easy graded for completion). Final: Take home very easy to get an A on of you follow the lecture notes as you take it.

Very knowledgeable and caring. Was very supportive & lenient outside of class. Class was graded by weekly open-note group quizzes, HW assignments, and 4 open-note take-home tests (including the final). Easy class, easy A.

If you want an easy A or just want to happily learn about Social Psych, than take his class. He's funny and extremely nice on if you miss any assignment. He want's to see everyone do well. The final is also optional..

I feel fortunate to have taken Professor Bradley for both Statistics in Psychology and Social Psychology! He is an amazing teacher who teaches you a lot and also is very caring. His assignments and tests are very straightforward and he is understanding about possible absences. I highly recommend him if anyone is looking to take a class with him!

This class was a huge disappointment. I have never been less motivated to attend a lecture course in my entire college career, and my attendance reflected that. The slides needed much more detail, and many of our assignments were moved earlier, reflecting that this class was not well-organized.

Had Bradley for PSY31 at Tufts. GREAT MAN, EASY A (and he does it on purpose!) Tests and quizzes are open-note. Quizzes are done in groups. Easy final project. Easy final exam (open-note, online, no time limit). Easy homework only graded based on completion. Many extra credit opportunities. I am so grateful for this man. Has an adorable son.

This was one of the best professors I've ever had at Northeastern. I ended this class with a 103%. As long as you apply yourself, pay great attention in lectures, and take notes you'll be fine. He also offers extra credit so take advantage of that. I did and it helped me end with an amazing grade. Overall a nice caring guy, I recommend him a lot.

Professor Bradley is a very nice guy with a passion for psychology, and it shows in his lectures. The class was relatively easy and there were a lot of discussion posts to boost your grade. However, you have to read the textbook to know everything on the test, as some of it just isn't covered in lecture.

One of my favorite professors. Dr. Bradley is very easygoing but knows what he is talking about, so it made learning statistics enjoyable. Quizzes are in-class with groups, and tests are take-home, open-note. He allows you to re-do questions you got wrong on exams and gives you the points back. No complaints at all. Definitely take him if you can.

dr. bradley is an extremely nice and overall great guy. it's easy to get an A if you do well enough on the tests (which pull some questions directly from practice quizzes + textbook), since the rest of your grade depends on open-note group quizzes, group discussions, and one project. you should read the textbook in addition to the lectures though

One of the best professors I've had. Makes the lectures very easy to follow and understand and really wants students to succeed. Very understanding and helps all the time. Really easy to do well in this class as long as you show up to class, pay attention and follow the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, took him for summer 1. Graded by 3 tests, homework, in-class quizzes, and a final. All homework and tests were done at home and online with no time restrictions. Lectures were easy to understand and he explained how to use SPSS easily. He offers extra credit throughout and it's actually quite fun to do. He's very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy professor, does assign homework but is very understanding when it comes to grades and requesting regrades. Tests are mostly online and open book, so definitely recommend.

Super interesting class, but an easy A. Classes mostly consist of lectures and participation assignments which are often discussion questions. These you can complete with a group. The final project was a group 15-20 min presentation on a topic of your interest from the year. These get a little repetitive becuase they go on for several weeks.

Dr Bradley is a good lecturer and I learned a lot! Also, all the quizzes are with groups in class and you can ask as many questions to him as you want. The exams are take home and online which definitely reduces stress as well. He is very open to feedback and wants you to succeed. Would recommend

Great professor! He is super interested in what he teaches, and his lectures are easy to understand. Tests are SUPER similar to practice exams, and he wants you to do well. Grade based off 3 tests (optional final can replace worst score), canvas "participation" questions, and group/open note quizzes. Take this class!!

Professor Bradley was a great professor! Allowed for quizzes to be taken open notes and in groups and as a professor overall was super understanding and caring, definitely relates to students by being human.

Even though attendance was not necessarily mandatory, there were graded assignments based on in-class discussions. The tests were very straightforward and built off of the online group quizzes we took in class. There was one group project at the end of the year which was not very difficult and an optional final if you wanted to boost your grade.

Professor Bradley used one class (of the week) for a lecture and the other two for a discussion which was really interesting. I found that to be more effective in learning and reeled me to attend class. We had a quizzes, discussion questions, 2 exams, and a group project (and an optional final). He kept class very chill and questions open-ended.

was a good introduction into psychology, very lecture based- barely any material on the posted slides which makes it difficult if you're a visual learner or miss class. lots of group discussions on topics, tests and quizzes are heavy on vocabulary so as long as you learn that you should do well.

The class is lecture-heavy, but as long as you show up and pay attention, the midterms and finals are easy. She is very understanding about extensions. The rubric for the final project is not very clear, but she is a lenient grader. I really liked her as a professor, and her lectures were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professors Brothers is an amazing professor that has a deep passion for architecture and that was evident in her course. While her Canvas page is not the greatest and her organization could be better, she compensates her digital ability with her information packed lecture slides. I would recommend this class to anyone!

There was technically a lot to read for this class, however I did not find them all necessary. The class is lecture heavy, but I found them engaging and she gave us a break in the middle of class. She is not always the most clear with what she wants but she is very flexible and understanding. I loved this class and would take it again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Brothers makes lectures into dialogues which help to digest the content. She cares deeply for the success of her students and also has a great sense of humor. This class does need good study habits for the final/midterm, but it is manageable because, across the board, she sets very clear expectations for tests/projects. I loved this class!

Cammy brothers was a fantastic lecturer her talks truly derive inspiration, she speaks with a genuine passion and interest in her content. She is sweet and kind and genuinely only wants the best for her students. Her grading is kind and the criteria is very straight forward. Thank you!

Canny brothers was the best professor to ever exist ever. Nobody could ever top the lectures that she gave. I would go to bed dreaming about the churches of lalibela because of the absolutely thrilling lectures. Thank you cammy for enlightening my academic journey.

Professor Brothers seems passionate about her work and the history but she also doesn't seem to do much work as she has 3 TA's for her class and I notice they do most of the work such as the grading and etc... besides the lecturing. 3 different TAs had separate grading styles and who knows what you'll get for your grades back.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: In the beginning of the semester, there were only 4 assignments on canvas. In the end of the semester, she added to 8 assignments, including attendance, paper, exams, weekly responds, note taking, and recitation performance. She left all works to TA and forgot to upload our final grade before the deadline of the semester. No clear criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really wanted to like this class. The material was so interesting especially as a stem major. Professor Brothers was just highly disorganized and oftentimes rude, and assignments instructions and grading was incredibly unclear. She lacked communication skills outside of class and it ended up being a frustrating experience.
Grading criteria is not clear. All works are graded by TA and sometimes they give C or EVEN WORSE.

Professor Brothers  is a grate professor and although she is a little unclear about the instructions on when the homework assignments are due this is because she is flexible. Some people are saying that she gives long lectures which is true but they are really interesting if you participate, if you take this class you will definitely learn a lot
Professor Brothers was great at teaching us the vast and diverse architecture styles of the world. She made every lecture fun and engaging, and I came out learning a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brothers is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about architecture history. As long as you come to class, pay attention, and participate in discussion questions (which are usually stemmed from inclass activities and discussion), you'll have a great time. The grading criteria may seem vague, but actually is extremely reasonable.

She did a great job at keeping long lectures very interesting. She provided a multitude of ways to learn through slideshows, documentaries, and museum visits. It is clear she is very knowledgeable and passionate about architectural history and I have recommended her to other classmates!

Took Spanish and Islamic Renaissance Architecture in spring 2022 in person. Was a very good class, the biggest portion of the grade was the final paper but the work was spread over the whole semester. She is a very understanding professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brothers definitely was enthusiastic about what we learned about so I found the long lectures to be quite interesting. However, her grading criteria was very vague and reaching her outside of class was nearly impossible. The homework for this class absorbed most of my effort as weekly readings were upwards to a hundred pages a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Disappointing! She doesn't really teach and passes you off to the TA. Minimal feedback. Boring lectures, too!
Unclear grading criteria (no rubric), doesn't grade homework personally

The actual time spent in class is fine, she just lectures the entire class about historical architecture. There are no words on the slides, and all notes are up to you to take. It is a lottt of information to take in, and the class is very long. The grades are, like others have said, pretty unclear. Not much instruction on papers given. Hw not bad

Looking at all of her negative reviews, I want to put some respect on Cammy's name! I think everyone is being overdramatic--given she doesn't always give clear details about assignments and due dates, it's more that she's flexible about everything. Although many complain about a lack of clear instructions, it translates to less harsh grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible. Her lectures are pretty interesting but she has HORRIBLE organization of everything.
