reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I dont know how to say this nicely but she is not a good teacher. Shes a fine lecturer and clearly cares about the topics we discuss, but when it comes to caring about her students and communicating expectations, she is terrible. She constantly condescends her students and says that if we want our assignments to be graded, /we/ need to ask her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gives very vague feedback on exams and assignments. When students ask clarifying questions it's like pulling teeth to get a clear answer. The only way to get feedback is to set up a meeting outside of class, but good luck in getting a quick response as they never check their email. Lots of "it's only worth 10%" responses to student concerns
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gives very vague feedback on exams and assignments, and there are very limited options for knowing what your grade is, as it's only based mostly on two exams and a paper. On the plus side, we got 5 minute breaks in the middle of our 100 minute lectures.

Bruell is a really good teacher and lecturer. His class can be a bit boring and feel repetitive (especially if you've already done criminology in the past), but he has a talent for sparkling debates in class about various subjects. Even though participation is not graded (but attendance is, be careful), he still manages to get people engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Provides all the materials you need to thoroughly understand the material. Homework is weekly and takes some time, but not unmanageable. Midterm and final are open-book, open-note with 4.5 hours to finish (more than enough time). Be careful of the methods you use, he WILL accuse you of cheating if they aren't what you were taught in class.

Professor Bruell is a gem—engaging, organized, and deeply knowledgeable. He blends humor with sensitivity, especially on tough topics. Once, during a domestic violence unit, he bought out a student's donut fundraiser supporting survivors and shared them with the class, saying, “Actions speak louder than words."
Would do an in class assignment and day “it wasn't in depth enough” but then when more information was added, still said it wasn't enough. The length of the final was not that clear either.

He is such a great professor. I had him for CRIM 5900 online over the summer and I learned so much. The class was a lot of reading and work, but it was worth it! He is very approachable and knowledgeable. Take a class with him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Bruell is one of the best professors I've ever had. He cultivates a dynamic and fun classroom environment that encourages students to participate in discussion and make comments to drive critical thinking forwards. He isn't an easy grader, but it is because he wants to see his students succeed and learn!

Professor Bruell is a great guy and a good professor.  His lectures can be a bit dull, especially if you're already familiar with the material, but nothing crazy.  He's responsive and helpful if you reach out with questions.  He's very clear in what he is looking for when it comes to assignments. Overall, I recommend this course.

This was an online summer class and the modules were organized very well. In my opinion, the grading was a bit on the tougher side, but nothing too crazy. I would definitely take another class with Professor Bruell again!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Even though this grad class was online, all the modules were so organized and the discussion posts were short and to the point. Does not assign busy work and the readings are actually helpful and you learn something!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Stats-Prof Bruell has little respect for your time as a student. He makes assignments due on holidays/ breaks, and always over the weekend. The problem he is expects students to respect his weekends and holidays and won't provide any help during those times. He also cancels or pushes out a majority of appointments students make with little notice.

I really liked Professor Bruell as a professor and as a person. The only issue is he doesn't realize how intelligent he is and that we aren't at his level as grad students. I often felt he looked at topics as very easy and simple when it was far more challenging for the class to grasp.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's nice, but he gets sidetracked and sometimes fails at refocusing the class. He does pick minute details out of vast amounts of information, so be sure you know your theories.

Excellent teacher despite being a grad student. Really cares about getting his students to understand the course material. Makes class interesting despite the dry topic. Attendance is graded based on easy short pop quizzes. One of the best.

Research Menthods can be a very tedious and boring class, but Professor Bruell made it fun and interesting! I definetly recommend him! His pop quizes were easy if you took notes and reviewed them before class & the exams weren't too bad, everything is off the powerpoints. Overall great teacher!

Professor Buell may be very young but he certainly does not run his course like a novice. He is obviously very engaged with his students, and even though the class subject is a little boring, he always tries his best to make it as interesting as possible. Even though he gives pop quizzes, they were simple. He tries very hard to make his tests fair.

He is a very smart guy and relates the material well to the students.  Very clear lecturer and there are some pop quizzes.  The research assignment is kind of a pain but not too hard.  Bruell is very fair and wants students to do well.
Very awesome professor. Really knows his stuff and keeps you interested! Wants you to do well! quizzes are a breeze and exams are not very hard either.TAKE HIM

Awesome teacher, awesome class. Has small quizzes throughout the year, but crams most of them in at the end. Has 3 tests throughout the year, so midterms and finals are only a third of the semester. Attendance isnt taken, but you need to take notes.  Book is never used, and tests are all multiple choice, t/f, and short answer
Very nice

Great professor. Uses Powerpoint lectures and a lot of discussions - always keeps the students interested. Very fair tests - just study the slides and read the articles. Pop quizzes are pretty easy, especially because he drops 2. Great class.

Good guy - although I'm not sure he grasped the idea that none of us really had an interest in criminal justice, his lectures and discussions were interesting and personal, he treated us like adults, and his tests were completely fair.  Just make sure you read the articles he assigns - he's known for a pop quiz here and there
Clear and organized during lectures, and is very concrete in his tests. It is not his goal to trick you.

He's a really good guy. I would highly recamend him. He doesn't think he is better than you and likes to see both sides of an issue. Talks to his students as peers. His classes are all powerpoint presentation, but he likes to keep the class involved with conversation. Also i never even bought the book for either of the 2 classes, hes pretty easy.
No Comments

Nice and funny teacher. very young and after getting used to things he becomes very funny. class consists of 30 minute leacture, two 3-5 page papers, and two tests. read the articles and come to class and get an A

Avoid this class unless you have nothing else going on. Mandatory volunteering plus 3+ assignments most nights, each taking 1–2 hours with tedious steps. Grading is harsh, the late policy is unforgiving, and getting a response outside class is nearly impossible. If you can get out of stacked cornerstone DO IT AT ALL COSTS
He chill and shi

Stacked cornerstone is a weed out class. I often had 40+ hrs of hw a week, group projects were very intense and grading was harsh. He's a very nice guy but has very high expectations in an INTENSE class. You will be LIVING in fyelic if you don't have a foundation of coding before this course. This class will erase your social life. Good luck.

O'Connell is a passionate, good professor. He is open to helping students at a moments notice almost 24/7 through teams, and is focused on leaving students with a solid understanding of the course curriculum, which is very important given the nature of the course. Put in some effort, don't expect to have your hand held and you will do great.

O'Connell's great. Available, gives good feedback, answers questions promptly. However, stacked cornerstone is so miserable that I wouldn't recommend anybody take it. The flipped classroom method means half the lectures are useless. The group project is frustrating. Do not take 1501+1502 if you have other difficult classes running concurrently.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His directions for group projects often is contradictory. The rubrics were different than the guide and it ended with us at one point getting a 65 on part of a project. With weekly assignments, I felt more self taught when it came to graphics and coding as the learning style was reversed and he would just show a presentation. He is online for help.

The overall class isn't that difficult, but taking stacked cornerstone is so much work, like 30+ hours a week. O'Connell is a pretty decent professor and responded to my questions and messages within a couple hours. I felt that the lectures did not connect with the homework. I would not recommend stacking cornerstone unless absolutely necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nothing that conceptually hard about the course but stacked cornerstone is grueling. 25-40 hours a week. Never take stacked cornerstone by choice unless you have a lighter schedule. Nothing bad to say about prof oconnell but his class was kind of dry. If you must take stacked try to work on the homework in groups to save yourself time.
classes were completely a waste of time, as we were assigned to learn the same thing online before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The workload for stacked cornerstone is absolutely insane and you will spend 20-30 hours a week doing homework outside of class. The instructions for his assignments are vague and often make no sense. Avoid taking stacked cornerstone if you can.
The instructor was very proficient in all of the course's aspects and was able to explain anything a student could have a question on.
he definitely is a fan of what he teaches, and that much is apparent, whether you agree with his teaching methods or not

Most of class is major group projects, but he uses a god-awful digital textbook software called tophat that integrates discussion posts and makes a few of these due a week. Class itself isn't that hard but turnaround time on projects during the summer is very fast, and discussion posts are inherently evil. Cool guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Was available for help, taught concepts well and was well organized
Very responsive. Lots of enthusiasm/passion. Frequent office hours and helpful online.

I think the professor was fantastic. They were very helpful in all aspects and were understanding when a student was having trouble. Coming to class was really helpful bc we would start assignments in class. He held frequent office hours and was always available to respond to messages on Teams.

The instructor did a good job explaining new software/coding languages. While there's some criticism about the difficulty of the course, you are in class to learn, and O'Connell provides an amazing environment to learn in.

He's very accessible outside of class and answers within minutes. This stacked class is extremely heavy, many all nighters are necessary. He is very helpful if you reach out to him. Assignment details are vague and can be difficult to follow when you don't even know what its fully asking. I would recommend him over the other professors for stacked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is a very content-heavy class, but Prof. O'Connell made it extremely manageable and easy to get an A if effort is put in. He is always accessible and responds quickly via Microsoft Teams, which helped me out during difficult homework assignments. The class ramps up during the last few weeks, but O'Connell supported us through the process!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: O'Connell is awesome. You can tell he really loves teaching, and his lectures are interactive, interesting + funny too. He is easy to reach out of class and always responds very quickly. The class is a lot of work, but it IS an 8 credit combined class. He is very easy with grading, and it is easy to do well if you do the homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clear lectures, clear assignments, and is willing to help outside of class. However, I don't think having a good and likable teacher should be top priority in a class with such simple material, escpecially when the workload in his class is much more than most other 1501/02 professors. Avoid if you're schedule already has high workload classes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is willing to work through things with students when they need help and is very accessible during the projects. He is fair in that if you communicate to him, he is understanding, and if you do not communicate with him, he will not be as lenient.
He was always prepared for class and was always willing to help. You can reach out to him at any time of day, and he is always there to assist.
He's a bit of a "tough love" kind of teacher. He teaches you a lot, but you have to work for it. Very well organized and gave lots of additional resources to reference for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: O'Connell is by far the best first year engineering professor. While his class is marginally more challenging, he is available at essentially all times and provides vey clear instructions for the course.

Professor O'Connell is always available for help, whether in person or on Teams. His assignments are challenging, but he is fair with grading. If you communicate well with him, he is understanding with work/deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He does not deserve the bad ratings! Really nice professor, answers every question, and is more than willing to help you. Also, he responds on teams almost instantly. Compared to the other stacked cornerstone class, he was a much more relaxed professor, and even gave us a lot of extensions on assignments. PRO TIP: GO TO TA OFFICE HOURS!!

O'Connell's not a bad professor but do not take this course unless you have to. Way more than double the work of a regular cornerstone class. The assignment descriptions are vague and lots of the homework includes parts of software you have never seen before. If you don't understand them and you're doing it over the weekend you're kind of screwed.

Of course its a hard class, it is your first engineering class. Go to lectures. Do the in class portions, in the class. He is incredibly understanding, and he'll help you reach your goals if you help yourself. He is very knowledgeable and open. He teaches and grades strict because that is what engineering is like in the real world.

O'Connell is super accessible outside of class. Anytime you're struggling with homework or anything at all just message him on Teams and he will respond right away. Lots of homeworks and work outside class but if you go to FYELIC and message the prof in time it's great. Very understanding and great specific lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I literally switched out of engineering after his class. Terrible professor. Though I did take this class during the height of the pandemic so everything was online, but judging by the previous reviews, not much changed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Every SINGLE class will be him reading from slides, he doesn't show/ explain any of the important material enough and if you need to take your attention away YOU WILL fall behind on the lecture, and if you're coding you might as will give up he will not let you catch up. Learn to teach yourself PLEASE, do not waste your time with him if you get him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You will receive little to no help on assignments, have a plethora of software to barely begin learning at the exact same time, and google will often be your friend. Good luck
Learned a lot from him this semester, and he was always willing to help inside/outside of class. Don't know why the ratings are low.
Not a good Professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Legitimately not sure how to describe how bad his class was. All of the other reviews are true. Literal constant homework assignments, grading is incredibly harsh (Canvas' "mean scores" tell-all), easily the meanest professor I've had in my years at NEU. Don't even consider asking about a grade received, it does nothing; may make things worse.

All of the other reviews are correct, he is very impatient and unclear about deadlines, really no time to learn and mostly force feeds poorly presented info. Final project has nothing to do with course content. FYELIC will be your best friend, really didn't learn much despite hours on hours that I put in. Take other profs if you can if not goodluck
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I was lucky to have a small amount of coding experience prior to this class. Professor O'Connell claims that the class is for an introductory level coder; however, I was reliant on a lot of my knowledge prior to the class to get through the assignments. If you do not know a topic prior to the class, expect to learn it on your own.

If there was a rating for their ability to crush any remaining passion I had left for engineering, he would get a 5/5. Maybe he's fine in other regards, but in this class, homework was overwhelming and he went way too fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Possibly one of the worst professors I've ever had. He reads off of lecture slides at 1000 mph and doesn't give you time to read It or think about It yourself. He doesn't teach he reads, I could do that on my own time. Assignment due every 2-3 days and It usually takes that time to finish an assignment. never get a break. never take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: In class, we go over a bunch of slides where the professor reads it outloud like were unable to read on our own. Doesnt really explain what were supposed to be doing properly which causes a lot of confusion and lots of hours spent on assignments. Be prepared to go to tutoring for every single assignment if you dont have prior knowledge of codin
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I do not recommend taking Prof O'Connell for cornerstone 2. Lectures consist of vague slides and him typing code on his computer and showing it on the projector with little to no explanation on what he just did. Unless you have prior coding experience, be prepared to get help on homeworks of which he gives a substantial amount of.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have no coding experience going into this class, you're lowkey screwed. Often times the homework is much more complex than what you learn in class so to get a good grade, get used to constantly going to tutoring sessions, working with upperclassmen, or just straight up teaching yourself. Very lecture heavy, most classes you work in silence.

Worst formatted course I have ever taken. Info in the slides is vague and not helpful for actual assignments. Lectures are not presented well. Quizzes are impossible to prepare for. Workload is astronomical. Worst of all he put all assignment info on TopHat, very unorganized and couldve been provided for free on canvas. wish I could rate 0/5.
Super chill and nice guy, had him for full cornerstone so he definitely worked us pretty hard but it was nothing I couldn't handle.

I do not recommend taking a class taught by him online. His slides and method of teaching is very choppy and does not make sense most of the time. Lots of typing code in silence and then sitting there expecting us to understand what he just did. Also a fairly harsh grader, and loves participation and attendance. Taught myself most of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: O'Connell is an amazing guy. He is well passionate on topics discussed in class. One major down side about his course is that you really need to acquire a solid background on what is taught. The fact that all lessons are posted online, and his expectancy of students to teach themselves, makes it hard for beginners to reach their goals.
Course should be taught online

O'Connell consistently gives more work and grades harder than other Cornerstone professors. However, he is also a better teacher and all around great guy. If you're willing to work for the grade, you will learn a lot from him.

Prof. O'Connell is a really chill guy. He is really helpful and clear about the group project assignments. However, his lessons for new software can be hard to follow and are mostly meant to be self taught. This makes the homework assignments really difficult, especially for students who do not have any prior experience.

The professor is a great guy but never teach/lecture in class. Every assignment and new program (for CAD and coding) are expected to be self-taught. This makes it very hard for beginners to learn a new program for the first time. An online class might help more. Give MUCH more homework than other professors of the same course.

He's pretty laid-back and doesn't care if assignments are handed in a day or two late. The class was pretty easy. He was a generous grader on AutoCAD/SolidWorks assignments and on our final assignments but was tougher on memos and presentations for our group design projects. The lectures were pretty useless but he took attendance randomly, so...
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GROUP PROJECTS--Would take again

reviews.comment: She does not use a normal grading system. Professor Britt grades only earned based on quality, and students have to meet every single requirement in her criteria in order to get an A or B. There is also a ton of homework and a huge chunk of time this class takes outside of class. Pick a god and start praying if this is a required class.
LOOOOOOVE professor britt!! this was the second class i had w her and could not recommend her enough. she is so smart, gives you so many opportunities to improve your work, and you learn a lot.

Professor Britt gives great feedback and is clear about each assignment. Attendance and completing the readings is mandatory since she cold calls to ask about the reading at the beginning of each class. Although your grade relies heavily on the one semester paper, she makes sure you are prepared and have been working on it throughout so it isnt bad

She is absolutely amazing and the most objective English teacher ever; the grading was fair and it is very easy to get an A if you follow instructions. She is super helpful during office hours and will walk you through homework, discussion posts, and major projects. Her exercises were fun and genuinely taught me new skills to improve my writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Britt really makes you work for a good grade in this class, but she makes it clear what she wants and gives great feedback.  If you pay attention in class + participate and go to her office hours to discuss her comments on your work, you'll do fine.  Building in time to go to office hours is a necessity for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof. Britt is great! Rhetoric was a required class for me and she made it interesting. She was really willing to work with us on papers and always found a time to meet, even outside of normal office hours.  There's a decent amount of reading in the beginning, but it levels off. She even does reading guides and discussions to help you through it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Britt is an amazing teacher.  She dedicates herself to the subject and the students she is teaching.  The feedback you get on your papers is amazing compared to a lot of professors, and she is always willing to meet with you and discuss your work.

She's amazing! Offers terrific feedback on essays, super helpful during office hours. Really wants you to learn, respectful of students and their opinions. Good at making extremely densetough readings accessible and easier to understand. I love her!!

Professor Britt is the best professor I have had at Northeastern. She is not an easy grader, but is clear and straightforward with her expectations and always willing to help you improve your writing. She is extremely intelligent and approachable. I have taken intro to rhetoric and advanced writing for pre-law with her and loved both classes.
Professor Britt was the most difficult professor I have ever had and also the best.

Professor Britt is the most difficult professor I have ever had. Not my worst grade, however. She challenges her students, yet constantly reinforces what she is teaching and what she is looking for from the class. Most class discussions are open and can be intimidating because she is very straightforward. But you'll definitely learn something.

Prof. Britt is one of the best I've had at Northeastern. Class is mandatory, but worthwhile. The paper seems intimidating, but you're fully prepared by the time you actually write it. There's one big test (easy if you take notes), two writing assignments and a rough draft and final paper. Gained valuable research skills through the work.

She is very effective. Yet, she is challenging. However, you'll leave the class as a better writer. My ONLY complaint was her grading of grammar. I have an English prof as a friend, and he helped me correct a paper. When I got the paper back, she still wrote I needed grammar work. It got frustrating. Otherwise, it is a great class.
Fairly good, sometimes boring, grading is very subjective

Britt is an excellent professor. She's intelligent, knowledgable, approachable, and on top of her game. She's a tough grader, but she will help you get the A. Listen to all of her suggestions, and your writing will improve 10 fold. She's not a lawyer, but she does have her Ph.D. Anything she doesn't know, she will look up and have the next day. A+

I had thought taking a writing course for legal studies would be helpful for one wishing to pursue law.  However, Britt is not a lawyer and has never been to law school and knows very little about what actual lawyers do.  While taking the course i was also tutored by a lawyer so I can back up my claims.  She is a rhetoritician, not a lawyer.
Great class, insightful discussions, very helpful. Can be a tough grader if your work isn't up to par, but if you're up for a challenging and rewarding experience definitely take one of her classes.

Professor Britt is very intelligent, articulate, and helpful.  She is very professional yet also approachable and friendly.  She facilitates class extremely well and has a great personality...you will learn a lot.

He was super caring and really easy to talk to. If you ever have any concerns, you can talk to him right after class or send him an email and he'll respond quickly (within a day). His grading is different from high school English, but he outlines his grading system within the first week and I honestly preferred it over traditional grading.

Genuinely one of the best professors Ive had, I really hope I get him again for more advanced courses. Sometimes Id head to the classroom early to use the empty space to study, and on days when he'd arrive early as well we would talk about all sorts of funny and interesting stuff. He's awesome, please take him, pay attention and you'll learn tons.

Literally such a caring professor who just wants everyone to enjoy the class and succeed. If you show up and participate (even in little ways) you will do just fine (obviously also complete the assignments). I loved going to this class because no two classes were ever the same from different discussions to new takes on writing. TAKE THIS CLASS!

I highly recommend taking Prof. Bushnell's class! Not only is he a passionate and caring teacher, but his grading criteria is clear from day one. He is helpful and accessible outside of class, and the material discussed in class is engaging. I learned more from this writing class than any other Writing/English class I've taken.
Take Jeremy! He really cares about you and cares about your grades. It's hard to do badly in his classes. Just show up, participate and you'll be fine.

Bushnell was the most caring and sweet professor -- honestly a life saver with his grading policy. As long as you do the work assigned and participate in class you will do well. Highly recommend taking first year writing with him!

Bushnell is super nice and cares about his students. The criteria to get an A is to literally do the work. As long as you submit the papers you get an A. There was a decent amount of time to write each paper and the class never felt like a burden. Would definitely take him if you have the chance.
Professor Bushnell is an awesome. He will give you an A if you participate in class and put effort into your work. He was a real life-saver this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor was very nice and understanding. Made class somewhat enjoyable. Clear grading criteria, so pretty easy to get an A in the class. Only three big papers in the whole semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Bushnell is a super cool guy. He's passionate about his field and he really wants students to succeed in their writing. The class is based on students attempting to get their work published and he takes a realistic approach to the publishing world. We workshop a piece written by everyone and explore other writers works. would recommend

Professor Bushnell is not worth taking for advanced writing within the disciplines. He is not clear about what he wants from students at all - take with someone else or take the class online.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He appears to care about his students, but if your interest do not overlap with his you will struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bushnell is a great english professor who teaches well and is also not a harsh grader. His assignments aren't boring and tedious since you get to choose your own topic to research and write about. As long as you follow the guidelines for the major assignments, you'll do well. He also gives good feedback so you can improve as a writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I didn't learn anything from his class, but he is incredibly clear about what he wants in your papers. It came down to a formula, and once you figure that out, it's easy to get a 100 on every one. Didn't enjoy the class, but you could choose most of your essay topics which was nice. My writing suffered, but give him what he wants & get a good grade

Seemed to know what he was doing, was clear in teaching and his standards, but was a pretty tough grader and it seemed a bit rigged at times. Didn't really take away much from the class. Not a bad teacher, just very forgettable and if you want a flat A you will need to both do the busy work and really know what he's exactly looking for on papers.

He is a nice teacher but I personally felt that he did not give the appropriate amount of feedback for the grades he would give. He tells you that you are doing good but keeps giving you a grade that does not reflect that.

Professor Bushnell is great! He is always looking to help you and if you go to his office hours he definitely will help you a ton! Participate in class a lot, keep up with the minimal readings he assigns, and hand  in the three papers on time following the rubric and you'll be fine. He is my fave english teacher ever and is super fair! Love him!

Jeremy is a great professor and super nice guy, really funny. The class itself is interesting, as well as helpful (if you're looking to get into publishing or be a writer). His assignments are pretty straight forward, not hard if you do them... The classroom vibe is really chill. I highly suggest taking Pub. Arts with Jeremy if you can!

talkative with no point. class is mandatory that is why all student have to listen to his nonsensical lectures. Not at all useful. There are so many great professors who are alienated to accommodate the toxic environment of MGEN.

talkative with no point. class is mandatory that is why all student have to listen to his useless lectures. Not at all useful. There are so many great professors who are alienated to accommodate the toxic environment of MGEN.

Awful.......

My worst nightmare
He can't teach you anything.

Lacks clarity of thought; content outdated, always makes mistakes in assignment, TAs always provide another description afterwards. He doesn't know how2 OOD and writes code worse than undergrad. The worst course I have taken with abstract requirement,  teaching content irrelevant to assignments and low efficiency. I don't want it to be a reason for not choosing NEU Boston campus, but I had an awful experience compared with students in Seattle and SV campus.

If it is not mandatory, I would never ever take his class anymore. Assignments are super hard without any explanation and help. A beginner is asked to write a complete project without syntax being taught.
not good choice

Although, the professor is approachable and has good command over the subject. He just goes on lecturing about the topics and won't bother to teach that in real life or hands on. MASSIVE COURSE LOAD, UNBELIEVABLE. You took 1 hour on coding and you take 3 entire days on debugging.

One of the worst lecturers I have ever seen in my life.

He can't teach you anything, including Java and application modeling. He used INFO5100 slides for INFO5001. He didn't even change the course code on the slide. He is the worst.
Kal Bugrara does not have the tech basics to teach any course. He's a successful businessperson, nothing more.

Lectures are completely useless I have worked for more than 4 years with Java & I can attest that assignments are not going to teach you anything. you will never know on what basis you have been graded. keeps the final projects marks as a secret from students even after many requests you will never got to know your score but Final grade. he Does not answer any mail.

He will waste your time and don't even give you grades. Very unclear grading method. Teaches zero concepts and zero coding.. will come late and leave early and will keep on talking worthless things. AED is mandatory so brace yourself for 4 months of ....
Prof. Bugrara is not a good teacher.

Teaches 0 coding and expected you to know everything but teach you nothing. TAs do all the jobs and our group worked so hard but received a B and other group did almost nothing but get a B+. Forget the fact that he is the teacher of class. You will learn nothing from him, however, he is your only choice for your first class.

Does not respect students. You could never find him in his office as he never comes to the college. Worst of all he does not know how to teach, and grading is so random. You may never know why you got B in his class. No explanation is provided.

I mostly had very good experience with professors except Prof Bugrara.   As a program director he controls other professors in his program and plays politics.  Northeastern University, please hire a better program director since you charge us a lot.

He is very short tempered.Being a Program director he controls all other profs of the department. Rude and worst man in person. If you take any class from his department he will dictate other professor to give lower grade.

Smart guy but doesnt know how to teach. Not enough coverage of Swing. If you don't know Java before taking this class, you will suffer a lot. I would suggest that you take the class with somebody else, but you don't have any other choice anyways. So if you get him, good luck.

If you follow and keep up with what he teaches in the class, I can guarantee you a hot gob at a top 5 technology companies. this guy is hands on practical experience. what i discovered is that, this guy is a universe of technology knowledge. but u need to ask him. he almost knows every thing about technology

Nice guy... Other than that terrible. He doesn't have a bad stile, the problem is that he teach useless stuff. He needs an urgent update in knowledge and get better TAs (who are usually useless) In general a bad experience in everything class-related

I began my Master Degree with the Java class(ISY 100) that he taught. I like his teaching style. Honestly, I never feel bored when taking his class. obviously, he's teaching in a practical way... he's like a scientist and I'm glad i took a class with scientist teacher
never take the class from this professor unless its mandatory. Dont expect any grades and morethan that dont expect that u will learn something.

Tests are difficult and he doesn't answer any clarifying questions during the test. Not the worst professor, but avoid if you can.

Bunce is overall not a bad teacher, but his lectures are so boring. He is redundant while lecturing, and I honestly learned better just watching the videos he recorded. Tests are all 50 MC questions and were not too bad. The class isn't that difficult, but I wouldn't take this class with him if your teacher being engaging is important to you.

Prof. Bunce is kind, caring and very knowledgeable who genuinely wants students to succeed. The course has 3 open response exams (lowest weighted less), 6 reflection articles (lowest dropped) and poll everywhere attendance with 2 drops. If you put in the work, you'll do well.

My complaint with Dr. Bunce was that his lectures were boring and very slow paced. All of his lectures are recorded which was really helpful. There are 3 exams, the lowest scoring of the 3 he weighs the lowest, he drops one quiz grade, and gives 1% extra credit at the end for trace. This gives you plenty of opportunities to get a good grade.
He is a great guy, and the class is easy enough if you are a behavioral neuroscience major. But im sorry, the lecture are a bunch of repeated information that makes me disengage.

A lot of materials in a semester, but exams were okay as long as u put in adequate effort. He also gave out 1% boost for your overall grade for completing the trace evaluatio,n which I think is very generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wouldn't encourage people to take this class unless necessary. Lectures are uninformative but mandatory. I had to teach myself the content before each exam. Incredibly harsh grader and gives no extra credit. Grade is 3 exams and 6 reflections. He's a nice guy, but this class was unnecessarily hard. @BNS students: take a different BNS core.

Theres so much content to learn esp. if you havent taken and bns classes before. Bunce is super passionate but I couldnt keep up with him and there was so much to memorize. Your grade is only composed of quizzes and exams so theres not a lot you can do to raise your grade. Attendance is also mandatory. Great guy but a lot of content to learn.

Professor Bunce is very understanding and an excellent lecturer. Getting an A is attainable if you're willing to put in a lot of work. He films all his lectures on Panopto (very helpful), and all of the questions on the Test can be found in the lectures. However, you will need to rewatch every lecture before an exam to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bunce is super passionate about what he teaches. His exams are based on lecture material and he is a very fair grader. Your effort in this class corresponds to your grade. Bunce is supportive, kind and accessible outside of class. Wants the best for his students. Material can be complicated, so go to class. Great for BNS students.

Dr. Bunce is honestly too disliked, he's great. Tries so hard to make class engaging even with dense material. Wants students to do well. You have to actually come to class to succeed, but if you pay attention and study the exams should be pretty fair. Weekly quizzes and poll everywhere help buffer grade so it's not just exams.

If you don't memorize each slide (and each midterm is about 80-90 slides each) you are cooked. All of his questions are so specific and he gives no other opportunities to raise your grade, even when half the class (I'm not joking) get below a D.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Bunce is a great professor. He explains things clearly and thoroughly and welcomes questions. Exam questions are heavily borrowed from weekly quizzes and PollEverywhere. Your grade is almost entirely based on exams, but he weights your lowest one the least. Attendance is via PollEverywhere, you can miss 3. Lectures are recorded.

Dr. Bunce is great! Exams are extremely fair; mostly all content comes from lectures, and pay attention to what he says (and not just the words on the slides). You don't really need the textbook content for the exams, maybe 1 or 2 questions (I would still skim it though). I personally enjoyed his lectures. Learned lots of useful information.

Professor Bunce is wonderful. His neuroanatomy course is moderately fast-paced, but he always reemphasizes important concepts. He is encouraging, and he provides you with everything you need to succeed (like recording all the lectures!). He is also helpful during office hours, and his tests are very fair. I hope to take another class with him soon.
He is really fun and a generous grader. He tends to go on tangents during lecture but they are usually pretty interesting. His office hours are super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bunce reads from a slidedeck, resulting in boring, monotonous lectures. On the bright side, his tests are an easy 50 MCQs that are pulled straight from the slides. I would take him again for the class, even if it is a little boring.

This man talks A LOT. Sometimes it does also feel like he grades based off of a set grade he decides to give you (I've lost points on tests and gone to office hours and he has said that I got the right answer but didn't answer it how he wanted me to even though he says we can answer it however). He does seem interested in what he teaches though.
He looks evil. PPT not designed for self-study-iers, class good, not boring

- lectures can sometimes be boring and material is made more complicated than necessary 
- exams are not too hard if you put in the effort and study (taken from slides and lecture)
- material is interesting and he is very clear when communicating the material 
- Good prof. and if your willing to put in some effort you will do in the class
professor bunce literally bombards students with information

He is a great professor thats passionate about what he teaches. Sometimes his explanations of pathways are a little rocky but then again they aren't easy so its not his fault. Can get caught up in tangential discussions which is good if you are curious but can be boring for some.

Bunce is probably the nicest person I have ever met. He clearly cares about all of his students and wants them to do well. Sometimes his lectures feel like a lot, and he can be monotone at times, but all lectures are recorded, so you can review anything you did not catch in class. The tests are multiple-choice, and no textbook is needed.

Nice teacher, lectures can be monotone and dry, but its valuable information condensed and made easier to understand. Lectures are recorded so it's easy to go back to if you miss class. Exam questions are pretty straight forward if you study the material. If you go to his office hours, he is very supportive and will answer any questions.

Professor Bunce is clearly a very knowledgable and passionate member of his field. His lectures can be pretty dry, but he's always excited to answer questions. I would say to make sure you are actively listening, because his tests often have material that he doesn't put in the notes. Despite that, tests were very fair, not necessarily easy though.

Professor Bunce is great! While his lectures themselves can be a little dry at times overall the course material was interesting and his exams are super fair as long as you study. He is really accessible both at office hours and via email and overall is just a really nice guy!
He is pretty good at making long, information dense lectures bearable. However, your entire grade is based on 5 multiple choice tests.

Professor Bunce really cares about his students and has a strong passion for neuroscience. Lectures can sometimes be a lot to take in, but if you visit office hours, he'll help clarify any ambiguous topics. Exams are very fair; there aren't any surprises. Overall, a great professor.

Absolutely loved Professor Bunce and his Neuroscience of Aging class. His quizzes and exams are easy as long as you show up to class and review the lecture slides beforehand. Overall a great professor, you could tell that he was really passionate about the topics we discussed in class and was very, very helpful when I went to his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Bunce is very knowledgeable. The lecture slides are all posted on Canvas but most of the information isn't summarized in the slides, so you have to take good notes in class. Always posts lectures on canvas. Moves pretty fast, but repeats info a lot and answers questions. Pay attention in class, study/do the readings, and you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Bunce is great! He knows his stuff and is clearly into what he teaches. He is super organized and has very clear expectations- great class would take one with him again :)

Prof. Bunce is a good guy. He's passionate about neuroscience, and you can tell in his classes. His lectures can be drawn out and repetitive at times, but he gets across the information. Grading rubrics are important, and he sticks to them. Tests are very specific but doable, so be ready to study to know all the information.

Dr. Bunce is a nice man and seems to care about his students, but if I'm being honest Neuro of Aging with him gave me a headache. He goes on super long tangents in class and then expects you to know stuff he mentioned once for the tests. Overall I found him super confusing, but at least he was easier on the poster project and write ups.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

He can spend the first half of class outlining what we did the class before. Tests are multiple choice and can be tricky.

I really enjoyed the content of this class but get ready to study a lot. No hw. 3 exams, 3 quizzes, if you don't do well, your grade will suffer. Definitely rewatch his lectures to study because some questions relate to very small parts mentioned once. If you memorize well, you'll do fine. I liked Jamie despite it all but I get the boring part.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This man's class made me want to switch majors. In fact, my roommate DID switch majors after taking his class. He is dry in his lectures and will put you to sleep. His tests are all MC but there are few of them, so if you bomb one you're screwed for the rest of the class. I actively avoid taking him as a professor for any other class.

Professor Bunce's Biopsychology class is incredibly boring. His lectures are dry and full of information. His multiple choice tests and quizzes are specific and very challenging. The questions do not seem representative of the material covered in lecture. I would not recommend this, at it was by far the hardest PSYC class I have taken.

One of my favorite professors at Northeastern. Material can be tricky but he is a very fair grader and not hard to do well in his class as long as you study before exams. Everything you need to know for exams he posts on Blackboard. He also posts all of his lectures on Tegrity so attendance is not mandatory. He really cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing and clear lectures. He is the best lecturer I've had at Northeastern. You need to attend or at least watch the lectures online. The material is not easy and a bit complex, and you have to show you understand it in the exams, but if you watch the lectures and read the papers you should be fine.

I had Bunce for Neuroscience of Aging and Biopsych and I really enjoyed his classes. As long as you pay attention during his lectures and take notes, you will do fine! He's super nice and willing to help and it's not hard to figure out what he is looking for on tests.

Bunce is a genius, but I am not. His tests are VERY specific. I have never worked so hard ina class in my life. I spend my spare time listening to his lectures. He is an amazing person, but I find myself always struggling to keep up in his lectures. It is A LOT of info very fast. Only take neurobio with him if you had him for biopsych!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Bunce is a boring lecturer. He posts his powerpoints on blackboard, but he actually reads his lectures from a manuscript that he doesn't share with the class. Thank God he records his lectures because this man talks WAY too fast to keep up. Quizzes and tests are all MC, but very very specific so study all details. Prepare to spend HOURS studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a very nice guy that is passionate about neuroscience. He gets pretty boring during the lectures. Never really paid attention during class and did just fine in his class. His homework assignments included LOTS of reading. Tests and quizzes were all short answer, but I thought they were pretty easy if you studied the readings and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best advice is to listen to his recorded lectures! All the information/ examples you need to do well on the exams/ quizzes are things he has said in lecture, you just have to pay attention. Overall, he is a very knowledgeable and fair professor, don't be afraid to go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Would take again

reviews.comment: Doesn't know how to make the class interesting, so its hard to maintain attention and he includes too much material. Exams are open response, and it seems impossible to get an A. Don't recommend to anyone.

Don't take this Professor. 1) Talks way too fast- you will fail his quizzes and exams due to his useless lectures. 2) Reads off of a script in class, but DOESN'T share it with us- as if digesting the material isn't enough to do. 3) A dozen worthless article write ups. 4) Takes points off for ANYTHING, almost impossible to get an A. Oh he's boring!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I took this class as an elective bc it sounded interesting and it turned out to be a nightmare. His slides are empty, no words even though he reads from his notes that he could share. Talks too fast to be able to type everything so you have to listen to his recordings. Quizzes and tests are open responses which makes the whole thing even harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Bunce is a solid choice to get started in the neuroscience path. He is sociable, knows what he is talking about, and is very accessible outside class. He wants you to do well. His tests are all short answer, and they are tough if you don't study. Put in the work and be interested in the material. You'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Bunce was one of the best professors I have had. There are around 15 articles that you read throughout the year and you are expected to write a short one page summary of each article. His quizzes and tests are open answer, but all tests are things that have been reviewed multiple times in class. Fair grader and does his best to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: i LOVE dr. bunce. such a nice professor, and whenever you need him just go to office hours or shoot him an email. very accommodating and willing to talk about class as well as longer-term goals. i had him for bio psyc and this course (neurobio) was very similar. didn't require much extra effort, notes were the same as from before.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Bunce really is a gem. The material can be dry, and it's hard for him to always make up for that, but he tries. He's kind, brilliant, and really wants his students to do well. I learned quite a bit with him.

Dr. Bunce was a great professor! He really cares about his student's learning and is always available for extra help. His classes are lecture heavy but they are interesting and the slides are always online. Definitely a tough class but that's expected of the course material.
He's very monotone. It's not hard content, but it is very much based on his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Need to put in some effort to pass. There's a lot of material, but if you pay attention in class and read the textbook you should be fine. Tests are based more on concepts and systems than details. He can lecture quickly, but if you ask him a question he's very good at explaining, and is available outside of class, beyond posted office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: lectures be drier than the saharan desert
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Straight forward class with interesting material. No need to get the textbook. Has his own powerpoint slides that directly translate to the testing material. Worth taking if interested in the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Bunce is a good person but his lectures are long and boring. The topic is really interesting but it is hard to concentrate for the entire class time. You will do fine on quizzes and tests if you study (or if you can manage to pay attention). On the other hand, he really knows his stuff and will help if you go to office hours.

Dr. Bunce is honestly my favorite professor at NU so far. The course is difficult, but he is ALWAYS willing to help. I even went into his office hours one day and asked him how he suggest I study for quizzes and exams, and he was extremely helpful. You can tell he really loves the subject which is infectious. Can be a boring course, but worth it!

Dr. Bunce is quite interesting, if you're interested in the topic. Very knowledgeable and clear about what he is teaching, will always answer questions clearly. Lectures can feel long but if you write down his clarifying statements about the slides and listen it will be fine. Super nice guy as well. Tests are  MC straightforward pathways/concepts.
Not that exciting of a class. However, he definitely knows what he's talking about so I would imagine that if you were really interested in a course topic you would find his class interesting.
Boring.

Prof. Bucar is excellent at teaching this class. This class is an easy A, just do your work on time. Theres lots of discussion posts and essays but could all be completed within a reasonable amount of time. I highly recommend this class if you are taking for credit or NUpath. Put effort into this class, work should only take about 1-2 hours weekly!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took her 'Selling Spirituality' class in Fall 2024 and it was great. flipped classroom, so did all the readings at home and the discussion and work in class. LOTS OF READING. but as long as you submit your notes and actually do the readings and go to class, and don't use ChatGPT for any assignments, you will do fine. Easy A. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor, the class discussions are so eye opening and although the readings can be long and dense it is worth it. Put effort into the large assignments as she has fairly high standards for those and don't blow off the small assignments, they pad your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: PHIL1271 (online): Readings were eye-opening and she's very passionate abt the material which makes the course super interesting. As far as grading goes: do readings + watch lectures and you'll be fine. Graded on discussion boards, 6 open-ended weekly reflections (~300 words), and 2 major essays: an Op-Ed and the final. Highly recommended.

Professor Bucar is incredibly passionate and really makes you think. Her class relies on participation and so as a result her class can be disorganized at moments. She is incredibly caring and I would highly reccomend the class. She is brilliant!

I loved this class, it was a flipped classroom and you have to do the reading before each class but as long as you do those things you'll do well. Didn't think it was a difficult class, but I also genuinely enjoyed the topic and found the readings interesting. The readings are long, the tests are straightforward and there is a final project/paper.
Class description on banner does not match the reality of the class. All you do is read and discuss. Bucar is short tempered with students and made me feel unwelcomed during office hours.
Sends email to class saying it is "dangerous" to post reviews here. beware.

Participation is really important, so you should talk every class. Easy to pass but hard to do well. Interesting but only learn a topic from one specific author so you don't learn as much as you could. And don't yawn...
topic is interesting but it is strictly a reading analysis class. would've liked to hear her opinions. guest lecturer was the best part.

I don't appreciate how much work must be done for a ONE-CREDIT CLASS, and why her TA grades part of some assignments but she grades others. The feedback from both is subjective, so it's difficult to know whose advice to follow. She often asks painfully obvious questions and makes it clear that she knows little about the architecture field.

She's really helpful but she goes over the same things a lot. One time we spent 2 lessons learning how to use in design when we were already taught it. tbh I think she just needs better coordination with studio class teachers.
Lynn is amazing. She coordinates every Architecture Co-op student, and still makes time to teach a class and visit with employers. If you want to do well at Northeastern, Lynn is the person to know!
Lynn gets you ready for co-op and everything she says will help in future. Pay attention because she notices everything you do.
Lynn is an engaging instructor and extremely helpful with the co-op process.
Lynn was an amazing co-op class teacher.  The exercises she used to get us ready for co-op were very helpful. Lots of fun! but make sure you show up on time

Very good critiques, lots of iteration and work but for the better. Very funny and smart guy. If you take his crits seriously there is no doubt you will improve as a designer. He forces you to think abstractly and on more than one iteration at once, many students find this difficult.

During a critique, I was told my design ‘looks like pad/tampon packaging.' Basic proof of his mediocre background, lack of true knowledge, expertise in the field and of course teaching etiquette. He dictates students to boost his ego. It's sad Northeastern doesn't evaluate professors on merit.

Professor gives no structures to his classes, does not know how to read rooms, made ignorant transphobic remarks in class, did not give helpful feedback, does not respond to emails. He gave helpful career and portfolio guidance, but is heavily graphic design focused. Would not recommend this course

You have to be very good with time management by yourself. All crit based, but he doesn't give good advice. Doesn't really enforce participation, my class was very small and people didn't really talk so i didn't get that much out of it. SO MUCH WORK. He is a fun guy but grade is determined mainly by how much he likes you.

Class is entirely critique based. He is entertaining but often harsh with crit and doesn't actually advise you what to fix, just tells you what you did wrong. Expects an excessive amount of drafts per project which was burdensome for my workload.

Prof teaches a very loose curriculum and our class had 3 main projects/deliverables. We'd often have a ton of work due with quite vague guidelines (purposefully so, to not hinder creativity as he said it). My class had a lot of people who didn't speak and he was ok with that, which was unfortunate. Unusual experience overall, not one I'd redo.

You have no indication of your grade until the very end, he says it is always subject to change. Funny and personable man, just make sure you're cool with foul language. A ridiculous amount of homework, a very high-stress class which has an emphasis on quantity over quality which is the opposite of what you want in a design class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Byron teaches his classes at a super quick level, and sometimes expects students know more than they actually do

Taking DS 2000 with Byron was a great experience. He showed beginners like me that you can do many things with python. In class sessions were helpful for homework and quizzes. Truly became on of my favorite professors at Northeastern.

He is more well-suited for conducting research instead of instructions. The math algorithms in this course are kind of PhD-level, but he cannot interpret them in an easily understandable way. The examples he uses are complex, hard to follow if you are not experienced in that area. If you are a math genius, take this course!

Class is only review of homework and textbook and syntax, so going is optional, but do know the quiz days. All homework and everything is online, so it's mainly focusing on the hw. Office hours are great. One big project by the end, using all that you know and how much you research. Amazing course, good prof.

I was an intern with Dr. Wallace (Byron, as he prefers). He got some really cool insights into the project at hand which made an otherwise obscure topic quite easy to follow. He even replies on weekends if it's urgent and is easily accessible on slack as well as in-person. So easy-going plus enthusiastic plus insightful which is amazing!
Hes my favorite professor that Ive had so far at Northeastern. I would highly recommend taking a class with him.

Byron is a lovable and cheerful professor. Yes, call him Byron and not professor as that's how he prefers it. I actually took him last semester but I wanted to make sure people know he's a good person. The class is kind of tough, especially for new people to CS, so be sure to ask questions and stay ahead of work. Good luck.

Honestly can't complain. Not his fault that the homework gets annoying at times, it's just the way the class is set up. Knows what he's doing, is happy to help and answer questions, and preps you well for the exams. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll fall behind pretty quickly if you skip (because you work in Racket...). Would recommend.

nicest professor I've had. This class wasn't hard to get a good grade in, but it was difficult to actually learn/understand the material. She sometimes got confused by her notes during her lectures and then assigned homework that she didn't know how to do. Let us correct quizzes and get extensions when needed.

Prof. Carrier is amazing. Her lectures and homework prepare you perfectly for the four quizzes she gives for the semester (no tests/final). She cares deeply about her students and is definitely one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern (especially in the cheme department).

The nicest prof. I've ever had. Her lectures are pretty clear and the homework prepares you well for tests. Only con was that she was extremely disorganized, but she is a very sweet person and understanding with extensions, which made up for it. Allowed test corrections for half credit, which I know helped a lot of people.

I would rather be taught organic chemistry by a degenerate camel with schizophrenia rather than suzie. i didnt think it was possible to be so mis-informed in a subject you are required to have a PhD to teach...
THE WORST TEACHER ON NORTHEASTERN"S CAMPUS BY FAR. PLEASEEEEEEE TAKE ANOTHER TEACHER IF U CAN. She is the WORST and I'm a very good student.
Most horrible teacher. Not helpful, book cannot be used to study because she doesn't teach from it. Memorization of the study guides is the only way to get a good grade.

By far worst teacher I have ever had. My life was miserable during this class. It was so bad a tutor couldn't even save you. I am pretty positive she got fired so no worries anymore. BU can have her back!

During the semester, 2 kids (or the same kid twice) got a question right on the blackboard. Both times resulted in the whole class applauding. I understand Orgo isn't supposed to be easy but unfortunately her lectures make things worse which is frustrating. You'd think that her tests would somehow be related to her lectures but they're far from it

Suzie is crazy.  Her tests are ridiculously hard and don't cover the material she covered in class.  She relies too heavily on her slide shows and doesn't actually teach us the material.  If asked a question she stumbles and she is constantly referring to her notes throughout lecture.  Avoid her if you can!

Made the mistake of concentrating on the lectures for the first Orgo test. She'll cover the basics but will throw curveball questions. The second test, I ignored her lectures and used soley the textbook and had a much better understanding of the material. However, if you have a friend who already took this class, cling onto them and don't let go.

Definitely not a good teacher. If youre looking to be taught organic chemistry, don't take Byun. Everyday I question how she managed to get a PhD in Chemistry, because she has the hardest time answering the simplest questions and frequently gets confused by her notes. Its like she doesn't understand what she's doing. Reading the book is necessary.

I respect the fact that Prof. Byun is new, however I feel that her incompetence, at any level of education, is unacceptable. Her nose is buried in her notes throughout class, writing and talking at the same time, as if she were talking herself through the material and not us.  Students did exams in pencil and changed answers for a re-grade.

If you are smart this class is easy.  I got a 100 on almost every test.  You have to read the book and notes and learn her test style and you should do fine, as her tests cover only a small fraction of the total material.  Yes, overall she's a pretty bad teacher and I didn't learn much, but if you put in the work you'll get an A.
If you can, avoid her.  Warner is even better.  She doesn't know the subject.  If you ask a question, she won't be able to answer it.  AHHHHHHHHHH!

You can't just rely on your lecture notes. She is very unclear with her teaching, and going to her office hours and asking questions is useless because her answer most of the time is, "You just gotta know" or she'll give you a page number. She makes it hard to establish a student-teacher relationship. She's always rushy in class and office hours.

The WORST teacher I've ever had here.  Suzie sucks.  She's just awful in every regard- she doesn't understand the material and is constantly corrected by students.  She goes through notes at a rapid-fire pace but doesn't explain them nearly enough, and asking her a question is a flat out waste of your time.

Okay, so byun is hard but so is orgo. She is no worse then warnner and i might say she is easier. She lectures and if you can keep up with her she makes sense out of all the concepts. Her grading is harsh but all averages for orgo are low. overall she wasn't that bad.
horrible teacher... can't even speak english!! in the second semester, she started using powerpoints and pointless!! practice exams are not helpful AT ALL!!

Class notes don't prepare you well for class, if you can even understand your notes because she goes unreasonably fast and without much clarity.  Test were too hard and had problems she never covered in class. constantly needed correction.  Avoid her if you can.

Byun makes orgo harder than it already is. Her lectures are usually fast and unclear. Her last test was incredibly hard and far off from the difficulty of the practice test. Not to mention the keys for the practice tests usually have mistakes on them. One plus- due to the complaints, she did a better job of telling us how the final was gonna be.

Terrible.  Lecture is useless as she usually doesn't know what she is talking about.  Gives practice exams that are usually wrong.  Also, make sure you check your returned exams because she usually makes mistakes while correcting or uses the wrong answers.  Avoid at all costs.  She thinks a class avg below 50 is decent and laughed about it in class

Worst teacher ever.  She has no clue how to teach and does not know what she is talking about in lecture.  She puts material on exams that was not covered in class or the text.  Going to class is pretty much useless as all learning is done through the text.  Gives practice exams but most of the questions on them are incorrectly answered on the key.

Terrible teacher.  Do what ever you can to get another teacher.  Her lectures are incomprehensible and tend to be all over the place.  She tends to speed through topics in class while everyone falls behind, not to mention she does not know what she is talking about.  Her tests are very difficult and often include material not covered in class.

She thinks a class average on an exam of below 50% is "healthy." I pray to God that she gets fired ASAP not only for my sake but for the entire student population. It is a shame that we have to pay around $50,000 a year and have it wasted in a class where you will learn NOTHING and your GPA will suffer, no matter what you try to do.

Please, if you can avoid it, take orgo with someone other than Prof. Byun! The average on the last exam was ridiculously low, and she thought it was funny! If you do end up with her, I guarantee you will be teaching yourself because she doesn't know how. As someone else said, she really should not be responsible for teaching anyone this subject.

It seems unfair to have a horrendous professor for Organic Chemistry. I mean, the class is hard enough without a teacher who comes to class every day like she stumbled in by accident, but Byun's level of complete incompetence in all matters organic chem is really the iceberg to the proverbial Titanic that is my gpa.

Going to class is completely pointless. She reads off her notes the entire time and cannot answer a question if her life depends on it. Students are constantly correcting her. Tests are not that hard but she doesn't write them herself and will not tell you what they are going to be on. all and all, a completely waste of my time.
her tests are hard (b/c she doesnt make them up)but she also doesnt teach the material at all..horrible teacher... avoid at all costs
WORST TEACHER I'VE EVER HAD..she doesnt understand the subject, and can definatly not teach it

Terrible teacher,constantly needs correcting by students, extremely unclear about how she will determine your grade, makes an already hard subject nearly impossible to understand, does not make up her own tests, i had to completely teach my self orgo
She is useless! Extremely hard grader and is clueless in class!

She is very chill and she makes you go outside a lot on fieldtrips and outside of class time for the projects but overall, the projects aren't bad, homework wasn't bad, classes can be boring, you won't know your grade until the end.

She's honestly a very sweet and caring person. She gives a lot of great feedback, and her class actually taught me a lot. She takes forever to grade, but I feel like if you converse with her a lot, she will give you a better grade on the essays. It's kind of content-heavy, though, and there are a lot of field trips.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You will grow as a writer in this course and the projects are very interesting. Be prepared to separate from the traditional five paragraph essay you were used to in high school. Carolyn is helpful and always available to give feedback and help students after class. If you have to take writing at Northeastern, take Carolyn you will not regret it!
It's 2 and a half months into the semester and we have no grades back yet

Professor Sirois is really nice and will always offer advice to guide you to writing better portfolios. The material is interesting and the classes not too hard. If you show up and make a bit of effort to write all the assignments, it's not hard to get a good grade.  I would definitely recommend her for first year writing.

Mrs. Sirois without a doubt cares for her students and makes sure the assignments are beneficial to us as students and interesting. She allows room for your own creativity and personality in the writing assignments which makes it unlike regular writing classes. I really enjoyed this class and her as a professor!

Professor Siriois significantly helped me improve my writing. She is very nice, helpful, and understanding towards students. The class content is interesting and ranges greatly, which keeps you engaged. She is willing to meet with you if you need help with anything and will always find a time that works for you.

Professor Sirois has been one of the best professor I have had a Northeastern. Pr. Sirois is very helpful. She will make the time to meet with you if you have need extra help. The projects in this class are very interesting and fun. If you put the effort and time to your work you will likely do well in this class.
Great Professor;  Assignments are straightforward and as long as you put the time into your assignments, you can definitely see yourself in the 'A' scale.

Ms Sirois was one of the best English professors I have ever had, dating back through high school. She will go out of her way to find extra time to meet with you and makes sure you understand the material. The essays covered everything from analytical writing to personal narratives and it was a great experience to do these and My writing improved.
Her lectures and requirements for assignments were confusing. So much work.
It is nice to take her class! She loves to help students. She will answer all questions that you have.
Great class

Although she ramble senselessly and the only improvement you find in your writing is from just having to write over and over again, this course is incredibly easy. As long as you show up, show you put in effort, participate in class, and organize your portfolio you will get an A.
SHE IS AN AWESOME PROFESSOR AS LONG AS YOU GO TO CLASS KEEP UP WITH WORK AND SHOW THAT YOU ARE PUTTING THE EFFORT IN....CLASS TAUGHT ME A LOT ABOUT WRITING AND PREPARED ME FOR MY SOPHOMORE YEAR!

She can be really lenient, you can submit stuff several days later and most of the time she wont care. Much course work but if you do a decent job and put effort into the organization of the folio you should get a good grade.  Dont buy the book, it's isnt useful you can find stories on the internet

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!! It is a waste of time. If you do take it do all assignments and try to word things nicely and to give the impression you understand the reading. If you follow those advices you should get an A.

She is very unclear when giving out assigning. It's hard to understand what is she asking for her assignments. Make your essays sound good and you will do well on her class. That's what i found out while taking her class, its how you say it and not what you're saying.

Very easy but PAINFULLY boring and EXTREMELY useless class. She is a nice person, but she rambles and is oblivious to the fact that nobody is paying attention. There is a lot of pointless work. The content is boring and the curriculum is weak. Unprofound and basic concepts are overanalyzed. The textbook is barely used so don't buy it.
She would be a better teacher is she would not go on talking about senseless things.
Had her in 1993, bad teacher if you get her drop the class. You pay enough at NU and it is not worth the money.
