Course was hard but she grades very easily. You can tell that she would much rather be doing cosmetic science and not gen chem.. Very sweet person, not the strongest teacher, she mainly just reads off of the slides and if they're difficult to follow you're cooked.

Sweetest and friendliest professor but her lectures were long, fast, and difficult to keep up with. Be prepared to relearn most of the content independently before exams—which make up almost all of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a sweet person; she does the best job possible at condensing a dizzying amount of content into one class. Her lecture slides are clear and she provides plenty of online resources in Canvas. Two tests and the final make up the majority of the grade in her class, with a few comparatively small, low-stress assignments/extra credit opportunities.

The course in general was long, but she has lecture heavy slides everyday. Make sure you are VERY familiar with each days content as it goes quick and she does not slow down. Her practice exams are very different from her actual exams. Nice person.

Prof. Cassano is very nice but you will need to put in effort and work hard to pass this class. There are only two midterms and a final exam that determine your grade. She only gives five homework assignments, which are not even about the chem hw . This class covers two semesters worth of material in one semester.Slides are easy to understand.
Very lecture and test heavy, but amazing class and very caring professor!

Dr. Cassano is not only knowledgeable but extremely passionate about chemistry. She made accelerated gen chem in one semester easy with her organized chem lectures and wide access to practice problems and resources. She is so nice too!

Probably one of the best teachers I've had. Lectures and slides are so clear and in-depth. Both walk you through examples step by step. Made accelerated gen chem genuinely enjoyable and somewhat easy. She posts all her slides, resources, practice problems, and textbook (for free) and her Canvas is super organized. Wish she were at Boston campus.

Hempel was tough in all the right ways. She gives constructive feedback and encourages asking questions with constructive responses. Most of which were explained through an example. Her class was not a cake walk by any means but she truly cares for her students. You need to put forth a lot of effort but she made it enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Carlene is an extremely caring teacher who values making close connections with her students. This being said, the class is very fast paced and once you get behind it's impossible to catch up unless you devote all of your time to it. I don't recommend taking the class with other writing heavy classes but if you want great feedback she is perfect.
Caring Instructor, she transmits the passion for journalism. Tough grader.

Be prepared to treat journalism like your profession, even as a first-year student. Carlene is super caring and wants her students to succeed but her expectations were unlike anything I've experienced before. Only would recommend for students who are absolutely certain they want to pursue the field of journalism in their future.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: One of the hardest classes I've ever taken. An intro class but she said, "I teach it like my graduate class." She pushes you to be better, but didn't teach core concepts. You can tell she cares so much, and she wants a close-knit community, but I just always felt stressed. She's very easy to contact though, and will work with you if you need help.

carlene is a fantastic professor who challenges each of her students in a way that is still empathetic and kind. all carlene wants is for her students to learn through her fast-paced, hands-on, collaborative approach that mirrors a true newsroom. you will do much better in this class if you facilitate a relationship with her and your classmates!!!

If you graduate from Northeastern as a journalism student without taking a class with Carlene first, you're doing yourself a disservice. She is the most caring and invested professor I've ever had here, and I've gotten so much out of her classes. She's makes a point to build a community in her class too, which is so refreshing at a big school.

Carlene is professor that is going to make you a better writer. She is one of the best professors Ive had at Northeastern. She is a caring and wonderful professor who has a lot of knowledge to offer. Her notes are thoughtful. The whole semester I felt that she was on my teamunlike some professors who make it feel like they want you to fail.

Carlene takes the time to explain the purpose behind every assignment so it never feels like she is challenging you for the purpose of being challenging. With good time management scheduling interviews (this is BIG if youre working full time!), the workload is very manageable. What I learned the hard way: if you want the A, do the extra credit

You learn a lot and the workload is incredibly manageable with some extra attention to time management. Shell dock points on papers that arent written exactly how she would have approached them and seems to dock points on papers that arent her own narrow definition of perfect. Definitely views herself as more important than she is to the field
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and avoid her. She is extremely demanding but in the worst way possible. I had to drop her class as soon as I met her because I knew she was going to make me want to die.

She's intimidating at first but deeply cares about her students. The class is difficult, but it is the best way to prepare for a career in journalism. She is an incredible mentor and will support you throughout the process of every assignment. Highly recommend taking her class, she will greatly improve your writing and teach you through experience.

I took Enterprise 1 with Carlene. She may seem intimidating at first, but this course will be your career's best friend. The classroom environment is stressful, but your writing will improve immensely by the end of your time with her, because she will teach you how to format an article to make it great.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: 1st JRNL course I took & it made me change majors. One of my first stories ever quoting higher ups, I couldn't get people to talk to me. She said if you don't have it on time, don't bother handing it in so I didn't. Next day she says if we don't have them by midnight we fail the class. Spent 10 hours 68 phone calls got it in at 11:30. Not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Carlene isn't just a professor, she's a mentor. She will fight for you to the death, but also immediately call you out for slacking. She will make you work for your grade and challenge you at every corner. If you take her courses, however, you will undoubtedly emerge as a stronger journalist. Don't be afraid to stand up to her.

I STILL have PTSD after taking Journalism 2 with her. I cried all the time because of this class. No voice recorder for interviews? Pretty archaic if you ask me. She is really hard to work with; I agree with the "my way or the highway" attitude. Work  SUPER hard or else you're screwed.

Carlene is easily the toughest teacher I've encountered at NU and her classes will completely stress you out. But she really knows her stuff and will make you such a better writer. There's NO cutting corners or getting away with not giving it your absolute best. Definitely recommend her classes, she is awesome

The class itself was pretty helpful. Carlene is tough though. Fairly archaic journalism methods (loves newspapers, doesn't allow voice recorders for interviews, pretty anti-tech all around). Difficult to work with her if she disagrees with you, and there's a good chance she will.

Intense, don't get give less than 100%. Ever. Gives tough assignments and throws you to the wolves early.  Yes,treat the course as a job, she'll push limits and give assignments that require jumping through hoops.  You really need to focus on honing your skills, because the final requires instinct over memory. Real 'rite of passage' type prof.
Carlene was an excellent professor! She demands a lot and isn't the easiest grader but she is always willing to help. If you want to become a better writer definitely take the class!
Don't take this class if you are an athlete.

Carlene scared the crap out of me. She is TOUGH but if you can survive her madness it will make you a far better journalism. Taking her class was like having a child, it was a full time job. You cannot slack, wait till the last minute or try to cut corners. Strick on cell phones. DO NOT SLACK and youll succeed in her class.

Carlene is very enthusiastic about journalism. It's hard not to enjoy, but she does teach somewhat antiquated methods (not allowed to record interviews and have to write longhand). Apart from that, J1 is very enjoyable with her. She's very open, is easy to talk to and will help whenever she can.

I had Carlene for both J2 and Magazine Writing. Yes she is a tough teacher, but she really knows her stuff and is genuinely interested in helping you become a better writer. She is probably one of the biggest assets to the Journalism School at Northeastern. If you get the chance to have a class with her, it would be worth your while!!

OK people, here's the deal with Carlene: If you're interested in journalism and want to seriously make a career of it, there is no one better than her. She's a wonderful person and tells it like it is. She'll write you recommendation letters if you do well too. Carlene is amazing, simple as that, but be prepared to work, she expects you to.

She is not that great of a teacher if she doesn't like you personally. She has a very "my way or the highway" attitude. I used to schedule appointments to see her outside class and she wouldn't show up!

She thinks she's a gift to the world of journalism.  Learn your AP style because it's on the tests and she grades you down if you don't have things the right way on an article.  I definitely recommend going to her office hours and having her edit your stuff before turning it in.  She doesn't mind at all and it'll definitely help your grade.
She is so nice and helpful! I loved this class. A lot of people thought it was really difficult, but I thought it wasn't that hard. It was just the right amount of difficulty.

Hempel is the best journalism teacher I've had in my five years at NU. I took J1 and J2 from her. She is by far the hardest of the teachers, but you will become a better writer/reporter because of it. While she is demanding she is very nice and will help you outside of class even after you complete the class.
No Comments
Ok, not that great.

She had this attitude of being better than us because we're students and she's a working journalist. She also made every lesson a personal story about her life, and not in a helpful "this is what I learned" kind of way. She has a HUGE ego. Couldn't stand her.
She is a cool chick for sure, sometimes wondered though if she was too cocky, which may have been reflected in grading.  Def sexy and knows it.

She's tough and expects a lot from her class, in this case Mag Writing. But, Carlene, for us to be able to write in magazine style instead of newspaper you actually need to teach what the difference is. My only complaint...

Carlene is a really awesome professor. She has a lot of experience in the field and she relates her experiences to the class. There's a lot of work to do and you'll hate the class at times but she made my writing really improve and she'll help you any time of day if you need it.
she's intimidating. she knows her stuff, but she'll make you or break me.

Really makes you decide if you want to be a journalist or not. She is a good professor and pushes you to your limits. She does not settle for less and will not take shabby excuses if you cannot do something. She is willing to help to the nth degree if you are willing to try. Great class.

Despite the amounts of work and time you have to put into this class, you will learn so much from Carlene. Yes she may be scary, but do not be scared of her. Participate, ask questions PROOF READ everything and work hard. It will pay off!
No Comments

She's tough. But she's the kind of tough to bring the best out in you. She's no easy "gal" but if you truly want to improve, you'll take the class. She works you hard, but she knows she does. Hard, but nice, and you'll be better off for it.

Carlene is by far the best professor i've had at Northeastern. She can be tough, and at first I resisted the hell out of her, but she challenged me and my writing will forever be better for it. Her bark is way bigger than her bite....don't be intimidated. If you let her she can teach you a lot.
carlene is a really nice person and a caring professor.  she kept things interesting and made me a better writer.  i want to take magazine writing with her!!
Besides being a great teacher, she helped me find direction in the school of arts and sciences.

I like Carlene as a person, too. She has a good sense of humor and tries hard to relate to her students (since she is still young, in her 30s). I was not crazy about her class, though. Maybe because it is an intro class, but I thought it was boring and mad

As a person, I'm definitely down with Carlene, but as a professor, I don't know. Definitely favors the apple polishers that work on the NU news, to the frustration of the other members of the class, praised the work of these little dweebs regardless of how

The best journalism prof I've had so far. Can be a tough grader, but she always listens to your concerns & tries to be fair. My writing definitely improved in her class. Also funny & easy to get along with. She knows her stuff.

Best teacher in the journalism department. She is a caring teacher who wants to see her students succeed. She knows what she is talking about - even though she might be a hard grader - she will make you a stronger writer and more knowledgable of journalism as a career.

Tough grader, but definately wants to help you become the best that you can be. Really cares about all her students. Makes early class interesting. Gives surprise news quizzes. Great course though I definately feel like i learned more in her class than any other so far.
really cares about her students and wants to help in everyway, but if you do not want to be a journalist DO NOT TAKE HER..there is a lot ofhardcore newspaper writing and practices
kind of a **** at times. Nice enough most of the time though.
Carlene is the best

Carlene is an awesome teacher-- very knowledgeable, funny and actually cares about her students (as opposed to most professors I've had).  She's not easy, but a journalism teacher shouldn't be.  You will learn a lot in her class and possibly enjoy actually going (I did).

i love carlene! wasn't a big fan of writing before i took her class, but she made my creativity come out. truly enjoyed the class and especially enjoyed her teaching it. she is so helpful and is willing to take your calls at almost any hour. one of the best professors and one one of the best classes
No Comments

Definitely not an easy A, you have to put in the work to get your grade, but if you complete all assignments she guarantees you get a B. Other than that, she is very sweet and listens to her students. I can tell she really cares about our mental health and success. She's always available for extra help if you reach out.

I loved Dr. Musselman! She is more than willing to take you under her wing if you show interest. Her essays and projects are made to pull you out of your comfort zone while still being simple. Grading is confusing and vague at times so be sure to ask questions! If you follow her guidelines and listen to her feedback you will do well. Super sweet!
Great women and professor,  available if you need extra help. Gives constructive feedback in each paper to help you improve.

Great Professor. Dr. Musselman will make you appreciate writing and you will enjoy writing about 3 essays and 1 video project/graphic novel. With enough effort and re-writes, you will be able to receive a good grade.

Great professor, really keeps class interesting. A tough grader, but really helps you to improve. She was very willing to meet with you outside of class to help you. I was in her honors section of College Writing, and class was always a lot of fun. She brought in food for us several times, and overall was my favorite professor this semester.

I was in her Honors section of College Writing. She's an interesting person, but will not give you a good grade if you don'r write what she wants to hear, which is sometimes hard to determine. Her written feedback is often vague and unhelpful, but if you go to her office hours and ask a lot of questions you can sometimes get the idea.

I took the honors section of Advanced Writing in the Disciplines. She is available to help you if you need it, but I found the class and the assignments really stupid and uninteresting. If you put in effort, you will do fine, but she thinks writing is the most important subject when Pharmacy majors have more important things to worry about.

Always ready to help. Well informed and enthusiastic. Accepts other opinions -- people who say otherwise couldn't defend their position well enough or didn't have the motivation or confidence to do it anyway. I got an A and I disagreed frequently -- maybe not with subject matter, but sbout writing styles and sentence structure.
Nice lady and passionate about her work. The history of english course is difficult to grasp, but she is a very kind and fair grader.

Cecelia loves what she teaches. I enjoyed listening to her lectures. She is always there to help you if you need it. Show up, do the problem sets. She offers a lot of bonus points and second chances! Just make sure you do them and hand everything in!
this class requires a lot of work, like any writing class. the assignments are somewhat open ended and can be confusing, but she is very easy to reach for help.
very helpful when you need help.  If you want to do well, you will, and you'll improve your writing on the way.
Best writing teacher ever

Ok...this goes out to all of the science majors who really, REALLY don't want to take Middler Writing.  TAKE THIS CLASS!  The writing part is the same as any other ENG 307 class, but Professor Musselman is always willing to lend a helping hand with papers.  Her teaching is enhanced by her bubbly personality and enthusiasm for science.

Prof. Musselman is the best writing professor I've had (I am a biochemistry major).  She is very straightforward with what she looks for when grading, provides direct answers and helpful feedback when inquiries are made, well informed, and very approachable.  I highly recommend taking her middler year writing class if you are a science major.

Very opinionated and if you argue with her she'll drill you until you give up. She really gets on my nerves. Other than that be prepared to write a lot of drafts. If you follow her suggestions you'll do pretty good.
No Comments
Is very opinionated like already said, although if you ask her how to improve your paper, she'll tell you what to do, and you'll do well.

Is all about the busy work.  Get on her good side by participating in class and asking her opinion about your papers.  Paper guidelines are very unclear,  I don't think she even understood them.  The worst english teacher I have ever had.

You have to spit back her information or you'll be marked down- easy class, just a lot of editting. Just hand in all your work, and you can't get below a B because we do SO many drafts. Harder than most writing classes.
Weirdo. Very opinionated. Share her opinion or get a bad grade. Has some weird views.

Professor Cetin is truly one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. He is super smart, relaxed and encourages participation that really helps us learn. I came into class liking Micro Economics, but three months in and I love that stuff. Definitely recommend!

He's so great and nice! His lecture is relaxing, and he explains everything clearly. He always asks us if we follow him and give a lot of actual examples to help us understand. One more thing here, people complain about his accent a lot. I don't think it 's a problem. English is not my first langue, and I can't understand what he says.
Tamer is the GOAT of Econ. I would like nothing more than to kick back and smoke with him. Chill guy, great flow, class isn't too hard.
You can't really understand him, but all in all not a horrible guy and pretty easy course.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Teaches from PowerPoints, hard to get much out of them. Tests are easy, based off the 1-2 hw assignments (MC and a few short answers) per unit, and the recitation class right before the test. Super chill, doesn't care if you come to class, very nice guy. Super accessible by email/office hours, v understanding. From Turkey, so his English is ehh.
this guy has no idea about anything in the subject. he copies the stuff he teaches from other books. he is sooo bad, if you want to understand try to avoid him.
The guy is sooooo bad. he has no idea about the subject and he doesn't know how to teach or anything. avoid him because you will not learn anything and you will spend money for nothing.
I don't know how northeastern university hired him as a teacher. The guy has know idea about the subject and has know idea about anything in IE.
Easily the worst teacher i've ever had to deal with. nice enough guy, means well, but NOT knowledgeable in area of study. always blames the TA, is very unprofessional, and CANNOT TEACH.
No Comments

Had him for Digital Simulation.  One of the useless professors I've ever had.  I'm still not sure what I even learned from that class.  Very unclear, and not an easy class.  Nice guy, pretty awful teacher for this subject.

Prof. Choffnes is an expert lecturer with deep knowledge of the material. However, the course workload is extremely high for an intro class. The syllabus is very ambitious, covering a vast amount of content that can be difficult to balance with other courses. It is a highly educational experience, but expect a very rigorous pace and grading.

Prof David is very passionate about Networking, the second half of his lectures are gold mines and will make you love networking, he gave some opportunity for extra credits and he is very accommodating, but project 3/4 needs infrastructure help from college, I really loved his classes, although i messed my finals still ended in decent grades
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: David is a nice guy! He knows a lot in his field and is always enthusiastic in class. As long as you fulfill the requirement (code run and get the result) you get whole grade. However the extra credit is challenging. Each assignment takes 1-2 days to finish(3-4 day if you do not familiar with tools) therefore the load is fair.
This is one of the hardest classes I've ever taken, but I did learned a lot about networks. Projects are well designed, exams are quite challenging. Prof. Choffnes is a great lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Class isn't too bad if you are willing to put in the work. Start the group projects early because they count for the majority of the grade. You get a notesheet for the exams which is very helpful. Don't skip lecture, he crams 2 lectures worth of info into each powerpoint. Textbook is not required but I found it very helpful (free online).

Professor Choffnes is a great guy, very knowledgable and passionate about the material. His classes are tough but he tries to help his students learn and is a fair grader. His lectures are entertaining and clear and he's really helpful in office hours if you are having trouble. 10/10 would recommend
Amazing Professor, completely understands the concepts and very willing to teach students. Not exam intensive and amazing projects.
good professor, very approachable but makes you read lot of research papers,

NUMBER ONE PROFESSOR AT NORTHEASTERN. His class is super easy BUT if you want to learn things you totally can because he is quite passionate. It is definitely what you get out of it, which I enjoyed a LOT. HIGHLY recommend!

I love professor Chichirau! Such a sweet and caring guy. His class is really simple, we have weekly quizzes that you take whenever you want, with unlimited time, and can use any resources you'd like. He records all his lectures on zoom as well.

VERY easy class. Neighborhood walk and reflection takes up one class a week. The lecture takes up the other class, but lectures are not needed at all. Discussion post and walk reflection are only weekly assignments other than the big final paper which is broken up into five smaller papers. But, he is a great guy and an interesting lecturer.
He's okay. Super easy, but honestly didn't learn much. The neighborhood walks were definitely the highlight of the class. Nice guy.

The class is fun, and he conducts weekly walks around Boston. You have to try to not get a good grade on the essays, which don't even have to have proper APA citations. Since everything is based on essays and discussion posts, he doesn't take attendance and his class was practically empty by the fourth week. This is a good elective for slackers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: George. What a great guy. Makes you want to come to class every day, even for 100min lectures, and the weekly neighborhood walks are a great experience too. Consider yourself lucky if you get a class taught by George.
This class is an experience. George is quite a guy. Wow. Take this class.
He is good

Great professor, perfect balance of learning and grading. I got lots of opportunities to practice what I learned with modern tech stacks, fair grading standards. I learned systematically about full stack web development with essential skills for nowadays SDE, I got interviews after took this course.

He just reads the PPT and shows no enthusiasm in classes. There is no difference if you just learn it yourself on Youtube. 
He used to give easy grades to students but NOW everything just changed. His Quizs and Exams become difficult and hard to achieve grades.

Course was a letdown. The midterm was packed with way too many MCQs, impossible to finish in time. The TA's grading is super harsh. Attendance is mandatory, so you have to show up even though lectures don't help much with the exams. If you care about your GPA, time, or tuition, I'd strongly recommend avoiding this class.

Everything changes in 2025, it is the most horrible and hard course I‘ve taken. You need 6-8hours for weekly assignment, midterm and quizes' mean are always lower than 70%. What makes it better? in final week, here is a project and final exam waiting for you. Class attending is required, but here is no credits for it.

His ux class is good!
CSYE 7280

I thoroughly enjoyed my time in the course as it provided ample opportunities for me to enhance my knowledge base. The class activities were instrumental in laying a strong foundation for me. The professor's provision of supplementary sources and articles served as invaluable resources for deepening my understanding of the subject matter.

I had a wonderful time during the course. There were a number of class activities which helped build my foundation. The professor would share additional sources and articles which helped me build a deeper understanding.

Classes are pretty straight forward. Its little hard to for beginners, but eventually one can built a career out of this course. Professor covers all the front end related topics that are currently used in the industry and keeps updating the course syllabus for every two semesters.
Very good

Easy grader. You will get an A without any effort. The TA's handle the class and the lab. The professor teaches word to word from tutorialspoint  (reads the slides). If you want to learn something, don't take this course. Or take the course and get an easy A :)

Insanely unorganized, took 2 quizzes in the span of one and a half months, now he realizes that we need to take 12 quizzes in total, now we have a quiz literally every class, 2 quizzes per class (2 quizzes per week).

His Chinese accent makes it impossible to understand anything he's saying, and he's a very tough grader, avoid at all costs!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is creative with projects, but understanding him is difficult since English isn't his first language (he mainly speaks Chinese). You'll need to study on your own because what's taught in class often differs from what appears on exams. Clearer communication would greatly help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: class was not very helpful and also difficult to understand but still had mandatory attendance. Also required participation which is a bummer. one group project which was pretty easy, and 2 midterms. Study the practice tests and you'll do just fine in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Super nice professor with a lot of help outside of the classroom. He is very dedicated to the success of the class. I recommend taking him if you plan to come and participate.
Loved him. Phenomenal professor and learned so much about principles of investing through him. Would totally recommend him!

I had Professor Chiou for Investments and he is a great professor that brings in real world events to teach and keep you informed. If you utilize office hours, ask meaningful questions, and show interest, he will go the extra mile to help you. Group projects are straightforward. I highly suggest taking him for any class he teaches!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Chiou is by far one of the most caring and supportive professors I have ever had. If you show up to class, show interest, and you are a dedicated person there is no reason you will not succeed. He continuously has acted as both a personal and professional mentor to me and I hope you have the opportunity to take his class.

Professor Chiou is extremely unprofessional. He does not grade fairly, does not explain his rationale for grades, and does not show any understanding of the course content or willingness to support students both in and outside the classroom. He's extremely rude & inconsiderate and overall the worst professor I've ever had - and I am graduating now.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most unorganized professor ever. The classes are randomly online without any notice. He's a very tough grader when it comes to group projects. Made us do a 45 min presentation and then it was never graded. Worst professor for this class.

Professor Chiou is great. He is very knowledgeable about finance. He cares about his students and wants everyone in the class to do well. The class is difficult, sure, but he makes the lectures engaging and fun. He does have an accent, but he is still understandable and clear.

Professor Chiou's investments class was a class I looked forward to attending. Before taking this class, I was hesitant because of the reviews on here. I was surprised to find out that Professor Chiou is extremely kind, funny, helpful, and knowledgeable. The course itself is hard, but he fosters a very positive learning environment.

Before taking Dr.Chiou I was nervous because of his score here, but, I came back to say he was a great professor. He may be a tough grader on group projects, but he gives you ample time to ask him for feedback before its due date. His tests can sometimes be random, but the prep you receive is enough to do well. He made class engaging and fun.
tough class, but really helpful!

Three exams and two group projects. Lectures are unorganized, disconnected from assigned reading, and often rambling. Even with perfect scores on all 3 exams, your grade can be lowered by 2 group projects which are assigned alongside vague grading criteria and obscure guidance. Forced to teach yourself or learn nothing at all.

Run! Tough grader! The worst professor in all my classes! I got an average of 95 in midterms and final but ending in a B? The grades for cases and group projects are so mean! You will learn nothing from the class, but learn all by yourself! If you truly want to learn something, take another professor! Please!!!

The teaching style relies on Connect. He also lectures on material that barely shows up on exam. Exams are "how well can you memorize the textbook?".  He makes you do a lot of group work and believes that you should spend 15+ hours OUTSIDE of class to work on the material. Ridiculous, don't take.
Run. Why would you take this professor? Bc you have to- there is literally no other reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor I have ever got in my life. Do not take any subject that he is teaching unless you wanna fail. He is very racist and is very partial to Chinese students and gives them better grade even if you are as good as them, even though you get A in all mid terms expect a lower grade as he wants to destroy students future. -R

Even with my full attention I cannot understand 1/2 of the words he says. VERY hard to understand which makes him a pretty bad teacher. I'm only one week into the class but I already know it will be challenging due to his accent and my lack of interest in finance. From what I can understand, for the tests I should just read the book. Don't take.

DON'T TAKE PAUL CHIOU!!! Even if you get all A's on midterms and finals you will end up getting a bad score due to this 1500 points. His class is full of cold-calling, and there is no learning in the class. In class, he cracks silly jokes to make it fun, but it will COST YOU SM.
An absolute incredible professor!

The content of his lectures had little to do with the content of his exams. He also creates non-anonymous question boxes for students to write about him, and then makes a slide show of the students' comments and spends an hour in class countering them. He liked to randomly call students' names, which made me feel embarrassed.

Avoid taking him for FINA6200. He acts like he's helpful but when you really ask for help, he judges, tells you to visit a stress center or reach out to his TA. Expects you to put in 10+ hours of studying each week as if no one has a full-time job or other classes. Be ready to be judged harshly on your group project too. Absolutely hated him...

He's a nice guy but you can barely understand him while he's lecturing. If you are not willing to read every chapter beforehand and teach yourself, you will have a hard time. He knows what he's talking about but just can't teach it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Avoid if possible. I learnt everything from the textbook, lectures were unclear and unhelpful. Professor made a lot of weird comments. Lectures never matched up with syllabus or the modules on canvas. Projects had no clear direction and when asked in OH would give minimal help. Take anyone else

This class was a trainwreck. Takes him 5-10 minutes to explain what another prof could easily explain with far more clarity in three sentences. Very unclear delivery (heavy accent if that matters to you). Constant noises over zoom made it hard to concentrate. I don't feel he respected students. Easy A, but if you actually want to learn, stay away.

Just great overall. He doesn't only teach from the TB and slides: he actively asks us questions from everyday news and opens up discussion on what effects each news has on the financial market and the economy. Not only that, he encourages students to do researches and provides detailed feedbacks in return. Life isn't complete if you don't take him.

At first I thought that this guy is a joke, but later on, it became clear that he really cares about students and is always available for help and explanations. We have done a vast number of questions in class so it was a lot of practice. Mid-terms are done as multiple choice questions on connect, so it's easy to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great professor!!! Highly recommend!!!
He doesn't teach at all, and you will leave the class having acquired no new knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Does not teach Investments. He teaches Corporate Finance in a Investments Class. He gives out 4 projects which are weighed heavily but teaches nothing about the concepts which are supposed to be used in those projects. He does not give enough feedback and cuts points if there are no page number on the projects submitted. DO NOT TAKE HIM. WORST PROF

This professor shouldn't be teaching! He has no real life experience and is simply the worst at teaching. Nobody can learn in this class despite the will to learn. Give less than poor feedback despite students asking him again and again. Very vague in grading and to be honest teaches Corporate finance in an Investments class.

I got all A's for homework and exams, but he decided to give me a 0% for participation and lowered my final grade to a C and later when I've tried contacting him, he refused to give specific details on what he discredited me for. I've been to all the classes and did not speak much, but it was surely not an F.

Very disappointed with this professor towards the end of the semester. How can one get an A- for the course after getting As for all of the exams? Obviously something is not right with the grading system. Seems like a nice person at first but it this will haunt you back at the end of the semester. Definitely avoid if possible.

This professor is easily the worst I've had at Northeastern. Here's the deal: the guy can barely speak English so in his lectures you can't understand any of what he's saying. My grade was an A until the end of the semester. In the final he added way more questions than the practice so I ran out of time.

Attendance is part of grade. Being in class doesn't help you complete the numerous cases or papers you could just look at the slides and learn it faster. Assigns multiple group papers and projects all due around the same time (like two days apart) and doesn't grade them and give them back in a timely manner. Trying to learn? take someone else.
The exam is not hard if you are prepared, while it is not easy to get an A for the group paper.

This prof does not lecture very clearly. The material is scattered and so is he. If you want to get an A you should see him during office hours to clear up his expectations for exams, participate as much as you can in class, and read the textbook. Make sure you have a good group for the project because that is a big part of your grade too.

Avoid at all cost. His grading is outrageous. Feebacks are worthless. You will learn nothing with this guy. You're better off taking Pichler or Muscolino. Near impossible to get an A in his class as the course is based on group projects only and two exams.

His assignments will scare you, but when you come out of this class with an A (its absolutely impossible to fail his class unless you're lazy) you will know it was all worthy. Now I fall in love with investments, a life-long useful subject. Just make sure you study. That's the key!
What a guy! Should be a stand up comedian!

Chiou the best professor I have had during my Northeastern! Once you get to know him, he's really down to earth and intelligent.  He will take the time to teach you as long as you don't slack off. Always willing to meet you  and available by e-mail. Use common sense and you'll be good to go.

Very hard to understand, I learnt almost nothing from the course, and passed only because I had some previous knowledge from FINA2201 and was taking Corporate Finance at the same time. I highly don't recommend him. The class is tough, and he makes it even more difficult, lacks clear explaining.

He is very very helpful and cares a lot about his students. At first I was horrified with his class because I couldn't understand him, but after two weeks everything got better. His exams are a joke, he puts the exact same exercises we do in class. It a very easy class.
Professor Chiou is a great teacher!  He assigned many useful projects and help us engage the real world. The portfolio projects allow us to manage money like fund managers.

I took two of Chiou's classes. Although they were VERY challenging, I learned a lot.  Chiou is very helpful, and provided class a lot of information beyond the scope of textbook.  I love the portfolio management project very much.   I believe it will help me in my future career in finance.

Chiou is an excellent professor and always is helpful to students.  He responses our questions very quick and help us to make sense cases.  Read your text and do your homework, the test is very reasonable.  He is a friendly nice guy.

Dr. Chiou is a difficult professor but he is very friendly and provides many opportunities for students to boost their grade. One of the only Finance professors that doesn't use Aplia. You need to put in time outside of class as his lectures are not very useful but overall he is a nice Professor that is always looking to improve his abilities

Do not, by any means, take class with him and encourage him in thinking he can relate to students. His English is abysmal, after class he would explain things in Mandarin to Chinese students, leaving the rest of us dumbfounded. He was rude, unhelpful, and unwilling to take steps to help in helping students learn. Don't fight this battle.

He's a nice person. But he shouldn't teach. His teaching style is confusing, unfocused and very very ineffective. The tests are a joke, as multiple choice questions do not have actual answers as the choices. Get ready to teach yourself everything, and avoid Prof. Chiou as much as possible.

He is literally the most ridiculous person I have ever met. His lectures and in class notes make no sense. It's hard to understand what he's saying half the time. He doesn't explain anything even when you ask for help and refuses to admit he may have made a mistake. I would not recommend him to anyone.

This guy is ridiculous. You cant understand a single thing he says, he is evasive and unhelpful every which way, and when you come to him for help he only tells you to either sleep less and study more. Every single moment around him was painful and I wont wish thin pain and misery on anyone. Wost teacher ever, avoid at all costs.
Hardest class in my life

Professor Miller is the best accounting professor I've had at NEU. I took Cost Accounting and Financial Statement Analysis with him, and he's been a great mentor ever since. He truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed academically and professionally. Highly recommend his classes if you want to really understand accounting.

Professor Miller is one of my favorite professors at Northeastern. He's really funny which helps make accounting less boring. The tests can be pretty hard but he gives tons of practice problems that help a lot. When starting a new unit, he has a "slides day" where he goes over the content, and then a "problem day" where we do practice problems.
Great person and instructor. Smartbooks and HW exercises aren't too challenging. Completing the handout questions will prepare you for the exams.

Excellent professor. Clearly cares about his students, lectures clearly, and aligns all of his course content with the textbook so you can review on your own. Very friendly and clearly knowledgeable on accounting from experience outside of an academic setting.

prof miller really cares about his students and is very personable and easy to reach. He is very funny which makes class more interesting. He also wants to make sure you do well, so he will give plenty of practice. make sure you do the practice and homework he gives you and you'll be fine. I switched my major because of this class.

Miller is a great professor, such a nice and down-to-earth guy. Exams are slightly difficult, so definitely a class you need to put a good amount of work in to. He's very helpful if you have any questions with HW, Excel Assignments, and the Case Study, and it's clear he wants his students to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: tests are very hard so study his practice problems really hard and you'll do just fine. excel assignments are soul draining so do them early. Overall really funny and great guy, offers really good life advice during class,  just don't fall behind !
10/10 guy. Super funny! Gave lots of life lessons and taught content effectively and efficiently. Would absolutely recommend taking this class, or any class with Professor Miller!!
Don't stress abt the class its Pass fail. if you are under a 75% he will give you a redemption online test. Wheather you get a straight A or bomb the final you will pass

Professor Miller is knowledgeable and supportive. He's willing to help students, but many of the concepts are taught in a way that emphasizes method over understanding. If you follow his approach and replicate the formulas, you can do well in the class.

Very nice professor, helpful, clear grading criteria. If you do the practice problems it is easy to do well in the class. I recommend taking him if you want clear path to get a good grade if you put in the effort.

Professor Miller is clearly shows an interest in the subject, and is great at taking the time to explain things and make sure students understand the content. He makes himself accessible to questions and provides helpful feedback. Do the smartbooks, homework, listen, and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A great professor with very easy exams and projects. Don't let that easy comment fool you though. It is still a course where you must work hard to get the grade the you want which he provides with. Gives you extra credit opportunity as well. Overall a great guy as well lots of experience in the field and great advice in terms of your career.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Professor Miller is amazing. You need to be prepared to do the Homeworks and SmartBooks for each chapter, which are interesting and quite easy if you have paid attention in class. 
In class exercises are very helpful for the tests. Even though attendance isn't graded, please go to his class. You will learn a lot and ace the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Miller is a legend and a great teacher. Teaches what will be on the exams and in a way that makes accounting easy to understand. Will be taking him for future courses if possible.

I took Professor Miller for graduate level accounting. I can CONFIDENTLY say that I learned nothing in this course. Class time was devoted to case studies that did not reflect the chapters and for which he did not have the correct answers to. I would recommend not to take this professor, but as an MBA student, you must so good luck!
He is hilarious, with great out-of-the-box context. and real-world examples. get ready to read textbooks and get prepared for sessions. will take classes with hi again if possible!
Awesome professor!

Professor Miller is one of the best accounting professors at Northeastern. He is very knowledgeable and passionate about the material he teaches. He is also extremely helpful and patient with his students, and he genuinely wants the best for all of his students. I highly recommend any class taught by Professor Miller!

This class was amazing, the professor gave amazing lectures and they were very interesting. By far the best professor I've had in my time at NU. The tests were 70% of the grade, including 2 midterms and a cumulative final. But, if you paid attention in class and practiced your exercises, the exams were not that scary. I learned A LOT in this class.

Very caring professor, Heavily accessible outside of class through text messages and emails. Do the readings and practice the practice problems so you understand the concepts and you will be absolutely fine. Brought my grade from a 79 on the first exam to a 95 on both the second and final exams. A case study is relatively easy and lightly graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Miller is probably the best managerial accounting Professor I could ask for. He is pretty much a lenient grader, and as long as you complete the practice questions, you should be good to go for any of his exams. This class is low stress, and he is super kind! Relatively easy to get an A

Truly one of the worst classes I ever took. If you want to not do or learn anything, get an easy A, this is the class for you. If you want to actually learn and be challenged intellectually in the slightest this was terrible. Learned nothing, only definitions of business words. He even said that you should not like your job and live for the weekend

Prof. Miller is a new professor so I was a bit skeptical but he went above and beyond my expectations! He teaches in such a way that if you attend the lectures and do the practice problems in class you won't have to study out of class. His case studies are also really fun and he gives great real world tips. One of the best professors I've ever had

I mean Miller is definitely a great professor, he provides lots of assistance for his students. The information he provides in his PowerPoint is clear and easy for students to understand the different key concepts in the course.  Easy A in the exam if you finish all or most of the exercises he provided in the canvas.

Best business professor I've had. His tests are pretty much identical to the review material. Extremely friendly and outgoing. Case Studies are pretty much just graded on completion. The only problem is that the HWs can get a bit long and tedious. But other than that it is a low-stress class.

Professor Miller was an all-around great professor. His lectures were well structured, he provided in-class time to go over study guides and challenging concepts which would be covered on the exam, and works hard to give his students a fundamental understanding of the course material. He's also just a personable guy!

She was a great professor, her accent is a little bit hard to understand at first but she will do whatever she can do to help you out. Also for her music elective class as long as you show up and pay attention you are almost assured at least a B. I suggest taking her class for sure

Prof. Ciucci is honestly a great professor. She can seem very intimidating at first, but once you get to know her and she gets to know the class, she's hilarious. Yes, her tests can be challenging, especially if you don't pay attention, but she really wants her students to succeed. She offers a lot of help and looks favorably on those who as for it

interesting course, she's little tough on grading the quizzes. Everybody in the class has to do a 5min presentation about an article she assigned to you. She remembers everybody's names, which quite fascinating. very helpful and lovely.

I loved having her as a teacher, she does assign a lot of material however she goes over it in class and explains everything as many times as you need.  She's very charismatic and makes her classes fun.  She's also very flexible with class rules and understanding.  I highly recommend her for anyone looking to have an interesting chill class.

I found her to be very confusing and difficult to follow. I feel as though she assigned a great deal of busy work. She gives a lot of reading, however the material you are tested on is what she goes over in class. Attendance is mandatory and she will deduct points if you do not participate.

She is not helpful and always seems angry. She uses big words that don't really make sense and picks out tiny flaws in everything you do. Her tests are always too long and she does not give you enough time to finish them. I would never take another class with her.

Dr. Cipriano is more than qualified to teach this class. Her lecture style evokes the momentum for students to keep going. While lecturing she strikes a balance between preparing us for the exams and fostering real learning. It is apparent that she is a very righteous person with a big heart. Overall, Dr. Cipriano is amazing to say the least.

She is amazing! Developmental Psych with her was a great experience, she really knows what she's talking about and clearly loves the subject.  She gives many opportunities for grades, including exams, a paper, and online assignments. HIGHLY recommend!

Developmental Psych: she's very nice, reads from lecture slides, makes everything available online, tells a lot of stories, brings her adorable baby to class to help us learn development. many different ways to score points (online video quizzes, in class tests, essay, virtual child simulation). Also helps that she's pretty attractive haha.

One of my favorite profs at NEU. She is incredibly knowledgable- her experience awes me. The powerpoints are great for taking good notes, and her stories are entertaining and useful. But most importantly she is very funny and nice and knows how to keep the class interested. Go to class, read the textbook, and you will get an A and have a good time.

I was not happy about taking this class but it's my favorite I've ever had at NU.  She organizes her thoughts well and really knows what she's talking about.  It was a little heavy on the lecture side of things, but really interesting nonetheless.

I took Stats and Developmental with Dr.C and she's great. She speaks in a way that's easy to understand, her powerpoints are very helpful and all online (so I skipped class a few times). All of our stats tests were open notes but a little difficult, developmental tests were very easy. Pretty much all multiple choice. She's a great professor.
Clear. Take home final. Made class interesting even though I didn't care about the material.

One of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. She's very dedicated to the class and genuinely wants you to do well (a lot of extra credit and very straight-forward tests). She also really knows what she's teaching and is able to clearly teach it. Easy A in a class where you still learn a lot
She's an excellent professor; highly recommended. Cute too ahah :)

She is a very kind person and is pretty young. However, her tests are hard and her grading is harder. Plenty of EC opportunities though. Her class was held in an auditorium which significantly made the learning environment suck; heavy use of power points.

i absolutely love this woman. her lectures are straight forward and filled with relevant examples. she's easy to get in touch with and brings in young kids for the class to observe which is really fun. tests are straightforward and don't have any tricks. take notes, use the study guides, and you'll get an A :)
Awesome class. A lot of class discussion but very fun. I learned a lot. What you get out of it is what you actually put in. Really like this class.

Nicest and most helpful teacher I have had at NEU. It is clear she taught young children prior, but it doesn't matter. She is easy to listen to and she actually helps you to learn the material, not trick you on the tests. Easy grader, I would absolutely recommend this class.  Really interesting in-class observations of children as well.
She is a great professor.  Very nice and always willing to help.  Pretty easy paper grader.  Tests are all multiple choice and she gives you a review sheet.  Lots of extra credit too.
She reads directly from the slides which gets extremely boring. She treats you like children, but the class is pretty easy. She grades papers very easy and overall the class is easy

A very frustrating class. Only read off the power point and I feel like class time was wasted in other students' personal stories.  New teacher, and is used to working with young children, therefore treats her students that way. I would recommend not taking one of her classes.

She previously taught young children, and it shows when she's teaching in a college classroom. . While she encourages class discussion, it usually went off into endless personal stories, which generally were irrelevant. All of the slides in class are taken directly from the book, which makes it easy to follow, but incredibly dull in class. I'd pass

Great Teacher! She is so enthusiastic and helpful. She wants you to do well and it shows. It is not mandatory to go to class, and she usually just reads through the slides with some discussion. Going to class definitely is helpful though when it comes to the tests (which are multiple choice). I would strongly recommend this class.

New, great teacher.  I wasn't interested in Developmental Psych, but all of the information taught in class is relative to anyone's interests. Fair grader, curves, easy in class assignments for points. Tests are all straight off of the slides that she posts on Blackboard. You do learn, and she makes sure her students are okay with the material

She literally accused half the class of using AI with zero evidence. She didn't know that OSCCR was punitive and just reported or threatened to report half the class. Ridiculous. Her classes are mandatory, but absolutely useless. I got 100s on every exam by reading the textbook, I had headphones on in every class, didn't listen ot a word she said.

Exams were unfairly difficult in comparison to the content we learned. She only gave the class 43 minutes to complete 55 questions for the final exam, which is much less than the time exams usually would be. She also yelled at a student for asking about their grade in front of the whole class.

Class is VERY easy, you can probably pass WITHOUT AI. Papers are graded leniently. The only thing that'll probably get you are the exams, so make sure to study for them. Idk why people hate her, she just doesn't want people using AI.
Not a fan of reversed classroom, weird attitude in emails, suspects students using ai and made a study out of it lol.

this class was very easy the whole semester, i didnt learn much from class but with the textbook my grade was good, 3 days before finals she accuses the whole class of using AI on a paper. she wouldnt look at someones version history because "she just knows" and "took classes on AI usage" she gave them all 0, i still have to get my grade back on it

Reported the entire class for AI usage with no evidence. Snapped at a student for even asking. Wouldn't let students explain, said "she doesn't want to hear it" and she "doesn't have time to debate with everyone." Regularly accuses students of cheating with 0 evidence.

I took her class over the summer and online, but really enjoyed her class. Professor Cisewski was very accessible online when I needed feedback on assignments or needed an answer to a question. There were about four papers for this class, but all of which straight forward and applied lessons from the book to real world problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took her PSYC4666 ClinicalPsySeminar. It's an amazing class that almost all classes were taught by students. If you are interested in clinical psychology, please take her class! She is a reasonable person and always caring students. Be prepared to read papers each week and write 2 pages reading reflection. No homework, just a paper needed.

She is a very caring individual and easy to access outside of class. The course has flipped model, meaning you watch lectures online and then discuss/apply knowledge during class sessions, however at the end of the semester I felt like this wasn't always the most productive. Exams can be pretty challenging as well, but it's an interesting course.

Dr. C is very caring, I took her class online but she was always very responsive to emails and enthusiastic about the material. There are papers and exams but they aren't too challenging if you stay on top of the textbook reading and her lectures. She explains things well and provides other resources for reinforcement.

The class is a flipped model, meaning you read the textbook and watch the lectures at home and mostly have discussions in class. Because of this reason, I felt like she didn't teach very much and I felt like some of the discussions weren't totally helpful. That being said, she is incredibly approachable and easy to access outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. C is a really great professor--if you have the chance to take a course from her you should certainly take advantage of it. She is textbook-heavy but also provides really insightful lectures and is extremely communicative and caring of each student.
love her

I didi find her course very interesting and she is very knowledgeable in what she teaches and I definitely learned a lot. This is not a terribly hard class but it does require constant effort with the 4 exams and 4 papers throughout the semester. My main issue is her communication issues, she usually takes 2 weeks to get back you if ever.
Class was super easy if you read the textbook you will be fine for exams. Professor is also extremely nice and topics were interesting.
She's actually the cutest human ever. I learned a lot. I'm not a psychology major but I would love to take another class with her. Lots of reading.

She is an easy A! She gave me full marks for all four essays in one semester! And her exams are not difficult, they don't require students to memorize a lot of concepts, but you do need to understand. She's a really good professor, and she's not strict. Make sure you take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Please just save yourself from trouble, don't take this class. I feel like I'm always bein notified of assignments toward the end of the semester... Even tho classes were recorded, i know instinctively that she is reading. Exams have nothing to do with lectures, but make sure you do the super long readings in case you unwisely choose this class...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took the course online and we read the entire psych book in 7 weeks. So yes, very heavy on the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: the worst teacher I have ever had at NU. Read straight from powerpoints huge waste of time and money!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: lectures were inconsistent, and class didn't go the whole time. Her exams were not based on our textbook and I feel like the class was a huge waste of my time because I learned nothing would not recommend her.
she was tough, gave lots of tests and lectures were too long. would not recommend

She was great. I took this class online but she was really engaging. She grades fairly and the tests were pretty direct from her slides, the textbook is helpful but has more info then she expects you to know. Overall great class

An absolute sweetheart. One of if not my favourite psych prof. This class may be different from her usual ones because it's an online one, but she was super flexible and made the curriculum easier because it was a stressful time. The exams and papers aren't hard but you do have to read the textbook and assigned materials. TAKE HER CLASS! love her<3

Prof. C is great, she is a lenient grader and gives extra credit opportunities. Her lectures are not mandatory, if you can make time to read the textbook and case studies on your own time you'll be fine for the exams.
She treats you like a person and makes class interesting and engaging.
love her!!!
LOVE HER!
Very nice professor and great at explaining any questions you may have
excellent teacher

She is a great teacher! Sometimes we spend too much time on one topic, but if we did, it was always beneficial. We would get into huge discussions which help you get lots of examples and the tests aren't too difficult. just make sure you follow the directions for papers and you should be fine :)

Great teacher!  Has a fun and engaging personality which helps the class go well.  Offers extra credit for those who attend class on days others do not.  Tests are fair but there are only four exams so each one is important.  Overall, a great teacher because she is passionate with the subject she teaches.

Took her for personality and she was amazing.  So sweet and knowledgeable and probably my favorite professor that I've ever had. Like the other person said, take the online quizzes for extra practice and you'll do awesome on the tests.

She's really nice and really helpful. I would definitely recommend taking her class. Make sure you read over the book and DEFINITELY do the quizzes from the book's website. But the tests mostly consist of her PowerPoints. She has a long paper on a celebrity - make sure it's long enough and that you include everything from the psychologist's theory.

She's very nice and is one of the few professors that actually knows what she's talking about. Loves what she does, and gives great examples on ALL the topics. Tests are pretty straight forward. Class is not mandatory, just go to the review session before the tests.  Gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit.

Made the content EXTREMELY easy to follow, classes were optional. If you don't feel like going to class, reading the book is fine. Class lectures were all that were necessary for the tests. So helpful and overall the nicest professor I've ever had.

Prof. Cisewski definitely knows psychology. The class is all thoroug powerpoint lectures but they are entertaining because she relates each concept with the real world. 3 exams and 1 final with extra credit opportunities. I tried not buying a textbook since quizzes are online. I got C's on my exams without reading. You actually learn in this class!

not the easiest course But this professor grades very fairly, gives partial credit& happily answers any questions(even stupid ones that some teachers are annoyed by)Overall, i think she is super helpful and surprisingly nice. the really tricky part is memorizing all the formulas but other than that just do the hw and go to class and you'll be fine

She's very clear in her lectures and notes, she tends to go a bit fast so its helpful to get the notes on blackboard before class. She's understanding and is willing to help with any problems.  Quizzes are not too hard as long as you study. Once you get used to the class its smooth sailing.

very interesting class. she explains things very well and knows exactly what she's talking about because she actually practices what she teaches outside of the classroom. oh yeah she's a total **** too, makes going to class that much better.

I took Foundations of Psych. my freshman year and got the worst grade I've gotten in all four years at NU. I studied hard and still bombed the tests. She's a Psych Professor...she wants to think she's smarter than you. The entire class is Power Point and BORING!!!! Psych can be interesting, too. I was disappointed!!!!

Fav professor this semester! She's extremely knowledgeable, always making helpful references to everyday & her work experience. Her speech is clear & easy to understand. All powerpoint lectures posted on blackboard. 5 MC tests. She makes it very clear what will be on exams. Doesn't take attendence but going to class & reading the book helps alot.
She seems annoyed when you ask a question!

This class was extremely easy. All the quizzes were based directly off of the powerpoint slides, which made it really easy. She only gave formulas for the final, but I'd say that this one a very easy class and she was a very good/interesting professor, even teaching statistics!

She provided a formula sheet for the final which was  extremely helpful. The rest of the quizes were straught from the powerpoint slides but she takes points off if your definitions aren't exactly in her words which is frustrating. She is willing to listen to student feedback and help when she can. Very understanding and nice even in Stats.

Her lectures will put you to sleep, when you raise your hand to ask a question she does see you most of the time and goes on teaching. She goes through material VERY fast and she grades your homework based on whether its correct rather than if you tried your best. Tought new info until the last day of classes, no review. Grades tests pretty tough.

A really nice lady. Flexible and understanding with her students. It was a little tough to take stats with her because unlike most profs she didn't let us use a formula sheet but I'd recommend her otherwise!  Her slides made things much easier.
No Comments

She is such a nice lady and you never have to take any notes b/c her slides sum everything up.  She can be a little repetative and boring but as long as you get the grade that you want, I dont care how boring it is.  Her tests are right from her notes. Not everyone even goes to class!!  Take her if u can!

She is a great teacher, really nice, posts lecture slides on blackboard as well as practice assignments. Offers extra credit before every exam. Answers questions, holds study sessions, very pretty woman, hardly went to class and still did really well, just read text and notes b4 exam. recommended.

Her class is wicked easy!  Most people don't show up for class but I found it helpful to go to class, however you deffinetly don't need to go to every class in order to pass.  She wants everyone in her class to pass so she does everything possible in order to help you out. Go to her study sessions!
real nice lady... notes provided for you which resemble tests.  not much work involved... attending class benefit of learning but not essential to pass. stick with her she's a fair grader!
Interesting class, and a really nice teacher. All of her lectures were online, so if you missed a class you could make it up.  Also, the tests were just like the lectures.
No Comments
I had to do a lot of self-learning for this course to complete the homework as well as the practicums; however, the professor gave a lot of extra credit opportunities.

Weekly assignments with extra credit for most to bump grades. Professor was ok, videos weren't great, the video recording discussions were worse. Group practicums were fine, if you have good teammates.

This class has a moderate assignment workload week to week but there are enough extra credit opportunities to bump your grade a whole letter if you take advantage of them. Didn't love the professor, didn't love having to record videos of me speaking for a coding class, and the 3 group practicums genuinely took years off my life.

This course had serious communication issues. Key requirements were never provided in writing, and relying on informal Teams posts caused many students to be unfairly penalized. Clarification attempts led to inconsistent TA answers, and the professor ignored emails and shifted blame. Even after escalation, no formal clarification was posted.

This professor assigned 3 projects with random groups. Expectedly, there were plenty issues collaborating, which the professor did not help handle despite my attempts to explain varying effort levels, resulting in a terrible grade for the first project. Does not contribute value outside of pre-recorded lectures - do not take her class.
heartless, cold, clearly does not care about her student's learning. Save your money

Honestly, a great and easy course. I do feel that because it was online, the instruction was very self-paced, and I didn't learn as much as I would have if I'd taken it in person. Assignments are due weekly (not hard and EC available on all hw and projects). Some stuff does seem repetitive, however, but if you do the work you'll have an A.

this online class has clearly not been updated in years, with many lecture code segments including outdated functions. grading is random, with TAs docking points for subjective reasons. assignments don't have clear instructions, and are "interpretative." i would still take this class bc its online which is nice but don't expect to learn a lot.
It was honestly pretty okay -- if you really wanted to go in depth on the DS topics you'd have to go out and do it yourself.

Her assignments are extremely unclear, and every time I try to get clarification from her or a TA, I get a convoluted answer that leads me to get the question wrong. The TAs are EXTREMELY harsh graders, and when I approached the professor about it, she did nothing. Other people and I have considered going to the dean because of her poor teaching.
So rude. Doesn't respond to questions and has extremely boring lectures. When you email her expect to wait more than a week for a response.

Asynchronous online course with two group projects. Easy if you have previous python experience. Office hours are hosted in teams and I had TAs fail to help on time multiple times, watch out for that.

This class was one of my favorite so far, people say her voice was boring but I thought it was calming lol. In all the hustle-bustle of CS, this was such a nice aside. Everything is super beginner friendly and overall it's just a good class. Dont love the pickiness of the TA grading though but otherwise they too are so helpful. overall 9.5/10

I took her class as asyn (online) and her teaching could not be worse. Her voice is so boring, literally zero excitements. Some of the contents in homework are not even covered in lecture. Please I recommend avoiding her if you are taking any of her classes.

A is 95, but she gives so much extra credit that it doesn't rly matter (my grade sat ~102% for basically the entire class). Stuff that appears on HW was gone over in lecture: keep on track w/ lectures and readings you'll be fine. Quizzes have 2 attempts and are open book so they're pretty free. She's got online DS3000 on lock, highly recommended.

Professor Clachar was excellent for Foundations of Data Science (CS 3000). Not too sure about her other classes, but I found her lectures, though sometimes boring, were super helpful as an introduction to Python and data science general. Would recommend taking this class with her if you get the chance.

She shows up to teach once a week for like 40 minutes. The class material itself isn't too bad, but she makes it hard by not teaching anything, and by threatening students to not "plagarize". Ma'am, this is a computer science course if the stackoverflow answer tells me to do xyz I am going to do xyz
The most boring course I have ever taken.

Worst instructor I have ever had. Unprepared, impatient, and unresponsive for questions. The online class structure was good enough, but it was built by other instructor in the prior semester. The fact NEU still keeps this instructor really made me think if I should have applied for other universities.

She is a part-time lecturer not a professor. When she is teaching this course, she even dont know what the codes on textbook and online videos are. She made many mistakes on her lecture and assignments. By the way, she is not friendly.
It's an okay class. I personally don't like lecture-heavy classes. Professor is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: so so boring but not too hard

Prof Santelices is amazing! She makes her lectures engaging and always ties them to personal stories and research. When she assigns papers, she lets you send drafts beforehand for feedback and is very accessible in and out of class. She is kind, accommodating, and overall incredible. She will change the due dates to what works better for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Claudia was an AMAZING professor. I took her biology class and had absolutely 0 complaints. If you pay attention in class, do the notes, and just put in effort, you will do just fine. The quizzes and tests always align with what she teaches in class, which is always appreciated as a student.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a great teacher! Clearly explains the material, with interesting personal stories. Workload is quite manageable and requires little work outside of class.

Claudia was very sweet! You could tell she cared about her students and wanted them to succeed. Her lectures were very interesting and her grading and tests were very forgiving. Her unique perspective as an anthropologist with interests in public health shaped the scope of the class in an interesting way too!

Claudia is the best! She's so easy going and wants all of her students to do very well in her class. She's always willing to work with students about anything, so don't be afraid to ask for assignment extensions or extra help with something. DON'T buy the book!! You don't need it, she'll assign readings but then she goes over everything in class.

Claudia is a fantastic professor. She is clearly passionate and experienced in her subject and her stories tie into her lectures well. FLEXIBLE: if whole class agrees will move due dates. BREAKDOWN: 4x 1 page reflections, 4x (usually take home) quizzes, midterm, final, one long paper. manageable workload/INTERESTING lectures. PAY ATTENTION IN CLASS

Amazing professor. She is caring, approachable, and gives inspiring lectures that are based on her own experiences. She wants her students to succeed in class and will help you achieve an A if you put in the work.

Professor Santelices is so kind and is willing to work with students who need quiz retakes, missed class, and allows the class to pick midterm and quiz dates.  She gives great feedback and uses her own research as examples so lectures are engaging. I loved her class and didn't need to spend much time outside to get a good grade.

Really liked the class and most quizzes and reflection papers were take home. As long as you try, she will give you a good grade. There were 4 quizzes (3 take home), 4 reflection papers (3 take home), a midterm and a final. She is very kind and sweet, she has come a long way from her previous reviews because the class and canvas were organized.

The class is super easy and she is a very easy grader.
