Everyone in the class got 100 for every reflection paper and take-home quizzes. the Lecture slides are boring and mostly common sense, so you do not need to study hard to get a 100 on her exams. Check canvas! She changes deadlines and posts assignments without mentioning them in class.

Class material is pretty dry but prof did pretty well making it engaging with her own stories/examples. Very kind person who wants you to succeed. Assignments are chill and based off the material on slides

Prof. Santelices was so understandable and very kind when it came to class! She is easy to talk to, and for me personally, finding a professor I can converse with in Spanish is nice. She has been one of the many public health class professors I really enjoyed having. Amazing person, but the lecture is boring. Quizzes and reflection paper are easy.

One of the best professors I've had. I took Anthropology of Latin America as a Spanish minor and totally changed my worldview. She shares her personal experiences in Chile as well as fieldwork, and shares profound, often unheard perspectives on the "third world" countries, capitalism, indigenous resistance, etc. I was captivated every lecture.

I found her lectures super interesting and she wasn't a super harsh grader. You need to study the material on the slides really well. The tests weren't hard but definitely harder than what we learned in class... She's not super great at communicating and will definitely forget your name even after meeting her multiple times; not very genuine.

Prof Santelices is a caring and enlightening professor. Amazing stories and experience in Anthropology. A bit iffy with technology and expect all assignments to be pushed back and delayed in grading. However, she really makes an effort to know everyones name and hear everyone out. IMO amazing professor, love coming to lecture. PARTICIPATE!

The class was an actual waste of money, as in the fact that many classes were cancelled and recorded for online. The most helpful part of the class is the slides, and I did actually come away from the class with helpful info. But was it worth the money spent on the class, no. Look for another class or even better, another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved her! She was one of the most caring professors at Northeastern! Through her personal stories, it is clear she is a professional and teaches for her love of learning. Her class was very lecture-heavy, but her material was always accessible, and students learned a lot. Grades depend mostly on exams, quizzes, and projects, not attendance.
Very kind, understanding woman. Barely knows how to use technology. I barely went to class and did well - if you stay on top of your coursework and STUDY THE CLASS SLIDES you'll do well.

Claudia is a really genuine, caring professor who has amazing life stories and lectures that brought me to tears on several occasions. It hurts to admit that she is all over the place with technology and deadlines, if she had a little more structure I'm sure she could be amazing.

Obviously cares a lot about the subject and has interesting stories, but lectures were hard to follow. Assigns way too much pointless reading. Assignments and exams were confusing, complicated, long, and frustrating. Not good with technology. Attendance was not taken but missing lectures does not help for later on. Class was all over the place.

Kind, passionate, good lectures. Everything else not so good. Horrible with technology. Extremely busy outside of class and didn't seem to have time to actually be a good professor. Her assignments can be confusing, especially the tests. Cancels class often, which is not a good thing. Could be good if she actually had time to focus on the class.

Dr. Santelices made lectures more interesting by adding her own experience of working in the field. You could really tell she was passionate about public health and how she has contributes and how we as students can further contribute. Assignments were based off of videos. As long as you pay attention to lectures and review, you'll pass. :)

Professor Clark is a tough grader, expects a lot, requires students to be prepared and participate in class. If you do the work and participate then you will be fine. If you don't then this is not the class for you. I learned so much from this man and his class and I can't be more thankful for Professor Clark.

Professor Clark was extremely bias toward the favorites, and his grading rubric was more on the subjective side of things. You really do struggle to realize what you learn throughout the semester, for he simply yaps about past case studies in discussions. The group project seemed straightforward, but his expectations for it are impossible.

This professor is knowledgeable about what he teaches. But besides that, he is someone I would avoid. He has favorites, and you will have a very tough time in his class if you aren't one. He gives vague instructions and no examples but expects almost perfection when turning in your work. He will take off many points for length, format, etc.

He is very knowledgable and aids discussions way beyond marketing. His rubrics and syllabus are very clear and organized. This class is lecture heavy and he is a bit of a harsh grader but he is great. I truly learned from him.

I was not fluent in English. He had a question sheet for every case. As long as the questions are prepared before class, I can read them out in class. Even though I didn't answer many questions, it helped me get out of my comfort zone. I feel that I have been effectively helped.

Very nice, very kind, very funny professor. But don't take his class if you don't like talking and answering questions in class, because class engagement accounts for 25% of your grade. The grades are a little bit strict, and if you want to get an A, you have to work very, very hard, both in terms of class participation and homework

Professor Clark is a fantastic man. His lectures are interesting, fun and engaging. He is extremely considerate of students. I wasn't able to contribute much at the beginning of the semester and he gave me many opportunities to catch up. Assignments are manageable and relevant. He's one of those professors that makes you glad you took the course!

Prof Clark is amazing. There's no textbook or exams. Every class is a case discussion, and the Prof encourages you to think critically about the situation at hand. I learned a ton about marketing. The group project requires you to make a new product for an existing company and create a marketing plan for it. Participation is 25% of the grade.

Clearly chooses favorites and sticks by them the whole semester. If he doesn't like you, there's no mending that (I tried). The most vague instructions but expects perfection. Will take off full points for tiny mistakes. He knows what he teaches but doesn't always like when you disagree - kinda invalidates your opinion. I'd avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting teacher. Very knowledgeable but often very petty and snarky. If he likes you you have an advantage over others. He's not good at providing feedback and he takes off full points for formatting errors (such as one too many decimals or incorrect use of spacing or word). Assignments graded out of 20 points even projects that are worth 40%.

Definitely a bit of a tough grader, he can tell if you haven't done all of the reading and are just spitting out a boilerplate nonsense answer. He gives plenty of examples and is always open to answering questions. He tries to bring in his own real world experience and asks for others' experiences as well. Really enthusiastic and engaging!

This is probably one of the worst professors I've had in Northeastern. Don't get me wrong, he knows how to teach and explain ideas, but he is so arrogant that the class is just horrible. It seems that he picks some favorites and there's nothing you can do after that. He also gives no rubrics at all for any of his assignments. heed my warning!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Toughest grader ever. Class is VERY participation heavy and that ends up being 25% of the final grade. No rubric for anything so its super hard to do well in papers. Math part he just assumed everyone knew so it was never really taught (10%). Very practical and focused on real life scenarios, but I would never take this class again.
Needs to take it down a notch.  Be ready to read and have an unhealthy amount of work.
Very strict tough grader and has preferred students

Professor Clark is a great professor- very enthusiastic and witty. He's clear on what he expects and how you should do it, and he'll keep class interesting. However, be forewarned: he gives a lot of work (papers, cases, and group project simulation due every class), and will always keep you until the very last minute of class time.

Prof Clark is one of the best profs at Northeastern. His teaching is straight forward and clear. He emphasizes practical examples and numerics in marketing. His experience shows in his style.TAKE THE COURSE. The cases are great however the text book wasn't as useful. I still kept it cos it was Kotler. Cant give that away!

Having graduated 8 years ago and now with the benefit of hindsight, Prof. Clark was hands down the best teacher I had at Northeastern. His undergrad strategy class was likely the most useful class I took, and he made the subject fun and the classes interactive. Excellence all around, I would encourage all UGs to take a course with Prof. Clark.
Excellent professor.  Well prepared.  Tough but goes into depth and makes you really think about each case study.  Smart, extremely nice, and professional.

Professor Clark is one of the best professors I had in the MBA program. His class lectures were interesting, his credentals outstanding, and his knowledge and experience in the field really show through his teachings.He treated everyone well and he seemed genuinly interested in everything all of us had to say.

I completely agree with the prior review. He has been the best prof. I have had so far at NU. His class is definitely challenging, but he helps you every step of the way. If all of the profs at NU were as good as him, it would be the best school in the US

One of the best professors i ve ever had. His expectations are clear, he values contribution, all marketing topics are approached through cases and this guy knows tons of Marketing.You ll learn a lot and you will appreciate his effective teaching.

She's very understanding and kind. I had a good experience with this class. As long as you stay on top of your work and make your deadlines it's easy. She gives great feedback on assignments, is always there to help and explain anything if you're confused, and makes class engaging. Highly recommended taking her class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Clark is very rude and her feedback may bring you to tears but it is helpful. The class is very easy. Attendance is mandatory and graded along with participation. She over explains everything, she probably talks for more than 75% of the class. If the class was just based off of work you do you'd be in and out in 20 minutes.
Very easy if you just do the HW and do the optional essay revisions before the final one is graded.

Horrible teacher. The class itself is quite easy, but she is incredibly rude and unhelpful in feedback. The organization of the course is also terrible, requiring several different Canvas pages open to understand what is required for a single assignment.

Dr. Clark, is a great teacher and the class is pretty straightforward. You have 4 major assignments and plenty of time to do them and get 2 day extension policy for all of them. Attendance is mandatory and part of your grade which is the only negative. If you do the work you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is super easy as long as you do your work.There are 10 journals, 4 big essays and peer reviews. I know it might seem like a lot but the way she divides everything is great and you have enough time for everything. You can ask for 48 hour extension on every single essay. The only thing is she is very big on attendance. But she is amazing.

She is very kind and provide all information about the big essay very clearly, if you follow her instruction, it will be easy to get a good grade. Many assignments are allow to do it again if you are not satisfy with the grade and she will provide comments for big essay for you to make some change and then give you the final grade, a easy class.

She is very passionate about her teaching. There is a lot of peer reviews and busy work. If you attend and complete all peer reviews, you are eligible for an extension for the major essays. Not a lot of reading. She is nice and helpful. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor seemed caring during COVID but reported me for unprofessionalism right behind my back. This has caused me SEVERE mental trauma/stress that still haunts me. I would NEVER trust this professor and this has also undermined my trust in ALL of the professors . They do not care about you, they are only here to get paid.

The class is extremely structured. The course is structured around a few papers which receive a lot of feedback allowing you to fix your work. My biggest advice is to complete your drafts fully to receive the most feedback possible. Complete your work according to the rubric and seek feedback through office hours to achieve an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really nice professor, and is always clear with feedback, rubrics, and instructions on how to do well in her class. The class does have a fair bit of busy work, but it's manageable as long as you stay on top of it. Can be a bit rough on your participation grade if you get sick or have an emergency of some kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: There is a fair amount of busywork and there is a homework assignment that requires writing a few hundred words usually after every class, but it is all quite manageable. Her grading criteria is clear and it is not particularly difficult to achieve an A if you simply put in the minimum effort required. Dr. Clark is very accessible as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Makes what should be a relaxed class an unreasonable amount of work, assignments are often confusing and require you to have 5 different tabs open to try and piece together what you're supposed to be doing.

Dr. Clark is super straightforward. Lenient deadlines, plenty of peer review, extremely minimal reading, responsive through email, abundantly clear rubrics, and very lenient grading. Ended up with an average very close to 100. There is more busy work than necessary but just showing a little effort generally gets you full credit.

Comments on essays are often short and give no personal feedback other than something along the lines of 'refer to original document.' Allows "freedom" of choice for essay topics but is actually really looking for something very specific and constantly shoots down ideas.

Her comments frequently are inapplicable or show that she did not closely read your work. In class, her "I am always right" mentality shows as she is consistently rude to students and disregards her own slip-ups. She makes an otherwise simple class an absolute pain in the neck. Avoid at all costs!
Overall the course is easy and should follow the syllabus. However, Dr. Clark tends to be rude to students through class or comments she leaves on your draft.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Shes very intelligent, gives great and detailed feedback, is always available outside of class and in office hours to help you through the essays. The process of writing essays is very helpful because you have three drafting opportunities: first draft for peer review (usually just an intro & outline), 2nd draft for instructor review & final draft
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She gives a minimal amount of reading, mostly toward the beginning of the semester. There is a ton of peer review for each paper (of which there are three, plus one final reflection paper). The class is pretty easy if you pay attention to the grading criteria she gives you for each essay, and she gives plenty of opportunities for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: i think a lot of Yall have skill issues in this course is she not super clear on what she wants in the group project: yes, But there is a TA for a reason so lock in. if you particpate and show up for class you wouldn't have. issues with the class. i like her and she is super nice.

Super nice lady- not the best teacher. Goes on really long, but interesting, rants, so doesn't cover a lot of necessary info in class. We legit didn't talk abt the final until 2 days before rough draft was due- good grader and just wants you to be engaged though

Professor Clough is incredibly intelligent and it shows through her lectures. The student gets out of this class what they put into it. Professor Clough is always willing to work with students when they reach out, so if you are struggling with the work or the class itself, reach out; you will find a lot of fulfillment this way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loves to brag and scare students that the world is coming to an end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Get ready to read!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lots and lots of reading. Easily 50-100 pages of reading for every class. The papers are tough, but the content is pretty enjoyable. She does explain concepts really well though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: I literally changed my major because of her.

Wowza, this class was genuinely challenging. Readings ranged from 30–175 dense pages. Lectures often repeated points from the readings and felt redundant. The environment could be intimidating, and participation was tough even though it matters. Professor Clough is EXTREMELY intelligent and has so much to share. Her office hours are truly the key.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Clough is a very smart individual. However, do not take her class. Her lectures are long and boring. Her instructions on major projects are very unclear, and she does not answer emails. She doesn't take attendance, but participation is a big amount of your grade. All grades come from outside of class, the lectures are useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She's very knowledgable but she doesnt have the best methods of teaching in an engaging manner. Her class is only graded by a few things (participation, 3 reading journals, group midterm and group final paper) and participation will make your grade drop so lock in for that but it is true that she will scare you that the government is falling apart

This entire class was basically current events. Along with that it was mostly conspiracy theories. She talks to you like children. She'll scare you with talk about the government falling apart then tell you there's nothing you can do. She went as far as to say we could be spies for Homeland Security. She was a sweet woman!

She didn't grade ANYTHING until the last week of classes. We had no feedback on any assignments, and on top of that, she treated us all like children. The syllabus was wildly unhelpful, and I was surprised by how many good reviews she got before this semester. I don't know what happened, but she was the worst professor ever.
Worst professor I've ever had at Northeastern. Never came to class, boring lectures, and holier than thou attitude. Take this course with literally anyone else

She does seem like a good professor but has a lot of stuff outside of teaching that occupy her. We had class canceled more times than not. Most of the grade was a group project and it was a good idea but she took a while to give feedback in order to submit for final. Overall I would not personally take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I ended with a good grade but it was still a bad experience. Her ratings were decent til this semester, not sure what happened but she is clearly struggling. You will do fine in the class except for participation, your grade might drop significantly bc of that. I wouldn't risk taking another class with her, you can def get an A with better prof
Don't do it. Waste of time and beyond frustrating.
the semester ends in a day and I still dont know what ill have in the class at all somehow.
Absolutely horrible experience.
Horrible. Will not grade assignments. worst professor I have ever had. Do not waste your money because she is fine wasting yours by not coming to class or helping you at all.
POLS1155: dont take. bad. super bad.
Absolutely horrible
Horrible class. Do not take it. Does not grade work and does not mind wasting your time.

This class was a waste of time and money. Little to no instruction on assignments. She will not show up to class or respond to emails. The class was focused on her political opinions when she did come to class which was rare. Uncomfortable and frustrating class environment. No grades uploaded until 2 weeks before the end of the semester.

POLS1155: Professor Clough is awful. It is April 6th, and we do not have a single grade in the book. If you want a professor to rant and spread conspiracy theories and always show up late without notice, then take her class. We almost never talk about class material. She has never responded to an email. Save your tuition, take another prof.

The first class she gave a lecture about how one class period comes out to $300 so don't waste time or skip, and then she missed 5 classes ($1500) with no backup plan or substitute material. She also didn't grade anything until the last month, so hopefully you did well on the few assignments you get because you'll be out of luck if you didn't
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof C is incredibly smart, she has super interesting work outside of the classroom- I deliberately took another class with her this semester. There is reading, but if you miss a day nothing happens. Following the guidelines is key + talk once a class for a 93+ in participation. She cares about her students and is easy to access outside of class.

She's obviously a very smart woman but does a lot of talking and not so much teaching. Gave students at least 50 pages of reading before each class and just reviewed what was talked about. Says participation matters but seems to like to hear herself talk more then asking students.

Professor Clough has high expectations and a strict classroom setting, but she is INCREDIBLE. Despite the assignments' difficulty, if you pay attention and follow the guidelines, she grades incredibly well. She is happy to help outside the classroom and has double the office hours of my other profs. Talk once a class for an A in participation!

Professor Clough was incredible. She was very passionate about every lecture, and class discussions during lectures were always very engaging and informative. I would definitely recommend taking her classes.

If you do the reading and pay attention, you will get a lot from this class. However, that can be hard because Prof. C's lectures are not very engaging. However, she cares a lot about the wellbeing of her students and is very open to feedback through an anonymous form.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Democratic Erosion with her. She's pretty passionate about what she teaches. If you don't care about Democratic Erosion you're gonna have an awful time. There are no tests but there are a good amount of papers.  Participation also happens to be like 30% of your grade. Take her if you like this stuff, avoid her if you don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: i think Prof. C is an awesome person but not a great teacher/lecturer. unless you're interested in political theory the lectures can be somewhat boring. there's a lot of reading (duh it's a humanities class) but most of the readings are explained in class and there's relatively little classwork/homework.

Professor C genuinely cares about her students and works hard to make sure the in class discussions are engaging and interesting. The class will be much more interesting and enjoyable if you participate and do the course readings. No real consequences to not reading them except you will have to go back to them when you want to do the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very theory-based. Only take it if you enjoy political theory and are good at it. Very lecture heavy and the lectures are boring. She's a nice person but I wouldn't take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class had lots of readings as well as having to write a ~150 word summary after each reading. However I definitely feel like I know the content. Graded on midterm, final, participation and an essay, each worth 25%. The tests are hard because you must know the authors you read by name. Only take this class if you like poli sci.

Professor Clough is a very nice person, but I did not enjoy this class. She makes students summarize every assigned reading (usually 2-3 per class, 100+ pages per week). This takes a really long time, and then in class all she would do is go over the reading. The lectures dragged on and weren't useful, but attendance is still mandatory.

Students do hundreds of pages of reading a week. Her chalkboard lectures simply go over the reading and drag on. The midterm was hard but graded liberally yet the majority still find it important to put in hours of studying. There are way easier Comp Pols teachers at Northeastern and though she is a nice human and responsive I wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy my time in Professor Clough's class. She took forever to grade and her lectures were not engaging whatsoever. She is a classic example of someone who is obviously booksmart but not meant to be a teacher. I did not get much out of the assigned readings and found myself less interested in polisci after taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Emily Clough is one of my favorite professors I've ever had- she is super available, she wants you to succeed, and she takes a unique way of addressing topics so things never get boring. You won't die if you don't do the readings, but they make the class more interesting, though they can be a little long. I took her twice and I'd take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved this class and this Professor. She is very passionate about the class and gives create lectures. She gives a lot of reading for hw so be ready. Sometimes 100+ pages to read per hw. She goes over the readings the next day. Very sweet. Go to office hours!! As long as you put in the effort, you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor C is not a good teacher. You'd be better off just getting the reading list from some previous student and do your own study. Her lectures are dull and uninformative, students said they just watch netflix in class which is a better use of time anyway. She is super uppity too which makes her unpleasant to speak too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Clough assigns a lot of work but there are no repercussions for not actually reading it. She doesnt give any feedback for assignments and just likes to hear herself talk. Smart lady, terrible teacher and will waste class time to talk about her baby and personal life . Waste of time and energy. Avoid her classes whenever possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Emily Clough is one of the best professor I have ever had to the blessing of having. She is super kind, always available, and committed to making me a better writer. Her class discussions really facilitated good discourse, though sometimes I skipped the readings bc they were a little long. And graded kinda easy, and no tests, just 2 medium papers!

LOVED professor Sokol. She genuinely cares about all her students and wants you to do well in class. You NEED to attend class to receive a good grade, and she is also very lenient with grading. There are 4 exams on lockdown and 2 projects in this class, but if you put in a few hours a week to this class, you're sure to get an A. Highly recommend.

While assignments and concepts can be challenging, getting a good grade in this class is not very difficult. You will need to study for quizzes. Sokol is super nice, even brought cookies for us one class. As long as you self-advocate if something needs to be changed, she will change it. She sometimes struggles with technology, but nothing serious.

I liked profesor sokol but she is not the best teacher. she struggles using technology and isn't clear in her grading. a lot of the class is self taught. Would not recommend if you are looking for a very hands on teacher.

Professor Sokol was a great teacher for elem spanish 1. we used the textbook and its homework assignments which were very user friendly. she would also go over the material in class and answer any questions we had via email or in the class. she is caring, but may sometimes come off as rude, which she does not mean to come off that way.

Don't listen to the negative ones! She's been a WONDERFUL teacher, very easy and fun class; brought chocolate on Valentine's day; extra credit for just going to a free spanish concert; very conversational. Only hard assignments were quizzes, accepted weeks late work for 100%. If there's a zero (she's not tech savvy), talk to her and she'll fix it.

I am going to save you do not take her. I read all the bad reviews on here and thought how bad can it be? BAD. I should have ended up with at least an A- she cannot work canvas, is so unorganized I would receive 0's on assignments because it would be a year late because she didn't change the dates from last year and couldn't fix it.

Professor Sokol was hilarious, and it was so clear she enjoyed the subjects she was teaching. Sometimes she forgets that we can't read her mind, and we end up scrambling to complete assignments she never even gave us, but she's so nice it doesn't even matter. Very entertaining class. Super light on the homework (never did anything outside of class)

Sokol is very nice and so funny. However, her class is extremely unorganized and lacks structure that makes it hard to actually learn course material. Be prepared to teach yourself grammar and vocabulary outside of class. Spent a decent amount of time on homework that I didn't feel like I retained. Had to study A LOT to get a high B+.

She is definitely caring about her students as she indeed checks in with students especially with students like me, who really struggle and need help! But she could definitely try to improve her teaching style because I basically learned everything from the class by myself. Handwriting hard to understand:( need to study hard to get B on her quizzes

She's one of the most disrespectful instructors I've ever had. She should NOT be allowed to teach. She's not a very intelligent teacher either. Take anyone else. I transferred out of Northeastern last semester and profs like her were one of the reasons why. Can't believe she gets paid.

You have to teach yourself and she can get in weird moods. Really wouldn't take again, but got an A. Just study the book the night before and you should be fine. Warning: the tests consist of these really hard listening sections that everyone screws up because it's not something you can teach yourself.

Claudia is so amazing. She really cares about her students, and she's really friendly; I had done really bad on the first quiz, and she spoke to me after class, and encouraged me to not give up. From then on, she always made sure to check-in with me. She also offers a bunch of extra credit opportunities like attending a Salsa Dancing Night.

I took Sokol for a dialogue to Argentina where she was the professor of record for the culture class. While the situation is fun and the Spanish language school is satisfactory, she did VERY little (delegated to unprepared TAs) and was unclear on grading of the few things we were required to do. Not very respectful, although she tries. DO NOT TAKE.

Claudia was a very easy-going professor, and really did care about her students. I think she cared more about your efforts to try and learn Spanish than your actual ability to speak it. Classes could be boring but it was an easy A  (as long as you show up).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: You'll get an A if she likes you and you participate. She doesn't teach anything. Be ready to teach yourself all the information she asks you to know for quizzes and tests. Class time is waisted doing group work and half of the class doesn't even do the questions. She won't even know if you are in class or not in class.

She's very LOUD, so at 8am it can be a little much. She'll also change your name to sound more "Spanish" (e.x. a girl name Jennifer became Josefina) so if that bothers you/offends you, don't take a class with her.

Claudia genuinely cares about her students. She will go over quizzes with you individually, give you a chance to make up points on quizzes, be available outside the classroom for extra help, and constantly ask for your feedback on the effectiveness of her lectures and activities. Go to class, you'll get an A.

Attendance is mandatory, she will be helpful if she likes you and if you participate in class. Accent is a little hard to understand, has a small sense of humor, but if she doesn't like you it will show in your grade. HW assigned each class that she goes over.  Quizzes are tough. If youre new to spanish, i would not recommend.

Profesora Sokol came into teach after my original instuctor cancelled class all the time. I went from knowing nothing for the first month of class, to being able to have an entire conversation (limited on topics) with a classmate. Loves participation, but since its a language class, thats pretty much a requirement. I highly reccommend!
doesnt actually teach, doesnt tell you whats on tests, takes tests away from you to check progress in the middle of the test. she has a good personality but she sucks at teaching

Loved her! She's hilarious and really made it easier to have the class at 8 AM. Really easy to get an A, make sure to go to the class because she'll take points off of your grade if you have too many absences. And she'll loved you if you're always in class. Love love love Profesora Sokol!

profesora Sokol is awesome! nice and funny lady, very very understanding. definitely go to class (she'll take off points) and do what is assigned, it's not even that much. class is pretty much always laid back.

she is amazing. she really just wants everyone to do well and enjoy the class. she tells you everything that will be on tests and although i said attendence was not mandatory she does keep track, but if u go over 3 absences she starting dropping your grade. but just explain things to her, she is very understanding and fun.
She knows the language very vell and teaches equally well
So funny. I loved Professor Sokol. She is a very easy teacher and is so funny and she doesn't even realize it. Great teacher. Take spanish with her.

Sokol by far is one of the best professors Nu has. She alsways has stressed that learning is there for you to take. Her classes are based around discussion and less on formal teaching. she is caring andkind to all her students. If your BSIB she is a must!
You're gonna have to put in some effort if you wish to learn spanish for the long-term.  However, she is an extremly nice professor who knows her spanish.
easy, but very unorganized/forgetful
very nice and easygoing professor. she made the 8AM class bareable.
No Comments
Great professor and easy content

I personally struggled with my grade in this class just because I am a bad test taker (every test/quiz is multiple choice) but I love our professor and the content in this class, would take again if I could

He's probably one of the best teachers I've ever had in my four years at Northeastern. His lectures are extremely engaging, informative, and a lot of the things you learn in class are applicable to your own life! He really cares about his students succeeding, and gives hints every class as to what things are likely to appear on a quiz or an exam.

Professor Cloutier is very dedicated to his work and that really reflects in his lectures. His lectures are informative and the tests and quizzes relate almost identically. He is so passionate in teaching the Intro to Exercise, Fitness, and Health and he is very personable.
Nice straightforward guy with a lot of knowledge in the field, easy class

I had Clark for INNO2301. I thought the course was pretty redundant, prof would often reuse the same slides. We had to buy a HBS packet with readings, but only actually read one for class (but later had to catch up to read others for the final). One big group project, pretty easy.
Nice guy and wonderful professor. Gives you everything you need to do well, has a sense of humour, and is always willing to talk after class. He also is not a strict grader.

Nice guy, not so great professor. Unclear grading structure, repetitive lectures going over the same frameworks, confusing Canvas, irrelevant syllabus. To do well, participate alot and specifically ask the professor what he wants out of the paper/presentation.
Great guy, super knowledgable and sweet. Class topics are bit repetitive but that's not on him. Always willing to talk after class. 10/10 Guy, 10/10 class

I though prof. clark was great. He gives you all the info you need in his slides, and his quizzes are very straight forward. He is also a lenient grader. Gave us candy on halloween, cracks jokes all the time, super sweet. Very respected guy. 10/10

I love this man. He cracks jokes in class, is down to earth, cares about his students, grades leniently. He wants you to do well, he curved our quiz, he is the best. I love this man. You also learn alot about family business. This was the only class I did not dread attending.
good professor, His slides are somewhat organized, but he makes up for it by being very supportive and approachable. Quite good at clarifying complex topics, making the material easier to understand.

No substance in the class, repeats the same things over and over and tells the same stories again and again. He sounds like a broken record, and never has evidence to back up any of his claims. Class is just his opinion, and he sells his own book as the textbook.

Professor Clark was one of the best teachers I have had. He made lectures interactive and made content focused on real-world material. There were reading assignments but he selected articles or cases that pertained to current events. I would highly recommend you take one of his classes before you graduate!

Great professor who teaches a lot of real-world knowledge. The class heavily focuses on a business plan that you write piece by piece and present EOY. If you come to class and participate you will do well. If you don't show up, don't expect to get a good grade. Not many HW assignments. Funny guy with a good sense of humor.

The class overall is pretty easy, but is pretty uninformative. You spend the whole thing writing a plan to get a loan from a bank. Most lectures ramble and its hard to keep track of whats important. Most of the instructions are really unclear for the assignment, and he provides no examples. That said, he is a kind grader.

An excellent professor that brings a great deal of real world experience and examples to the class. Lectures are informative and interesting. He isn't great about getting grades back in a timely manner, but is not a very hard grader. A solid choice if you want a professor that actually makes you enjoy going to class.

Nice guy, boring lectures. Doesn't respond to emails or give back grades. The only kind of challenging part of this class was the group project, so be aware of your team. Sometimes things not so clear. Except above a B+ with average effort.

The class was very enjoyable and fun! The class was really easy, pretty much no HW and easy projects. He is also an easy grader too. However, I felt like I did not learn that much about entrepreneurship.
No Comments

Ted is the best friggin prof at NU...Have taken every Entrepreneurship class with him..I will be graduating in the Spring of 07 and am pissed I cant take like a Bird Watching elective with him..thats how awesome he is...well you get it..take his classes if you can
great teacher, easy class...
Very enthusiastic and easy as can be! Be sure to get him for all your ENT courses.
Lectures and statements are sometimes unclear.

I would love to know what he has accomplished... seems like nothing... gives everything you need to pass tests... along with all the Ent professors... if you want an elective with an easy 'A' then take him or Eddelston...
Professor Clark is one of the best teachers I've had.  He is very helpful and has some great ideas.
For an asynch class, this really isn't bad, the work is easy, but just make sure you do it in time

This is an online course where you have short quizzes, and work to submit. You have about a week or so to complete every assignment, and they should not take any more than 30 minutes. For a 1 credit class, it's a lot more work than expected, but easy.

Pass/fail course, and everyone should be able to have an easy pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: never met this professor since CS1200 is online. this class just gives you a lot of work to do but it is manageable. I usually completed it in 30 minutes to an hour and im set for the next week. this class is pass or fail, super easy, no stress if you manage your time well!
lots of homework for a one credit class, and it's all group work. but that speaks to cs 1200 in general, not just claire. she was really sweet and gave good feedback, but was a bit of a dry teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: CS1200 has lots of homework for a one credit class, but it offers guidance for dealing with college problems in general. Easy A if you complete most assignments. Attendance is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Had him for a analytics capstone course. His teaching style was very hands-off. He prefers a self-managed approach to the capstone.

I had this class with both him and Glenn Pierce and honestly it was a little boring at times, but they both made it interesting. Glenn and Paul were definitely great professors and really took the time to help us out if needed. The could be disorganized at times but it wasn't too much of an issue. I would recommend him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: My favorite teacher at Northeastern so far. If you have to take business stats, definitely take Cleary. Often gets off topic during lectures, but no homework and lets you make a cheat sheet for tests. Very caring teacher who wants to make sure you understand everything (don't be afraid to ask questions, he loves it).
I had to read a lot outside the classroom since the lectures were sometimes a little unclear. Other than that the Professor is very understanding, and he is very clear on what you'll get tested on.
Tests are super tough and NOT open book. Doesn't communicate through emails or blackboard. The class average was about a C-.
Willing to help if you participate and ask. Long and boring lectures. Doesn't use blackboard or a syllabus really. Barely any homework and no project. Tests are harder than the problems he gives.

100% there for you. Students didn't get some material so he pushed back the schedule a lot. And he curves. The final ended up being our exam #3. He is willing to sacrifice time to make sure you understand. No stats project, barely any homework, always ends class early. Doesn't use Blackboard or have a detailed syllabus. Nice guy, sometimes boring.

As a person Paul Cleary is a very nice old man and cares about his students. His class is very boring and the lectures are confusing. The class has no set curriculum and he really covers only what he wants to. Barely any homework and you do not really have to study to do well on his tests.

Professor Cleary is the best, honestly my favorite teacher. He always pauses to make sure everyone understands what he is talking about, and does a lot of examples that he ends up putting on the quizzes. The quizzes are also open note, and he will give you points back if you argue your case. He makes himself available and will chat with you.
Insanely easy. Open notebook tests. Heaven for A's. (don't listen to the guy below me)
Doesn't care about the class, says he is gonna teach stuff and he doesn't. Avoid. Veryy boring
Really nice teacher, the quiz are easy.
extremely boring. Not clear. DO NOT recommend

People did generally well in this class. He doesn't really follow the syllabus but he is very clear what are on tests. Also, there weren't many chapters that we went over throughout the semester unlike other stats prof so studying the final exam wasnt that bad. Also, if you miss a few classes, its not a big deal. Take his class. I'm glad I did.
he is my favorite professor, very nice.

he is a very nice professor, it is easy to get high score in his exams. His practice questions and home works are similar as the exams questions. High recommend this professor if you wanna high grades.

It's hard to stay focused in class, the way he teaches is boring. He doesn't use Blackboard at all and won't even send you one email in the whole semester. The schedule on the syllabus doesn't have dates so if you skip that one day where he announces when the next exam will be you're screwed. He's nice to students but I do not recommend him.

It's hard to stay focused in class, the way he teaches is boring. He doesn't use Blackboard at all and won't even send you one email in the whole semester. The schedule on the syllabus doesn't have dates so if you skip that one day where he announces when the next exam will be you're screwed. He's nice to students but I don't recommend him.
very approachable professor. consider to take his class.
Such boring lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is a hard class. Not hard to get a good grade just a lot of work.
Prof Dunne is definitely a challenging class but gives many opportunities to succeed. If you put in the effort, you get an A.

Professor Dunne might be knowledgeable about data visualization, but when it comes to teaching an academic class he simply seems like he doesn't know what he is doing. His lectures are just talking about random topics as he reads from slides he made years ago. Assignments have nothing to do with the lectures and you will not receive any help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Worst professor, I have taken in my life! Claims he teaches a design class but all of his hw and projects are technical. Takes multiple days to respond to emails. When you need help on the hw, well good luck with it because you will find none as the professor will only point out console messages and the TAS for the class are simply clueless.

Prof is clearly passionate  Imagine putting hundreds of hours into a disorganized class and going 2 1/2 months without having any idea about what your grade is, risking your ability to graduate or maintain a scholarship etc. or even learning and using that knowledge in the next assignments. TAs are bad,  don't take this unless you're nasty at JS.

If you can take this class with another prof, pls do. I can't stress this enough. There are no clear grading standards and he takes points off as he pleases. It's so frustrating. The TA's are horrible too. I have had such a terrible experience in this class

Terrible professor! Doesn't teach anything remotely related to the HW in lectures. Very harsh and completely unreasonable grader takes off many points for  ridiculos things such as not including name or not tagging pages on GradeScope. Class is so disorganized and the professor seems clueless about how to run an academic class. Do not take!

Grades take 2+ months to be released and homework assignments are useless. Lectures are boring and not related to the homework assignments. The professor holds everyone to a very high level while making the TAs teach class sometimes and not grading anything. However, this class ended up being very easy because you don't end up learning anything.

Professor Dunne is one of the better professors I have had at Northeastern. 
He isn't the most socially savvy, and his lecture structure could use some work. 
But he is a very genuine and caring person who is passionate about the topic of Data Vis. He is very helpful in office hours, and just wants his students to succeed if they put the effort in.
Worst professor ever. Biggest mistake I made is taking this course. Non-sense and waste of my tuition

Waste of my tuition. Don't know what I've learned in this "writing class". All kinds of inexplicable demands for HWs and Projects. Always get 0. Only spend one class teaching how to write code, assuming everyone is skilled in programming in JS, Python. Don't take the course with this daydreamer with obsessive-compulsive disorder.

Worst professor I've ever seen. Two quizzes with 6 multiple choices questions worth 10 points of the total grade. Don't know what he's doing in lecture, showing ridiculous pictures in slides. I taught myself JavaScript-d3, HTML, CSS, Python, Tableau the whole semester. Making last-minute grade change without reason. No recording during the pandemic

The worst professor I've ever taken. The syllabus is a mess. The only thing I got out of the class was all the bad habits I acquired while teaching myself javascript (d3), html, and CSS at the same time. Will give 0 on assignments. Mandatory attendance/participation during COVID, no recordings. makes last-minute grade changes. Very slow email.
hes so funny like sometimes the lectures can be a little dry but he makes abstract ideas and philosophy easier to understand. He's not a tough grader. He's nice.

He gives 10 bonus points just for introducing yourself at the start. A lot of the work is group project based but with a good group it's very manageable. Very enjoyable and relaxed summer class, I highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor, and even better grader. I went into this class with no prior philosophy knowledge and he took time to clarify and help me out. As long as you say something during class conversations you'll be fine (25% participation). Only 3 assignments the whole semester but he's such a light grader it's not a problem.

Professor Connors is very passionate about teaching philosophy. I found his class to be enjoyable and not difficult. It is very philosophy and reading heavy and I would not recommend taking this class if you know you will not be interested in the content, but you can get a lot out of it if you fully engage and do the homework- watch the videos too!

Prof Connors knows a lot about what he teaches. Many students in my class did not participate, and it is definitely more enjoyable if you/other people do. There are few assignments. To get participation credit you must speak at least once each class. It is not difficult, but the readings can be dense, especially if you are new at philosophy.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Connors is very knowledgeable about what he teaches. This class is very confusing if you have no background knowledge about philosophy. You have to be good at reading complex texts, but Dr. Connors has helpful informational videos that make the readings much more easily understandable. If you participate it will be very rewarding.

Prof  doesn't do a great job of explaining material or relating it to current society. Very strict rules, but will be flexible if you have something going on. Assignments are not difficult at all but was left with an overall feeling that I didn't learn much and the content of the class is no longer relevant to philosophical discussions.

Professor Connors is clearly passionate about philosophy however he is not great at teaching it. He often seems unable to answer students' questions about what a specific philosopher means. He grades incredibly easy and gives very vague feedback. There are only three assignments the entire semester, one of which is a group paper/presentation.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I dont know why Codesso has 2.6 rating, hes amazing! He genuinely cares for his students by always doing hands on problems which has really helped me and Ive learned the most from this class than any other. Just do the pre-class assignments. Ppl who rated him bad js didnt do well. Hes super caring!

He is kind, lenient, available, and thoughtful. You have three big projects and he grades easily. The class is what you make of it-- can learn a lot or easy A. He also dresses up for Halloween. Take his class!!

Best profesor ever. Very caring about his students and wants everyone to do well. If you show up to class, do the worksheets before exams, you will get an A. Codesso is the goat. One of the Best profesor I ever had.

He forgot to post assignments halfway through the semester. Didn't really learn much at all during his class, and I never felt challenged or inspired by anything we discussed. Lots of 'code' in our projects was just his that he told us to copy. Easy A if you want to waste 4 credits.

Mauricio is really a detriment to both the accounting and data analytics programs at the school. I feel like if anything, my data skills suffered as a result of atrophying over a semester with him, and I wish had the opportunity to have literally anyone else teach me coding and databasing.

There are three exams for this course and one case study (group project-20%), midterm 1 (10%), midterm 2 (15%), and the final exam (25%), so this course is EXAM HEAVY. The case study took so much time and was overly complicated, and at least he gave everyone an A on that case study.

Mauricio is an awful professor and a detriment to Northeastern's accounting/data analytics dept as a whole. He's required for a lot of programs, which is tough for students who genuinely wanted to learn coding and data analytics. If you have any option in the matter and genuinely want to learn, avoid this professor AT ALL COSTS.

Professor Codesso doesn't spend much time on just lecturing during his classes but stresses a lot of hands on practice that he then goes over. All of his tests were multiple choice, including the final, so as long as you pay attention in class, you will be able to ace any test he puts in front of you.

The worst professor I've ever had!!!!! He assigns many assignments while failing to teach all the essential things. I did not learn ANYTHING also BEWARE of the final project because it will screw you up. He will not give any shit no matter how much you struggle or even if there is an error in the assignment directions.

Was genuinely excited to learn coding for my grad program, and this man completed ruined any ambition for that. Absolutely no useful class instruction, he never responds to emails, and his class consists of copying and pasting premade code he often writes incorrectly anyways

Hands down the worst professor in the business school. If you want to learn python, go to youtube or datacamp for free, since that's what you end up doing in his class anyways. He's never prepared for class, and has absolutely no clue how to explain tech heavy ideas to relative novices. Avoid him at all costs if you can.
Codesso is the goat. Take him if you can

He is not a bad guy at all. Most of the hws are on Connect, which almost serves as the lecture. If you really put effort into the hws on connect, the lecture will be easy. By lecture I mean some talking but mostly example problems. He is a pretty funny guy, responds to emails fast outside the class, and his tests are pretty easy.

He regularly made us download add-ons and programs via a remote server that regularly crashed our computers, which was problematic in a Zoom class. Then he begged for good reviews on this site and other surveys, so this guy is really just a complete unprofessional mess. Dont take him, hes terrible.

It is highway robbery that this guy's class is mandatory. The skills learned don't translate at all to the workplace, and any skills you do learn will be entirely through Datacamp because this guy STINKS at teaching. I spent 5 hours each week in class, and I honestly cannot tell you one thing that he taught me, not the online assignments.

I took Prof. Codesso through NUFlex online. He does a solid job at times of outlining the course and knows the material; however, English is not his first language, so his written materials can be confusing and his lectures border on unintelligible at times over Zoom. His communication skills are unfortunately not at an acceptable level.

Prof Codesso is super easy going. I had him during NUFlex fall 2020 and he was considerate of student needs in terms of extensions and extra help. He answers emails pretty quickly (usually within a couple hours). A lot of assignments on Connect but are manageable and also worth most of the grade. He is a great guy and wants his students to do well

I loved having Professor Collins as a professor and I found her classes to be very interesting. I would just be aware of the amount of reading that is required as well as the fact that some of her instructions were not clear when it came to the presentations that we had to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Collins was amazing and super nice. Going in I didn't expect to learn this much, especially as a non-criminal justice major. But it broadened my perspective for a lot of current issues we have. The course itself was a lot of reading and writing every week based on three books. But you do learn a lot from all of them along with the discussions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Collins is a great professor and extremely knowledgeable. The course was a bit disorganized but the actual class content was really good. It's discussion-based through most of the course based on 3 books you read. The class is not hard and is an average amount of writing, the best part is the guest lectures she brings in and her own input.

Dr. Collins is the most amazing professor I've ever had. Attendance is mandatory but the class is so interesting I would never even consider skipping. You have multiple required readings but all the texts are interesting and none read like a textbook. Grades are based on group presentations, discussion posts, and attendance. EC is an option!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of guest speakers (which are super interesting), very smart professor. However, for this class, while she is not a hard grader, there is a lot of work. There are 5 2-3 page papers, a final, and a ton of reading every week. There is also one group discussion you and a few classmates lead. Also unnecessarily rigid and rude to her students.

Dr. Collins is very sweet and I enjoyed the course material, but be warned that there were around 200 pages of reading per week that were required to participate. There were also papers close to ever week that had to be checked by the writing center for credit. The class is not necessarily hard but it is a pretty good amount of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: RUN do not have him as a teacher. His workload is insane and it's going to drive you nuts.

Great person, bad professor. Be prepared to have homework every day. The work isn't hard but there is just a lot of it and it's time consuming. You will learn a lot in stacked but I wouldn't take it again if I had the choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: coach mukasa is an amazing person, but the amount of work he gave was enough to make me realize the little things in life. his class was a lot of work but he was forgiving with assignments and project deadlines. hes reachable thru teams as well and overall is a funny and caring professor.

Mukasa himself is a great person, however his class is a LOT. I took full cornerstone with 1501/1502 combined and struggled through the semester. Prepare to do a lot of homework of all different types. You will learn a lot, but maybe at the cost of your sanity.

Workload heavy, but overall manageable. I took stacked cornerstone. The flipped classroom was pretty annoying (a lot of extra hw that you have to learn from). A LOT of groupwork (at minimum weekly memos). i had no experience going in, now i know autocad and solidworks decently. I like the teacher a lot; he can be reached through Teams and is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There is a lot of work that is assigned for the class but that is just part of it. He is super easy to talk to and understanding of any reason for an extension. Truly wants the best for his students and was super helpful when conflicts would arise with work load.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mukasa is a great professor, but his section specifically has much more work than other sections. I would say if you want to go above and beyond and learn skills that could help you a lot in your personal engineering pursuits, then take him. But if you want a good experience and just want the credit for your degree take a different prof.

I highly recommend that you take this course with another Prof. It is unnecessarily difficult and work-heavy in comparison to the other courses and teachers. While I learned a lot, I don't think it was worth the sleepless nights (I'd never pulled an all-nighter before this course),mental breakdowns and overall poor experience I had in this class.

Don't choose him. The amount of work in his class compared to the other sections for cornerstone, especially stacked cornerstone is absurd. Want to write about 20 pages each week in addition to 3-4 hours of assignments for just this course a day then choose him. He is a poor lecturer and does not give good feedback or set clear expectations.

Had him for stacked cornerstone, way too much homework. The kids with other professors for stacked cornerstone weren't nearly as overwhelmed as we were. Super enthusiastic and nice guy, but while he did give extensions for the homework a lot, it piled up quickly, especially for someone who's never coded or CADed before.

I took Mukasa for Stacked Cornerstone, for which he taught the programming section. He assigned way too much work, to the point which I experienced physical distress. His assignments were unclear and harshly graded. However, he is knowledgeable in programming and is willing to help students.
Professor Mukasa was extremely helpful and kind. This class was difficult for me, but he was always there to help.

I had him for Stacked Cornerstone and his class was fast-paced and software-heavy, but he is genuinely one of the most caring and accommodating professors I've ever had. He was always available to meet outside of class and answered any questions I had promptly on Teams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: All cornerstone classes, especially stacked, have a lot of work and are big on group projects. Mukasa is a super sweet and caring teacher, and he really wants his students to do well. Super easy to get an A as long as you do all your work. Workload is manageable if you use resources like FYELIC and get help from classmates.
Immense hw workload, very doable, easy A if you do your work. Not the greatest teacher but tries to be accommodating and is very fair
C. Mukasa super friendly
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mukasa is a nice guy and passionate, but not great teacher. lectures feel useless when you get to homework assignments. Assignments are tedious. Group work is a HUGE part of the course, unless you have a good group, you're screwed. Homework instructions (or lack thereof) tend to be contradicting. Taking stacked is doable but very time consuming.

Insane amount of group work so if your group sucks its over for you. Had to write a freakishly long final report and memos every single week (aka more writing than an english class). Homework is time-consuming but  you'll get a good grade if you follow the rubric. Instructions can be super confusing though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very caring and approachable. During our final exam he would offer help when people where having mental breakdowns (clearly not meche's trying to do solidworks). He let some people post it hours later because it crashed. tough class but the grading is clear as long as u do your stuff your set for an A.
Other reviews might say he doesn't reply but he must have changed his ways because he always replies. Tough class and assignments, easy grader and super friendly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mukasa only responds sometimes to messages. He has fun in class and the classes are lighthearted but all assignments are basically "figure it out yourself" based. Completely trial and error. It is hard to get in touch with him and often times the problem will not be resolved. The TAs grade almost everything so its good to communicate with them.

Prof. Mukasa is a nice guy who clearly cares about his students and wants them to learn. But his class had so much more work than most of the other profs, his assignment instructions were convoluted and contradictory, and the coding is near impossible without prior experience. Be prepared to get no sleep for a whole semester.

If you're in cornerstone at all, you're absolutely cooked, especially if it's stacked cornerstone. The workload is immense no matter the professor, but in my experience, Mukasa has been working to accommodate my special circumstances this semester. He really does care, and if you reach out, he'll try to help you if he can.
Great professor! Loved the homework. Very creative. Funny guy. Don't believe the haters!

Lectures are not related to coursework. Homework is only doable if you have prior experience with the programs. He grades based on how much he likes you so dont get on his bad side. He doesnt know how to write a homework assignment and will give you the most convoluted instructions. Id write more if I had the space; do NOT take him.

As stated on my other review, he isn't a great professor. Although he is passionate in what he does, his teaching skills are subpar. He gives hours of unnecessary homework and doesn't explain his assignments very well. There's also lots of filler, as he generally doesn't cut to the point. Great person, bad teacher.

Overall, Professor Mukasa was a difficult teacher. Although his class was fine itself, he was convoluted in giving instructions and on more than one assignment, I had no confidence I was completing it correctly. He is a great person, but his teaching skills are questionable. The class isn't hard, but he wasn't confident of the content.

He is enthusiastic, yes. Otherwise really confusing to learn from. We kept telling each other to "interpret the assignments how you want" because they were not clear that we would all do them differently. My only saving grace was having previous experience.
Convoluted Instructions for all assignments. Difficult grader. English not first language.
Extremely incompetent. Doesn't know what is happening

Nice person to approach but has no idea what he is doing. His lectures are disorganized and when you ask questions, he doesn't know the answer most of the time. Homework is much harder than what is gone over in class, so expect to be in extra help a lot.

Mukasa is a nice guy, but the man can't teach. He's really bad at communicating effectively to students and oftentimes gets confused with his own course material. There's WAY too much homework and it's all busywork. Even though it's easy, it's so annoying to complete. Again, super nice, and he means well, but he's so out of touch with his students.
awful professor, great human

This dude was absolute garbo. He never explained assignments and his homework was so hard. Also anytime you ask a question, he gets mad that you didn't pay attention. I should have dropped when I had the chance. 1/10 would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Mukasa was incredibly nice, and clearly cared about his students. I learned a lot, and made friends due to his group work. However, assignments were often confusing, and things disorganized. Many of my classmates were very rude to him, but he took criticism well, and improved throughout my two semesters.

There was SO much homework for this class, especially compared to other cornerstone professors. Be prepared to hear about how everyone else's cornerstone classes are a breeze while you suffer through hours of c++ and random ethics research "assignments" (they're basically essays). If you don't go to class you will have no idea what is going on.

Mukasa gives a ton of busy work w unclear instructions which means random points off for dumb things. He really wants to help students and get feedback but there is a just a disconnect and he doesn't understand how to. No one ever had their camera on or participated but lots of extra credit means its a super easy A and content is sorta interesting

Horribly organized and a ton of assignments. He clearly doesn't know what he's doing for most of what we do, and is very condescending and rude. Though it's an easy A, it's really not worth the grade.

I had him 1st and now 2nd semester. During Cornerstone 1, he was unclear about all instructions. Apparently he was an EE major, but you could not tell. His only redeeming quality is the sheer amount of extra credit, which he doesn't do anymore in Cornerstone 2. I got an A+, didn't go to class or take the final. Avoid this class or collaborate.

His homework assignments have confusing instructions. when he asks students for feedback, and they give it, he gets mad and says they are wrong. There's also so much work every week, and he doesn't make it very clear when stuffs assigned. He marked me for plagarism for turning in the same thing as a group member on a GROUP project.

Mukasa is a decent professor some of the time, but he is extremely unclear about his expectations for assignments and group projects, with the latter making up a huge portion of your grade. He is quite frustrating to talk to, and puts emphasis on participation and pointless busywork in the form of endless feedback and memos. I would stay away.

You can tell Mukasa really cares about his students, but he is new to teaching and this shows. He is not very good at lecturing and his instructions for assignments, as well as the grading criteria, is very unclear but he gives so much extra credit that as long as you do the work (which there is a lot of) it's virtually impossible to not get an A.

Very very difficult person and grader. Would not recommend. I really depended on my peers for help with assignments, which while a nice way to make friends freshman year, should not have been their responsibility. For reference, I had no experience coding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's organizationally a mess. You never know what's due or when, or how what you're doing connects to the curriculum. He focuses primarily on mechE projects in a general engineering course. Anything you learn will be from peers or self-taught, but he is an extremely easy grader and gives loads of extra credit. It's not worth the A though.

Mukasa is a very nice guy who cares about the input he receives from students. While there was a fair amount of busywork, I didn't find that it took up too much of my time. There are plenty of opportunities for extra credit, so getting a good grade is no problem. Mukasa has room for growth teaching-wise, but I wouldn't say he was a bad teacher.

Overall the professor is passionate about the topics and cares about his students. He gives many difficult assignments. You definitely have to work hard for a good grade in his class, but he is a generally fair grader and offers extra credit opportunities.

Overall, Professor Mukasa is a pretty good professor. He gives interesting assignments and is available for feedback. He structures his classes well. However, there is a ton of work and he is a difficult grader. His grading criteria is also not very specific or easy to understand, which is frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's ok. He gives alot of work, but he's flexible. I submitted an assignment 1 week late and he waived the late penalty because it was my first time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very unclear instructions. Assigns so much busywork. Grading is confusing. Be prepared to do the assignments with classmates, because they're pretty much impossible by yourself.

Professor Mukasa is extremely unclear about what he wants when he assigns work. Most of the coding homework was just busywork, and if you want to learn to program, find another teacher. He was extremely unforgiving with the group project amidst the COVID-19 pandemic and is the worst professor in the department.

Gives unnecessary busy work compared to other profs. Grading criteria is unclear and you lose points for things you weren't even aware you were being graded on. Takes more time to figure out what what needs to be done for an assignment than it take to do it. Mukasa refuses to give straightforward answers to questions even when necessary.
Very fast paced class, poor teaching of coding unit so get ready to teach yourself. Lots of homework that takes a long time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a new professor, so he changes his plans alot based on student feedback. The homework is not hard, but it does take up alot of time. Pay super close attention to the rubric if you don't want to lose points. He gives extra credit sometimes too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Doesn't give clear instruction or will give 3 different rubrics for one project and expect you to know which one to follow, resulting in a loss of points for which the reason remains unclear. Friendly person. If you haven't coded previously, get ready to teach yourself and be in FYELIC constantly because he did a terrible job teaching that.

Good at taking student feedback and adjusting his teaching style. Very difficult homework. A lot of time spent outside of class. Pace was too fast at first and material was not clearly explained but he got better after taking student feedback. Lectures weren't boring.

He is a very nice guy and genuinely wants to help his students. However, as he's new his teaching skills are a bit lacking. He isn't good at explaining things, which with the heavy homework load and his tough grading policy mean that you often lose points due to misunderstanding directions. He is forgiving with late work though.

DJ is one of the best professors I have ever had. His lectures are super informative, and all lectures are recorded live on zoom if you cannot make it to class. He genuinely cares about every single student in his class, and helping them succeed in becoming an EMT.

Jolliest prof ever. He is so enthusiastic about teaching EMS that you just naturally succeed in his class. If you show up to lectures and put in the work, you will 1) be jolly af and 2) succeed in the class. The course lowkey has the most work I've ever had in my life but it was SOOO worth it bc both DJ and Ben really want you to succeed.

DJ is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is so caring and makes every lecture enjoyable with his enthusiasm and kindness. The two exams are a little tricky, and there is a skills practical, but he works with students during lab to ensure everyone can master the content. Truly one of the nicest people I have ever met.

He's genuinely one of the best professors that I've ever had. I love his lecture style, and he gives amazing feedback in simulation labs and class. He is so clearly experienced in his field and loves everything about it. He's very passionate, which makes him such a great teacher.

Took Basic Clinical Skills with DJ, both the class itself and DJ were great! Definitely learned skills that were extremely helpful for co-op interviews. It's a easy class with a majority of online assignments and a practical exam at the end. To do well show up, participate and actually learn the skills for the practical exam at the end.
