This has been by far my favorite class at Northeastern, and DJ is the main reason! He and the other instructors for the course are so knowledgeable and really want you to succeed. Course is, by nature, lots of textbook reading but you learn so much from him. He's a quick responder to emails and is eager able to help.

DJ is so awesome!  Great professor with a passion for all things EMS. He responds quickly and is strict, but not in an unreasonable way. If you utilize all of the tools he gives you, it is basically impossible to not succeed. 10/10 DJ is the best.

Basic Clinical Skills was one of my favorite classes that I've taken so far. You get CPR certified in this class and learn a lot of useful skills for coop. He is very quick with emails and extremely knowledgable. There are online quizzes every week but theres only one hour of lecture and one 2 hour lab. 10/10 would recommend!
He takes the time to get to know his students and will put in the effort to ensure their success.
eccentric guy! but good at supporting you throughout your coop process
Richard is simultaneously a professor and a therapist for all his students. He is so knowledgeable, helpful, hilarious, and approachable. My favorite!!
Best Professor in NEU. Simple as that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Richard is an incredible advisor. He is clearly passionate about his job and his students. Attendance is mandatory and he does have a weekly assignment but the assignment is a breeze.
Richard is hilarious. Had a fantastic time each and every class. He really cares about getting you placed in a co-op. As long as you show that you're doing your part, he'll be there to help.
Great guy and funny! Makes classes interesting and helpful. Cuts straight to the point.

The funniest professor I have ever had i was rolling on the ground laughing every class and actually wished class was more often. Also by far the most helpful coop advisor because he's there everyday and does so much work to get you a good job. He is the only professor i keep in touch with. Like mentioned before this guy is the man.
Very hilarious guy in class. Quirky and weird in the beginning, but you get to wish every professor was like him. Will have you laughing most of class, just hope your not the butt of his jokes.
WORLD CLASS HOTTIE

conley makes the class interesting, and gives you absolutely everything you need to know about interviewing and getting a great co-op.  i specifically scheduled myself into his class for my next co-op class because his class is just that entertaining and informative.  all hail, richard el magnifico
Great

Richard Conley is the best coop adviser at Northeastern University. A friendly, patient, and caring person who goes out extra miles of his way to help students. I highly recommend students to change their last name to have him as coop adviser.
Richard is awesome!  He is most definitely the best co-op coordinator there is at Northeastern.
No Comments

Conley is probably the funniest teacher at northeastern. Take his co-op class! It consists of him basically talking/making fun out of the whole class, and he is absolutely hysterical. ALWAYS willing to help you out at anytime, and will definitely help you get a good co-op job. Simply stated, he is the man.
Richard is awesome. Very easy class with a hilariously inappropriate guy. TAKE THE CLASS.

Very funny guy. If you want some serious strict professor, don't have him. He gets everything he needs to get done but in a fun way. This is not your typical class but it was one of my favorites. If you're sensitive, don't take his class. If you have a good sense of humor, you'll love it. He definitely doesn't mind helping you out.
funny guy.
Good class, it's easy and he's helpful.
Conley is a great professor, don't know if he actually follows any sort of agenda for his class, but it's a lot of fun for something school related.   P.S. say he's hot....he's a little insecure
I'm very disapointed he didn't write any quotes.
No Comments
No Comments

Although the class was a little disorganized, we talked about a lot of interesting things and brought up a lot of topics that make you think.  It's hard to tell if you're doing well in the class or not, but I'd still recommend people to take this class.

Rather unstructured style of teaching (doesn't give deadlines, expectations in advance, etc.) can be frustrating for students who like to stay organized. Easily strays from the topic at hand. Acts chummy but probably won't do you any favors.
Cool guy, very helpful.
He cares about his students alot. Course is very hard but he cares abt students
Very difficult class but it's all curved.  He's a great professor who cares about his students a lot.

Prof Cortes is awesome. The class was tough (lots of tests, tons of practice problems, and a really fast pace) but honestly, I've learned more here than in any other class at Northeastern. He's strict but fair, super funny, and really knows his stuff. Easily the hardest class I've taken, but also the best.

The professor is extremely rude and disorganized. He would constantly go off the planned schedule and seemed chaotic. Would NEVER recommend him to any student who actually wants to learn. His rude demeanor turns students away from being excited about the class material. I've never disliked a professor this much.
so many quizzes and he drops two but its lockdown browser and camera on. the content was so hard to understand. i recommend taking this in person rather than online cause it is extremely math heavy
very unorganized and quiz is way too hard and pointless
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Risk management was very hard.

Absolutely loved Felipe Cortes. He hates memorization and will go through the intuition of every process and problem with you. Quizzes are hard but the class is graded on a heavy curve (Top 50% get at least an A-). Honestly a gem in the otherwise meh group of finance professors at Northeastern. I thought he was pretty funny too.

By far the best professor I had. I am glad I took his class before graduating. In just one class, he rekindled my passion for Finance. He is very technical but always wants students to focus on intuition first and then on the math part. Awesome class!

This class is so hard, I literally gave up... super nice guy, but you should be afraid if you choose to enroll. Is willing to cover concepts and answer questions, but this class will leave you not even knowing where to start asking. Northeastern prerequisites will not really prepare you.

In just half semester, I learned more Python and Investments than in the previous two classes. It is amazing how he incorporates previous classes and helps us fil in the gaps. Get ready to learn with him, he is truly a gem. Best class and Best professor at the Business School. He is strict but fair and wants us to be technical. Amazing class.

Amazing Class. I never expected to learn so much about Bitcoin. He offers a very clear perspective on the limitations and uses of crypto. The class is very stimulating. He clearly loves to teach. the class is test heavy (too many quizzes) but I agree with him. This helps the learning. Definitely recommend if you want to learn and be challenged..

Absolutely horrible professor. Extremely unorganized, will give assignments one day before the due date. Expects you to know everything. Does not explain what he wants in the assignments and is super inaccessible as well. AVOID AT ALL COST
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Canvas is not organized at all! he is always unprepared for classes and will randomly decide to take quizzes later or earlier without informing anyone. He expects you to read his mind when it comes to keeping up with his class and expects you to know everything from before. Very inaccessible outside of class as well.

As time gets closer and closer to the end of the semester, the knowledge would be more and more difficult. No assignments but there is a quiz at the beginning of the class. The knowledge is very practical. Some mathematical logic would be used to understand the knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are intense, but extremely informative. Jam-packed with real world examples. Really digs into the fundamentals of any concept. Will get into the finer details of anything he's talking about. Passionate about what he teaches. Challenging yet rewarding. 10/10 would recommend his class, if you have any interest in the class that you're taking
Fair grading, he is really passionate about investment. The concepts in class are building up from the beginning . You gotta know them all, but overall great professors.

Professor Cortes was amazing! He explained tough concepts in a digestible manner and gave lots of real world context to the material. The class was tough but very doable if you put the work in outside of class. I would recommend reviewing over the lecture materials regularly and doing all the practice problems he gives. Highly recommend taking him!

I really like Prof Cortes. The 4340 course is quite technical and we does his best to deliver the intuition without sacrificing technicality. There are students from various backgrounds which makes the class go slower sometimes, but I think Felipe does a great job handling it. Learning a lot so far!!!

An incredibly technical and repetitive professor. The epitome of "talking at you" rather than teaching you. He rambles on with little time to ask questions. He won't stop, like a freight-train of unnecessary filler words and confusion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His grading system helps most people do better in the class but even though he drops the lowest 2 quiz grades, know that it's hard to do well on the quizzes since the questions in class are much easier than the ones seen in quizzes. Must know your calc concepts! Worked super hard and still didn't do well - class dropped my overall GPA
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Cortes really wants students to understand the materials in class. He repeats concepts and provides multiple examples. The grade for the class is based mostly on quizzes, which are given weekly. He requires students to do 2 homework assignments, which were extremely long.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Knew I liked Felipe day 1 when he said not to bother buying the textbook. He truly cares about his students, and you can tell he works hard on his lectures and curriculum. I struggled a bit in FINA2201 and liked this class far better. As far as his ranked grading system goes, it didn't affect me, but I know it benefited some.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Even if you have zero interest in investments, trust me this class will leave you inspired to learn more. Prof Cortes is a great lecturer and always offers super easy examples to make sure everyone understands the complex concepts. The material he teaches is above undergrad level but that's what makes this class so rewarding and interesting

Felipe is super straight forward. Although the material was hard for some, he teaches you important concepts. As long as you show up to class, take notes, pay attention, and study, you'll get better than a B-. He rewards effort and gives ample opportunities to get points.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best finance professors at Northeastern. Took investments with him, class is pretty quantitative and requires some econ and math backgrounds (simple calc and algebra). If you want a solid foundation in investments, take him. I look forward to taking his Financial Risk this fall.

I learned SO much from this class, and definitely learned about investments more than other sections I would guess. HOWEVER, his grading system is completely flawed. I received a 94% overall in his class and received a B+ because of his curving system, as did a lot of students. So obviously in this class, hard work doesn't necessarily pay off.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing prof. Very hard though. The grading isn't tough, it is based on your rank in the class. 40% of grade is pass/fail, the quizzes/midterm/final really define the grade. 25% of the class get A/A-, the last 22% get B- or C+ (unless you skip class/ don't hand in HW). It is rewarding, a must take class if you wish to work in investments later.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of the hardest classes I have ever taken, but completely worth it. Although my grades were not as high as I would have liked, I learned a lot in his class. He is great with feedback and is always there for you if you don't understand the content. However, make sure you brush up on your calc--his class is very math-heavy. Go to all the classes!
By far the the most difficult class I've taken at Northeastern but it is also the best one so far. Amazing professor, keeps challenging you! I recommended his class to all my friends!

Felipe Cortes, funny guy, gives great feedback during office hours however class is often unclear and the mathematical aspect only brushed upon. If you take Fin3303 with him, you HAVE to be good in calc. Tests are curved, lots of group projects.
Hard course but if you work hard you end up learning a lot. I enjoyed the class even though it was hard.
Really hard course! The hardest 3303 course exam and contents when compare to other professors' . Nice guy but very very hard exam

Very nice guy but a terrible professor. Doesn't use examples. So you will go through weeks at a time of looking at formulasvariables without doing actual hands on workexamples till the homework assignm... Chose to focus on theories rather than actual investment material. I sup. that's what happens when an academia with no work experience teaches.
Great class but with a lot of work. He seems interested in the content he teaches, which is very good to see.

Prof Brown is great. As long as you do the work with effort you will pass. He takes a while to give back work but states this at the beginning of the sem so nothing is unexpected. Straightforward course and discussions made heavy readings easier to understand. If you do the work this should be a smooth class.

Prof Brown is a great teacher. The course itself I took with him had boring content, but he was very nice and friendly and I learned a good amount. Also very generous with grading, literally just go to class and do the work and you'll be fine

So sweet and kind, but don't take his class! He is so disorganized, i feel like even he doesn't know what is going on sometimes. he is very smart just a bad professor. literally never graded anything until thanksgiving break, meaning u would never get feedback for the following thing due. never stuck to syllabus, cancelled class all the time, etc
I thought he was a very personable and caring teacher. Sometimes his lectures were very text-heavy, but other times we would have fun activities. Super easy class, would recommend!

Dr. Brown is the best prof. I've had at Northeastern. Amazing, down-to-earth guy who allows all viewpoints in class, which is hard to come by here. You definitely should take him, even if not for this class, for another.

Overall an amazing professor. Extremely kind and understanding. Exams and quizzes are all online and open-note. All assignments (including quizzes and midterms) have automatic extensions. Easy A if you do all the work.
He is friendly and likeable. Online open-book tests, even final and midterm. Likes European politics. Liberal, pro-democracy bent. Sang a broadway song in class once.

This professor made the course interesting and engaging in a subject I did not previously think I would like. He confirmed to me I wanted to be a political science major. One of the best POLS professors and the course is not hard as long as you talk in class and put in some time on the paper.

Colin is a very chill guy, he cares about his students and checks in if you're not in class a few times. all his quizzes/tests are open everything. lectures could get realllly dull sometimes, he just talks at you a lot and research methods isn't the most exciting class. but he's a great guy and really passionate about his subjects
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took Comp Pol with him. If you're invested in the topic this dude will be the best professor you've ever had. and if you don't really care and are just taking this class as a pre-req, then he's easy enough that you wont have any problems.

He was always so funny in class and super understanding about assignments, quizzes, essays, and tests. This course does have a lot of reading but I found most of it pretty interesting and you'll find he's a very fair grader. His lectures are clear and he makes sure everyone understands what he is talking about before moving on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Okay so he is the sweetest guy, but I could not follow along with what he was saying most of the time. His lectures were long-winded and kind of confusing, many question marks and unfinished sentences on his slides. The class is easy and the assignments were very manageable but I found it difficult to feel like I actually learned something.

Very good professor, he's genuinely interested in what he's teaching and is very understanding. Big perk is that if he's wrong or doesn't understand something he won't talk out his butt, if you have a question or comment he takes it seriously and listens to you. Will definitely take again, and even switched to a combined major in political science.

Professor Brown was very interesting. Honestly, the hardest part of his class was the quizzes only because the TA was not consistent in grading. All the quizzes and tests were taken home, online, and with open notes. Attendance was taken but as long as you didn't miss often they didn't care. Had a Zoom option to listen in. Overall very chill class.

Prof Brown is great. If ur thinking ab taking research methods in poli sci make ur life easier and take it with him. The main grades in the class are a midterm, group projects, and a final quiz. v straightforward class and he's such a nice guy.

Pretty interesting lectures and the content and readings were enjoyable. The syllabus and canvas page made it a bit difficult to know what was due when. His grading scheme is very flexible and forgiving which is nice. He gave good feedback on papers and group projects, so there's a nice mix of grades. Funny and down to Earth guy. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was really easy in terms of how he grades, but is really time consuming due to the large amount of papers and long readings. And you actually need to do the readings and be prepared to talk about them in class. His lectures were sometimes dry, but he's a really nice and chill professor who cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nice man... poor teacher I think the main problem is that he is too disorganized. He assigned three of the biggest assignments of the semester for the same week. Also, the professor doesn't do anything to accommodate those who don't learn from reading. This class made me question if I want a career in politics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Poor guy would thrive teaching a more interesting class. Content is boring, but he's a fair grader who's very interesting as a person. Much of the reading depended on other people, so pray to get lucky with your group assignment. Exams were online and open book (phew). Great professor, boring class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, solid professor but class is mostly just him lecturing and it can get very boring if you are not really interested in the house material. Generally an easy grader and quizzes and final are take home that you do online.

Prof. Brown is a great professor. The class material itself is very boring, but it was required for my major. He makes it as interesting as possible, and is understanding with things like attendance/homework (although those are still important). For example, our midterm was open note. Overall, a great professor assigned a dull course.

I loved Professor Brown's class, I think he's passionate about what he teaches and integrated a lot of his own experiences and research into his lectures. The only thing is he did not post any of his lecture slides online, but if you pay attention to what he says and take notes it'll be fine. Also, the readings did depend on other group members
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great teacher, smart and helpful.

He clearly knows alot about what he is teaching and was able to convey it very well, lecture are very engaging and he doesnt flex his knowledge on you. Very caring and accessible outside of class. Amongst the best professors you can find. The only negative thing would be that he doesnt use powerpoints and instead uses the blackboard

Very enthusiastic professor you can tell that he actually cares about his students, gives lots of extra credit opportunities. Classes are mostly lectures but still very interesting, sometimes hands-on simulations are engaging
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I genuinely enjoyed taking Professor Brown's POLS1155 class. I have his class from 9:15 in the morning and I am definitely not a morning person, but I have NEVER fallen asleep once in his class. He is so passionate about what he is teaching and he definitely cares about his students. He is so organized and an easy grader! Most quizzes are takehome.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Is a teaching professor but sometimes his lectures are all over the place. Does give a sheet of key terms before each week. LOTS OF READINGS & additional group readings. He tries to cover too much information. Tests are open note but require specific details from random reading. Offers extra credit assignments. Nice guy, sometimes unclear feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Every single lecture gives interesting and relevant material. While the visual aids are lacking, the lectures are still great. Great man, great class.

Professor Brown is a wonderful professor who likes to combine lectures with class participation activities that provide lots of opportunities for extra credit. He is very knowledgeable and is very lenient in terms of the work he gives. Can be lecture heavy most of the time, however.

Really loved Professor Brown for Comparative Politics! Explained things in a very easy-to-understand way and seemed to really care about students. Only thing was that tests were basically all on supplemental readings (and there were a lot of them) but the midterm and final were open note.
Northeastern's greatest professor. If you haven't taken her then youre missing out. Thats it.

The best professor I've had at Northeastern - she's a real gem. You can tell she loves CMB and she explains things really well. She's also super nice and helpful when you ask her questions (some profs can be a little condescending or don't always explain things very well). Highly recommend!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's so kind and caring of her students. Her enthusiasm for bio makes the lectures more interesting. She really prepares you for the exams by providing study guide questions and practice exams; grading for the exams is also fair. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Shes an amazingly professor. Her lectures are engaging and the coursework is very meaningful. But she cant keep track of time!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really loves the topic and it shows. So long as you go to class you'll do fine. Most of the grading is the exams but she's a fair grader. All around a smart and kind professor and scientist.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The best teacher I e ever had! She is extremely helpful. Her lectures provide you with great notes and reflect her exams. She also gives you past exams as study tools. She wants you to succeed and understand her subject. Honestly take her if you can she's amazing and extremely helpful! I wish all teachers could be like her.

Dr. Cram was by far the best professor I have had during my 3 years at Northeastern. She made the class fun, applied real life concepts, and always had a great attitude. Clicker points during lectures were an easy grade booster and made the lectures interactive which made paying attention easier. Her exams were fair, and helpful in office hours.
Very enthusiastic. Keeps it simple but ensures that she conveys everything that she wanted to. Not too taxing.Would love to take another of Erin's classes

Cram is so genuinely nice, and really wants you to do well. She dumbs down the information and holds your hand through the class. Seriously, on several occasions I felt like I was back in Kindergarden. The lab for this class is horrendous, but her lecture is excellent.

Relatively easy class. Prof. Cram knows all about topics relating to her research - meaning some other topics difficult for her to teach. Overall a good class, however the lab is another story with a couple of long scientific papers to write.

I loved Cram. Some people complained that she just reads off the slides, but I liked going to lecture and thought she did a good job organizing the material. I could tell she really knows her stuff and loves genetics. Just know everything in the slides and on the practice exam and you'll do well.
Pretty easy to understand. Powerpoints give most of the information that you need to know so it is easy to catch up if you miss class.

A little different teaching style.  You will have to write a couple short papers and read some literature.  We gave a presentation as well.  Overall it was pretty good though, exams are hard but fair.  I would recommend taking this class with her the other proffesors arent that great compared to her.
No Comments
If you are looking to be a geneticist and get your bases in this class... you probably won't.  Cram is very easily flustered, but she means well...
Classes were boring overall. Weekly quizzes and homework were fine, but midterm & final were graded like she has a vendetta against every single person. 56% class average for the final & no curve.

This class was not great. The labs, ILS, and in-class polls were perfectly easy, but the Homeworks took 4+ hours, and the midterm and final were horrific, not to mention that they were graded like I personally offended her. The lectures did not help at all, and it might have gone better for me if I had just skipped class and taught myself.

She's very boring and each lecture is hard to follow. The class is clearly organized and you can get an A for both physics 1 and 2. Personally she doesn't work well for me, but I can see how other students may enjoy her teaching. She definitely knows what she is teaching though.

Don't get all the bad reviews. Has so many good examples and practice problems in class and truly cares about her students and that they understand it all. The ICAs are easy and free points, and you can miss up to 12. That being said, it is still Physics 2, so it is a hard class, but she makes going to class fun and helps you learn well.

I really liked Professor Di Credico. Her quizzes were very reasonable and we had in class activities that would help us prepare for the quiz. The exams were also very reasonable, with the grading being generous. The class to finally help me understand physics. I took her class in the summer so it might not be the same during the normal terms.

People are right that the lectures are not super useful. Homework can be tough but the book is free and has basically all of the theory and equations you need to ace it. Plus cheat sheets are allowed on quizzes and exams so if you can write it down you should have an easy time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring, don't prepare you for the homework and there's an in-class question for participation. Use your time better and just read the textbook. For the final exam, she refused to allow regrade requests and shut down any inquiries about the grading, while confidently stating that she and her TAs are incapable of making mistakes.

As a professor she is really not great. Her lectures feel like hour long yap sessions where she really only covers the topics at the most surface level, not as deep as the homework or tests take them. She did a poor job preparing students for tests. Most of my learning was done doing the homework or in ILS. Luckily the grade has a lot of padding.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Genuinely such a mediocre professor. The lectures will give you general concepts but do nothing to actually help you solves problems or develop a real understanding. Completing homework's will get you infinitely more knowledge than lectures. If you struggle with non-physical application this class will be a major challenge.

She's pretty good considering how hard Physics 2 is to explain, but her lectures are too vague/conceptual and don't prepare you to actually solve questions with numbers. The midterm and final are rough and there is a lot of homework, but it balances in your grade overall.

she is an okay professor for a difficult course with a big lecture section. however, the slides were super vague and lectures were fast and confusing. the ILS professors are better for actually preparing for the quizzes and tests. i didn't feel like i missed anything if i missed a lecture

This teacher is genuinely terrible. If I never went to class I would be in the same spot as if I came. I listen during class and sometimes we arrive at the end of the class and I've realized we have learned nothing. Also she is very hard to communicate with as she is very rude and has a rather large ego. I would rather pick any other teacher.

I took Physics I over the summer, and she let us know it moved at a much faster pace since it was compacted into 2 months. Had 2 homework assignments a week, which was time consuming but helped a lot. Lectures were confusing at times but she was willing to answer questions and provided examples. Had a quiz every week and she graded fairly.
She is unprofessional and made unfair assumptions about her students.

I took Energy, Env. and Soc. Fall '23. The workload is light, with a simple weekly homework and 3 in class assessments. Before each assessment there was a detailed review which it made it easy to get an A. Prof. Di Credico has a good sense of humor and I would definitely recommend the class if you are interested in energy or need an easy SI credit.

Grading boundaries are generous. Grading of midterms and homework is extremely fair. The homework is equal to (and sometimes harder than) the midterms which makes it good practice before tests. If you are struggling she is happy to help. Let us redo a midterm problem because the wording was a little confusing. Makes the hard topics seem possible.

Professor Di Credico takes an accelerated physics class and transforms it into digestible homework chunks.  Her grading curve is insane, where an 85 is an A-.  She is accessible outside of class and responds quickly to emails.  As long as you understand the homework, the class she teaches should be no trouble.

She is all over the place. The lecture slides make no sense if you want to re-read, she barely does practice problems and rambles a lot. If you get a good TA for ILS you will be fine, but if you don't you will have to teach yourself everything. Then again, I haven't heard great things about any of the other physics 1 professors.

She is very kind and knowledgeable, but she goes very fast in her lectures so you must pay attention. No matter what teacher you have for physics you will have to do pearson hw twice a week but she often gives examples similar to the problems.

I loved Professor Di Credico! I never really understood physics before her class, but she lectures so clearly that everything makes sense. She is very good at explaining, is passionate about physics, and offers so much help during office hours.

Physics is difficult. Luckily, Prof. Di Credico understands this and does everything she possibly can to effectively teach the material. I found her lectures to be the most engaging across my courseload. She tries to prepare her students for the weekly ILS quizzes and course exams with tricky practice problems.

I took PHYS1132. She was a very passionate lecturer, funny, and very chill. She gave very in depth study guides, and gave full freedom on the final project. The class was informative and she tailored the topics to your interests.

Physics 2 is already a really hard course and Prof. Di Credico makes it even harder, it is hard to fully grasp concepts from lectures and the homework is sometimed too hard. However, she is very understanding with students and easy to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Physics 2 is already a rough class, Di Credico doesn't make that any better. Her lectures often don't match the homework which both don't match the tests. The labs are better than physics 1, but still full of the IPL hassle. She's not great at listening to feedback. She completely disregards any feedback on how she teaches. Overall mid teacher.

I took PHYS1151 over Summer 1. The double acceleration proved very difficult, but Professor Di Credico was very aware of how difficult this made an already difficult course. While she can't make physics easier, she made class engaging and created a safe space in which to ask questions and receive help. She made my semester!

Prof. Di Credico is super attentive and wants to get to know all of her students, very understanding and open to provide help. Took it during the summer so very fast paced and lots of homework but if you do all the homeworks and go through the quizzes the midterm and final are very straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are decent, but sometimes she doesn't fully explain her work which can be confusing. Homework was due two times a week and was time consuming, but helpful for learning the material. Quizzes/tests weren't impossible, but definitely challenging. A good thing is exams don't make up your entire grade (midterm = 15%, quizzes = 20%, final = 25%)
Although she is a lovely lady outside of class, she really fails at the most important part: teaching. She has an inability to understand how her teaching directly impacts the grades of her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst physics professors ever. Sure she may be nice but her lectures are no where connected to approximately four hours of homework every week if you have her in the summer. The group interactions and quizzes really brings physics nowhere and I had to drop her class due to heavy conflict issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures and board work were essential to passing. Only used the textbook for difficult HW problems. Two HW sets a week, each about two hours long if you understood the concepts from lecture. Challenging content but lots of practice before tests which are the majority of the grade. Very kind and actually takes time to understand students' questions
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Even though she was nice, she did not know how to teach at all. Her lectures were pretty much useless, and I learned the most from youtube videos since the masteringphysics was no where near what we did in class. The entire course is so mismanaged, and I think this runs in the entire physics department.

Definitely one of the better profs I've had so far. Did a great job of making me feel cared about as a student. Also more than willing to help outside of class and has a good amount of time dedicated to office hours. My only complaint is the large amount of masteringphysics work which sometimes didn't even align with where we were in class.

Very difficult especially if you have never taken physics before! The professor only really teaches the formulas and does not explain the concepts well. She also only explain how to do really simple problems but the homework and exams are very difficult!

Do not take this course if you have never taken physics before because the concepts are not well explained in class whatsoever and you will need to learn everything in your own. Also a tough grader. I recommend getting a free tutor and scheduling appointments before every quiz and test.

The professor is so unsympathetic. She started out the first day saying getting bad grades is important to make you stop caring so much about them. She taught the class as if you already knew physics. The homework was difficult and you will have to self study and the quizzes and exams were even more difficult. the exams are similar to the quizes.

The physics curriculum for first year engineering is pretty similar, so most of the students have the same exams/quizzes/homework. As a lecturer, I think Professor Di Credico is really nice and passionate. She moves around a lot in the classroom and tries to keep students engaged. I really liked her class.

She was very kind and excited to teach us. She clearly knew the material and would explain things thoroughly if you asked questions. My only complaint was the frequency of the quizzes/tests due to the fact that i took it over the summer. It was a little much and made the class more difficult bc we'd get tested on material we learned the day before

Her teaching style is amazing! I love her comical real world examples. I'm really glad she breaks down the different sections of physics and tells us where certain topics go. She also writes (and keeps!) all the equations on the board.
Professor DiCredico is an amazing professor at the Physics I ILS. She gives a great review of the week's lectures, which makes quizzes seem easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Average physics prof. Explains rudimentary things clearly, however she does struggle with more advanced problems and concepts (like the ones found in the homework). However, the class still wasn't too difficult.
She is a good person, but a bad professor. She has trouble explaining concepts clearly or simply capturing the attention of her students.

The lecture is just a way for the profs to give you the equations you need.  Other than that, you'll learn absolutely nothing.  She does not go over examples and does not teach anything related to the quizzes or homework.

The main problem with her is that her lectures really are unrelated to the physics homework as well as the ILS course and lab. They are unhelpful, and a lot of the learning you do is done by yourself via textbook. This makes the class very annoying to deal with, although it isn't incredibly difficult (it's an intro class). In sum, take someone else

She is so great. I took physics 1 for engineering with her and made it so simple, because she is very organize. Keep in mind that she explains the new materials only; however, for homework, you need to keep in mind for pervious materials as well. Personally, I found her very helpful, I did not study well, but I got an A in the course thanks to her.

Had her for physics for engineering 1, shes absolutely useless at teaching physics. ended up getting through the class by going through high school physics notes. the textbook is also useless, but not as much as her. her lectures dont apply at ALL to the masteringphysics hw we have, and i end up teaching myself through google. nice person, bad prof

I found the lecture completely useless. What she taught did not line up with homework and definitely not the quizzes. Got through the class by relying on what I learned in high school physics. Attendance is required, but I found going confused me more than helped. I ended up sitting in Dunks and answering the online poling from there.
Very nice and helpful! She might be difficult to understand sometimes, but she does her best and her class is super easy. Take any physics class with her!
Really a bad teacher ever!!!! never give us a study guide before text. the classes is not clearly. moreover, no drop the lowest and no curve over the semester!! do not take her class!!

Great ILS teacher! Get her if you can!  Much better than the lecturers and actually goes over examples.  She summarizes the material well and makes sure everyone understands before moving on.  She provided an extra review session for the exam as well which turned out to be extremely useful.

DiCredico was the best ILS teacher I could have asked for. She loves teaching and always makes up her own examples for the topics and will not stop the teaching portion until everyone feels confident, though this leaves little time for Post HW. She is very accessible outside ILS and will answer emails quickly. Get her if possible!!

BEST ILS TEACHER EVER!  Seriously, if you have her for Physics 2 ILS, she is extremely helpful.  My lecture teacher (George Alverson) taught me nothing but she explains everything very well and happily answers all your questions.
she doesn't teach you what you need to pass the course. you don't have to show up to class to end up with a good grade..

She is a great lecturer, but focuses on deriving equations rather than application and problem solving. I hear she's a good ILS teacher, to show you how to DO PROBLEMS, but if you get someone else for ILS you might be screwed for the midterm and final where you have to APPLY what you learn. It's not her fault the lecture/ILS structure doesn't work.

The material is not the hardest but she cannot explain any of the concepts and she provides no examples, she makes the class more difficult than it has to be. I would pay more attention to the book, maybe go to class to see what she thinks is important so you can get an idea of what will be focused on. You may want to try to read the book.
Horrible, horrible teacher. She does not know how to explain concepts, even though she does understand it. Do not take this class.

Physics 2: lecture with allessandra is worthless. she only derives formulas and attempts to explain theory. She never uses examples or actual problems to explain anything...   However, she would be probably be good in any teaching format that DID have such examples. Like ILS or Office Hours. but maybe its just cause shes pregnant.

The material itself is not hard, however sometimes she is difficult to understand.  Has a tendency to "improvise" on the board, which is a good teaching technique, until you're midway into a problem and realized you messed the entire thing up.  My advice is to go to class, take notes at the beginning, but don't follow the examples on the board.

At first I thought she was just an okay, nice, average professor.  As time went on, I grew to really like her teaching style.  She is very good at introducing new concepts and making the class as painless as possible.  She covered everything we needed to know for the exams.  She was also very friendly and approachable.
He mostly bases his teaching in talking to the class rather than slides. There were many many readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is the first time I've enjoyed a history class. There's a lot of reading, but it's always interesting and he makes the work manageable. Lectures are extremely engaging, he can answer just about any question, and is always available for office hours. Tests are difficult and papers can be hard, but overall enjoyed the class and learned so much!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor and person. Loves teaching and cares deeply about both his students and the material

Professor Cross is so passionate about the subject of Of Princes and Utopias, making lectures extremely interesting. Only take this course if you love to read and write, the reading assignments are pretty lengthy but definitely manageable. This course is a great way to study philosophy.

Prof. Cross provided the tools to succeed while being flexible in times of need. He relates to his students as human beings, which made this process, though painful, much more enjoyable. Prof. Cross is skilled in his academic writing, and as a witty historian, "retired musician," and photography hobbyist, his knowledge spans multiple IA disciplines

This was easily one of my favorite classes I've taken so far due to Professor Cross' passion for the subject and his interesting lectures. If you're at all into history beyond what he discusses, he will have a detailed answer for your questions. Highly recommend this course and this professor.

I am so glad that I took this class. Professor Cross is easily accessible outside of class, incredibly easy to talk to, and his lectures are genuinely very interesting. His lectures are fascinating, informative, and they consist of theories from both Western and non-Western authors. Overall, if you have a chance to take this class, do so. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very nice person! Talkative and inspiring.

Cross is one of the smartest people I have ever had the privilege of learning from. He is incredibly passionate and well-researched, and truly cares about the success of his students. His lectures are engaging and thought provoking, though are often fast-paced. He holds his students to a high standard and grades you as such, but it's worth it.

Took 2 HIST courses to round out my minor. Assigns too many readings, the content of which is not necessarily tested on exams nor required to write the papers. (You do not NEED to read everything, but should get a good sense of what the course is about.) I struggled to keep up (Econ major.) Great lecturer and kind man; +readings shld be optional.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Cross's lectures were incredible and just a joy to listen to. The first textbook we used was enjoyable to read as well. There are a lot of readings and it is very difficult to make up work if you miss a class, and the entire course is graded on a midterm, a final, and two big papers. It was still definitely worth it for his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Can't lie this was the most work I put in for any class last semester. It's really reading intensive especially at the beginning. The reading can be dull sometimes but it's made a lot better by Cross' lectures. His lectures are really engaging and he's really knowledgeable. Plenty of room for discussion and really interesting class.

Overall, Prof. Cross's lectures were very interesting. It was often a combination of him teaching the historical context of each reading and a discussion about the readings. Course graded only on two papers, a midterm, and final. It is evident that he is passionate about the topic!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lecturer and reasonable grader. If you attend class frequently and do the readings you will be well prepared for the papers and tests. Definitely one of the better professors at Northeastern, who illuminates the nuance and complexity of history rather than force a distinct narrative.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Cross's class Of Princes and Utopias. The professor proved to be an amazing lecturer, aided by the fact that he seemed genuinely interested in what he was talking about. Lots of reading, but not too many assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Cross is nothing short of an amazing professor. I took him for an elective history course and was shocked by the sheer depth of his knowledge and lecturing ability. The course was graded based on two papers and two exams, but if you do the reading, attend the lecture, and attend office hours you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class was interesting, and Prof Cross was very helpful and an amazing lecturer. He is very passionate about the subject and can answer any question you ask. The exams for this class are pretty easy (2 exams), but the 2 essays are difficult. They are weird prompts and are LONG essays ( 7 pages & 10 pages MIN). A lot of work.

Even though I didn't receive an amazing grade, I loved his class. It is obvious that he loves teaching and enjoys his own class. The exams and papers were hard for me. However, I would love to have him as a professor again.

a good person but wouldnt take again. too much info info with no time to process & doesnt like questions in class. downplays the need to know dates but makes a good portion of the exam about dates. slides are useless. terrible grading system. I feel like he didn't read our final papers and just put in random grades tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cross is a decent teacher with an unclear grading scale. I thought my peers wrote better papers than mine, but I still received a higher grade. He is a nice guy though. Unfortunately, his grades just don't match the feedback he provides. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This Hurts me to say cause Professor Cross is so Nice but I didn't really learn anything in his class. All he did successfully is give me anxiety. His reading don't really help you understand the subject material. He is clearly passionate but doesn't make you excited to learn if anything he makes you excited to leave class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Professor Cross's Of Princes and Utopias course as an Honors Inquiry. He was incredibly passionate about the topic material and made all the small history details we needed to know very easy to grasp. The course centers around a bunch of philosophy readings from Ancient Greece through the Enlightenment, and you will need to read them all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Cross is one of my favorite professors. He's so clearly passionate about the subjects he teaches, and he always happy to talk to students after class regarding any questions they may have about the class content (or even about history in general). The papers and exams are difficult, but if you put in the work, you'll be fine.
good teacher and lecturer, really nice guy. tough class.

Awful. If you didn't understand something, he would have no way of explaining it differently and instead you make you feel dumb for not understanding it. Office hours were not helpful and often inaccessible. Homework took hours. Textbook was as unhelpful as his too fast lectures.
Prof. Craig's class was challenging. Material was hard to grasp, exams were harder than what was taught & homework was heavy. I suggest considering other professors before choosing this course.
He is a good professor and explains each problem by citing an example. His office hours are simply amazing.
He can't explain things clearly, class is boring, hard homework. Just terrible.
Weekly quizzes, but they're always a 1 line answer and the midterm is no harder than the homework

Prof. Maloney is a "real Math professor" who is not there to teach "Real Math". He explains numerous math methods that are helpful to model and solve any mechanical/physical/chemical/biological phenomena. Pay attention to his lectures, do homework sincerely, you will ace the exams and excel in using math as tool. Thank you, Prof. Maloney.
A REAL scientist, humble, respectful and fair.

I had a 93% for all tests + HW, weighted as per criteria he gave in the syllabus, did ok for final, and got a B, on a really easy course on Grad level Math. What's more is that I talked with a bunch of people to realise that it wasn't just me and that the other professor who taught the same course gave As for half of his class. Would not recommend
Really Easy! Took Math and he is always dancing in the class
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She was awesome! I took cultural history of Spain with her and even though the material was boring she made the class so fun
Very knowledgeable about the subject matter, I watched movies that I would have never seen unless I took this class. Super inclusive and understanding.

Cristina was such a fun and engaging professor for an otherwise potentially boring class. She took time to go over grammar which not everyone does. She is very forgiving with late work and partial credit and her class was a great experience overall. The class (SP 2102) itself can be a lot of extraneous work at times but she made it more fun!

One of the best Spanish teachers I have ever had. She makes class so fun and engaging and treats everyone with so much respect. She is super understanding with late assignments and is always available to talk. There is a lot of work but she makes it manageable and is always willing to help.

Cristina is the absolute best. She knows that SPAN 2101 is a class most kids take only because it's required, but she manages to make it so fun. You never know what to expect with her making each class very interesting. A lot of work but that's not her fault. She really cares about her students and does everything in her power to help them suceed

She is amazing so funny and every class is very interesting. She is also very understanding with turning things in late or missing class. She teaches like a drama and you learn the important cultural things not just dates and names.

SPAN 2101 is a very dense class, with lots of homework and quizzes, but Cristina makes the class as fun and interesting as possible. She is incredibly understanding and flexible when it comes to grades and due dates, and does weekly check-ins with everyone to make sure they are doing ok, would 100% take Cristina's class again

Cullen is a good prof, there are 3 tests which you don't really even have to study for, if you just paid attention to class you can get an A on every test, There are a lot of readings for homework but they aren't that bad, theres also some anime episodes/movies and other movies for homework which was cool. She is a nice person overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really nice, grades fairly, interesting, and offers good feedback.

Prof Cullen is very knowledgeable and her passion is infectious. The course consists of a few papers and 3 exams, all of them were very straightforward. Be aware that you don't watch the films in class and therefore have to watch them on your own time.

Professor Cullen is so considerate and easy to talk to. She really knows her stuff and makes lectures very interesting and relevant to students' interests. Fairly easy course with short-answer HW questions and a few papers, but you definitely learn a lot.

Professor Cullen is truly a great professor! The class is quite easy but very informative and I enjoyed every assignment we did. The homework consisted of watching anime, reading manga, and other pieces related to Japanese culture. I can confidently say I was excited to come to class every time and really took away a lot in the end!

She's an amazing teacher. I loved the class (Japanese pop culture) so much, we focused on many issues and interpretations in japanese history and modern culture. There's two short papers (2 pages ish) and two question sets (10-questions each, but you have to be concise), and one final research paper (5-6 pages). Classes are interesting

Professor Cullen is great! For CLTR1700, Cullen really knows her stuff and makes class engaging. Sometimes lectures are tied to hw assignments, but hw is really not much work. Even the question sets and essays were kind of fun! If you want an interesting, low-work class, take CLTR1700 w Cullen! Highly recommend.

Prof Cullen is very nice and she really enjoys what she teaches. The lectures and homework are super interesting, I wasn't familiar with Japan's pop culture before taking the class. She made us watch anime and read manga which was a completely new experience for me. Very interesting class with engaging papers and no exams.

She's nice, class has some really cool discussions. Tests are fair (especially since they are take home). I spent a couple hours on each paper and did well. The open-ended research paper was cool, great class to learn more about modern japan//recent history.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I got 100% on this course, very easy if you put in the effort. I don't know how difficult it usually is, but during the pandemic where exams are take-home I got 100% on both midterm and finals, although I did spend quite a bit of time on it. If you spend around 5-6 hours for each assignment you are pretty much guaranteed an A.

Prof Cullen is respected, knowledgeable, and kind-hearted. Her lectures are clear and very interesting, and I love her use of videos and real-life examples. Some of Japanese culture is weird but she handles everything very well. Her class inspired me to take a dialogue to Japan, and I felt well informed thanks to her class.

Professor Cullen gives off a "mom" vibe. She's clearly very knowledgeable about the content and going to lecture is required, but she always discusses things in a kind and interesting way. This class was interesting (I even found myself enjoying the readings we had for homework), and the exams weren't bad either. Would definitely take her again.

Prof Cullen's class was so fun and unique. I learned so much about Japan that I didn't know before, and she was so knowledgable and clearly loves what she teaches. Her tests are fair and the final presentation and paper was so fun! Keep an open mind about some of the stranger parts of Japanese culture and you'll get a lot out of this class!

Horrible, unprepared lectures, and so obsessed with in-person attendance (huge irl lecture). Developed traps to trick students about attendance (is it really that deep..) very sassy as well...10% off your grade for every absence, but attendance is also worth 10% of your grade overall ARTG 2262

Derek is really good at balancing lectures with hands-on classwork. He's not a tough grader so putting effort into your work will always yield good results. He has a lot of experience in game design so he gives very thorough feedback for projects and is really good to talk through ideas with. Overall I recommend you take a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class bc it was a requirement so it wasn't all that interesting for me. Derek is a good prof and definitely willing to help out. relatively easy grader if you just show some effort and do the assignments. I found the class a bit boring but it honestly just wasn't my thing. not his fault though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This Professor made me fall in love with game design. He was clear and if you didn't understand you could submit the wrong thing and he will let you redo it for no credit off. You either get a 100% or a 0% you just have to do the homework to get an A. It was really fun too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He taught way to slow and focused on material that was not important to tests. He never posted grades on Canvas so you never knew what your grade was. Everything he went over on review days were on the test, so that was great.

Took Stats online with Professor Curry and he was super helpful. He provides slides and his syllabus is pretty clear. Textbook/problem sets were all accessible online through Cengage and the layout was very easy to navigate. He's lenient with due dates if he knows you're actually trying.
He makes calculas fun and easy. I really enjoy his teaching methods.  He is very helpful and convenient.

Great professor and amazing lecturer. She made class very enjoyable and if you study for the tests and follow the guides everything is made easy, even the final paper and exam were ridiculously easy. Makes you want to participate more in class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Cury is the person who solidified my decision to switch from a pscyh major to international affairs. She's incredibly helpful in office hours, especially nearing exams. She loves participation, so try and speak up in class! Although there is a lot of reading for this class, she breaks it down in powerpoints. Her accent is awesome too.

Professor Cury is an excellent professor. Her enthusiasm for international affairs could not be more evident when she lectures.  Her exams aren't too bad, just study and you'll be fine. She also really encourages classroom discussion so come to class ready to participate and do the readings!!  She assigns reading quizzes throughout the semester.

In class lectures covered no content and were honestly kind of fun if you didn't think about how much you were paying for a 0 content class. She didn't really cover content & treated class time like a joke but you have way more essays/in class presentations than other ORG B sections and her grading on that extra work is harsh and not transparent.

She asks students to do a lot of stuff  but seldom provides any feedback of value. Unfortunately I did not learn one single thing from her. Often times, you can clearly tell she has no ideas what she is talking about...

Terrible class. Definitely different than any other section of it because she prides herself on her "innovative ideas." The class is basically funraising 101. You have to form a class organization, develop a hierarchy, and do a bunch of fundraisers. Papers are lengthy, attendence is mandatory..it's just too much for HRM 201. Don't take it with her!

Terrible class. Definitely different than any other section of it because she prides herself on her "innovative ideas." The class is basically funraising 101. You have to form a class organization, develop a hierarchy, and do a bunch of fundraisers. Papers are lengthy, attendence is mandatory..it's just too much for HRM 201. Don't take it with her!
No

The sweetest professor ever! He breaks down material very well, tests are pretty fair just make sure you study the slides he provides on the study guide! Class is graded on 3 tests, simulation game, and some homework assignments which are straight-forward.
Great professor truly cares about each one of his students

The sweetest professor ever and really cares about his students. He shows funny videos at the beginning of each class and is always willing to offer extra help. There was little homework and grades were based on a few assignments and tests. Tests are pretty much all memorization and a bit of math. He's the best I def recommend!!
Literally the sweetest prof. Barely any HW, three exams that make up most of your grade. Going to class is good because some info is only mentioned in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I ended up dropping this class bc I'm awful at supply chain but this man is amazing. He's the sweetest and most wholesome prof I've had at NEU. He genuinely, truly cares about his students and is always encouraging. If you like supply chain, pls take his class.

Sweetest man ever. You definitely have to go to class to do well on the exams since he verbally relays a lot of info that is not on the slides. He also definitely will like you a lot more if you attend because my grade fully got bumped up from a B+ to an A-.

Professor is a really caring guy and treats all of his students like his kids. the class is determined on three tests which is just memorizing the slides presented in class. barely any homework and its not weighted anything, definitely recommend this prof. he plays a cat video before every class its so cute
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: your grade in this class is based off of 3 tests, so don't mess one up (like I did). Other than that, it is not work heavy at all, just be sure to study hard when assessed.
Absolutely best professor! Easy, caring, flexible on deadlines. Sweetest man!

Tests are pretty much all rote memorization but pretty easy to study for since he provides the specific slides. He allows unlimited attempts on the simulation modules and there are a few extra credit opportunities. Lectures are kinda dry. It's an easy class + nice professor but I didn't learn much of anything.

Great prof OAT. Gives extra credit, only has tests + HW. Extremely kind and understanding if you talk to him outside of class he will happily help. His tests require lots of memorization but he gives you the slides to study.

Super caring, but if you're not good at memorizing I wouldn't take his class. However, he gives you unlimited attempts on the stimulation, has his own videos to help with excel problems and has review videos to follow for test days. Highly recommend going to review sessions. I feel a lot more confident with excel after taking his class.

He is the sweetest professor who wants to see everyone do well. Hes so flexible and very understanding. Tests are based on slides he provides which you have to memorize the tests are all about memorization. Homework on connect was annoying and the 4 assignments he gives are so easy on excel. Textbook was not needed. Really sweet guy I recommend

Professor Eroglu is one of the most caring, kindhearted professors I've had at Northeastern. He teaches in a lecture format and explains everything very clearly with good examples. He gives humane breaks for my 3-hour class period, during which he usually plays funny cat videos. His class was very interesting and he will be missed next semester!

Such a wholesome professor. Started off each lecture with a cat video, and was an extremely fair grader. The only issue I have with him is he was useless in office hours when I went to review my exams he didnt really explain what I was struggling with and told me to look at his slides at home. But class time with him was good.

Such a sweet man! Provided daily cat videos, super flexible on deadlines & will work with you to make anything better for you and your schedule. I would 100% take him again. The assignments are designed to help you learn excel & the sims are hard but after enough attempts you can def get them! overall love him!
The absolute sweetest man. So helpful and genuinely wants you to succeed. Would 100% take him again.
So easy to follow along. He explains absolutely everything. Very flexible with deadlines!
He is the best professer
Not too much work, but the Connect assignments are time consuming. Detailed lectures, but spends too much time explaining one concept. There are 2 midterms and 1 exam, which were all 30 minutes long.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most caring/nicest professor at NEU and genuinely wants the best for everyone. The test are very multiple choice heavy, which is not my thing but I was able to do alright by just making flashcards of the slides he told us to study. Very accessible outside of class and would recommend going to his office hours before exams. Would def recommend

I took this class only to fulfill my business course requirements but was blown away with the Professor's way of teaching and caring for his students! I highly recommend to take him in all possible supply chain-related classes. Professor Eroglu wants you to succeed so if you put enough effort and seek help you will have a good grade!

Cuneyt Eroglu is a very kind and helpful professor. He genuinely wants students to get a high grade. The course is by itself very heavy on memorizing definitions and concepts. Be aware you will have to memorize and know lots fo concepts. Final exam was not cumulative. I would recommend taking the Supply chain with him!

Cuneyt is one of the kindest, most caring professor I've ever met. He uploads all the slides and lets you know exactly what slides are going to be on the exam. His lectures can be a bit boring and it's not the easiest class at Northeastern, but I've never met a professor who cares more about his students than Cuneyt. Take his class, it's worth it!!
Cuneyt is a great professor! goes over relevant material on exams and the course material itself isnt too hard either so I definitely had an enjoyable experience in supply chain.

Follows the syllabus given. Teaches very well. Very kind and helpful to students. Always accessible and gives feedback. Brings in distinguished speakers from the industry to interact with. Lightens up the mood by playing a silly youtube video. Emphasizes on real-trend, practical metrics happening in supply chain industries. Tools: SAS, Excel

The BEST nicest professor out there he is so cute he always plays little youtube videos at the start of class and is an all around nice guy! the class itself was pretty hard but he is very helpful and understanding. best professor at neu.
He is the nicest prof in the class. He will help you if you need.

Professor Eroglu is the sweetest guy I've ever been taught by. By far the easiest SCHM class at NEU. No need to come to class, just memorize the powerpoint slides he gives you and you'll ace the exams. 4 easy assignments, 5 easy simulations and 3 exams (final not cumulative). 10/10 recommend!

I took him for transportation. But the reason you do well or not isn't because of attendance or how much you actually learn about supply chain its because the test's are more like random trivia then what he actually tells you is on the test or is covered in the pointless classes. I've gotten A's in all other supply chain classes but his.

Nicest Prof in Northeastern, absolutely recommended. Make sure to study the slides  well and you'll be more than fine for the exams. NO: group projects, mandatory attendance, or participation! A few out-class assign and game simulation. Also, buying the book is a waste of money.

Extremely helpful and nice guy always started class off with a youtube video to brighten up an 8am class.  Really is accommodating when it comes to making up a test would really recommend him as a professor.

I love this professor! He is hilarious and charismatic, and truly helps students if they don't want help. He's not a very hard teacher either. I would definitely recommend him if you love the topic. SCHM is naturally boring, but he really made it so much more interesting.
One of the best professors! So passionate and makes the topic exciting (for supply chain management). Recommended!

Prof Eroglu is passionate about the subject and has a great deal of experience. He is also committed to his students and truly wants everyone to succeed. If you are struggling, he will help you. This class is NOT boring! It is designed to teach the fundamentals of the subject and it does just that. Prof. Eroglu makes it very fun & interactive!
Seriously THE nicest guy ever. So understanding and passionate about his teaching. Would definitely reccommend him!
Nice guy, easy grader.  Two homework assignments and three exams.  Exams composed of about 50 mc and a few short answers. Class is mostly taught by powerpoint and through videos.

Funny professor, tries to make a boring class interesting. He has the worst grades distribution, 40% on MT & 60% on the final, THAT'S IT!! He gives some extra credit points for classes with low attendance.
Very easy class. Very nice guy. Relies heavily on power points for in-class lectures. Attendance is not mandatory. If you study the slides closely before each exam, you will do fine.
Talks about a lot of things but the course. Appears to be nice but grades poorly. Gives poor advices that leads to bad grades. Shows a funny video before every class. Very boring otherwise.

Supply Chain Mgmt/ Logistics. Knows A LOT and talks A LOT about what he knows. Fair enough. The class is fun if you participate otherwise it's a lot of listening. Easy class but pay attention when it comes to Excel. Ask exactly what he expects and this will be a successful class for you.

Hes an easy teacher, a "nice guy", but classes are boring. He relies way too much on powerpoint (google death by powerpoint) He should include less stuff in his powerpoints and try to use the chalkboard more. Other than that, hes really easy.

Easy class - great teacher! He knows that operations is an easy class and he sets up the course in that way. Quizzes are easy, final is a mash of all quizzes, but be careuful on the assignment (tricky). Gives 100% on participation. If you want to get an A,definitely take him!

This was an online course for me, and I still can say she is horrible. She is VERY rude, petty, not willing to help struggling students. Her grading has no rubric and seems like she hands out grades based on how she's feeling. Does not keep her politics out of class. Made us buy a textbook, yet never uses it. Also says "so forth and so on"- What?

I really enjoyed the class. There are quizzes every week based on the lecture from the week before but don't worry, as long as you paid attention, the quizzes are easy. She gives the midterm and final but if you paid attention, attended, class, and took notes you'll do fine. She does give several extra credit opportunities over the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I am an A student. Rarely have I had issues with professors. However, this class and teacher had me pulling out my hair. First of all her grading system as it's setup is confusing and leaves no room for error. I would expect a teacher to sympathize with her students, rather she is apethetic. She is very petty.

Veronica was definitely interested in her students and the subject matter (Comparative Politics). She was well prepared for all classes and clearly put time into her lessons. The only drawback of her class would be her grading. Exam style needs some revision and she doesn't provide much help with preparation for the exams (no study guides!)

Veronica is very smart and knowledgable but she expects a lot out of her students, sometimes a little too much. She is great to deal with one on one however, so highly suggest going to her office hours. Take notes during class because she gives no study guide and does not make ppts available. She is a great person, tough grader. Overall she is good

Research Methods:Terrible course. It should be understood that this course is rather dry and can feel a bit redundant. She did not help with this. Extremely rude and condescending. She could not have cared less about our concerns. She instead would use class time to recruit for her dialogue and occasionally redefine terms she had previously defined
She is a hard grader, sarcastic and condescending TA. She laughs at every bad joke Prof. Urman says in class. Yelled at a student because he was using his phone.
I really liked Veronica! She was really funny and relatable, and was very well-informed. I enjoyed having her as my TA.
Definitely very nice and very helpful!  She made things much clearer, and was always willing to talk and explain topics.

TA/Recitation for Comp Politics. Very nice & helpful w/ papers. Opinionated, but entertaining and open-minded. Helped clarify lectures & gave additional information through article readings. Gives little handouts at the end of recitation w/a bunch of random info - so funny! I fully recommend her!
Very petty, she will take points off of your average for any silly reason.  She will never admit that she is wrong even if she directly contradicts the book.
She would always hand out Chapter Outlines which definitely helped me understand the subject matter a whole lot more. Great teacher and is always there to help if you ask.
She is amazing.

She was a pretty good professor. The entire semester I thought I was in perfect shape and then bam there came the final which was terrible. Still maintained about a 93% in the class overall in terms of points but somehow that ended up being a B+ by her calculations? I know there is a curve but I don't think it should be detrimental...

Cynthia was probably my favorite professor my first semester here at Northeastern. She understand the material she teaches and makes everything really clear. If you pay attention in class you get an A, if you don't, you get a C. But overall, incredible professor.

The class itself is not too hard, as long as you read the early chapters in the book and you make an effort to pay attention and participate in class. She is very helpful and is one of those professors that will answer specific questions on the test. Highly recommend for all people taking accounting.
Good Professor!!

Jackson is a pretty good teacher. If you show interest and participate in class, she is more than willing to work with you to help you out. Like the other comments, she is prone to make mistakes, but in my opinion it is nothing major. My only complaint is that the TA grades the majority of the work, not her. Also book is barely/if at all needed.

She makes mistakes a lot, but if you put in the time the class isn't too bad. She is the nicest woman I have ever met and LOVES accounting. She is more then willing to help. Definitely recommend her, but the class does require some work.

Professor Jackson wants to be helpful, but she really has no idea what she is doing.
