In class he like to make it entertaining by laughing at his own jokes etc. The content is cool, and he makes it very understandable. I did not have to spend a lot of time outside of class doing work. Would def recommend him to anyone taking this course.
THE GOAT! Take this class you will not be disappointed. So caring and easy to reach outside of class.

GILLEN IS MY GOAT! 

Perhaps one of the most forgiving professors I've had at Northeastern yet, and is available very frequently outside of class. Most of your grade in GE1501 is determined by your projects, so as long as you don't slack off and leave your teammates in the dust there's nothing to worry about. 

Would take his classes again!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very nice and caring. Lectures are interesting, and homework is not hard at all.

Professor Gillen was the best professor I've had for 2 semesters of my college life. He'll give you homework due every Sunday and some classes have these simple homework for the night of, but it is never that challenging. He cares for his students so much and is willing to listen to everybody and their struggles. You're lucky if you're his student.
Great professor. Puts in the work to make the lectures super engaging and is honestly a great guy. He makes. a lot of sense. Would recommend.

Dr. Gillen is great. He is a fairly easy grader but cares about his student's success. Group projects can be long a broad but you are offered a good amount of feedback on them. There are no exams in this class and the HW does not usually take too long each week. Info presented in class is usually helpful and Dr. Gillen is very accessible outside.

Super nice guy -- always willing to help students outside of class. Class can be somewhat difficult for people without CS or AutoCAD experience but Dr. Gillen provides great recourses. The only complaint I have is group projects -- if you're put with a lazy group you end up doing ALL the work. Other than that it's fun class taught by a chad prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love Professor Gillen. His class is always super welcoming and he clearly cares for his students. Hes very helpful with homework assignments and in class activities. The group projects are kinda broad which can be difficult, but not bad at all.

Gill's the man. Very chill, plays music in class while we do work, and sometimes plays games w the class like labeling memes, etc. He is v knowledgable and is able to explain something when you ask him. Always encouraging and very supportive. The homework isn't bad at all. It's doable and group projects are kinda fun. Overall nice and awesome guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor, the only thing I concern is to get an A, you need to get 95/100, which is higher than other courses. But the course itself is pretty easy.

Professor Gillen is one of the best professors I have had at NU. He is clear and easy to understand, his lectures are engaging, and the group projects are fun. He is also extremely willing to help students outside of class and wrote several recommendations for me.

He is good teacher that does really care about his students. He is extremely easy, especially when compared to other cornerstone teachers. You may not learn all the material quite as well as you would in other class just because of how easy the work is, but in the end it doesn't really matter.

Professor Gillen was great. He knows the material and can answer questions; if he is ever unsure, he is completely honest. Lectures are interactive and engaging. He allows time in class to begin homework assignments, and the lectures correlate well to the knowledge you need to complete the homework. No complaints.
Good professor. The class is pretty easy if you just pay attention and do your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: professor douglass is a super nice guy, he makes jokes in class, and he is overall really genuine. all lectures are posted, it isnt that hard of the class, it is weekly canvas quizzes, 2 midterms and a final.

He cares about his students and always takes time to ask how everyone is doing. Class is very lecture heavy, if you don't show up it will be confusing because he often explains past what is on his slides. I recommend him 100% if you are an ESS major, great introductory course to the subject. Tests/weekly quizzes are not hard if you study!

The exams for this course is literally harder than OOD. They are much harder than what a 1000 level course should be. Don't know why he believes a good class average is a 83% when the this is a science elective for most.

DO NOT RECCOMEND!! this class was easily the worst decision I've made so far at northeastern. I found the professor to be nice but the exams and homeworks are quite excessive/difficult for a 1000 level course. I should have dropped this class as soon as one of the first days he said that the average grade for an intro class was a c+ or b-.

RUN. Took this class as an env sci elective, thought it would be a fairly easy introductory class but Dr Douglass has decided to dig too deep into the content, as if we're all aspiring climatologists. This class is solely the reason why I'm switching out of ESS in the fall :/

Avoid. For an introductory earth sciences class, Dr Douglass makes it really hard. Study guides before exams aren't very useful as exams are all application-based, and often times there are misunderstandings in questions, due to which he needs to adjust everyone's grade. Wouldn't take again, and this class is why I switched out of env science.

I was a business major taking this for NUPath and as a class I don't recommend it for others taking it for a similar reason. Though, Professor Douglass was super awesome. I was struggling a bit at the beginning of the course but I showed up to his office hours and he was super helpful. Class is only graded on tests and quizzes though which is tough

AMAZING PROFESSOR! Definitely one of the best at NU. His lectures are funny and super helpful. Although the tests and the quizzes can be very hard at times, the content aligns with what is on the test. Overall awesome professor as we cares about the topic as well as the students!

Awesome professor! Lectures were never boring and were always very fun to do. Weekly quizzes and 3 exams determined your grade. Exams were extremely difficult and felt very trick-ish at times and since they were such a   big part of the grade, they caused a lot of anxiety. However, professor Douglass was very nice so I would recommend taking him.

Easily the best professor I have ever had in college. I took two classes with him, a year apart, and it is clear he is a very talented professor who is passionate about the material he is teaching. He gives the best lectures at NEU. His exams are pretty difficult, but he is a very fair grader, especially when it comes to assignments and projects.

Professor Douglass was great. His lectures are engaging and funny; he made a 100-student lecture feel like a small class. He is extremely knowledgeable about the subject area, and if he is ever unsure how to answer a question, he is honest about the limitations of his knowledge. No complaints.

Way too much information for an NUpath class. Just reads off slides and homework assignments are not beneficial. Test questions are difficult and even if you follow study guide, it does not help much because the questions are application based. If you have the choice, take another Gen Ed requirement.

Dan is an amazing professor who I'm very lucky to have had twice. He cares so much about his students and makes sure no one is ever behind. Passionate and knowledgeable about climate change as well as very accessible outside of class. Lots of dad jokes woven into lectures are a big plus. Take his class!

Professor Douglass was always accessible and willing to work with students. There wasn't too much homework and studying was just a normal amount. His lectures were interesting and he made an effort to engage students

He is a nice guy and understand the material well, but the NUFlex class with him is not engaging at all. He lectures off of 10 slides for over an hour and occasionally sprinkles in a breakout room. Not dynamic or discussion based at all. Very test heavy. Does not really exude any passion in studying or fighting climate change.

Douglass is super sweet and enthusiastic. He loves what he's teaching and cares for his students. His classes are just lecture but he also records them in case you miss a class. The classes are graded on weekly quizzes and 3 exams. He always answers questions and emails right away. Pretty cool guy.
He's a really great professor. But the course has a lot of homework. You need to go to class and take good notes. Definitely not a course to get an easy A.
really great teacher, even though his classes are mostly lectures he finds ways to make them engaging. Always cracking jokes

Just have to pay attention, be present and take notes in class to get a good grade. Dan keeps things interesting and also records all of his lectures and posts them online, though I hardly ever needed to use them. Cares a lot about his students and tests were very fair.

Professor Douglass is the best. His lectures are really thorough and all you need to study from. The weekly quizzes are an easy grade booster and his tests are fair with only a few tricky questions. He's quick to return emails and always wants people to come to his office hours. Take his class :)

All together wonderful. Thorough lectures, but sometimes the wording can be poor. Best professor I've had so far. He's always super interested in what he teaches, and he actually made me excited to learn about geology. And if you love dad jokes, you're in for a treat.

Dan is probably one of the best professors I'll have. He's extremely helpful and super accessible outside of class. The course content was super easy, but he would make a few of the questions tricky on tests, which can add up. There are only 2 tests and a final, so there's not really any room to mess up, but just study and you'll do great

Love him! Super nice and love his dad jokes. All lectures on tegrity so not really necessary to show up but I loved this class, really interesting (although first half was way more interesting than last half). there were 9 homework assignments, pretty easy just making graphs and analysing. 3 exams all MC. Highly recommend this class! Very easy.

Professor Douglass is one of those rare professors who understands that complications happen outside of the classroom, and is willing to assist you to get the best grade possible. He genuinely cares about his students and is enthusiastic about the course. One of the best professors at Northeastern.

One of my favorite professors in my 5 years at NEU. He is very knowledgeable and his passion for the environment is obvious during every lecture. He makes class interesting and accessible for non-science majors. Always willing to work with students to make sure they're learning and successful in his class. Super nice guy and sneakily hilarious!

Dan Douglass is by far one of my favorite professors at Northeastern. He makes learning anything about the environment so fun and engaging. He pours his whole heart into lectures and making himself available. He just wants to see everyone succeed and crack a few jokes about Ghostbusters, Spinal Tap, and any other references your parents would get.

One of the nicest most accessible and caring professors out here at Northeastern. Ensures each student is able to do well and is extremely passionate about what he teaches. Would definitely take any class he's teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Roth is very straightforward. Tests are completely based on power point lectures, don't even bother reading/ memorizing the textbook, you won't need it. He occasionally gives "surprise lectures" which show up on the exams. Although he goes really fast, attending lectures is the biggest tip to passing this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Douglass made a seemingly dull subject (rocks) my absolute favorite class. He was passionate and funny (be prepared for dad humor) but did not force students who clearly didn't wanna be there to care. Attendance was not mandatory and he records all his lectures and uploads them. I would take any class Professor Douglass taught.

Professor Douglass loves geology and it is obvious in his teaching.  He does his best to make class interesting to students and he has very clear ways of explaining processes that make the information easy to understand.  I needed to take this class for my major and didn't think I would be that into it but it was my favorite class this semester.

An amazing Professor. His gives a lot of quizes but they're on blackboard and you can use the class' notes to take them, which he posts after each lecture. There is a final essay, which you would work on while the semester goes on. He is very interesting, creative, smart and funny which helps endure a 3 and half hour lecture. I would recommend him.

An amazing teacher! Super nice, funny, helpful and lovable. No attendence, all classes are recorded and available in tegrity. No homeworks. 10 online quizzes (lowest grade dropped, 2 tests and 1 final. No need for textbook if you pay attention and take notes in class.
Funny, kind, helpful, passionate and overall very lovable. Only problems: handwriting/spelling, confusing notes, confusing wording on tests/quizzes.

Douglass is an awesome professor. He's super nice and helpful. Went to his office hrs every week; failed both midterms but A on the final so got a B - and I have no interest in science. 3 tests, 10 online quizzes, no assignments. Textbook is useless. Work hard and you'll do well.

Tried extremely hard in his class... went to all lectures, saw him at office hours every week... but tests do not cover the material in class and are poorly worded. He tries to help but his tests are unfair.
Great Professor. Pretty much favorite class that semester. If you go to class, you'll do fine without a lot of effort. No assignments, only 10 online quizzes and 3 exams

if you show up to class and take notes, your golden. no need for the textbook. 3 tests that with a little studying you'll do fine. 10 online quizes that are a breeze. def likes to help his students so take this class

Global Climate Change was a really accessible science class, and Douglass is one of the best professors I've had.  Understanding, interesting, passionate, clear, available (for student appointments), and funny.  Great professor.

loves what he does and loves teaching about it. enthusiastic and very helpful if you don't understand something. you probably won't need the book, but it's a good backup if you miss anything. definitely recommend him.
Great guy, likes to make corny jokes and then laugh at them. hardly went to class and still made it out with an A-
Great teacher. I hate environmental science, but Douglass made it extremely easy and bearable. Went to class about 50% of the time and still made out with an A. Very nice guy.

took him for global climate change. weekly online quizzes. not too hard. barely used book, very interesting and doesn't shove global warming down your throat, only talked about that last part of class and he admitted there was a lot to learn about it....great guy
Certainly one of the better professors I've had. Clear, helpful, enthusiastic, non-mandatory attendance, and he has sense of humor. High fives all around for Douglass.
He is a very nice, cool guy but tends to be unclear on homework and test questions. Tests are easy if you study and go to class. NO need to buyt the book (I did not open it once!!!)

Professor Douglass is an amazing professor!! If you can take a class with him- don't second guess it for a minute. He is also helpful outside of the classroom- friendly, approachable, and, I must say, adorable! I wish every class could be taught by this professor- I cannot say enough about him.

Excellent prof. Quizes and exams are fair and he gives practice exams to work on. His notes are excellent. DO NOT buy the book unless you want it for ref or if youre a geo maj. You dont need the book bc of his notes. Go to class though so you get the notes. This is one of the best classes ive taken. You will learn a lot and retain useful info.

Awesome Professor!Class is very interesting and isn't too hard as long as you pay attention. Douglass is an amazing guy, very kind and helpful...not too bad on the eyes either ;) I loved this class, and recommend taking it.
Just about as easy as it gets, while still teaching the information well. Exams and quizzes are very fair.

Dynamic earth. great prof & really nice outside of the classroom. definitely approachable if you dont understand something and hes more than happy to explain anyhting. tests are catered to whats mentioned in class, never opened the book. basics and fundamentals to geology and helps you in other geology classes!

Really nice guy, fair grader, I have zero complaints.  You don't need the textbook, but make sure you go to class and take notes.  I only took Dynamic Earth for the science requirement, but if I were actually into geology I'd take another class with him in a second!

Douglass is a good professor, I never even read the textbook, put in an average amount of effort and I got a B so it isn't that hard.  Make sure you attend class, his notes are really good and help a lot and w/o you will not be a happy camper!  Remember to take the online quizzes and go see him for extra help...

If you put in the effort you'll do fine.  He is an excellent teacher and gives the best notes.  I hardly needed to look at the book at all.  We had a weekly quiz and then the exams.  Interesting class, even for non-majors
I thought the class was going to be boring, but it was quite exciting. The prof was very nice and helpful. You just have to read the chapters and come to class to get the notes.

Like with any class, you get what you put into it. If you do the work it's not hard to get an A. There is never any question about what to study and the exams are extremely fair. He also encourages people to come to his office at any time and knock. However sometimes the analogies about topics are too abundant. Oh and the textbook was awesome.

definately not an easy A, but he is fair - IF you try you can do well. he is super enthusiastic and seems to like teaching a lot, he will help you a lot if you go to office hours. geology isn't my thing, but he made it at least a little interesting.
horrible professor...boring and hard.

Worst professor I have ever had. Boring and hard. First year teaching, so decides to hand out IMPOSSIBLE exams, 9 chapters at a time, on useless specific information. Class average on mid term was 72. DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY...BIG MISTAKE IF YOU DO!!!!

He is an extremely nice person but a difficult professor to handle as a CS major. It was difficult to keep pace with this class especially since he assumed a lot of us had prior knowledge. The tests were unnecessarily hard and the scores were not curved. To give credit where due though, he did curve the final grade a lot so in the end, it was ok.

I took EECE 2322 (couldn't select the course) as a requirement for my major. I did not enjoy his teaching style and he is infamously known for his difficult tests. The exams were not curved, however the final grades were curved quite heavily. I went to office hours frequently and found him helpful at times, yet at times it was hard to keep up.

He wasn't bad. I look back and feel like he did set me up for future classes. However, the pacing sucked. It's supposed to be a class for beginners in Python, but it felt like you had to have prior experience otherwise you fell behind. Assignments got graded late and the tests were hard. If you had to take him, it's not bad but you could do better.

Although he is a nice person, I did not enjoy his teaching & grading style. I was very enthusiastic in the beginning & would regularly go to office hours. Midterms were almost impossible (5% of what we took in class & assignments came). Didn't enjoy what I was learning & was very unhappy with my overall grade, given my dedication & persistence.

He's a great professor - if you're pre-law.  The course is very discussion heavy, but there is only one grade for the total number of discussions.  He doesn't provide much feedback.  If you ask for ways to improve, he is unlikely to respond.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class and the subject matter. You will read the entire textbook, weekly discussions, a paper and 2 exams. He also has amazing lectures to steer you in the right direction. Very accessible and responds quickly to questions. If you do the work, you will learn and will get a good grade. Make sure to join his lectures.

Not many assignments, but he's EXTREMELY picky about his requirements. He will message/inbox you until he gets what he wants from you. His instructions are not very clear. Be prepared to overwhelm by his inbox messages!!!!! He is obsessed with canvas messaging.
Constant lecture - nothing really related to marketing - just a bunch of random stuff for an hour and a half.

Really nice prof but bad grading. You will get a 3.5/4 no matter what you do. Your entire grade is determined by the final project and participation. He says attendance is not mandatory but it counts towards participation and if you get a B in that you will get a B overall. I don't feel like I learned anything I didn't already know.

Take home chapter (30 pages each) quizzes before almost every class. He likes super outgoing students, so SIT IN THE FRONT. He tells everyone "speak up!" "I can't hear you" constantly, makes it hard to participate then harshly grades participation. Lectures are summary of chapters, repetitive. Easy concepts but do not recommend this prof.

JUST SHOW UP AND YOU WILL BE FINE. This class is not difficult as long as you participate in class and show up for daily attendance. He is a nice guy, as you show interest in what he is teaching. Grading can be a little unclear, but overall, it's great. Do not question your grade because it will not change. You get what you get.

Every week we had a quiz based on the last chapter we read and it is open note and at home, basically just homework. Our mid-term and final were the same thing, only he was more strict with grading the final. We had a group project, but we were graded on our presenation and not the project itself. I would recomemnd this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Easiest class I've had at northeastern. Class was cancelled like half the time as well. Only thing that is “hard” is participation but if you speak once a class it's fine. Would recommend to anyone who isn't a marketing major!

Easiest professor. All quizzes are online and open note. Grade is determined by one simulation project. You don't have to do good on the simulation, you just have to have a good presentation. If you participate a LOT in class, he will like you. Sit in the front, and laugh at his jokes. If you actually want to learn marketing, don't take him.

Easy A. Durant wants everyone to do well, and half the time he cancels class or lectures super quickly and lets you out early. Class consists of weekly quizzes (online, not lockdown), a group project, and an easy exam. He is lazy and it is boring, but it's very light and easy. He also seems experienced which is a plus.
Disaster. Cancels any class, whenever he wants to, and provides an unworthy excuse. However, for students, he does not excuse absences and is extremely strict. Not caring

Great professor who knows his stuff and has an infectious personality. I thoroughly enjoyed the majority of his lectures. The class is merely matching deep thinking common sense and buzzwords. Assignments are easy to follow and easy to do. He's a great professor who cares about his students future. Take him, take him, and take him. You won't regret

Graded by a few things for sure. Rob makes this class very easy. There's no taste, but there are home (non lockdown) quizzes on each chapter. Do well on those, understand basic concept, you are going to be just alright. There is one group project, ace that, you don't have to worry.

Professor Durant is one of the most unprofessional professor I've had during my time in Northeastern. He doesn't explain the concepts well in class and seems uninterested in teaching. His motto is "I want you to fail" and he takes that too literally making it impossible to get an A; hard A-. Not a good grader too, very subjective grading.

Thought this would be an easy class at first, but he quickly became passive aggressive as people did not participate/slacked off. Instead of correcting this, he would give very low grades on the few graded assignments (THE CLASS HIGH WOULD BE UNDER 90). It's hard to imagine how anyone could've ended with an A. Did not learn much. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: do not take this professor! his lectures are very boring, and is a harsh grader for participation. the highest participation grade was 85%. easy class in the beginning, but refuses to give full credit on the presentation/paper at the end of the semester. you have no control over your grade

Honestly he was a very lazy professor. He was funny at first, but his lectures are so boring. No one participates and instead of trying to fix the issue, he just has the kids present the slides to each other. Also he doesn't hold students accountable in group projects. I ended up doing all the work for my group but not the grade to reflect my work.
Easiest class in the business school and the best marketing professor. His grading is so light and he wants you to succeed. He is a professor you want to take for marketing no matter what.

Super easy A. Not a very interesting class because he basically just reads the chapter summary during class. To do well in this class, make sure you do well on the weekly online quizes, take the marketplace simulation seriously, and participate in class. You don't really have to ever read the actual chapter, just go to the chapter summary.

At first, I thought this class was going to be the easiest class I ever took at Northeastern and quite frankly it was. But he switched up really fast. His lectures are boring and consist solely of fluff. I didn't learn a thing in his classes. Assignments were pretty easy. But participation and attendance are mandatory.

He's great at the start... don't take him if you actually want to learn marketing. His classes are extremely mandatory, or your grade will drop to a 15%. Little homework and his lecture provided absolutely nothing, but he made the class easy to pass... unless you don't participate or show up. No midterm and the final is a joke (one page paper).

Course was very boring and repetitive.  Did not actually learn anything important and the professor was not understanding.  Put over 80% of the grades in during the last week and the highest participation grade was an 85%.  Do not take if you actually want to learn anything and have actual control over your grade.

Very easy but also very boring. Grades were put in at the end and he was kind of harsh especially with stuff like the presentation and participation. If you're a marketing concentration and looking for an informative and exciting introduction to your major -- this isn't it. If you're looking for an easy A to knock out a requirement -- this is it.
Great class, informative lectures, very passionate. Only negative is attendance is mandatory

This class is hard. There is nothing wrong with the professor himself, the curriculum is what is stacked against you. Dransfield is a good teacher that seems to get a bad rep from these reviews. He is always willing to answer questions, explain things further, and is a very generous grader. He gives you everything you need to succeed in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield did everything he could to make it possible to get a good grade in this notoriously difficult class. He  is a very intelligent guy and great lecturer, he records the lectures daily, gives partial credit on multiple choice questions, and was great with curves. If you need to take chem1151, Dransfield is EASILY the best choice

Dr. Dransfield is extremely knowledgeable in his field (Got his phd in atmospheric thermochemistry from harvard) and his incredible talents are almost wasted on first year chemistry. He is a great lecturer and will debate chemistry or quantum mechanics with you all day if you want. Highly recommended for motivated students who want to learn.

This professors class was good but he talked really fast which made it hard for me to learn. He's very passionate about chem but when you don't know what's happening, he has a tendancy to make you feel silly.

My biggest advice is to study and practice problems ALL THE TIME. He did an amazing job all semester. I received a bad grade because I did not adapt to the class's difficulty quickly enough. He gives you a ton of resources and support to do well. He's a stickler for participation, so come to class with a good understanding of the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Any bad ratings from here are really outdated, because Dransfield was the GOAT. He's both energetic in lectures and easy to approach afterwards and is willing to help out anyone who shows up to office hours. Grades were curved a lot too, to the point where the average grade in the class was like a low A-.

Bad ratings for this professor are cope. This guy is the first professor at the school that I've noticed genuinely cares about his students academically and emotionally.He is disgustingly educated and a great teacher.He emphasizes LEARNING.Try your best, do what he advises you to do, and you will get an A. I didn't get an A cos I didn't listen.

I don't get all the bad ratings. Prof. Dransfield was a great professor, he explained concepts very well. The content was challenging and tests were very difficult, but he gave partial credit on multiple choice, curves were generous, and offered extra credit opportunities. If you put in the work and attend his office hours, an A is very attainable.
i always hoped the T broke down so i had a reason to miss the class and avoid hearing him yell throughout the whole lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic professor, his lectures are super helpful. Participate in class, he's more likely to help your grade if he knows you. People that don't like him just don't pay attention, I got a 64 and 71 on 2 of the 4 exams and still ended up with an A- so I hope that helps! He scales too and provides a bunch of different resources for practice.
not helpful at all. very test heavy and wouldn't let me take a day off for recitation WHICH IS A ZERO CREDIT COURSE because i had the flu.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is great at teaching and if you put the work in you can do well in this class -- even if you hate/suck at chemistry. Although, at times he can be a little belittling and rude but he also knows what kind of student he is talking to. Sometimes you will hate his class, but in the end he was a great teacher for a fast paced and difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: awesome guy. he is very enthusiastic which makes the class better. lots of content, but as long as you really try to apply yourself + understand content you'll be okay (exams curved + extra credit). he's also super understanding and helpful, but can come off as blunt or sarcastic (he means well).

Prof Dransfield is honestly one of the best professors I've had. At first he might be intimidating but if you ever go to one of his office hours you'll see he's always ready to help and knows how to explain concepts clearly. He's the best lecturer but note taking can be hard so just make sure you do that after each class. Work hard you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great guy and a super engaging lecturer. Raise your hand as much as you can, and don't take it personally if he says you're wrong. Lots of scare tactics at the beginning, but if you keep up with his material, it is very doable. The negative comments are understandable but blown a little out of proportion

Absolutely never take this professor. He is possibly the rudest man I have every met in my life. I do so much and nothing works. I went to office hours and he just told me I was dumb and needed help. WHAT DO U THINK IM THERE FOR SIR. I literally cried after and slightly in front of him and got no apology

I found Dransfield's class to be quite engaging, even from the perspective of a student who doesn't like chemistry. He was funny, caring, and made class fun. I would take him if you have the choice for chem professors.
Maybe the worst professor you will ever have, especially as a first year. He will berate you for asking simple questions, shame you for having a life outside of class and makes an
Single handedly the worst professor I ever had or

Professor Dransfield is a very engaging lecturer who is clearly passionate about what he does. Not sure why there are so many comments about him being condescending he might chuckle a bit if you say something silly but don't take him so personally. Gen chem here is two semesters fit into one so its a lot of work but the curve is generous.
He is clearly passionate about what he does but he's very demeaning and makes you feel terrible when you ask questions. Hard tests too.

Professor Dransfield works hard for students to understand the material, not to memorize. Exams were very difficult, but he does prepare you well for them. I strongly recommend attending all lectures and his office hours. He is more than happy to go over difficult concepts.

CHEM 1161 is notoriously tough. His exams are challenging, but if you apply yourself it is possible to do well. I'd recommend him as a prof to anyone who asked. He's a great guy. Don't be scared by any low ratings. If you show effort and grit, he'll help you get to the finish line. Best prof I've ever had hands down

He made me hate learning. 10% of your grade is attendance taken off a chemistry problem on the info you just learned. If you get it wrong you only get .5 attendance for the day. It's a hard class. He thinks it's fun to create the most difficult test possible. I could write a paper on how bad he was. If you have the option pick another professor!!

This guy cares and wants you to succeed. That being said, he needs to cram a lot of material into a very short time. It will be tough, but Dransfield knows what he's doing. His PhD is from Harvard in Atmospheric thermochemistry and he also does interesting research. Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He loves his scare tactics. Be prepared for him to tell you you should drop the class; honestly, don't listen. With how he curves, it will be easy to get a b- or above if you do all the homework and attend recitation. He can seem harsh, but he cares about what he teaches. His tests are just incredibly hard and hard to prepare for. But he's good

Dransfield didn't make the class difficult, curriculum crams a lot of info into a semester, so we moved fast. Funny, explained topics very well, and ensured frequent office hours, especially closer to exams (I recommend these). Find the textbook online for free. You don't need it to do well if you took AP. Records lectures, so you can review notes.

Funny and engaging lectures, probably the best part of the class. He answers questions, but often runs behind in his plan for the lecture. However, he likes to put ambiguous questions on the multiple-choice section and makes you guess between two answer choices. This is especially annoying since the final exam is entirely multiple-choice questions.

Great lecturer and he cares about what he does, but he can be VERY condescending. Asking questions is a coin toss between getting an actual answer and being made to feel stupid for even asking it. Test averages are usually terrible but he heavily curves
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dransfield didn't make the class difficult, curriculum crams a lot of info into a semester, so we moved fast. Funny, explained topics very well, and ensured frequent office hours, especially closer to exams. Find the textbook online for free because you don't need it to do well if you took AP chem. Records lectures, so you can review notes.

I think Dransfield does a great job making chem interesting. I really liked chem and I attribute that almost entirely to Dransfield himself. That being said, he has a tendency to come off as condescending to students that ask questions that may seem obvious. If you show interest, he is willing to put in time outside of class to ensure you succeed.

If you didn't take AP Chem in hs, prepare to struggle. If you're honors/not ChemE, I would recommend avoiding taking his class for the honors credit. Interesting class, but dented my GPA. He moves fast, covers topics even outside the curriculum, and hw/recitation problems were much (purposefully) easier than the midterms/final. Be cautious.

Professor Dransfield was overall a great professor. I didn't take AP Chem so I was a little nervous. It is great that he curves the exams A LOT (about 10-20%) and the final as well. I had a B for most of the class but after recitation was added and the final, I ended with an A-. I would recommend him. It is not easy but he is ALWAYS eager to help.

While he is a good lecturer and clearly cares about what he teaches, it's impossible to ask questions or get clarification. If you don't already know the concepts don't even ask him. He'll make you feel like the most unintelligent person on the planet when answering them. I kid you not he laughed at me when I asked him a question in class.

Professor Dransfield is so passionate about his field and such a passionate & high energy lecturer. However, the first-year engineering chem class is difficult (he says this the first day). If you're fine with being challenged, Dransfield is a fantastic professor. His research is in climate science, something you will learn a lot about in his class
It's Gen Chem...what can u expect

Dr. Dransfield moves at a very quick pace, and it's really difficult to keep up at times. It's a lot of material for one semester, and he does his best with what he's given. Tests are hard, but he's always available outside of class and is really helpful one on one. Grading is also extremely fair. Showing up to class/recitation is 20% of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is amazing and he aims to challenge the best students in his class, so his exams are a bit tricky, so if you like chemistry and are good at it, go to his class, you'll find him fascinating. If you have questions, don't hesitate to ask him. He loves to answer questions both in and out of class. "Thinking is more important than memorizing."

Chem1151 was honestly the hardest class I've ever taken, but the only reason I still liked it was because of Dr. Dransfield. The content is really fast, there were four exams counting the final, and overall the class was just hard. But Dransfield was always caring, had awesome engaging lectures, and was available outside of the classroom.

Professor Dransfield is very passionate about chemistry and it reflects everyday in class. I took AP chem and decided to retake this course to get an easy A before orgo, but I was mistaken. I did receive an A but this course was very very hard. Overall I thought his lectures were very engaging and his class was my favorite this semester.

Unless you are in love with chemistry and took AP Chem, PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. He teaches at such a high level and if you don't already know the concepts you will not understand. If you already took AP chem, you will enjoy his teaching pace. BUT I DID NOT UNDERSTAND A SINGLE LECTURE. Be prepared to put in a lot of effort.

Dransfield is a great guy. He's a little intimidating and blunt, but is super helpful when approached one-on-one. Tests are a little difficult, but definitely manageable. There are lengthy homework assignments each week, but they can really only raise your grade. If you can put in the time to study, you'll do well in the class.

To be honest, if you see yourself as less self-disciplined and "searching for a comfortable" person, just don't take his lecture will be much easier for you. Professor Dransfield's class requires 100% attention in class and 5-6 hours of after-school work to do well. Chemistry is hard, and getting good grades depends on self-studying.

Teaches super fast and teaches harder than the other chemistry classes. Teaches some unnecessary things and got into Orgo topics. 3 midterms and one resurrection final. Homework and participation points to get your grade up. Exams are fairly hard. You can do well in the class if you spend hours a week in the class.

Professor Dransfield is one of the most arrogant people I have come across. Instead of helping a student understand when they have question, he will automatically make you feel lesser without actually explaining anything. He can be unprofessionally aggressive when dealing with students and does not to seem to care about understanding the material.

He's arrogant, passive agressive and intimidating, which makes you not want to ask questions. Not comprehensive and there are no make ups. Even though the midterms are off class hours and online, they are very hard. At least he curves them. His lectures are heavy and he goes in a very fast pace. DO NOT take his class. avoid him at all costs.

This is the worst professor I have had in my life. He is extremely rude and is not understanding. He goes through the material as we were all familiar with it, making it intimidating when we would like to ask questions. For the midterms, they are extremely hard although he curves it at the end. Also, he has no respect for his students at all.

Take this class if you enjoy chemistry and would like a challenge. Do not take this class if you are looking for an easy A. If you take this class carefully balance out your schedule with easier classes if you can. Professor Dransfield can be intimidating and talks highly of his class, but have confidence in yourself that you are able to do well!

He is so passionate about chemistry. You're graded on participation (in-class poll everywhere), three midterm exams, a final (can replace midterm scores), weekly homework, and recitation attendance. He knows he's a hard teacher and offers plenty of extra credit and outside support. You have to engage with and stay on top of the content to do well.

Professor Dransfield works extremely hard to get through all of the material because it is so much stuff. You definitely have to have some discipline and put in hours of work outside of class. I definitely recommend a study group! There are 3 midterms but he has a resurrection final! He has office hours and so do the TAs which are extremely helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield's class is the hardest college class I've taken so far. Not having a strong chemistry background, I struggled greatly. He went so fast that I could not keep up at times. His tests are extremely difficult and I barely passed all of them. To pass this class, you must dedicate a few hours a day studying for it.

Professor Dransfield is a great professor but the class goes very fast and is pretty difficult. You should definitely devote time outside of class to studying and making sure you know the material. The tests are hard but extra credit and the weekly homework assignments help your grade. Having a background in chemistry will help you immensely.

Professor Dransfield is an efficient lecturer, he is able to convey his points easily, but he speaks too fast and the class is very difficult. His tests are also very difficult and backtracking is disabled. The only way to be adequately prepared for this class is to have taken AP Chem (I did not, and I struggled, but my friends who did did fine).
He pulls the high school teacher "I'll wait" phrase when students don't know answers to his questions within literally 10 seconds of him asking it.

for the exams and the final you had to answer the question before moving on to the next one. Also, once you submitted answers to questions, you couldn't go back and revisit. Prof thought this would prevent cheating but all it did was waste time and leave you with literally seconds left before the end of the exam.
YOU MUST GO TO CLASS IF YOU WANT TO PASS. This professor is amazing, but it will be difficult to do well if you don't study regularly and show up to all classes.

Professor Dransfield is a great guy and professor, but the course is rough. It moves at a very fast pace that he worsens by adding in unnecessary material. The exams are MUCH harder than any examples he gives. He does offer many opportunities for extra credit, which is much needed. Overall, you will learn a lot in this class but it is hard.

The lectures are so fast and very dense. You can fall behind in notes and in the class very easily. He is very enthusiastic about chemistry, so I had high hopes in the beginning. If you have a good background in chemistry, go for the challenge. But if you are not confident in chemistry, do not take. He is also extremely passive aggressive.
Sometimes when students asked questions, prof Dransfield would literally laugh in their face. He's so pretentious and passive aggressive and his exams were so unbelievably hard.

The lectures went EXTREMELY fast and we were given new material for the final TWO DAYS before the final test. The lectures contained WAY too much information and I walked out extremely confused after every class. Be prepared to do most of the learning on your own outside of class and spend 30+ hours studying for each exam to barely scrape by.

professor dransfield goes extremely fast in every lecture, theres lots of homework and often he comes off a bit pretentious in class. but if youre confused he truly wants you to understand. He really wants you to succeed in his class. keep up with lectures and do practice problems from the textbook!

He the best lecturer I have had so far in college. He is engaging, interesting, and provides helpful ways to help you understand the content. It's a lot of content, but that isn't his fault, and he does everything he can to help you. He is very accessible at office hours, answers questions very well, and will work with you until you understand.

Professor Dransfield is a dedicated professor who loves chemistry and is thorough. However, CHEM1151 is basically 2 semesters of chem in one (fast). Also, while homeworks and quizzes may be straightforward, his exams are EXTREMELY HARD. One of the hardest courses I have ever taken and I only got through with excessive studying. Go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield is so enthusiastic about chemistry, and it's shown throughout the lectures. He goes through units fast so study every unit thoroughly. DO NOT DO LAST MINUTE STUDYING. THE TESTS ARE DIFFICULT SO BE PREPARED. TIPS: Do well on the quizzes and HW to boost your grade. Also find a study group! Resurrection Final is the move!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield is a great professor. He is passionate and occasionally funny, and he really wants you to learn. He is put in a tough position teaching a stacked class, but he manages to get through all of the material and more. I took an honors section of the class and I don't recommend it. The tests are way harder than other sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture is like drinking through a firehose. I had him for honors gen chem, and he will teach the honors section additional topics, so we go insnaely fast.. Very nice teacher, cares about people who works hard, but I think there was too much information.

Professor Dransfield is passionate about Chemistry but goes very quickly. He always says we are behind but added a new chapter to the final that is not even in the curriculum (I would've rather spent the extra 2 days on review). He is not an empathetic professor at all. Prepare to put in lots of work outside of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Dransfield is a good professor, but the amount of material he goes through is insane. Started off not liking him too much, but by the end of the class his dedication to his students really shone through. He tries to make the class as bearable as possible, but he can only do so much. Midterms are tough but bearable. Resurrection final is clutch
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good teacher, class is tough but he makes it as easy as possible. This is my third year of chemistry, so it wasn't too hard for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Had him for an Honors section of Gen Chem for Engineers. Very enthusiastic about all the topics, but he goes through lectures VERY quickly. Homeworks are reasonable. Exams are extremely time-sensitive and fairly difficult, though he curves final grades to compensate. Also, definitely ask him questions about kinetics or global warming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He may talk fast and cover more material in a semester than seems possible, but he's a phenomenal teacher. Midterm averages are low, but mostly because people intentionally bomb them knowing they can make up for the bad grade with the resurrection final. He's a tough professor, but I learned more in this class than any other at Northeastern so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice and funny guy who has a lot of knowledge about the subject, but this class is a CHALLENGE. I study at least 25 hours before each exam and barely scoot by with a B/B- on each. Be prepared to be overwhelmed in lecture, take hours to do homework, & study your butt off. Definitely harder than other chem sections for this course. Learned a lot tho!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He taught so fast it was impossible to keep up. We where like 5 chapters ahead of the other section. It got to a point where he wouldnt even accept some questions because he wanted to go faster.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class average was generally around a 75 with a curve. He talks like you're watching his lecture on 2x, so get ready to write. He's super lecture heavy, with weekly HW that's about 25 Q's. I studied for 12-15 hrs per test and averaged mid-high 80s, but I'm not naturally great at chem. Wouldn't take him again, but he's a cool dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: First off- This course is VERY difficult. If you aren't already pretty comfortable with high school chemistry, prepare to be confused 90% of the time. Be aware, the professor is not very understanding.

This professor made chemistry very difficult for me to learn and to deal with emotionally. Many tears were shed because of conversations with him. I personally was not receptive to his harsh delivery at times, and I would have preferred a more understanding and compassionate professor. I will say that the homework assignments are manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: THIS CLASS IS HARD! If you're taking this class prepare to have the ride of your life. There's a lot of material and the course goes by veerryy fast. Start studying on day one and I recommend watching Organic Chemistry Tutor after every lecture to make sure you understand everything from that video. He's rly nice but pls take this class seriously.

He's an incredible person, but his class is way harder than any of the other profs. Tests are incredibly difficult and not like practice problems. Lectures are great, he's very passionate about chem, and really cares about his students. A good amount of homework, but nothing crazy. Lots of studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield was a good professor but his classes and tests were considerably harder than the other chemistry professors. His classes were very fast-paced but he was always in a good mood, ready to teach. Attending classes was definitely a must to do well in the course. There were lots of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield, though new to Northeastern, is by far one of the best professors. His class is not easy, and it won't be easy. However, he is the most caring and passionate man I've met and won't let you fail as long as you put in the effort and the work. Try hard and. you will succeed in his class. Go to his office hours if you need help!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I had a great time in Dr. D's class. The lectures were thought-provoking and he cares about his students. Tests are worth a lot but aren't too difficult. Absolutely take the class if transportation even remotely interests you!

Great guy, even better professor. Dr. Dulaski's lectures were incredibly engaging and useful if you're someone interested in multimodal transportation. Keep in mind he's very test-heavy (like 80% of overall grade), but if you go to class and engage with the content you'll have nothing to worry about.

I was so grateful to be in Dr. D's transportation class. I loved starting class with transportation news, keeping the class up to date with current events. Class content was engaging and if you payed attention in class exams, while worth a lot, were not very difficult. Would recommend to anyone interested in transportation!

Amazing guy, AMAZING professor. Keeps you very engaged in class and makes sure that you understand every concept you'd be expected to know. Have him for CIVE4554 and had for Statics, has been fantastic in both and has clear expectations of his students. Only complaint I have is he is very hard to reach via email.

I've taken five classes with Dr. D during my time at Northeastern. Take his classes. They're usually difficult, but you learn a ton. He deeply cares about his students and has unmatched passion for transportation. He is extremely detail-oriented, and accessible outside of class for help (book a meeting or go in-person!). Hands down my favorite prof
Dulaski is the greatest professor of all time. Love this guy
He's the best!
The GOAT. Cannot make statics any easier.

Can't recommend enough. Establishes a friendly, first-name relationship with EVERY student. Wants you to do well and will do everything he can to ensure you do well. Lectures were great, homework is helpful, and exams are very fair. Funny guy too.

Dulaski was such a great statics professor. He was so caring and kind and really wanted his students to be successful. He has been the best professor I have had at Northeastern and I could not recommend him enough. He does in fact call on you during class but it keeps you prepared. He also will not judge if you don't know the answer. Great guy.
Overall a GREAT teacher. Dulaski is a super nice and respectful person. He explains concepts well and encourages questions. I would 100% recommend and would definitely take again.

Professor Dulaski is a great Statics professor. While I took the class in summer so it was an accelerated course, he had reasonable tests and homework. His notes are very clear to follow and he always makes sure everyone understands the material. His tests don't trick you, they just ensure you are grasping the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor

Ran a bit like a high school class, short homework due almost every class, 6 exams throughout semester, calling randomly on students. Very good at communicating topics and helping students who aren't grasping at first. Respects students and commands respect in turn.
Great professor. Prepares you for the real world! More than any other professor. He expects a lot because he gives you a lot to learn.

Highway design was not an easy class, requirements for hw format were pretty strict, final project took time, especially design part in CAD. However, it's been a year since I took this course and I still have all the info left in my brain. Lots of work but it was worth it. Also by the end of the semester the class turns into almost a family.

Talk. If not, he'll call on you. Do practice problems for  midterm and final. There is also a paper due for this class. I recommend do the paper from AWD on transportation and use it again for his class. Homework take forever to do but that's just him. Remember, MEMO formats. His class gets harder each time he teaches it. Highway and Transportation
worst! choose the other professor. she conducts exams completely unrelated to what she taught. The professor seems to not have a clue about what she is saying and her syllabus is outdated.
Great class!

Public School Professor
A Employed person
Never Taking it again

The professor just rushed in the last and we students ended up losing marks in the last homework because she missed out on discussing the possibilities of a specific type. 
The TAs are inconsistent , the grading was unfair.
Especially in the exams too many questions to solve, which made us losing our grades further.

Worst professor I've met in Northeastern University. There are too many homework and tests.Each task requires a substantial amount of time to interpret, as the instructions are often unclear. TAs grade the homework without standard rubric, seem to reflect individual interpretations rather than a standardized approach.
The class was very boring and the professor seemed to agree with any solution brought up by the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do not recommend this professor. The material itself is not difficult, however the professor behaves very spitefully towards students when it comes to grading, and generally communicates in very inappropriate condescending manners. Exams have near impossible time limits, and participation points are given however she feels like.

My biggest complaint is her lack of professionalism. She responds to piazza posts in condescending tones (all caps, sounds irritable, etc). Was a no-show for one of her office hours, no explanation given. Her exams are difficult and there are 3 (also a project). Her grading scale is weird (can only get an A with 95%). Lectures are painfully boring.

The content covered in the class can be readily acquired through YouTube tutorials, requiring minimal time and costing nothing. Regrettably, I feel the class did not provide any value for the money and time invested. Moreover, the professor's assistance outside of class was notably lacking.

The professor spent weeks explaining some really simple concepts repeatedly. She doesn't seem to realize she's teaching master students. Sometimes she doesn't seem to like students asking her questions either. The course doesn't include some important database concepts. If you want to take an easy class and don't expect to learn much, take this.
Curriculum seems outdated. Needs update

While the professor is knowledgeable of SQL concepts, she is not commanding enough during the class. She tends to accept solutions during lectures from students which makes it unclear and vague to understand the concepts. The lectures are very boring unless you interact. The exams can get scary if you don't manage time.

Well-structured online course, but lectures are very long and there are so many of them. The tests are 51% of the grade and are based on all the lecture videos. Professor Durant offers study sessions each week to go over the materials, which is helpful though. Definitely not an easy A as it is a 95-100 grading scale, so be ready to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Very lecture heavy, but lectures were boring. The amount of work was overwhelming. For an asynchronous class, there wasn't a good sense of an online community. 

Directions for assignments can be unclear, and if you ask questions on piazza it is also hard to get a clear answer.

The pre-recorded lectures are well structured, so I rarely went to lectures. There is a final group project of 1-3 people which was a great way of applying class knowledge on a domain of interest. The negative part of this class is that your grade depends on 3 exams, each worth 17% of your grade. Prof.'s office hours are great for learning.

Grade distribution is very weird. 1 exam holds almost equal weightage to the other 10 assignments. Very average teaching. Apart from SQL stuff, she isn't able to convey her dbms knowledge to the students.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the professor's lecture. The grading criteria were clear so there wasn't a surprise when the marks came out.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Professor Kathleen is very caring and teach with a lot of passion. You will learn a lot from her lectures. Make sure to read the book before every lecture. Homeworks are easy. 

Exams are long and you have to be very very careful about time management. Practice as much as you can before every exam. There are 3 in total (51% of total grades).
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Assignments took hours every single week. Not sure if it was the content being extremely difficult or the teaching but I'm assuming it was a mix of both. Between the weekly videos and the assignments I saw the excel screen more than I saw my own family this semester.

I figured it couldn't be too bad since it was asynchronous, but I was apparently very wrong. professor durant makes just about all the lecture videos which are extremely time consuming (about 3-4 hours worth of videos alone) each week and they are rarely ever helpful for the assignments. instructions are unclear and she is very unhelpful in piazza.

I really enjoyed Professor Durant's class. I thought her lectures were clear and extremely thorough. She also held copious office hours (more than any other professor I have had at NEU), which was truly appreciated. She also looked to give partial credit on exams wherever it was available.

Gives you almost everything you need to succeed in class lecture. Skim the reading before hand, answer a few questions, and you will be set. Start the final project early. Most homework can be completed in about an hour. First 2 tests are hardest. The homework exactly covers the material for tests.

Prof. Durant is a very understanding professor. She is clearly passionate about Databases and would love to give you practical advice from her career experience.

I did find her exams to be tedious - not difficult and found myself not having enough time to complete the Test, but the Prof. was understanding and curved the results.

Professor is a very nice person but can be dry and fairly confusing about material - reading textbook seems to give equal if not better information. She's extremely helpful in OH though. Poor grading scheme, classmates and I would receive different grades on same submission because of TAs. HWs are often unrelated to class or test content.
Nice person, easy material, horrible lectures
Easy homework, tough exams with unreasonable amount of time, unfair exam (students will receive different questions with different difficulty)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. Lectures are unclear and hard to follow. I think I could've learned the course material in half the time. As other's have mentioned, she simply reads off of her notes and doesn't seem to really know what she is talking about.
For 80% of the time, her lecture has nothing to do with her homework. Tough tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is often disorganized and confused about her own content. Seems like a nice person but I wouldn't take a class with her again. This class became very confusing very quickly and most students in my class agreed with me on this.

She's definitely making progress, at least as a professor for a remote class on Canvas. She organized logistics very clearly on a separate website, including every week's schedule, readings, assignments, grades... etc. , which made me feel safe remotely. The database course needs many readings prepared for each lecture. Intensive but fun.
